spots.name: Play Weiqi (the game of Go)
spots.desc: As a symbol of Chinese culture, Weiqi is one of the world’s great strategy games where a few simple rules lead to limitless possibilities. Weiqi is hugely popular in Chengdu to the point where it has been nicknamed Weiqi City. Chengdu Weiqi Classroom is the only place where foreigners can study this game with English speaking assistance.

spots.desc: The pavilion houses a museum dedicated to the Chinese poet Dufu and contains pictures and information on other famous Chinese poets as well. spots.name: Badaling
spots.desc: The most popular tourist section of the Great Wall because of extensive, quality renovations. However, very crowded with other tourists. Give yourself about 2-3 hours to climb up the wall if you're a slow climber, an hour or less if you're speedier. The hike is a challenge with plenty of steep hills, so once you get a bit into the wall the crowd thins quickly. A cable car and a "sliding car"…
spots.price: Tickets to climb the wall are around ¥40 (discounts available for the young and the disabled); Audio tour service…

spots.name: Qingdao Jiaozhou Bay Bridge
spots.desc: This massive sea-crossing bridge, approximately 42.23 km long, opened in 2011 and was once among the longest sea bridges in the world. It spans the Jiaozhou Bay, connecting the main urban area of Qingdao with the West Coast New Area. The bridge features six lanes and a speed limit of 80 km/h. From the bridge, you can enjoy expansive views of the sea and the busy Qingdao Port in the distance.
spots.hours: Open 24 hours daily (may be temporarily closed during severe weather conditions such as strong winds, heavy fog, or…
spots.price: Toll only. Private cars approximately ¥30-40 (depending on vehicle size, as per official on-site rates). No pedestrian…
spots.addr: spanning the Jiaozhou Bay between Shibei District and Jiaozhou City,

spots.name: Niujie (Niu Street) Mosque
spots.desc: Famous Mosque build in 996 and the oldest and largest of the mosques in Beijing. Structured as a traditional Chinese palace, but also uses typical Arabic decoration with a lot of red colour. A must see if staying for more than a few days. The Muslim presence in the area is obvious with many Muslim shops and Arabic signs around.
spots.addr: 88 Niu Street (牛街88号 Niújiē)

spots.name: Yu Wan
spots.desc: Fish balls, a Fuzhou delicacy, minced beef and pork inside a fishy flour ball of dough in a thin broth, excellent. Also just called 肉丸 (rou wan) but check they are fish nonetheless.

spots.name: Huang Guo Shu Waterfalls
spots.desc: The sightseeing bus costs ¥50 per person and is valid for three days. The escalator costs ¥30 one way or ¥50 round trip.

spots.name: Tianmen Mountain
spots.desc: Tianmen Mountain (Tianmenshan, 天门山, meaning Heaven's Gate Mountain) is a scenic and historic mountain in Tianmen Mountain National Park, Zhangjiajie, in northwestern Hunan Province, China.

spots.name: Great Bao'en Temple Ruins Park
spots.desc: Once one of Nanjing's greatest Buddhist temples, the Great Bao'en Temple was destroyed by the Taiping rebels when they occupied the city in the mid-19th century. There is now a museum at the site. The Porcelain Tower, which is said to have been one of the seven wonders of the medieval world, has been reconstructed and affords great views over the city.
spots.price: ¥120 (discounted to ¥80 if you buy the ticket on the website)
spots.addr: 1 Yuhua Road, Zhonghuamenwai, Qinhuai District (秦淮区中华门外雨花路1号)

spots.name: Hanging Monastery
spots.desc: Lodged precariously on a cliff-face, this monastery is one of the more remarkable sights in China: a complex of 40 rooms linked by mid-air walkways. It appears to be stuck into the side of the cliff, but is actually supported by stilts. It was built in 490 and renovated several times, including in 1900; much of the current structure dates from the Ming and Qing Dynasties. Visiting is not…
spots.price: Entry full ¥115. Students, 60-69 half price. Disabled (残疾人), 70 and over, less than 1.2 m tall children free

spots.name: Id Kah Mosque
spots.desc: First built in 1442, it is distinctive for its yellow walls and Central Asian architecture. As with any place of worship, you should dress modestly, meaning your legs and shoulders should be covered, and women should wear a hijab. You should remove your shoes before entering the carpeted area. On Eid, you can see the local Uyghurs dancing on the square in front of the mosque.
spots.hours: Open 08:50-22:00 though closed during prayer times

spots.name: Beijing Workers’ Stadium
spots.desc: A major modernised stadium and entertainment complex anchoring the Gongti district, hosting football matches, concerts, and large-scale events.
spots.addr: Gongti North Road

spots.name: Erhai Lake
spots.desc: Visit Guanyin Temple and several islands. Go with a group and enjoy a great day out. Boats can be easily arranged as the owners come into town to drum up business and you can see what you are getting from the photobooks they carry. Ferry rides at real stations cost around ¥30. There are signs indicating that fishing boats and paddle boats can't carry tourists, although it is unclear what the…
spots.price: A ¥30 entrance fee is charged for lake visits, plus ¥50-100 per person for a day

spots.name: Fuzhou jasmine tea
spots.desc: Fuzhou jasmine tea is one of the city’s most famous traditional drinks and a hallmark of Fuzhou (Min) tea culture. Fuzhou is widely regarded as one of the birthplaces and major centers of jasmine tea production in China.

spots.name: National Indoor Stadium
spots.desc: A multi-purpose arena used for ice sports, concerts, and events, remaining an active venue within the Olympic Green complex.
spots.addr: Olympic Green, Chaoyang District

spots.name: Jingshan Park
spots.desc: Jingshan is another former imperial garden with some imperial garden architecture. A popular next stop after leaving the Forbidden City from the north gate, this 23-hectare (57-acre) park is built around Jingshan, the artificial hill created with the soil dug to build the Forbidden City's moat. Literally meaning "Prospect Hill", it is also variously known as Coal Hill or Feng Shui Hill. Those who…
spots.addr: Jingshan Front Street

spots.name: Ningming Huashan Rock Art Scenic Area
spots.desc: One of the most notable examples of ancient rock paintings in Asia. The paintings were painted by the Luoyue people between the 5th century BC and the 2nd century. The paintings can be seen at 38 locations in the region but it is the Huashan (or Flower Mountain) site, which is the most famous as this is where the paintings are most clearly visible. Hence the paintings take their name from that…
spots.addr: County Highway X570, Chengzhong Town (城中镇县道X570)

spots.name: Loulan Ruins
spots.desc: A ruined city in the Lop Desert. The city was the capital of a small kingdom of the same name, which began to flourish from the 2nd century BC onward. In the 1st century BC, the kingdom came under Chinese control and was renamed Shanshan, but the city itself continued to be known as Loulan. The city was abandoned in the 4th century AD, apparently due to the Tarim River changing course and…

spots.name: Zhangye Danxia National Geological Park (Qicai Danxia)
spots.local: 张掖丹霞国家地质公园
spots.desc: A unique geological landscape with layers of rocks of different colors and mountains in the background. It is one of the highlights of Gansu province. Be aware that despite seeming like it is in the middle of nowhere on a map, the site is heavily commercialized, filled with shops selling tourist snacks and knick-knacks, touts on megaphones, speakers and screens blaring Chinese pop music…

spots.name: Bezeklik Thousand Buddha Caves
spots.desc: Stand high on the cliffs of west Mutou Valley under the Flaming Mountain. Of the 83 original caves, 57 caves remain. The murals cover an area over 1,200 square meters in more than 40 caves. Beginning in the Southern and Northern Dynasties, the construction experienced Tang Dynasty, the Five Dynasties, Song and Yuan dynasties. The caves had been the Buddhist center of Gaochang. Near the end of the…

spots.name: Ayding Lake
spots.desc: It's a few kilometers to the south of Turpan and marks the lowest point of China and is 154 meters below sea level. The salt lake completely dry, and there's a globe monument marking that point. You can rent bicycles for ¥20 to cycle the 3km from the entrance the globe. Not a whole lot to see.
spots.price: ¥30 per person plus ¥10 if you drive in

spots.name: Beihai Park
spots.desc: Beihai is a former imperial garden centred on a lake with interesting religious and garden architecture. There's a big island and white pagoda which was built in the 17th century. The giant buildings westward outside are PRC's Ministry of Defence and General Staff, which, to be honest, ruin the scene of the west bank. On the north bank, you can visit some small but beautiful gardens. Beihai is a…

spots.name: Beijing Zoo and Aquarium
spots.desc: (They do have pandas but displays aren't as good as other places in China, such as the Panda Breeding Centre in Chengdu, Sichuan Province). The animals are kept in very small cages in which they pace to and fro in sheer restlessness and desperation. The lion and tiger building is particularly disappointing, housing a collection of large felines in concrete cages without any natural habitation.…
spots.hours: Zoo: Apr-Oct 07:30-18:00; Zoo Nov-Mar 07:30-17:00; Aquarium Apr-Oct 09:00-17:30; Aquarium Nov-Mar 09:00-17:00

spots.name: Yuyuan Garden
spots.desc: Beautiful traditional Chinese garden in the heart of Shanghai, next to the City God Temple.
spots.addr: 279 Yu Yuan Lao Jie, 四牌楼

spots.name: Nanjing Road
spots.desc: It is certainly Shanghai's best-known shopping street, and probably China's. At around a million shoppers a day, it is also one of the world's busiest. It has been busy for generations; Amy Tan's novel The Kitchen God's Wife mentions a figure of 100,000 visitors a day in the 1940s. Nanjing Road starts on the riverside at The Bund and goes about 6 km west from there to Jing'an Temple. It continues…

spots.name: Mount Putuo
spots.desc: Mount Putuo (普陀山 Pǔtuóshān) is an island and National Park in Zhoushan, near Ningbo in Zhejiang province, and derives its name from a sacred Buddhist mountain at the center of the island.

spots.name: Kanas Lake
spots.desc: Kanas is a Mongolian word meaning "beautiful and mysterious lake". Kanas Lake is located in the northern part of Burqin County. The lake comes from the glacial meltwater of Kuitun, Youyi Peak and other mountains and the local precipitation. The lake is 1,374 meters above sea level and covers an area of 45.73 km2. It is a mountain lake and inland freshwater lake located in the Altai mountains and…
spots.addr: Altai Prefecture Burqin County 232 provincial highway (阿勒泰地区布尔津县232省道)

spots.name: Baima Temple
spots.desc: A must-visit in Luoyang, White Horse Temple is revered as China’s first officially sanctioned Buddhist temple and one of the oldest in the world, dating back nearly 2,000 years. Though it has been rebuilt multiple times, it retains its historical and spiritual significance, drawing numerous domestic tourists. The temple complex also includes an international section with temples donated by…
spots.price: Tickets are normally ¥35, but cost ¥50 on public holidays
spots.addr: 6 Luobai Road, Luolong District (洛龙区洛白路6号)

spots.name: Stone Forest
spots.desc: This is a UNESCO listed site of remarkable karst geography. Good weekend or day trip and lots to see. Visit early to avoid crowds.
spots.addr: 70 km southeast of Kunming, about 2 hours by bus from Kunming East Bus station

spots.name: CITIC Tower (China Zun)
spots.desc: Beijing's tallest building (528m) completed in 2018. Its distinctive shape is inspired by the ancient Chinese zun ritual wine vessel and it dominates the CBD skyline just southeast of Guomao.

spots.name: World Trade Center Tower III
spots.desc: Just north-west of Guomao station, this 338m skyscraper is Beijing's second tallest building. It houses offices, the China World Summit Wing hotel, and restaurants and bars with panoramic city views. The terrace at Migas Mercado offers one of the city's best nighttime views of the illuminated CCTV Headquarters.

spots.name: Jiayu Pass
spots.desc: A rather modern and rebuilt part of the last fortress at the Great Wall towards the west. Includes the generic camel rides and archery stores to distract from the rather meager attraction. Take bus no.4 to last stop, north of the town. Western terminus of the Ming Great Wall of China, trapezoid-shaped fortress overlooking the Gobi Desert. Looking over to the mountain is almost the best part of…

spots.name: Huajiang Canyon Bridge
spots.desc: As of 2025, the world's highest bridge at 625 m. The bridge features a glass sightseeing walkway, specialty coffeehouse with panoramic views and has facilities for extreme sports (e.g. bungee jumping) integrated.

spots.name: Lugu Lake
spots.desc: Lugu Lake (泸沽湖 Lúgū Hú) is on the Yunnan/Sichuan border in China. It is a nice lake between Yunnan and Sichuan to relax one or two days. The area is protected from extensive development.

spots.name: Pork floss
spots.desc: Pork floss (Rousong) is a signature food product of Fuzhou and a familiar part of everyday local cuisine. Fuzhou is widely regarded as one of the key centers for traditional pork floss production in China.

spots.name: Helan Mountain National Forest Park (Suyukou)
spots.desc: This section of the Helan mountains features rugged rock ridges with a thick forest on one side. A concrete walkway hanging onto the cliff face ascends to the nearest peak in about 5.5 km. Near the entrance to this path, a network of trails accesses a lower ridge and some valleys and canyons. The ridge is also accessible by ropeway, and features two pagodas and a suspension bridge over a canyon.…
spots.addr: Zhensu Road, Helan County

spots.name: Mawangdui Han Tombs
spots.desc: While this may sound like a tourist attraction, it is simply the ditch in which the tombs were uncovered. There are no artifacts present as everything is now in the Hunan Provincial Museum.
spots.addr: 89 Guhan Road, Furong District (芙蓉区古汉路89号)

spots.name: Sayram Lake National Park
spots.desc: An excellent spot to explore the Tianshan mountains

spots.name: Lugou Bridge
spots.desc: Dating back to the late 1100s and spanning the Yongding River, the Lugou Bridge is both architecturally and historically important. Noted by Marco Polo in the 13th century as a "very fine stone bridge" it came to be known in the West as simply the Marco Polo Bridge. An incident between Japanese and Chinese forces here in 1937 marked the beginning of the Second Sino-Japanese War.

spots.name: Tongji University
spots.desc: The main campus is in Yangpu District. The university is served by the Tongji University station (同济大学站) of Metro Line 10, which brings you to the southeast gate of the university, facing Siping Road (四平路).

spots.name: Detian Waterfall
spots.desc: At 200 meters wide with a 75 meter drop, the Detian waterfall, located primarily on the Chinese side of the Sino-Vietnamese border, is definitely the highlight of the area, as well as being the fourth largest waterfall along a national border and the largest such waterfall in Asia. Because the amount of water cascading down the waterfall differs with the season, the waterfall will change…
spots.price: Standard adult tickets are ¥115; discounts are available for persons aged 60 to 69 and children between 1.2 and 1.5…

spots.name: Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum
spots.desc: The most famous Ming-era site of Nanjing, Ming Xiaoling is the mausoleum complex of Zhu Yuanzhang, also known as the Hongwu Emperor, the first emperor of the Ming Dynasty. Most of the monuments are lined up along the mile-long Sacred Way (shendao), which runs from the Square Pavilion (Sifangcheng) with its giant bixi turtle to the artificial hill under which is the emperor's burial chamber. Look…

spots.name: Mount Heng
spots.desc: One of China’s Five Sacred Mountains. The mountain range runs 150 km from Hengyang to Changsha. Of the cluster of 72 peaks, the most known is Zhurong Peak. Mount Hengshan is acknowledged as a holy place, the most scenic mount of the Five Sacred Mountains in China. To reach Mount Heng/Nanyue from Hengyang City, take a bus from Zhongxin or Linghu Bus Station (¥7-13 depending on time and bus); or…

spots.name: Sanxingdui
spots.desc: The ruins of an ancient Chinese city where archaeologists discovered remarkable artifacts that radiocarbon dated circa 12th-11th centuries BCE. Sanxingdui (Three star mound) is the name given to this previously unknown Bronze Age culture. First excavated in the 1930s, the site continues to yield surprises to the present day. Between 2020 and 2022, archaeologists working on the site discovered six…
spots.addr: 133 Xi'an Road, Guanghan, Deyang (德阳市广汉市西安路133号)

spots.name: Dianchi Lake
spots.desc: Plateau lake with improving scenery. Historically, a pearl on the Yungui Plateau, the ecosystem was severely damaged in the 1960s by conversion of wetland into farmland. Great efforts are made starting from the 1990s to reverse this damage. Today the northern tip of the lake is gated by a series of causeways. Trawlers are working around the clock to purify the water. The best places to see the…

spots.name: Old Town of Lijiang
spots.desc: Walk around, watch people, shop, drink and eat. There is a bonfire at around 19:00 at the Si Fang Jie (四方街), the central plaza. Many local folks dance there, apparently entertain themselves. Tourists are welcomed to join. And if you get there early in the morning, you can avoid the crowds.
spots.price: Entry to the old town is free. The Old Town Maintenance Fee was abolished in 2017. However, some attractions within the…
spots.addr: Gucheng District (古城区)

spots.name: Jade Dragon Snow Mountain
spots.desc: A mountain massif (also identified as a small mountain range) visible from Lijiang and snow-capped all year round. Its highest peak is Shanzidou (扇子陡; Shānzidǒu) at 5,596 m. The view of the massif from the gardens at the Black Dragon Pool in Lijiang is one of China's finest views. The far side of the mountain forms one side of Tiger Leaping Gorge (虎跳峡; Hǔtiàoxiá).To reach the mountain area, you…

spots.name: Monument to the People's Heroes
spots.desc: A cenotaph with round-the-clock honor guard commemorating the PRC's veterans and war dead. Illuminated at night. Usually blocked off unless there is an important ceremony or visitors, but even then only those participating can go to the base of the cenotaph. However, you can usually get close enough to take pictures.

spots.name: Tashilhunpo Monastery
spots.desc: The traditional seat of the Panchen Lamas. It was constructed in 1447 and is where the Panchen Lamas resided and conducted their religious and secular duties. Covering a floorspace of 300,000 square meters, the monastery is enshrined with the world's largest gilded bronze Buddhist statue, the 22.4 meter high statue of Maitreya Buddha.

spots.name: Tianshan Tianchi National Park
spots.desc: Tianshan Tianchi National Park (天山天池国家公园) is in Xinjiang, in North West China. It's listed on the UNESCO World Heritage list.

spots.name: SEG Plaza
spots.desc: This most famous electronics market has ten floors of small stalls selling electronics and accessories. The first two floors are wholesale components and the rest is mainly dedicated to consumer goods. Most customers are expected to buy in bulk when buying small things like wires or cases, but they will sell individual pieces for reasonable prices. It has kind of a maze-like layout, so it's good…

spots.name: Dr. Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum
spots.desc: Resting place of the first president of China, who led the 1911 revolution that toppled China's last imperial dynasty. A beautifully designed complex that features a fusion of traditional Chinese and Western architectural styles. Closed on Mondays.

spots.name: Heng Mountain
spots.desc: World Heritage Tentative list (UNESCO). This is the least religiously important of the 5 Sacred Mountains of Taoism.

spots.name: Duge Bridge
spots.desc: The Duge Bridge crosses the Beipan River canyon on the border between Yunnan and Guizhou provinces. The bridge is part of the G56 Hangzhou–Ruili Expressway between Qujing and Liupanshui. It has a main span of 720 m and was constructed between 2011 and 2016.
spots.addr: G56 Hangzhou–Ruili Expressway

spots.name: Xixia Wangling National Park
spots.desc: Xixia Wangling National Park (西夏王陵国家公园) is just west of Yinchuan in the Ningxia Autonomous Region of China. In 2025 the imperial tombs of the park were listed as a .

spots.name: Yonghe Temple
spots.desc: The temple was built by Chinese emperors who harbored a deep fascination for the Tibetan (Tantric) version of Buddhism. Over the years, many Tibetan and Mongolian monks lived and taught here, and some are still in residence today. The temple is famous for its 18m (60 ft) statue of Maitreya Buddha carved from a single piece of sandalwood. The temple was saved from destructions during the Cultural…
spots.addr: Yonghegong Dajie, at intersection of Second Ring road

spots.name: Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge
spots.desc: The official crossing into North Korea. Passage is only by vehicle or train. Travellers are not allowed to walk across this bridge.

spots.name: Yumen Pass
spots.desc: Another fortified mountain pass. The Yumen Pass was built around the same time as the Yang Pass.

spots.name: Sera Monastery
spots.desc: Founded in 1419 by one of Tsong Khapa’s (the founder of the Gelupa sect) eight disciples. It became famous for its tantric teachings, while Drepung drew fame from its governing role. Sera was smaller than Drepung, with 7,000 monks, but was very rich and comparable in power. The monks of Sera were considered clever and dangerous.

spots.name: Central TV Tower
spots.desc: A tower with an observation deck at the height of 238 meters, providing a view of central Beijing. Below the observation deck is a dedicated television cultural center at 235 m, with a virtual television studio scene. A revolving restaurant at 221 meters provides both food and scenery.
spots.price: ¥90 for admission ticket; ¥258 for lunch at the revolving restaurant; ¥308 for dinner at the revolving restaurant
spots.addr: 11 West 3rd Ring Rd Central

spots.name: Wanda Plaza
spots.desc: Wanda Plaza has stores all over the country, this is the first one in Zhuzhou. In although not in the busy streets, but after all, is the first Wanda Plaza has a lot of traffic, business is also a lot of, many are the first Zhuzhou, there are large supermarkets Wumi supermarkets, the price is also more pro-people.
spots.addr: 589 Yunlong Avenue

spots.name: Mixue Ice Cream & Tea
spots.desc: Mixue Bingcheng is affordable and popular among young people. There are chain stores in any city, so it is worth trying.

spots.name: Chao lake
spots.desc: This is the great lakes of China. Sights on or around the lake include Lao Shan in the middle and Zhongmiao Temple on the northern bank. There are also some natural springs. Catch bus at 合肥汽车站 (Hefei Bus station) at 明光路168号Míngguāng lù 168 hào.

spots.name: Wangfujing
spots.desc: Beijing's most famous shopping street, nowadays with mostly the same international brands and modern malls you will find anywhere else in the world. The street is pedestrianised for several blocks, making it pleasant to walk around. Several large malls in the area such as Oriental Plaza (see below) and Sun Dong An plaza. One useful shop is the Foreign Language Bookstore, at the northern end of…

spots.name: Yellow Crane Tower
spots.desc: It has repeatedly burned down, so the present tower completed in 1980 is mostly concrete, on the site of twelve previous wooden incarnations. Tower and associated buildings are atop the ridge of Snake Hill, looking down on Number One Yangtze River Bridge and the confluence of Yangtze and Han rivers. The complex includes Snake Hill Park, the Yellow Crane Tower, and the Mao Pavilion into which many…
spots.hours: Apr-Oct 08:00-18:20, Nov-Mar 08:00-18:20. The tower is open for an additional 20 minutes
spots.addr: No. 1 Xishanpote, Sheshan, Wuchang District (武昌区蛇山西山坡特一号)

spots.name: Shilin
spots.desc: Shilin (石林, Shílín) karst region, the "Stone Forest", is a national park in Kunming Prefecture, Yunnan province in southern China. The huge pillars of stone, formed by erosion, look like something out of a fantasy film. The park is large, too big to see all of it in one day. It has several different areas and many interesting nooks and crannies, and you can easily lose yourself on the winding…

spots.name: Double Ninth Festival
spots.desc: It is on the 9th day of the 9th lunar month, usually in October. This festival celebrates longevity and respect for elders. In Zibo, it is common to hike up local mountains such as Mount Lushan, enjoying the crisp autumn air. Traditional foods like steamed buns and Boshan-style mutton soup are popular choices during family gatherings on this day.

spots.name: Bingling Temple / Bingling Si
spots.desc: Bingling means 'ten thousand Buddhas' in the Tibetan language.. This is a cave grottoes, with the highlight of 27m Maitreya Buddha. Can be visited in 2h on normal walking speed.
spots.price: ¥50 for main entrance, and various fees (¥80-200) for select caves

spots.name: The Star of Nanchang
spots.desc: Formerly the world's tallest Ferris wheel (they still say it is), with a height of 160 m.

spots.name: Zhengyangmen
spots.desc: Built in 1419 as the front gate of the inner city wall. It was only used by the emperor on his way to Tiantan. Now it houses exhibits with photos and models of the old city.

spots.name: Foguang Temple and Nanchan Temple
spots.desc: Fóguāng and Nánchán temples house two of the oldest buildings in China (the one in Nánchán being the oldest known wooden structure and the one in Fóguāng the grandest of preserved wooden buildings of the Tang dynasty). As of 2011, tourist agencies do not appear to serve these destinations, which gives them a wonderfully secluded feel. They can be visited comfortably on a 4-6 hour excursion from…

spots.name: Shanghai Grand Opera Palace
spots.desc: The Opera Palace is often listed as one of the ten best opera houses in the world. Performances are normally "classic" Western-style opera.

spots.name: Si duhe River Bridge
spots.desc: Sidu River Bridge is located at the junction of Yichang City and Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, in the high mountains of Wuling Mountains in western Hubei Province. The bridge connects Yichang in the east and Enshi in the west, and is listed as the 16th section in the Shanghai-Chengdu Expressway (now known as Shanghai-Chongqing Expressway), which is one of the key control projects of…
spots.addr: Badong

spots.name: Shanghai University
spots.addr: Shangda Road, Baoshan District

spots.name: Qiandao Lake
spots.desc: Qiandao Lake, the Xin'an River Reservoir, is located in Chun'an County, Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province. A small part of it connects to the northwest of Jiande City, Hangzhou City. It is an artificial lake formed to block the upper reaches of the Xin'an River to build the Xin'an River Hydropower Station. After the completion of the Xin'an River Reservoir, the dam intercepted the upper reaches of…
spots.addr: Chun'an County

spots.name: Little (Wild) Goose Pagoda
spots.desc: Completed in 709 AD. Now administered by the Xi'an Museum.
spots.hours: Mar 15-Oct 31: 09:00-18:00; Nov 1-Mar 14: 09:00-17:30, no entry in last 60 minutes, closed on Tuesdays
spots.price: You can claim a ticket for free to walk around the temple area. But you must pay ¥50 (student half-price) to enter the…
spots.addr: 72 Youyi West Road, Beilin District (碑林区友谊西路72号)

spots.name: Imperial Ancestral Temple
spots.desc: This was the temple where the emperors and other members of the royal family would pay respect to their ancestors. The buildings are original, though much of the interior, including the ancestral tablets, were destroyed during the Cultural Revolution. It has since been repurposed as a museum dedicated to the working class Chinese.
spots.price: ¥2, does not include entry into buildings

spots.name: Olympic Green Tennis Center
spots.desc: A major tennis complex that continues to host professional tournaments and public sporting events.
spots.addr: Olympic Green, Chaoyang District

spots.name: Capital Museum
spots.desc: New high profile history and art museum located in an impressive building. Exhibits include the history of Beijing and artifacts from throughout China's history.
spots.price: Free, tickets must be reserved three days in advance on the official website
spots.addr: 16 Fuxingmenwai St (复兴门外大街16号 Fùxīngménwài Dàjiē)

spots.name: Cathedral of the Immaculate Conception
spots.desc: The original foundation of the cathedral was in 1605, making it the oldest Catholic church in Beijing, the current building in Baroque style dates from 1904.

spots.name: Yalu Zangbu Grand Canyon
spots.desc: The Yalu Zangbu Grand Canyon is one of the most magnificent Grand Canyons in the world, surrounding the world's 15th highest peak, Nangabawa Peak (7,782 meters above sea level). The Grand Canyon is known for its spectacular geological landscape, primeval forest and rich ecosystem, and is known as "the last secret place on earth". The river in the canyon is winding and the rapids are rushing…

spots.name: Maotianshan Shales
spots.desc: A UNESCO World Heritage Site rich in fossils from the Cambrian Period. Some of the fossils are displayed at a small on-site museum, but the majority of them are now kept at the Chengjiang Fossil Site World Natural Heritage Museum.

spots.name: Tianjin Binhai Library
spots.desc: Part of the Binhai Cultural Center, it's a futuristic-looking five-level library.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:30-20:00 (only the first three floors are open from 18:00 to 20:00), Mon 14:00-20:00
spots.addr: 347 Xusheng Road (旭升路347号)

spots.name: Disneyland Park
spots.desc: Shanghai Disneyland is divided into six lands. Upon entering the park you will arrive in Mickey Avenue which replaces Main Street U.S.A. found in other parks. With its central location, the Gardens of Imagination serve as the park's central hub and features seven gardens: Garden of the Twelve Friends, Melody Garden, Romance Garden, Woodland Garden, Garden of the Magic Feather, Fantasia Garden…

spots.name: Tianjin Radio & TV Tower
spots.desc: The eighth tallest freestanding tower in the world. But this one might be one of the most spectacular as it is surrounded by water.
spots.price: ¥45 (observation deck only), ¥100 (observation deck plus library, art displays, VR experience and more)

spots.name: Qianling Mausoleum
spots.desc: The shared tomb of China's first and only female emperor Wu Zetian (武则天) and her husband Emperor Gaozong of Tang Dynasty (唐高宗). The best preserved of the Tang imperial tombs. The main burial chamber has not been excavated, though the burial chambers of the tombs of five attendants, one court official, one military officer, two princes and one princess have been excavated, and the latter three are…

spots.name: New Century Global Center (Chengdu Global Center)
spots.desc: New Century Global Centre consists of New Century Global Shopping Centre, Ocean Paradise, Intercontinental Hotel, Central Business City and Music Fountain Plaza, etc.; [1-2] It is divided into four districts, namely, East, West, South and North, and the main body of the building is made of sea-blue colour, with white floating boards articulating the undulating body of the building into a whole.

spots.name: Maijishan National Park

spots.name: Songyue Pagoda

spots.name: Taining

spots.desc: Danxiashan (丹霞山, Dānxiáshān) is a geopark in Guangdong, China. A landscape of stunning cliffs, steep and rounded red mountains, caves, forests, and lakes in rural Shaoguan, Danxiashan is still little known to foreign visitors.

spots.name: Shanghai Disney Resort
spots.desc: Approved in 2009, Disney sought to build a theme park in Shanghai that was both "authentically Disney [and] distinctly Chinese". It opened in mid-June 2016 and received 5.6 million visitors that year, an average of around 28,000 a day. It is Disney's third theme park in Asia and the only one in Mainland China. Most attractions are in Chinese. Maps and schedules are available in English. As of…

spots.name: Ditan Park
spots.desc: Park with a lot of cypresses and also a small amusement park area.
spots.addr: Andingmenwai Street (安定门外大街; Āndìngménwài Dàjiē)

spots.name: Nanjing Museum
spots.desc: Eleven exhibition halls display a mixture of poetry, bronzes and silk artifacts interspersed with cultural displays. Worth pondering over are a jade burial suit and an arched door from the Ming era Porcelain Pagoda. A great place to spend humid or rainy days.
spots.hours: Tue-Fri and most public holidays 09:00-17:00, Mon 09:00-12:00, no entry in last 60 minutes, closed on the first day of…

Included in the tour is a "Chinese marriage", a look at carved tree roots, followed by a boat ride through the garden canals. The incredible collection of bonsai trees ('pen cai' or 'pen jing' in Chinese) at the end of…
spots.addr: Dongbei St

spots.name: Liuhe Pagoda

spots.name: Fuling
spots.desc: This is the first tomb of the Qing Dynasty in which Nu'erhachi, the founder of the dynasty, is laid to rest. It dates to the early 17th century and is constructed in traditional Manchu style along lines of Chinese fengshui. The area is listed, along with the other imperial tombs of the Ming and Qing dynasty, as a UNESCO world heritage site and a AAAA-rated tourist site on the Chinese national…

spots.desc: This is, first of all, a huge park with both green spaces and an enormous open square with an equally-impressive ancient palace gate (the palace is Tang dynasty, built in 634 AD). There's a model of the palace next to the gate. The square sometimes hosts public performances. The park even has an IMAX theatre. The park, gate and square are accessible for free. If you pay for admission, you can…

spots.name: Fayuan Monastery
spots.desc: This Buddhist temple was built in 645 and rebuilt in 1436-1449, which makes it the oldest existing in Beijing. Now, it is the site of the Chinese Buddhist Academy and the exhibition center for Buddhist cultural relics, and is also an important institution training young monks and Buddhism research. The temple covers 6,700 square meters. The main buildings are Gate of Temple, Heavenly King Hall…

spots.desc: A historic Catholic church established by the French Jesuits and completed in 1703.

spots.desc: A Buddhist temple founded in 1882 with two Jade statues of the Buddha imported from Burma. There are restaurant facilities with steamed dumplings. This is a bit of a hike from Jing'an temple, so consider taking a taxi or at the very least the Metro up to nearby Changshou Road Station. Note that Changshou Road is a different station than Changshu Road.

spots.name: St. Ignatius Cathedral
spots.local: 徐家汇圣依纳爵主教座堂
spots.desc: The area was under renovation in 2018, but the cathedral is open. Don't wear slippers or anything that resembles it, they are strict on decent outfit rules.

spots.name: National Art Museum of China
spots.desc: China's premier art museum with over 35,000 m² of exhibition space in 21 halls on four stories. Collection exhibits both ancient and contemporary work, with some Western art as well.
spots.price: Free, but only 4,000 tickets available until 16:00 daily
spots.addr: 1 Wusi Street (五四大街1号 Wǔsì dàjiē)

spots.name: Grand Buddha at Ling Shan
spots.desc: The main attraction of Lingshan (灵山) is Grand Buddha, one of China's largest Buddha statues at over 80 m tall. The whole Lingshan area is a tourist attraction built only in 2008 so there is no history to find here, with a musical fountain which plays out the story of the birth of the Buddha, as well as the Brahma palace (梵宫), a very grand palace with the pillars made of sandalwood, built to host…

spots.name: Zhaozhou Bridge
spots.desc: A great masterpiece of Chinese civil engineering. Created around 600 CE under the Sui dynasty, it survived numerous floods and earthquakes, and is considered nowadays as the oldest stone single arch bridge in the world. Adjacent small museum with a collection of stone carvings, steles and statues from the vicinity of Zhou County.
spots.addr: Zhao County (赵县; Zhàoxiàn)

spots.name: Yarghol Ancient City
spots.desc: Ruins of an ancient Silk Road town. This city was established during the Western Han Dynasty and continued through from the period of Northern Wei Dynasty. (If you want to take the bus, take off the bus 102 at the last stop and walk the next 5 km. Alternatively, from the last stop of the line 102, you can hire a vehicle for around ¥10 to take you the rest of the way to the site.)

spots.name: Pavilion of Prince Teng
spots.desc: One of the Four Great Towers of China and setting for the famous poem Téngwáng Gé Xùjì by Wang Bo during the Tang Dynasty.Tengwang Pavilion, is located on the east bank of the Gan River, at the intersection of the Gan River and the Fuhe Old Road, and is a landmark building in Nanchang City and a symbol of the ancient civilization of Yuzhang. It was built in the fourth year of Tang Yonghui (653)…
spots.addr: No. 58, Antique Street, Donghu District

spots.name: Ancient Observatory
spots.desc: The observatory, built in 1442, has been open to the public since 1983. Ancient star maps and instruments to watch stars can be seen here. Displays on the history of Chinese astronomy, and several large astronomical instruments set on top of an old watchtower of the city walls.
spots.addr: 2 Dongbiaobei Hutong (东裱褙胡同2号; Dōngbiǎobèihútòng)

spots.name: White Cloud Temple
spots.desc: Taoist temple established in 793. Houses the Chinese Taoist Association and a Taoist Health Clinic.
spots.addr: 6 Baiyunguan Street (白云观街6号 Báiyúnguànjiē)

spots.name: Zhujiajiao Town

spots.desc: Part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties". spots.addr: Qingdongling Branch Road, Liupanying Village (六盘营村清东陵支线)

spots.desc: Longhushan (龙虎山) is a National Park outside Yingtan City, Jiangxi Province, China. It is a part of the China Danxia UNESCO World Heritage Site, and is a UNESCO Global Geopark.

spots.name: Ruoergai

spots.desc: Qinhuai River, a tributary of the great Yangtze River, is 110 km (about 68 mi) in length and covers a drainage area of 2,631 km² (about 1,016 sq mi). The river used to be called Huai River, and it is said that the river was channeled to the city of Nanjing during the reign of Emperor Qin Shi Huang, so it was named Qinhuai River from then on. Qinhuai River is the largest river in the Nanjing City…

spots.name: Presidential Palace

spots.desc: Spend half a day exploring the headquarters of past emperors and the Nationalist government. The Palace includes the former offices of many top governmental officials, including Chiang Kai-shek and Sun Yat-sen, as well as the former residence of Sun Yat-sen. It is one of the few places in mainland China where the flag of the Republic of China still flies. Informational placards around the palace…
spots.hours: 08:00-18:00 in summer, 08:00-17:00 in winter. Closed on Mondays

spots.name: Leifeng Pagoda

With escalators, elevators, and a totally new pagoda places on top of the foundation, there is not much to see within the pagoda…

spots.name: Tianducheng
spots.desc: A neighborhood built in Parisian style, including a 108 m replica of Eiffel Tower, fountains and landscaping.

spots.name: Putuo Zongcheng Temple

spots.name: Confucius Forest
spots.desc: The Cemetery of Confucius, or "Confucius Forest", is a cemetery where Confucius and more than 70 generations of his descendants have been buried. spots.desc: Which literally means the Coming of Winter, falls on December 22. In Zibo, families mark the occasion with hearty meals, often including dumplings (饺子), which are believed to keep the body warm and healthy during the cold season. spots.name: Dagukou Forts

Perhaps of greater interest is the Dagukou…

The pavilions along either side have displays about Confucius and the history of Confucianism. The courtyard is a pleasant place to relax or watch art students practice sketching. Open until 18:00 in summer…

spots.desc: This 6-km bridge over the Yangtze has sculptures that are classics of Chinese sociallist art; with workers and farmers carrying tools, soldiers carrying weapons, and all of them holding books, most likely Quotations of Chairman Mao Zedong (better known as The Little Red Book). The bridge was built after Soviet advisors left China during the Sino-Soviet Split of the 1960s, and is therefore the…

spots.name: Tiger Hill Pagoda

Some buildings have been reconstructed and a 48-m tall brick pagoda with seven stories and eight sides remains, though now missing its wooden outer skin. It is one of the few remaining examples of pagodas of this type and is sometimes called the "Leaning…

spots.name: Lingyin Temple
spots.desc: Meaning "heart of the soul's retreat", this temple west of the West Lake is an active Buddhist temple at the bottom of a hill. The tomb of the Guangxu Emperor, the last…

spots.name: Beilin (or Stele) Museum
spots.desc: Remarkable collection of 4000 inscribed stone tablets, covering scripture, poetry, classic Chinese texts, triumphs of rulers, family history, and practical affairs such as instructions to rebuild a school. The 7th century Nestorian Stele (Showroom 2, first exhibit on the left) depicts the coming of Nestorian Christianity to China.
spots.hours: Mar-Nov: 08:00-18:30; Dec-Feb: 08:00-18:00, no entry in last 45 minutes

spots.desc: Hengdian World Studios is a theme park centered around film production. Visitors can tour the movie sets and experience the charm of film-making. It is one of Jinhua's iconic tourist destinations.

spots.name: Military Museum of the Chinese People's Revolution
spots.local: 中国人民革命军事博物馆
spots.desc: A great place to read the official Chinese version of what happened in Chinese military history, from ancient times up to 1949. There are also airplanes, boats, guns, missiles, rockets and vehicles on display (including U.S. military hardware evidently seized during the Korean conflict). spots.name: Temple of the Moon Park
spots.desc: The altar was built in 1530 during the Ming Dynasty for use in ritual sacrifice to the Moon by the Emperor of China. The altar and the surrounding grounds are within a public park. The altar is no longer intact, though the surrounding walls remain.

spots.name: Siling Co
spots.desc: The largest lake in Tibet. There are a large number of black-necked cranes and some 120 species of birds in total.

spots.name: Sanmenxia Dam

spots.desc: A well-known Taoist temple at the centre of the Old City, one of the biggest examples of traditional Chinese architecture in Shanghai. You can find local snacks and food as well as other traditional Chinese decorations in the surrounding commercial area.

spots.name: Longyou Grottoes
spots.desc: The Longyou Grottoes are a series of at least 24 large artificial sandstone caverns located inside Phoenix Hill, just north of the centre of Longyou on the north bank of the Qu River. They are thought to date to a period before the creation of the Qin Dynasty in 212 BCE, but there is no record of their existence prior to 1992. They were discovered when a local spent 17 days pumping out one of the…

spots.desc: The Drum Tower was built in 1272 and relocated here in 1420; the Bell Tower was built around 1700. The towers were first used to play music and later on to tell Beijingers the time. Now they house a 63-ton ancient copper bell and a number of ancient/replica drums. Free guides start tours at specific times, and the Drum Tower has short performances every hour or so (usually at half-past). There…

Due to the amount of premium ingredients and time that goes into making it, it is very expensive and must usually be ordered several days in advance.

spots.desc: Focuses on Western Science. Entertaining and educational for children. The building is quite impressive.

spots.name: China Art Museum Shanghai
spots.desc: The former China Pavillion for Expo 2010 now is a museum of Chinese modern art. Permanent exhibitions focus on some of the best-known Chinese painters' works, the history of Chinese modern and contemporary art, and the culture of Shanghai. Visits start at the top and you work your way down through the galleries, whose quality decreases a bit the lower you go in the building. On the top floor is…

spots.name: Puning Temple
spots.desc: This temple houses the awesome statue of Guanyin. She measures 22 m high and is the tallest wooden Buddhist statue in the world.

It is located within a Buddhist temple, some of which was rebuilt in the Qing Dynasty. There is an active temple in the back built in 2001. Only the ground floor of the pagoda is open to visitors. Inside the pagoda, you can see a big Buddha statue.

spots.name: Tomb of Apak Hoja
spots.desc: A massive, elegant building created in 1640 in typical Islamic style. Also a pilgrimage site. It claims to be the resting place of the legendary "Fragrant Concubine", although the traditional Uyghur tale of her rebellion against the Qing imperial family is omitted in the tomb's accompanying introduction.

spots.name: Yuelu Academy
spots.desc: The Thousand-Year-Old center of culture and learning of southern China. Established in 976, it is the spiritual predecessor to what is now Hunan University. Rich in history and beautiful period architecture, a visit to the academy will put you in touch with the ancient elites of southern China. You can find all the history on the website and then visit the academy yourself, wandering through its…
spots.hours: May to October: 07:30-18:00. November to April: 08:00-17:30. The Museum of Chinese Academies (中国书院博物馆) opens and shuts…

spots.name: Changsha IFS

spots.desc: Tiantaishan (Mount Tiantai, 天台山) is in Tiantai County, Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province, China.

spots.name: Kumbum Monastery
spots.desc: Perfectly situated and beautifully appointed throughout the monastery with frescoes and murals. Butter sculptures, frescoes and padded embroidery are the three treasures of the monastery. Kumbum means A Hundred Thousand Buddha Images in Tibetan, and it is one of the six great Gelukpa monasteries boasting enormous influence in both the religious and secular life of the Amdo (Eastern Tibet) region.…

spots.name: Siguniangshan National Park
spots.desc: Siguniangshan National Park (四姑娘山国家公园 - Four Maidens Mountain National Park) is in Aba Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture in Sichuan province.

spots.name: Huazhong University of Science and Technology
spots.desc: The campus is decorated with a number of parks and lotus ponds, and plenty of public sculpture, including the monuments to Mao Zedong (at the main entrance of the main campus), Albert Einstein (near the dorms and the dining hall on the Eastern Campus, 东校区), and Confucius (in front of the Academic Building West 12, 西十二教学楼, in the western part of the main campus). The forested Yujiashan Mountain…

spots.name: TianYi Pavilion
spots.desc: Tianyi Pavilion is the oldest private library in existence in China. A complex of gardens and small buildings, Tianyi Pavilion was built in 1561 in the Ming Dynasty (1368 - 1644). The Tianyi Pavilion is not only world famous for its wide collection of books, but also for its unique architecture and elegant landscape. The Tianyi Pavilion has a flush gable roof, and is six bays wide and deep, with…
spots.addr: Tianyi Street No. 5, Haishu District (海曙区天一街5号, China)

spots.name: Yang Pass
spots.desc: A fortified mountain pass built during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty. Part of the Silk Road and the Great Wall of China.

spots.desc: The traffic island is almost ringed by a subway, enter from north side next to Metro entrance. Great tower with ancient bells to toll the time for the city. Short musical performances every hour or so.

spots.name: Luofu Mountain

spots.addr: Changning Town, Boluo County (博罗县长宁镇)

Allow about 2 hours to see both the excavation hall and the exhibition hall.Site featuring various tools and art pieces from around 3,000 years ago. The amount of unearthed items is just massive. They include pottery, blades, jade items, building foundations and various golden art pieces. There are two main buildings: the hall constructed over the…

spots.addr: 2 Jinsha Site Road, Qingyang District (青羊区金沙遗址路2号)

spots.name: Central Conservatory of Music
spots.desc: The main purpose of the conservatory is to educate musicians. Concerts now and then.
spots.addr: 43 Baojia St (鲍家街43号 Bàojiā Jiē)

spots.name: Zhenguo Temple
spots.desc: Zhenguo Temple is a 1000-year-old Buddhist Temple north of Pingyao. It is the only remaining temple in China built in the architectural style of the Five Dynasties Period (10th century). It shares the UNESCO World Heritage Site designation together with the Ancient City of Pingyao and Shuanglin Temple. Zhenguo Temple was first constructed in 963, during the Northern Han Dynasty, when it was known…
spots.addr: 12 km northwest of the Ancient City of Pingyao

spots.name: Nánshān Temple
spots.desc: To the south of Táihuái village, arguably the nicest monastery in the area is Nánshān Temple. Invitations to ride a horse en-route. Although there are more signboards at Nánshān Temple in English than at many others, non-monks are not welcomed to stay, and neither are Tibetan monks. These rules and a slight distance from the centre have maintained a greater realistic ‘monastic’ non-conflictive…

spots.name: Weiyuan County
spots.desc: A county under the jurisdiction of Neijiang city, it has a mix of rolling hills, ancient villages, fruit orchards, and scenic nature typical of the southern Sichuan Basin. Weiyuan is particularly known for its fig production and a relatively undeveloped, local travel experience.

spots.name: Mutianyu
spots.desc: This is a magnificent section that is as equally well restored as Badaling with greener surroundings. It is a lot less crowded than the Badaling section. But the hike is a bit more difficult than Badaling. Choose Mutianyu over Badaling for your introduction to the Great Wall if you don't mind the hike. There is also a fun theme park like toboggan ride (¥55)(see below). You get choose cable car or…

spots.name: Shishi Sacred Heart Catholic Cathedral
spots.desc: Built in the 1860s, it is one of the oldest church structures in the city, and the largest of its kind of Southern China. It is used for worship.
spots.addr: 56 Yide Rd (德路旧部前)

spots.name: Liziba Station
spots.desc: This is where Chongqing’s metro line takes a surreal detour—straight through the middle of a 19-storey apartment block. The train literally whooshes through the building, making it one of the city’s quirkiest photo-ops and proof that Chongqing’s engineers never shy away from creative solutions.
spots.addr: No. 39 Lizibazheng Street

spots.name: Xiaotayuan Mosque
spots.desc: A historic mosque that combines Chinese and Islamic architectural styles. Shanghai's largest mosque, with a separate women's mosque next door.
spots.addr: Xiaotaoyuan Jie 52

spots.name: Kaiyuan Temple
spots.desc: The largest and most famous Buddhist temple complex in the area. The well-landscaped grounds house two famous tall pagodas, several temple buildings, an ancient stone turtle, and a variety of religious art. The Xi Jie (West Lane) outside of the temple is a busy shopping street, with all kind of shops selling souvenirs, joss paper and other Buddhist items, snacks, and books. The Ancient Ships…
spots.addr: Xi Jie near Xinhuan Bei Lu, northwest of downtown

spots.name: Qingjing Mosque
spots.desc: The only surviving mosque of the many that used to exist. It is over 1,000 years old, and was rebuilt in 2009 so the dome is now restored after a 200-year absence. Well worth a visit.
spots.addr: Tumen Street

spots.name: Xuanwu Lake
spots.desc: One of the lakes in Nanjing. There are three islands in the middle, all connected by causeways, equipped with a children's amusement park, a small zoo, and beautiful views of the city and Purple Mountain. Guests can also rent paddle boats. The lake's picturesque nature is a tribute to the beauty of Nanjing, which is so revered in China. free.
spots.addr: No. 1, Xuanwu Lane, Xuanwu District, Nanjing

spots.name: City Wall of Nanjing
spots.desc: The City Wall of Nanjing was designed by Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang (r. 1368-1398) after he founded the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) and established Nanjing as the capital. To consolidate his sovereignty and keep out invaders, he adopted the suggestions of advisor Zhu Sheng to build a higher city wall, to collect grain and to postpone the coronation. Building the wall took 21 years, and involved 200,000…

spots.name: Lion Grove Garden
spots.desc: Has an incredible collection of pitted, eroded rocks that were greatly appreciated by classical Chinese scholars. It was originally part of a Buddhist monastery. The gardens are a reminder of the Buddhist story of the lions. The layout of the garden follows many twists and turns. It is easy to get quite lost in these winding paths.

spots.name: China Tea Museum
spots.desc: In addition to tea, the collections of the China Tea Museum also include tea culture carriers, including tea utensils, tea paintings and calligraphy, tea stamps, tea culture inscriptions, tea boxes, tea advertising leaflets, letters, silk and tea banknotes, tea shipping and sales orders, tea packaging paper, tea shop price lists, tea house tea plaques, as well as tea customs, tea poems, tea…
spots.hours: Daily 09:00–17:00, last admission 16:30, closed on Tue
spots.addr: 20 Longjing Road, Xihu District

spots.name: Baiyang Lake
spots.desc: China's largest natural lake offers peaceful water scenes and expansive lotus gardens. Boats are available for small groups, and some islands on the lake have restaurants that cook with local ingredients and hotels for overnight stays.

spots.name: Shanhua Ancient Monastery
spots.desc: Built in the Tang Dynasty, rebuilt in the Liao Dynasty, and then largely destroyed by war, the monastery was rebuilt in the Jin Dynasty under the supervision of the great Southern Song scholar Zhu Bian. The temple has four high-value ancient buildings: one from the Liao Dynasty and three from the Jin Dynasty. The mountain gate (Hall of Heavenly Kings), the Hall of Three Saints, and the Puxian…
spots.price: ¥50 (full price during peak season); ¥40 (full price during off-season)
spots.addr: Yongtaimennei Street (大同市楼房巷南寺街6号)

spots.name: Drum Tower
spots.desc: Great tower with drums to toll the time to the old city. Short musical performances every hour or so.
spots.hours: In high season (April 1st to October 10th), opening hours are 08:30-21:30, the last combo tickets are sold at 19:00…

spots.name: Guoqing Temple
spots.desc: Located in Chengguan Town, Tiantai County, Taizhou City, Zhejiang Province, it was founded in the eighteenth year of Sui Kai Emperor (598), initially named Tiantai Temple, and later took "If the temple becomes, the country is Qing" and changed its name to Guoqing Temple. The temple covers an area of 73,000 square meters.The eminent monk "Wise Master" (Zhið «®) of the Sui Dynasty founded the…

spots.name: Chaoyang Park
spots.desc: The largest park in Beijing at 3 km by 1.5 km. The park features an artificial beach, two large swimming pools, a bungee jumping tower, boat rental, concert stages, sports areas, a number of amusement park rides and flower areas. The individual entertainment options might not be impressive, but the size of the park and the number of local visitors makes a stroll here delightful anyway.
spots.addr: 1 Nongzhan South Road (农展南路1号; Nóngzhǎn Nánlù)

spots.name: Lakes of Shichahai
spots.desc: A large area north of Beihai Park that encompasses 3 adjacent lakes (Xihai, Houhai, and Qianhai) enjoyed by locals for a long stroll along the lakes. The quiet lake area turns into a busy nightlife hub around the crossing point of the eastern end of Houhai and Qianhai.

spots.name: Mausoleum of Genghis Khan
spots.desc: This is not the actual tomb of Genghis Khan, as he was buried in an unmarked grave in a secret location. Rather, it is a temple dedicated to Genghis Khan, and a major place of worship for the ethnic Mongols.

spots.name: Shanghai Urban Planning Exhibition Center
spots.desc: More interesting than you'd expect given its name, this museum documents the history of Shanghai and attempts to chart its future, with changing exhibits on the first two floors and a permanent exhibition on the rest. Many historic pictures from the 19th century introduce still-existing historic places. There is a heavy focus on eco-friendly satellite cities with spacious public centres and loads…
spots.price: ¥30 for adults, ¥15 for students and children
spots.addr: 100 Renmin Dadao

spots.name: Badachu
spots.desc: Badachu is comprised of eight Buddhist temples and monasteries at the foot of the Western Hills. Restored in the 1980s, the whole area is now a park and popular tourist destination for Beijingers wishing to escape city life.

spots.name: Shanghai Zoo
spots.desc: See the giant panda and many more exotic animals at this spacious and modern zoo that's for the most part a far cry from the concrete animal prisons found elsewhere in the country (such as Beijing). Be prepared for some shocking behaviour by other visitors. Note that the good amount of space given to the animals means that a lot of walking is involved. There are some fairground rides for the…
spots.price: ¥40; children less than 1.2 m (3 ft 11 in) in height are free with paying adult

spots.name: K11 Sky Garden
spots.desc: If you are on a low budget or you want to have some free fun, buy some cheap drinks in a grocery and go up by elevator to the 6th floor of the 61-floor K11 skyscraper. Then you turn right and right again, to find one of the two sky gardens (the other one is left and left), with empty tables and chairs and a nice view on the city. Best timing for this secret place is at evening with your partner…

spots.name: South Yandang Mountain
spots.desc: The scenic area is full of peaks and ridges, criss-crossing streams and ravines, dense caves, and rushing waterfalls. South Yandang Mountain not only has beautiful natural scenery, but also has a cultural gathering of the three religions of "Confucianism, Buddhism and Taoism", with numerous cultural relics and unique folk customs.
spots.addr: Yandang Village, Nanyan Town

spots.name: Simatai
spots.desc: Simatai (司马台; Sīmǎtái) is a rugged and dramatic section of the Great Wall of China, located in Miyun District, roughly 120 km (75 mi) northeast of central Beijing. Unlike heavily restored sections like Badaling, Simatai retains much of its original Ming-dynasty masonry.

spots.name: Tianjin Italian Town
spots.desc: Tianjin Italian Town is the former Italian Concession that was built in 1902. It covers the area from Coast area to the Victory Road. Across the river from Italian Town lies the Ancient Culture Street, Peace Shopping and Pedestrian Street, Tianjin Financial Road, Little White CBD (小白楼) and Tianjin Municipal Government. Owning the unique location, the Italian Town is merged with different…

The building has been cut through with large voids and chasms, creating a roof-scape with the scale of a traditional village, in contemporary architectural language. The exhibits are nothing special…

spots.name: Tomb of Emperor Jingdi
spots.desc: A Han dynasty tomb containing 50,000 doll-sized terracotta figures. There are human figures (think small and naked version of the terracotta warriors) as well as a whole army-like formation of life-like animals (pigs, dogs, etc). spots.desc: Here you can watch and enjoy the atmosphere of international auto and motorcycle racing, including the FIA GT Championship, A1GP (World Cup of Motorsports), Asian Formula 3 Series, Asian Festival of Speed and ZIC's very own Pan Delta Super Racing Festival. spots.name: Guangxi University
spots.desc: An example of a good provincial university with several tens of thousands of undergraduate and graduate students. Includes classroom buildings, dormitory buildings, and large administration buildings on a very large and beautifully landscaped campus.

At the foot of Yuelu Mountain is Yuelu Academy. You can also get up/down by shuttle bus (¥20) or cable car (¥30 up, ¥25 down, ¥50 both directions).
spots.addr: Yuelu District (岳麓区)

It is home to some 60 giant pandas, but also has some red pandas and a colony of black-necked cranes. The pandas are basically on display for tourists but views are much closer than is possible at most Western zoos. (If you want to get…

spots.name: China World Trade Center Mall (Guomao)
spots.desc: A large high-end shopping complex integrated into Beijing’s central business district skyline. The mall is dominated by luxury and premium international brands, business-oriented retail, and upscale dining. It caters primarily to office workers and affluent shoppers rather than tourists, with pricing and positioning firmly at the premium end of the market.

spots.desc: Steps away from the east gate of Fragrant Hill. Acres of greenery and flowers for those tired of urban smog and traffic noise. Sir Johnston, teacher of the last emperor Puyi, had a villa in Cherry Glen, a silent and beautiful retreat in the Gardens. In the spring, the gardens hosts special exhibits of tulips, peach and plum blossoms, peonies, and the like. Separated by the Fragrant Hill Road, the…

spots.name: Great Bell Temple & Museum
spots.desc: Also known as the Temple of Awakening Life (觉生寺 Juéshēng Sì). Home to the 15th-century Yongle Great Bell which, at 6.94 m tall and 46.5 tons, is the largest bell in China. The 227,000 Chinese characters inscribed on it spell out Buddhist sutras. Subway Line 13 to Dazhongsi, and then walk 400 m west.

spots.name: Guangji Temple
spots.desc: Buddhist temple built around 1460. Burned down in 1934 and was rebuilt in 1952 and further renovated in 1972. It is supposed to look as it used to, but it does not really look old. The temple is functioning as a center for Buddhist thinking and learning and it is also the headquarters of the Chinese Buddhist Association.

spots.name: Tang Dynasty Three Pagodas
spots.desc: Offering one of the best preserved Buddhist structures in China. The Central Pagoda is almost 1200 years old and represents a period when Dali was a Buddhist Kingdom. The Congshen Temple behind the Three Pagodas has been rebuilt and reopened…

spots.name: Tanzhe Temple
spots.desc: Buddhist temple dating back as far as the Western Jin Dynasty (more than 1600 years ago). It is one of the oldest and largest temples in Beijing. The site is especially beautiful to visit in April when the surrounding Magnolia trees are in full bloom.

spots.name: Babaoshan Revolutionary Cemetery
spots.desc: Built as a temple, it was made into the chief cemetery for Communist Party figures. Buried here are artist Xu Feihong, writer Lao She, and many of the most important CCP leaders.

spots.name: Longhua Temple
spots.desc: One of the city's less-visited temples for foreign visitors, but an important one and one of the most popular for Shanghai residents during religious festivals. It is one of the largest ancient Buddhist temples in Shanghai. The first temple was built in 247 CE, but it was destroyed and rebuilt under the Song dynasty, 977 CE, and several times since then. It is a temple of the Ch'an sect of…

spots.name: National Natural History Museum of China
spots.desc: Large museum with a lot of information on nature, but some of the exhibitions are a bit old fashioned. Exhibitions cover paleontology, zoology, animal behavior, botany, the original of human beings, dinosaurs, aquarium, the human body, cells, skeletons and an interactive park.

spots.desc: A series of natural limestone bridges. They lie within the Wulong Karst National Geology Park, itself a part of the South China Karst-Wulong Karst UNESCO World Heritage Site. In Chinese, the bridges are all named after dragons, namely the Tianglong (天龙桥, Sky Dragon), Qinglong (Azure Dragon) and Heilong (黑龙桥, Black Dragon) bridges. Among others attractions, there is an adrenaline via ferrata along…

spots.name: Imperial Academy
spots.desc: The academy was the highest level college and location of examinations for the civil service in Imperial China. Very much related to the neighbouring Confucius Temple in that the studies and exams were conducted in the Confucian tradition. Displays documenting the history of the imperial exams system and the lives of students. Pleasant courtyard, slightly quieter than that of the temple. Open…

spots.name: Jiming Temple
spots.desc: Jiming Temple is the most popular temple in Nanjing and it is located convenient to downtown.
spots.price: Tickets are ¥10, which includes 3 free incense with every ticket. Price may rise during popular seasons (e.g., Spring…

spots.name: The Garden of the Master of the Nets
spots.desc: Founded in 1140, and rebuilt in 1770 by the bureaucrat Song Zongyuan. The enclosed complex of house and garden is one of the smallest, most beautiful, and most perfectly proportioned in Suzhou. Don't let the small size deceive you, this garden has enough to occupy you for half a day or more. On certain evenings there are demonstrations of many traditional performing arts.

spots.name: Cold Mountain Temple
spots.desc: Established in the Liang dynasty (502-557 AD), most of the buildings date from the Tang Dynasty except for the five-storey pagoda which was built later.

spots.name: Suzhou Museum
spots.desc: Designed by I.M. Pei, whose family came from Suzhou. Pei lived most of his life in the US and was a very successful architect there, known for the glass pyramid outside the Louvre in Paris, the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in Cleveland, and other landmarks. He came out of retirement in his 80s to return to Suzhou to create a museum that married his modernist sensibility with his sense of the…

spots.name: Baoguo Temple
spots.desc: Baoguo Temple is seated on the mountainside of Lingshan Mountain, about 15 km (9 mi) away from downtown. As a cultural relic spot under state-level protection, it was established in the Eastern Han Dynasty (25-220) and rebuilt and expanded in later dynasties. Now a museum, the present Baoguo Temple is a mixture of constructions made by various dynasties. It's wooden main hall is over 1000 years…

spots.name: Zhongyuan Tower
spots.desc: This 388-metre high tower is the 10th tallest tower in the world and has great views of the city. On the third and fourth floors of the observation deck, you can see the largest panoramic painting in the world.

spots.name: Great Mosque of Hohhot
spots.desc: The oldest and largest mosque in the city built in 1693 in Chinese style. Architecturally, a beautiful and unique mosque well worth visiting. The well maintained mosque has an active community. Be sure to catch prayer at sunset which looks like it takes place on a movie set. Adjacent to the mosque is a street with Muslim vendors and restaurants.

spots.name: Huining Fu
spots.desc: A few kilometres south of Acheng centre, you'll find the ruins of, the capital of the 12th century Jin dynasty. It's been declared a national historic reserve, and apart from the ruined city walls there's a museum on the site as well.

spots.name: Hushan Great Wall
spots.desc: This Ming Dynasty section of the Great Wall of China, which travels parallel to river, was restored to decent condition. The section is steep so watch your footing. Buy a ticket at the long distance bus station for ¥6.5 and the trip takes about 40 minutes. The bus driver will drop you off at a T-intersection right by the Wall. Ride hailing from Dandong to the entrance of the wall costs…

spots.name: New Yalu River Bridge

spots.name: Shaanxi History Museum
spots.desc: This museum houses a collection of local artefacts that span the province's history from the Neolithic period through the Qing dynasty. In particular, it contains fabulously well preserved pottery from the nearby Banpo neolithic village (also worth a visit) and many excellent Shang Dynasty bronzes. Although some guidebooks call it "one of the best museums in China", its old fashioned…

spots.name: Zhongnan Mountains
spots.desc: The Zhongnan Mountains are a branch of the Qin Mountains located south of Xi'an. the range's highest point is Cuihua Mountain. Other notable peaks and places in the Zhongnan Mountains include Lou Guan Tai, where Taoist sage Laozi is said to have dwelt and conveyed the Dao De Jing. Later this was also a place of dwelling for Nan Wutai and Guifeng.

spots.name: Zhaoling Mausoleum
spots.desc: Tomb of Emperor Taizong of the Tang Dynasty (唐太宗), widely regarded to be one of the most capable emperors to ever rule over China. spots.desc: See the Han era tomb of Xin Zui, the Marquess of Dai, and her 2,100-year-old preserved body. Her body was still moist and flexible when they found her, with completely elastic skin, and looks more real than Ho Chi Minh. Also at the museum are many exhibits on all kinds of Han Dynasty artifacts, including pottery, lacquerware and an impressive collection of silk.

spots.name: Wanping Fortress
spots.desc: A Ming-era defensive fortress next to the Lugou Bridge. Shell-holes made in the 1937 Japanese attack are still visible. Take subway line 14 to Dawayao. Then walk 500m south on the Jing-Shi Expressway side road (stay on the west side of the expressway). After 500m, a street turns off to the west, and it's a 200m walk to the fortress.

spots.name: Jietai Temple
spots.desc: Though not as popular and well-visited as Tanzhe Temple, this smaller Buddhist temple is definitely worth a visit. It was built about 1400 years ago, but its most famous features have been added later during Ming and Qing dynasties. A special attraction of this site are the huge pine trees, some of them being hundreds of years old.

spots.name: Cuandixia
spots.desc: A beautiful ancient mountain village. It is very small, only around 70 traditional court yards. It is renovated nicely and seems rather authentic. Go in the weekdays if you want peace and quiet. In the summer months the climate is nicer than in Beijing because of the cooler mountain air. In the winter it could be cold, but the beds are heated, so it is still possible to go. Do at least an…
spots.price: It costs ¥30 for tourists to enter the Cuandixia area

spots.name: Sun Yat-Sen Memorial Hall
spots.desc: Dedicated to the founder of the Republic of China and local hero Dr. Sun Yat-Sen. It was constructed in 1931 and built on the original site of Sun Yat-sen's presidential office on Yuexiu Hill.
spots.price: Admission is free for the park and ¥10 to go inside the hall
spots.addr: Dongfeng Middle Road

spots.name: Gong Cha (贡茶 巴中店)
spots.desc: Offers classic pearl milk tea, brown sugar boba milk, and roasted oolong tea. The flavor is rich and sweet, with a strong tea aroma under the creamy milk base. A good choice for first-time milk tea drinkers.
spots.addr: Near Central Pedestrian Street, Bazhou District (巴州区中央步行街附近)

spots.name: Thames Town
spots.desc: A very convincing English-style village, complete with pubs, cobbled lanes and a church. Only residents are missing, and empty stores and streets make the place looks like a film set even though it is very popular with newly-weds taking photos of themselves in front of the massive church. Definitely worth a visit for its eerie, unlikely atmosphere.

spots.name: Sihang Warehouse Battle Memorial
spots.desc: The Sihang Warehouse is a historic warehouse on the north bank of Suzhou Creek. It was built in 1931 by four banks, hence the literal name of the warehouse is the 'Four Banks Warehouse'. In 1937, the warehouse became a flashpoint in the latter stages of the Battle of Shanghai; see Pacific_War#China for context. At that time, it was being used as the headquarters of the 88th Division of the…

spots.desc: Completed in 2019, this suite of eight buildings also known as Laifushi is one of Chongqing's newest landmarks. Its most notable feature is the 300-meter long, 250-meter high skybridge named the Crystal, which connects four of the buildings together and which is recognized as the second highest skybridge in the world.

spots.addr: Quanshan Road, Fengze District (丰泽区泉山路)

spots.name: Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall

spots.desc: A memorial for the hundreds of thousands of Chinese who died at the hands of Japanese troops in Nanjing during World War II. Two partially excavated mass-burial sites reveal victims remains in situ, accompanied by insightful information boards around the walkway. The elongated sites sympathetically restrained architecture and beautifully maintained gardens are interspersed with sculptures, murals…
spots.addr: 418 Shuiximen Street, Jianye District (建邺区水西门大街418号)

spots.name: Qixia Temple
spots.desc: A one-time retreat for Emperor QianLong, the temple at the foot of maple forested hillside now draws hoards of less exulted visitors to clamber along the network of trails connecting fancifully named pavilions, ponds, tombs and natural stone features. spots.addr: 南京市栖霞街88号

Around a third of the army officers who fought for China during the Second Sino-Japanese War received training here, including Chiang Kai-Shek. As of May 2024, the museum is closed for…

Learn about ancient civilizations in the area (most of which were not based in Zhengzhou, but nearby cities such as Kaifeng and Luoyang), and even see a dinosaur bone or two in the area. The museum is one of the three key museums in China along with one…

The construction of the canal was considered an incredible feat at the time and the story of its…

spots.desc: The palace was built by the first Ming Emperor in 1366 and stretched 2.5 km in length. It was completely destroyed in the Qing Dynasty and what remains barely hints at its size. In the tree shaded southern half are the small section of wall holding the huge arches of the Meridian Gate, five stone 'Outer Dragon' bridges and an array of megaliths, some baring fragments of carvings. This active monastery 20 km (12 mi) from Ningbo houses a bone fragment of Sakyamuni, Buddhism's founder, as well as artifacts, paintings and calligraphy - some personally written by Chinese emperors. The tomb sits on the west facing east, and the plane is shaped like a "甲" shape. The deepest part is about 15 meters…
