spots.desc: An eight-storey building on the Bund featuring a highly visible clocktower nicknamed "Big Ching". Built in 1927, it is seen as one of the symbols of the Bund.

spots.name: HSBC Building
spots.desc: The grandest building on the Bund is now home to the Pudong Development Bank.

spots.name: Universal Beijing
spots.desc: The first Universal Studios theme park in China opened its doors in July 2021, and the full operation started on 20 September 2021. There are seven zones: Hollywood Boulevard, Jurassic World Isla Nublar, Transformers: Metrobase, The Wizarding World of Harry Potter, Kung Fu Panda Land of Awesomeness, Minion Land, and WaterWorld with tickets valid for all rides in all zones.

spots.name: Museum of the Western Han Dynasty Mausoleum of the Nanyue King
spots.local: 南越王博物院王墓展区
spots.desc: This is a tomb for the king of ancient South China during the Western Han era.
spots.addr: 867 Jiefang Road N. (解放北路878号)

spots.name: Tholing Monastery
spots.desc: The oldest monastery in Ngari Prefecture has dozens of preserved ancient wall paintings and frescoes. Tsada Clay Forest has been declared a national park, where you can see the largest tertiary strat earth forest in the world.

spots.name: Nanxiang Old Town
spots.desc: A very picturesque and peaceful area, with no Western tourists and delicious food available. Some streets are old or renewed but still keep the old style, while other parts are modern residential blocks with an old look at the ground floor. On side streets you can discover tables with gambling locals sitting around. The canals, bridges, pavilions and tourist-oriented shops are not missing.
spots.addr: 218 Huyi Highway

spots.name: Sheshan
spots.desc: Two hills with large (and crowded) paths and stairs. At the top of the biggest hill sit a large catholic basilica built in 1935 and an observatory.
spots.addr: No. 9258, Waiqingsong Highway

spots.name: Longtan Park
spots.desc: Park with lake, boats for hire, teahouses and a restaurant, children's playground, pavilions, a bird market and a lot of dragons. There is also a climbing wall and a roller skating area in the park.
spots.addr: Longtan Road 龙潭路

spots.name: Shimao Ruins
spots.desc: The ruins of a neolithic city, which flourished between 2300 BC and 1800 BC. A new archaeological museum opened at the site in November 2023.
spots.addr: Shimao Village, Gaojiabao Town (高家堡镇石峁村)

spots.name: Baiyun Mountain (White Cloud Mountain)
spots.desc: Is a great place to relax and enjoy a day among lush, rolling hills. It also offers great views over the city. The road to the top in most of the daytime is restricted to park trams and pedestrians. To get to the top lookout point, you can use the main roads or trails. There are many places to rest and refreshments are available along the way. It is a great place to see people enjoying nature and…
spots.price: Park entrance ¥5; Cable car round trip ¥40; tram from ¥20; other attractions ¥5–10; packages available from ¥25

spots.name: Guiyuan Temple
spots.desc: Built in 1658, Guiyuan Temple is known as the first zen temple to be built in Hubei Province. The most famous and impressive building in the complex is the Arhats Hall, which contains 500 arhat (Buddhist saints) statues. When you enter, from whichever part you choose to begin exploring, you are supposed to count the arhats. When you have counted to your current age, you are then supposed to write…
spots.hours: May 1st to Oct 7th 07:30-17:30, Oct 8th to Apr 30th 08:00-17:00, no entry in last 30 minutes
spots.addr: 20 Cuiwei Road, Hanyang District (汉阳区翠微路20号)

spots.name: Three Gorges Museum
spots.desc: Across the People's Square is Three Gorges Museum, well worth a visit for its exhibits on the Ba culture and the area of the three gorges downriver from Chongqing. Also noteworthy are a series of exhibits on life in Chongqing during the Qing dynasty, the early republic, and the World War II era.
spots.addr: 236 Renmin Road (人民路236号)

spots.name: Rasuwa Fort
spots.desc: A ruined 19th-century historical stone fort constructed by the Rana dynasty along the river border. It sits immediately adjacent to the modern customs post.

spots.name: Najiaying Mosque
spots.desc: A large mosque in Nagu Town, northwest of Tonghai Lake

spots.name: Yulin Caves
spots.desc: A Buddhist cave temple site featuring 250 polychrome statues and 4,200 square meters of wall paintings, which date from the 7th to the 14th centuries.

spots.name: Wutong Mountain National Park
spots.desc: At just over 900 meters, Wutong Mountain is the second tallest mountain in the Pearl River Delta after Hong Kong's Tai Mo Shan. The Wutong Mountains are a popular challenge for hikers. This has been a recognised beauty spot since at least the Ming Dynasty, when it was included in the Eight Great Views of Xin'an County and was celebrated in poetry. There are several routes to the top varying…

spots.name: Kongtongshan National Park
spots.desc: Kongtongshan National Park is in Gansu Province of China.

spots.name: The Gate of China (Zhonghuamen)
spots.desc: The southern gate of Nanjing's city wall; this massive gate is one of the best preserved parts of Nanjing's city wall, and one of the best remaining examples of early Ming defensive architecture extant anywhere. The wooden castle at top was destroyed by fire, but the immense masonry (each complete with the mason's name and home province by order of the emperor) substructure remains. Two…
spots.addr: 8 Jiefeng Gate, Zhonghuanan Lu

spots.name: Confucius Temple
spots.desc: Once an imperial examination testing center for the entire Jiangsu region, this museum comprises a tiny fraction of the once-massive original buildings. The rest of the site is a massive, labyrinthine market; a top tourist draw in Nanjing and a place where you can get all your haggling out of your system. Get your picture taken with the Confucius sculpture and grab some tea on one of the gondolas…

spots.name: The Retreat and Reflection Garden
spots.desc: In the township of TongLi (同里) in Wujiang district, about 30 km south of central Suzhou.

spots.name: The Garden of Cultivation
spots.desc: Make sure to go all the way towards the back inside the garden to see the best part.

spots.name: Temple of Mystery
spots.desc: A large Taoist hall perpetually obscured by a curtain of joss smoke of devotes eager to placate the gods inside. It has a large market area, many small shops with a range of goods aimed mainly at either devotees or tourists. The temple was established in the 3rd century and broadened to its present size in the Song Dynasty, where it became a popular spot for travelling magicians and acrobats. The…
spots.addr: east end of the pedestrian shopping area on Guanqian Jie

spots.name: Pudong Mosque
spots.desc: The initial mosque building was constructed in 1935. It was expanded in 1984 and rebuilt in 1995 to its current size.
spots.addr: No. 375, Yuanshen Road

spots.name: Oriental Art Center
spots.desc: This is mainly a center for the performing arts with three theaters of various sizes. There is also an exhibition area.

spots.name: Zhejiang Provincial Museum
spots.desc: The largest comprehensive museum in Zhejiang province. Contains many rarely-seen treasures from Zhejiang, especially the celadon porcelains. It shows the elite culture of traditional China in Jiangnan region. In the museum, there is a self-service rental Museum collection guide.
spots.addr: 25 GuShan Road

spots.name: Jingci Temple
spots.desc: Just off Nanshan Road, built in 954, the Jingci Temple has a huge 10-ton bell inside. Located on Nanping Road, they ring the bell 108 times here to ring in Chinese New Year. It is also rung every evening for much fewer times. Jingci Temple is the site of the legend of the miraculous well, which can be seen on the grounds of the temple.

spots.name: Zhejiang Museum of Natural History
spots.desc: Due to limitations on visitor numbers, visitors are encouraged to make a booking on WeChat before visiting the museum. However, this might not be practical to do if you can't read Chinese, as the booking system is in Chinese only. The museum has another branch in Anji.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: No. 6 West Lake Cultural Square, Chaohui Subdistrict, Xiacheng District (下城区朝晖街道西湖文化广场6号)

spots.name: Dongqian Lake
spots.desc: The largest natural lake in Zhejiang, and a popular spot for locals to visit. It's possible to rent tandem or triple bicycles, or boats, to see the lake. Several scenic spots charge admission, including a causeway through the middle of the lake (¥30) to Xiayu Temple (霞屿禅寺) and "small Putuoshan". A variety of very old buildings overlooking the lake have been turned into tea shops. is near the…

spots.name: Er Qi (February 7) Memorial Tower
spots.desc: Museum inside a rather garish double pagoda that looms over February 7 Square. Inside there are exhibits explaining the city's development.
spots.addr: Er Qi Square, 230 Er Qi Road, Er Qi District (二七区二七路230号二七广场)

spots.name: Thousand Buddha Mountain
spots.desc: It is one of the three major scenic spots in Jinan and used to be known as Lishan. During the reign of Emperor Kaihuang of the Sui Dynasty (581-600 AD), due to the prevalence of Buddhism, thousands of Buddha statues were carved along the mountain terrain, hence the name Qianfo Mountain.
spots.addr: Lixia District

spots.name: Jinci Temple
spots.desc: AAAAA Tourist Attractions of China. Jinci Temple, an ancient ancestral temple, was founded about 1400 years ago and was expanded during the Sui, Tang, Song, Yuan, Ming, and Qing Dynasties, resulting in a variety of architecutural styles. Today it comprises of over 100 halls, towers, pavilions, terraces, and bridges and includes some of the best Song Dynasty sculptures and buildings still extant…

spots.name: Benxi Water Caves
spots.desc: A large limestone cave system divided into dry and water-filled sections. The main experience is a boat ride along the underground river, passing stalactites, stalagmites, stone columns and large cave chambers. About 2.8 km of the cave system has been developed, including a water route extending more than 2 km into the cave. The temperature inside remains around 12°C throughout the year, so a…
spots.price: Around ¥150 for an adult ticket; prices may vary by season and ticket type
spots.addr: Xiejiawaizi Village, Xiaoshi Town, Benxi Manchu Autonomous County

spots.name: White Horse Pagoda
spots.desc: The construction of this 12-meter stupa was ordered by Kunarajiva, a Buddhist translator, in 384. It was rebuilt in the 1840s.
spots.addr: Xiangyun Road (祥云路)

spots.name: Dafo Temple
spots.desc: Holds the largest wooden indoor reclining Buddha in China at long, high. This temple is the reputed birthplace for the Mongol emperor, Kublai Khan.

spots.name: Dinghu Mountain
spots.desc: Dinghu Mountain is a forested mountain and nature reserve in Dinghu District. It is part of the Xinghu Scenic and Historic Interest Area together with Seven Star Crags. The area includes Baoding Garden, Butterfly Valley, Feishui Waterfall and Qingyun Temple, and was established as China's first national nature reserve in 1956.
spots.addr: Shangshan Road, Kengkou Town, Dinghu District

spots.name: Tianya Haijiao
spots.desc: One of the most famous beaches in China, and a traditionally popular spot for romantic couples. The beach is often too overrun by tourists for visitors to be able to appreciate its natural beauty, but has been famously alluded to by various ancient Chinese writers and in modern Chinese pop culture.

spots.name: Anshun Bridge
spots.desc: A scenic, historic bridge crossing the Jin River in the middle of Chengdu. A bridge at this location was mentioned in the writings of Marco Polo. However, in the 1980s the bridge was destroyed by flooding, and was rebuilt in 2003. There is a restaurant on top of the bridge.
spots.addr: 66 Binjiang Road East, Jinjiang District (锦江区滨江东路66号)

spots.name: Golden Summit
spots.desc: With a towering, multi-face statue of Samantabhadra and vertigo-inducing views of the cloud sea around the mountain, the peak makes a perfect reward for the thigh-shattering climb from Baoguo.

spots.name: Black Dragon Pool
spots.desc: Quite large place with some nice natural scenery together with traditional building styles. Don't forget to take pictures on the center bridge where the Yu Long Xue Shan (The Jade Dragon Snow Mountain) can be a perfect background. Popular with locals, whom you can find dancing or playing games such as mahjongg or Chinese chess. You can also hike up Elephant Hill if you're feeling energetic. Walk…
spots.addr: 1 Minzhu Road, Gucheng District (古城区民主路1号)

spots.name: Nanning Mosque
spots.addr: Zhonghua Street, Youjiang District

spots.name: Yaohan
spots.desc: This is one of the most popular large-scale shopping centers in downtown Jiaxing. It integrates shopping, entertainment and catering. It is an ideal shopping and leisure place in downtown Jiaxing. The downside is that parking is not easy here, and the traffic is often congested.
spots.addr: 1360 Zhongshan Road, Nanhu District,

spots.name: Happy Valley Amusement Park
spots.desc: Amusement park established in 2006 and by far the largest in Beijing covering around 1 km² and comprising more than 40 rides divided in different themed areas.
spots.addr: Xiaowuji North Road, Southend of East Ring Road Four (东四环南路小武基北路; Dōngsìhuánnánlù Xiǎowǔjīběilù)

spots.name: Changchun Temple
spots.desc: Built by the Wanli Emperor's mother in 1592 during the Ming dynasty, it's also the Xuannan Cultural Museum.

spots.name: Xizhimen
spots.desc: One of the most popular markets for locals is located in Xizhimen, next to the zoo. To get there, in front of the zoo there is a new huge building, which is just another big market, but behind it, there is the wholesale market, with the best prices, and a lot of genuine goods (clothing). This market is much more local than others listed here, and is perhaps not ideal for the less adventurous…

spots.name: Púsà Peak
spots.desc: The two main temples in Táihuái town are Xiǎntōng Temple and Tǎyuàn Temple, both to the west side of the Qīngshuǐ 清水 river. A good way to see these is to start at the top of the hillock that they are on (Púsà Dǐng), and walk down the hill through all 3 monasteries. This way you walk down, not up the flights of 108 steps. The number 108 has considerable symbolical value for Buddhism.
spots.addr: Just to the north of Xiǎntōng Temple and Tǎyuàn Temple

spots.name: Tǎyuàn Temple
spots.desc: The white stupa in the centre of Tǎyuàn Temple has become a symbol of Wǔtái Shān.

spots.name: Fengguo Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple dating from the Liao Dynasty. The temple's main hall is one of the oldest and best-preserved ancient wooden structures in China.
spots.hours: 08:30-16:00 (November to March), 08:00-16:30 (April to October), no tickets sold in last 30 minutes
spots.addr: 18 East Street, Yi County (义县东街18号)

spots.name: Famen Temple
spots.desc: This Buddhist temple, which records mention as far back as 67 AD, contains a 13-story brick pagoda as part of the monastery. This pagoda fell down in the rain in August 1981 and revealed a 1000 year old underground vault full with 2,400 treasures belonging to the Tang and previous dynasties given as offerings. These included gold and silver utensils, glazed wares, porcelains, pearls, precious…
spots.addr: Fufeng County (扶风县)

spots.name: Wugongshan National Geopark
spots.desc: Long ridge with grass on top, which is much more spectacular than it sounds. Good for hiking and camping, also some ancient Taoist altars.

spots.name: Liulichang
spots.desc: There is no production here any more, but rather antique stores, selling Chinese painting, handicrafts, and used books. The area was popular back to the Tang dynasty, but the small shops were amalgamated into state-operated units during the 1950s. It was redeveloped as a tourist area after 1979, but has failed to regain its former popularity. Nevertheless, it is picturesque and you can still find…

spots.name: Temple of Agriculture
spots.desc: See the Museum of Ancient Architecture.

spots.name: Taimu Mountain
spots.desc: Known as the "wonderland on the sea", it sports many high and steep mountains, spectacular rock formations, secluded caves, a foggy climate, and additional rivers and parks. Taimushan Railway Station (太姥山站) serves passengers visiting Taimu Mountain.

spots.name: Qiandeng Ancient Town
spots.desc: A picturesque ancient water town 15km south of Kunshan near the border with Shanghai. Qiandeng is listed as a national historical and cultural town and as a scenic spot.
spots.addr: 1 Shangshu Rd (尚书路1号)

spots.name: Fahai Temple
spots.desc: This 15th-century temple has some of the best-preserved and extensive Ming frescoes to be found.

spots.name: 王屋山 (Wangwu Mountain)
spots.desc: One of China's most famous Taoist mountains, it's also the birthplace of the legend of "Foolish Old Man Moving the Mountains." With its majestic presence and numerous Taoist temples, it's a representative attraction in Jiyuan.
spots.addr: Northwest of Jiyuan City

spots.name: 小浪底水库
spots.desc: Visitors can tour and take photos at the Yellow River's large-scale water conservancy projects, and learn about the facilities for water diversion, power generation, and flood control.
spots.addr: Xiaolangdi Town

spots.name: Ersha Island
spots.desc: Ersha Island is an attractive upscale area with lots of green open space. Towards its east end are the Museum of Art and the Concert Hall, see listings.

spots.name: Dafo Temple (大佛寺)
spots.desc: An impressive and large Chan temple with a history of over one thousand years (though it has been destroyed and rebuilt a number of times). It is one of the five largest temples in Guangzhou.
spots.addr: Beijing Road

spots.name: Longxing Temple
spots.desc: Built in the Tang dynasty, features a huge 22 m high bronze Buddha statue donated by the Song emperor in the 11th century.

spots.name: Tumen River Bridge
spots.desc: Look over the Tumen river into North Korea. Access restricted for non-Chinese citizens.

spots.name: Splendid China & Chinese Folk Culture Village
spots.desc: It combines two different sections. The first part is a miniature park of China. You can find the famous Forbidden City, Terracotta Soldiers, Tibet Potala Palace, Huangshan Mountains, Yunnan's Stone Forest, and of course the Great Wall of China. This miniature park covers 300,000 m², fully forested with beautiful greenery and flowers. The second part consists of dozens of houses, temples, yurts…
spots.hours: 10:00–21:00; Splendid China closes at 18:00, but there still is night bus tours of Splendid China

spots.name: Shenzhen Bay Park
spots.desc: Actually a long series of connected parks on reclaimed land along the coast of Shenzhen Bay, stretching from the Shenzhen Bay Bridge all the way to the mangrove forest park in Futian. Attractively landscaped and well maintained with lovely walking paths along the water, a nice place for a stroll or a bike ride. The most popular section seems to be Talent Park (人才公园 Réncái Gōngyuán), which has…

spots.name: Friendship Pass
spots.desc: A pass signifying the border between China and Vietnam. Note that the pass lies just within the Chinese side of the border.

spots.name: Hongyadong
spots.desc: Near Jiefangbei, a recreation of the old Chongqing, clinging to the side of the mountain with many small shops. A tourist place but you can find recreations of old local crafts here and genuine local food.
spots.addr: 88 Jialingjiang Binjiang Road (嘉陵江滨江路88号)

spots.name: Shanghai Happy Valley
spots.desc: Theme park.
spots.addr: 888 Linhu Rd (上海松江区林湖路888号)

spots.name: East China University of Science and Technology
spots.desc: A university.

spots.name: Nanhui New City
spots.desc: This development was planned by German architects and is built around a circular man-made lake; it includes a planetarium, shopping, and massive office and residential development. Target population was 450,000 but it has not grown as quickly as planners hoped. There are eight university campuses on the west side with about 100,000 students.

spots.name: Wenmiao Temple
spots.desc: The Temple to Confucius, with Shanghai's most famous vintage book market.
spots.addr: Wenmiao Lu 215

spots.name: Guangji Bridge
spots.desc: It was built in the Southern Song Dynasty (1170 AD), a bridge partly made of small boats. It was rebuilt a few years ago and now costs ¥60 to cross (one way). You may have seen a model of it in the old Guangdong Provincial Museum.
spots.hours: Generally open daily from 09:00-17:30; weekday schedules may differ, e.g. 10:00-17:30

spots.name: Nanputuo Temple
spots.desc: This is a large Buddhist temple complex, with parts being over a thousand years old, mainly dedicated to the bodhisatva Guan Yin who is sometimes described as the Goddess of Mercy. Mount Putuo in Zhejiang is one of China's "Four Great Mountains of Buddhism"; "Nanputuo" means "south Putuo". Visitors can climb the mountain behind the temple for beautiful views of Xiamen and surrounding nature. The…
spots.addr: 515 Siming South Rd, Siming District (思明区思明南路515号)

spots.name: Tianjin Eye
spots.desc: The world's second largest Ferris wheel and the only Ferris wheel built on a bridge in the world. The Tianjin Eye has a diameter of 110 m and 48 transparent gondolas with 360º views. Ideal for seeing the surrounding scenery at a glance. One round requires 28 minutes. On the highest point, it is possible to see the scenery within a radius of 40 km.
spots.price: Adults ¥70, children under 1.2 meters ¥35, couple VIP ¥899 (2 persons within a separate gondola, can avoid queuing)…
spots.addr: Yongle Bridge, Sanchahekou, Hebei District (河北区三岔河口永乐桥上)

spots.name: Qomolangma
spots.local: 珠穆朗瑪峰國家自然保護區
spots.desc: Qomolangma National Nature Reserve (Chinese: 珠穆朗玛峰国家级自然保护区) is in Tibet, covering the Tibetan or Chinese side of Mount Everest.

spots.name: Kunming–Hai Phong Railway
spots.desc: Constructed by French capital and Chinese labor at the beginning of the 20th century, the Yunnan section of the meter-gauge railway connecting Yunnan and Vietnam is a feat of engineering. Although there is no passenger service on most of this line anymore (trains run on the standard-gauge line instead), the railway is preserved and continues to have some limited use for freight. A commuter…

spots.name: Tongjiao Temple
spots.desc: It was used by eunuchs but now is used by nuns.
spots.addr: 19 Zhenxian Hutong, Dongzhimen Beixiaojie (东直门北小街针线胡同19号; Dōngzhíménběixiǎojiē Zhēnxiànhútòng)

spots.name: Shenzhen Mosque
spots.desc: The largest mosque in Shenzhen.
spots.addr: No. 7, Meilin Road, Futian District

spots.name: Chongqing East railway station
spots.desc: If you’re into grand architecture and sheer scale, Chongqing East Railway Station is worth a stop - even if you’re not catching a train. Opened in 2025, it’s billed as the largest railway station in the world, a futuristic mega-terminal of glass and steel designed to handle the endless flow of high-speed trains crisscrossing China. Step inside and you’ll find cavernous halls, sweeping rooflines…

spots.name: Luoyang Bridge
spots.desc: A bridge that is considered one of the four ancient bridges of China. Its namesake goes back several centuries, although the railings look remarkably well preserved. But look at the pillars and that may be more indicative of its age.

spots.name: Jinjue Mosque
spots.desc: The mosque traced its origin during the Hongwu Emperor of Ming Dynasty in 1388.
spots.addr: No. 28, Shengzhou Road, Qinhuai

spots.name: The Surging Wave Pavilion
spots.desc: One of the oldest of Suzhou's wonderful collection of private or "scholar's" gardens. More densely forested than other gardens, so ideal for hot days when you want to escape the sun. This garden is best viewed from within its many pavilions, with windows framing different views.

spots.name: Panmen city gate
spots.desc: This gate is renowned for its unique structure as a combined water and land gate. It was built as a gate in a city wall built in 514 BCE, but the present structure is from a 14th century rebuild. The remaining wall is 300 m long and 5 m high. Visiting Pan Men includes access to a large and rather lovely garden with ponds and pavilions (feed the koi for ¥2), a boat ride, the city water and land…
spots.addr: DongDa Jie

spots.name: Century Park
spots.desc: This is Shanghai's biggest park. Unfortunately, there is a lot of concrete and paved roads, and many areas have vegetation that is still under development or poorly cared for. Still a good and relaxing get-away. Bike rental available (expensive, from ¥40 per hour).

spots.name: Huqingyutang Traditional Chinese Medicine Museum
spots.desc: The only themed museum with traditional Chinese medicine in China. Huqingyutang is also a traditionally famous medicine store keeping the traditional medicine culture of ancient China. It was created by Hu Xueyan, a representative of Huizhou merchants.

spots.name: Qiantong ancient town
spots.desc: Qiantong, Ninghai is an ancient town south of the Yangtze River. Among the 2000 household in Qiantong 80% of them have “Tong” as the surname. Since it is located in front of the Baixi river, it is named Qiantong (“Qian” meaning “before” or "in front of"). The town has been around more than 760 years, successive generations of Tongs choosing to remain here. If you've been to other "ancient towns"…

spots.name: Xiangtangshan Grottoes
spots.desc: The Xiangtangshan Grottoes are a group of Buddhist cave temples carved into the mountainside. They are the largest grotto complex discovered in Hebei and one of the major religious grotto sites in China. Excavation began during the Northern Qi dynasty (550–577) and continued through the Sui, Tang, Song, Yuan, and Ming dynasties.The site consists of 16 main caves and around 4,000 statues…
spots.addr: No. 12 Taihang West Road, Fuyang East Road Subdistrict, Fengfeng Mining District

spots.name: Da Zhao Temple
spots.desc: The oldest Buddhist monastery in the city constructed in 1579. A 2.5-meter silver statue of Sakyamuni Buddha is among the temples most precious treasures.

spots.name: Inner Mongolia Museum
spots.desc: Exhibitions of the flora and fauna and history of (Inner) Mongolia from the stone age until modern times, as well as on minerals and mining, space exploration, and dinosaurs. Although not all captions are in English there is still a lot of information available and it's not difficult to understand the exhibitions.

spots.name: Yalu River Broken Bridge
spots.desc: This bridge reaches only halfway across the river, the other half having been badly damaged by American bombing during the Korean War, and got disassembled by the Koreans. The last section of the broken bridge is no longer accessible to the public, but most of the bridge is still walkable. Bring your own binoculars to get an even closer view of North Korea.

spots.name: Xiguan Mosque
spots.desc: One block south of the Taoist Temple. A modern newly built mosque with simple modern design.
spots.addr: Metro Line 1 Xiguan Stn. Located on Cuiyingmen

spots.name: Helan Mountain Rock Art
spots.desc: These carvings were done by Chinese nomads some 10,000 years ago. They run the gamut from portraits and totems to scenes of hunting, grazing, war and dance. Many of the trails accessing the rock art were destroyed in a flood in 2016 and have not been rebuilt as of 2018, leaving some of the most famous parts inaccessible, but there is still a lot to see. A museum displays photos of similar ancient…
spots.price: ¥60 plus ¥10 for the electric golf cart (mandatory)
spots.addr: Helankou Rock Art Site Park on the Eastern Slope of Helan Mountain, Helan County

spots.name: Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region Museum
spots.local: 新疆维吾尔自治区博物馆
spots.desc: Highlights include a few mummies on display and other artifacts. If you start your trip around Xinjiang, the museum gives you a very good introduction about the history and minorities.
spots.hours: April 15th to October 15: 10:00-18:00; October 16th to April 14th: 10:30-18:00; no entry after 16:30; closed on Mondays
spots.addr: 581 Xibei Road, Shayibake District (沙依巴克区西北路581号)

spots.name: Tangerine Island
spots.desc: This beautifully landscaped park contains a large number of rose bushes, orange trees, a bamboo garden, and a gigantic sculpture of the head of Mao in his youth. Tickets for sightseeing busses that stop at five spots can be purchased for ¥20, and small cruise ships circle the island. Walking from the metro station to the Mao head is 3.3 km and takes about 35 min.

spots.name: Wuhouci Temple
spots.desc: The temple is adjacent to Jinli Ancient Street, so visitors can combine both in one trip. Allow about 1.5 hours.This temple is built to commemorate Zhuge Liang (诸葛亮), who was the minister of Shu (蜀) in the Three Kingdoms Period. He is famous through the Chinese novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms. There are dozens of dust covered statues of obscure historical figures behind glass and not much…
spots.hours: May to October: 08:00-20:00, November to April: 08:00-19:00, no tickets sold in last 60 minutes
spots.addr: 231 Wuhouci Main Street, Wuihou District (武侯区武侯祠大街231号)

spots.name: Mountain Villa with Embracing Beauty
spots.desc: Mainly a rock and water garden.

spots.name: Temple of Heavenly Bliss
spots.desc: Large and active Buddhist temple.

spots.desc: The oldest and most venerable of the roast duck restaurants. Quanjude is slipping these days, but its fame still brings many customers, mostly tourists eager for the classic experience. Quality varies by location. The most reputable of Quanjude's 14 branches is the listed Qianmen location, which has been rebuilt as part of the changes taking place in Qianmen Dajie. Other branches are at Hepingmen…
spots.price: Ducks cost ¥199 each and ¥99 for half a duck

spots.name: Lüshun Russo-Japanese Prison Museum

spots.desc: Locating on the Huangpu River, this place used to be a power plant and a pavilion for Expo 2010, now the first state-run contemporary art museum in China. It also holds the Shanghai Biennale of contemporary art. You can see the industrial relic of the power plant and the contemporary artworks as well.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 11:00-19:00 (last entry at 18:00), open on all national holidays
spots.price: Free except for special exhibitions. In 2016, combination ticket for the two special exhibitions was ¥60, ¥20 with a…

spots.desc: At the northern tip of the Bund, was the legendary home of the "No dogs or Chinese" sign — which in fact never existed, although Chinese not accompanied by foreigners were indeed banned until 1928. The Bund Historical Museum located here is also worth a quick visit.

spots.name: People's Park
spots.desc: Entry into People's Park on the north half of the square is free, but all attractions listed below are on the edges of the park, not inside.
spots.addr: No. 185, Renmin Avenue

spots.name: Zhenru Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple built in 1320. In the middle stands a nine-storey pagoda, the ground floor of which is open for visitors. Special elements are prayer wheels, a colonnade along the river with a bell collection, paintings, stele and a fish pond. A major renovation will end in August 2018, but it is open during renovation. The entrance is on Lanxi Road near to Beishi Road.
spots.addr: 399 Lanxi Road

spots.name: Museum of the War of Chinese People's Resistance Against Japanese Aggression
spots.local: 中国人民抗日战争纪念馆
spots.desc: The largest museum in China dedicated to the Second Sino-Japanese War.
spots.addr: 101 Wanping Fortress Inner Street, Lugou Bridge (卢沟桥宛平城内街101号)

spots.name: Cheng'en Temple

spots.name: Heytea (巴中万达广场店)
spots.desc: A popular Chinese-style tea brand known for fresh fruit tea and cheese foam milk tea. Drinks such as grapefruit green tea and cheese oolong are lightly sweet with a rich creamy aftertaste. Clean environment and stable quality.
spots.addr: Wanda Plaza, Bazhou District (巴州区万达广场)

spots.name: Songzanlin Monastery
spots.desc: Impressive structure becoming less of a monastic institution, more of a tourist destination. The temple was restored by an architect named Xu Wei Han in 2005 to reflect its past glories. Minor restoration are still done (August 2017) which could limit access to some parts of the monastery.

spots.name: Shanghai Botanical Garden
spots.desc: Covering 81.86 hectares, the garden has a diverse collection of Chinese plants. Its sections are the penjing (bonsai) garden, penjing museum, tropicarium, magnolia, peony, bamboo and conifer gardens.

spots.name: Gongqing Forest Park
spots.local: 上海共青国家森林公园
spots.desc: A large forest park that provides an escape from the urban confines of the city. Great for picnics and relaxation. Features thrill coasters, miniature train ride, pleasure boats, mini-golf, bumper cars.
spots.price: ¥15, children under 1.2 metres free when accompanied by an adult. Activities inside the park cost extra. Separate…
spots.addr: Northeast corner of Nenjiang Road (嫩江路) and Jungong Road (军工路). Ticketing booth along Nenjiang Road just east of Jungong Road, or along Jungong Road north of…

spots.name: Puji Monastery
spots.desc: This is the most accessible and famous monastery on Putuoshan. Nearby there are hotels, restaurants and interesting shops. A public ritual performed by the monks runs from 4:30AM to 7AM. It is crowded at this time, so unless you are interested in the ceremony, it's best to visit the temple outside these hours.

spots.name: Huangya Pass
spots.desc: Huangya, means "yellow cliff". The pass on the Great Wall of China takes this name from the yellowish hills and rocks nearby. It was built in 557 AD, was repaired for the first time in the Ming Dynasty with bricks, and for the second time in 1985. In 1986 it was listed as a key heritage protection site of Tianjin City. Now it is also a patriotic education and national defense education base of…
spots.addr: Huangyaguan Village, Xiaying Town (下营镇黄崖关村)

spots.name: Panshan Scenic Area
spots.desc: Panshan or Mount Pan is a famous mountain noted for its scenery and its many Buddhist temples.

spots.addr: Lianhualing Village, Guanzhuang Town (官庄镇莲花岭村)

spots.name: Guishan Televsion Tower
spots.desc: The 221-metre high tower on Tortoise Mountain (Guishan) is a major landmark on Hanyang's waterfront. There is an observatory and a revolving restaurant at the top.
spots.addr: Guishan Park, 1 Guibei Road, Hanyang District (汉阳区龟北路特1号龟山公园)

spots.name: Great Hall of the People
spots.desc: Chongqing's Great Hall of the People (and the People's Square in front of the Hall) is an architectural symbol of Chongqing City. This is where the Chongqing Municipal People's Congress, the legislature of Chongqing Municipality, meets. Its construction began in 1951, but its design is traditional and mirrors those of China's ancient classical dynasties. It somewhat resembles an enlarged version…

spots.name: Live House
spots.desc: If you enjoy a lively atmosphere, want to hear live music, and have a more immersive interactive experience with your friends...
spots.addr: Guilin Street Longxin Central Avenue Business District

spots.name: Lingxiao Pagoda
spots.desc: Tang dynasty pagoda in Zhengding.

spots.name: Dongjiadu Cathedral
spots.local: 董家渡圣方济各沙勿略堂
spots.desc: Built by Spanish Jesuits in the 19th century, the historic seat of the Bishop of Shanghai. A relatively small church near the river, outside the old city wall. In 2018 the church is surrounded by a huge construction site and it's closed.

spots.name: Hangu Pass
spots.desc: Hangu Pass is located on the plateau to the west, Jue Jian to the east, Qinling Mountains to the south, and the Yellow River to the north. It is one of the earliest established fortresses in Chinese history. It is located in Wangduo Village, 15 km north of Lingbao City, and is close to the bank of the Yellow River. Due to being closed in the valley and as dangerous as a letter, it is called Hangu…
spots.addr: Hanguguan Ancient Culture Tourist Area

spots.name: Larung Gar Buddhist Institute
spots.desc: the largest Tibetan Buddhist institute in the world 15 km from Seda town. A permit may be required for non-Chinese nationals to enter the institute.

spots.name: Qianshan National Park
spots.desc: Qianshan National Park (千山国家公园 lit.Thousand Mountains) is in Liaoning Province of China.

spots.name: Yading
spots.desc: Yading (Chinese: 亚丁) is in Sichuan, China. This contains the National Nature Reserve of China (亞丁國家級自然保護區菅理局宣) known under the same name, and at 4000 m. The only gateway is the town that used to be known as Riwa but was renamed (Xiānggélǐlā, 香格里拉镇). The town is a complete rebuild and has no intact old town today, however it is a good option if you are coping with high altitude since it is below…

spots.name: Dafen Oil Painting Village
spots.desc: In 1988, a Hong Kong businessman called Wong Kong, who had a business specialising in reproduction art, decided that there was no future in Hong Kong and set up in Dafen, even though it was not in the SEZ. Soon he was joined by artists from all over China, some classically trained but many just talented amateurs fresh from the paddy fields. And so Dafen was born. It is set in what was once a…
spots.addr: Dafen Village, Buji, Longgang District (龙岗区布吉街道大芬社区)

spots.name: Hualin Temple
spots.desc: Hualin Temple is a Buddhist temple in downtown Fuzhou, which functions as a small museum and no longer provides Buddhist services. Built in 964 AD and survived over 10 centuries, this is the oldest wood architecture extant in South China (south of Yangtze River). The temple has a typical Tang dynasty style with simplicity and elegance. Despite its great historic and architectural importance, the…
spots.addr: 华林路78号 (78 Hualin Road)

spots.name: Litchi Pork
spots.desc: Litchi Pork (Lizhi Rou) is one of the most iconic dishes of Fuzhou cuisine, a branch of Fujian (Min) cooking. Despite its name, the dish contains no lychees; it is named for the rounded, reddish appearance of the pork pieces, which resemble peeled lychees after cooking.

spots.name: Rural Minbei and tea plantations
spots.desc: The area surrounding Nanping is dotted with tea plantations, bamboo forests, and traditional villages, making it ideal for travelers who enjoy a slower pace of life and natural scenery.

spots.name: Wuyi rock tea
spots.desc: Including Da Hong Pao, Shuixian, and Rougui. Best bought from reputable tea shops or markets.

spots.name: Southern Shaolin Monastery
spots.desc: A reconstructed Buddhist temple built on the remains of an old Tang Dynasty temple, claimed to be connected to the Shaolin Monastery in Henan Province which is one of China's most famous centers of martial arts. There is another Southern Shaolin temple in nearby Quanzhou.
spots.addr: Linshan Village, Xitianwei Town, Licheng District (荔城区西天尾镇林山村)

spots.name: Caoqiao Mosque
spots.desc: The mosque traced its origin during Qianlong Emperor of Qing Dynasty.
spots.addr: No. 26-32, Ganyu Lane, Qinhuai

spots.name: Yangshan Quarry
spots.desc: The three sections of a gigantic stele, which the Yongle Emperor commissioned for the mausoleum of his father the Hongwu Emperor can be seen here in situ. The project was never completed, as the Ming engineers realized that there is no way the stone monoliths could be moved out of here to Ming Xiaoling.

spots.name: The Couple's Garden Retreat
spots.desc: Built in early 20th century by a couple. Many small garden rooms lead you from view to view. Each window or hall perfectly frames a set of plants, rocks or trees. Every inch of the garden has been carefully thought out. Most of the garden consists of covered walkways, so even though it may rain you will be able to enjoy this garden without getting wet.

spots.name: Slender West Lake
spots.desc: Very slim lake winding through the park area just northwest of the city center. Several pavilions dot the park around the lake that was designed to mimic the west lake in Hangzhou.

spots.name: Tiantong Temple
spots.desc: Tiantong Temple, 25 km to the east of Ningbo, situated in the national Forest Park of Tiantong. Tiantong Temple was built in 300 CE. The temple has more than 20 ancient buildings. As a holy place of Buddhism, Tiantong Temple is not only an important temple of Linji Sect but also the father of Soto (Caotong in Chinese Sect) in Japan with 8 million disciples in 33,000 temples. It plays an important…

spots.name: Zhaobaoshan
spots.desc: A large forested hill where the Yong River empties into the ocean, it has several rebuilt temples, a 57.6m-tall pagoda you can climb since the elevator seems to be broken, Sanskrit inscriptions on exposed rock, a grotto, and remnants of multiple small defensive walls. Adjacent museums cover local naval history and military hardware. Don't expect tranquillity - a freeway tunnels through the centre…
spots.price: ¥60, or ¥30 for Ningbo residents, children, seniors 60-69, and students. Three nights a year it is open 18:00-06:00 for…
spots.addr: 10 Zhaobaoshan Road, Zhenhai District (镇海区招宝山路10号)

spots.name: Tangut dharani pillars
spots.desc: The Western Xia empire was destroyed by the Mongols in the 14th century, however a community of Tangut people from the Western Xia erected these pillars far away in Baoding in the 16th century. It is one of the few examples of the complex Tangut script found outside of Western China.

spots.name: Luoyang Museum
spots.desc: The museum houses historical relics from Luoyang’s era as the capital of thirteen dynasties and serves as an important site for understanding the city’s cultural history.Very well done museum featuring an extensive collection of ancient Zhou Dynasty bronzes as well as Han and Tang Dynasty porcelains, nearly all of which were made and found in the area, giving a sense of the former grandeur of the…
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:30, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: Nietai Road

spots.name: Qingdao TV Tower
spots.desc: Visitors take the elevator to an outdoor observation deck that offers panoramic views of Qingdao.The tower has an indoor viewing area and an outdoor platform. The observation deck is at an altitude of approximately 230 meters. On clear days, visitors can see the coastline, the old town, and the modern eastern districts. There is a small café and a souvenir shop on site.Tea, snacks, and beer are…
spots.addr: 10 Taipingshan Rd

spots.name: Tianlongshan Grottoes
spots.desc: AAAAA Tourist Attractions of China. Tianlongshan Grottoes is a series of 25 caves carved into the mountainside of Tianlong Mountain and well known among Chinese art experts for the fine Buddhist statues and decorations which were sculpted within. The earliest of these caves were built during the Eastern Wei Dynasty (534-550), and additional caves were added in the Northern Qu, Sui, and Tang…

spots.name: Liaoning Provincial Museum
spots.desc: A high-quality museum featuring Liaoning history from the stone age to the Qing dynasty, with many relics of China's past found in the area (3rd floor). Also houses large collections of Chinese traditional art and calligraphy, plus temporary exhibitions. There may be queues to enter during main public holidays.
spots.hours: April to October: Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00. November to March: Tue-Sun 09:30-16:30, no entry after…

spots.name: Tuyoq Valley
spots.desc: A pretty Uygur village at the base of dramatic sandstone hills. As of April 2025, this village was in the process of being rebuilt for mass tourism, in the same vein as Kashgar’s new Old Town.

spots.name: Khotan Museum
spots.desc: Free entry to look around, all items have tags in Chinese, Uyghur and English. Tours available in English for ¥10. Museum has one floor of artifacts including two 2500-year-old mummies. Closed for lunch so arrive early enough to orient yourself vis-à-vis local architectural sites.

spots.name: Qingyun Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple on Dinghu Mountain, with origins dating to the Ming dynasty. The present temple was established in 1636 and preserves traditional Chinese architectural features. It was designated a National Key Buddhist Temple in Han Chinese Area in 1983.
spots.addr: Dinghu Mountain, Dinghu District

spots.name: Huawei Ox Horn Campus
spots.desc: A European-themed model village serving as a campus for Huawei engineers, with twelve building groups connected by a tram system. Contains clones of parts of e.g. Český Krumlov, Verona, Bologna, Budapest, Granada.

spots.name: Zumiao Temple
spots.desc: Inside is a Confucius temple, Memorial Hall of kung Fu legends Wong Fei-hung and Ip Man, and among other things regarding Foshan history.

spots.name: Leiqiong Global Geopark Haikou District
spots.local: 雷琼世界地质公园海口园区
spots.desc: Covers 108 km². China hosts one of the few dormant volcanic clusters from the Holocene period (about 10,000 years ago). The volcanic cluster in Haikou comprises 40 volcanoes and some 30 caves, however, most visitors only see the most spectacular volcano and crater. The lava rock villages in the volcano area offer a unique countryside scene and a glimpse into countryside life/culture. Notable…

spots.desc: Hailongtun is a ruined middle age castle south of Zunyi. Built atop a mountain it has spectacular views and is one of the few examples of middle ages military defenses remaining in China.

spots.name: Jinli Ancient Street
spots.desc: This neighborhood is part of the old city of Chengdu; it features hotels and small stores built in an old-fashioned style. Antiques are sold in a variety of different stores. It is very popular among both tourists and locals, especially at night, with many bars, restaurants, and nightclubs. You will find a lot of famous local snack food over there, prices ¥1-10. Restaurants and bars in Jin Li…

spots.name: Wannian Monastery
spots.desc: A large monastery with a fantastic statue of Puxian Bodhisattva, who is depicted as riding a white elephant with six tusks. The monks there are great, and they add a good deal to the ambience of the mountain. A part of the temple is a modern re-construction.

spots.name: Yuantong Temple
spots.desc: With a history of more than 1,200 years, Yuantong Temple is the grandest and most important Buddhist temple in Yunnan Province. King Yimouxun of the Nanzhao Kingdom built the temple in late eighth century. The restorations from the Qing Dynasty onward has not changed the unique mixed architectural style of the Yuan and Ming Dynasties.Unlike all other Buddhist temples, you enter Yuantong Temple…
spots.addr: 42 Yuantong Street, Wuhua District (五华区圆通街42号)

spots.name: Siberian Tiger Park
spots.desc: This is without a doubt Harbin's "must see". Not for the faint hearted or obsessive animal lovers. There are literally hundreds of tigers in several huge pens. If you want to go by bus instead of taking a taxi, take the 88 line (facing the train station, walk into the small street on your left for 300 m before seeing the bus stop) to Shangye Daxue 商业大学. It should take about 30 minutes, and it is…
spots.price: For just ¥100 (¥90 to get in and another ¥10 for the bus) you can ride in an open bus with metal caging around it. The…

spots.name: Dongguan Basketball Center
spots.desc: Home of the Guangdong Southern Tigers.

spots.name: Longquan Monastery

spots.name: Xiǎntōng Temple
spots.desc: Xiǎntōng Temple, perhaps the largest Temple, is where Buddhism took over from Daoism as the main religion in this area.

spots.name: Shennong Tower
spots.desc: The Shennong Tower is a landmark building in Zhuzhou, and climbing to the top of the tower can provide a panoramic view of the entire city of Zhuzhou.

spots.name: Zigong Dinosaur Museum
spots.desc: Located on top of the Dashanpu Formation, China's most famous dinosaur fossil site, where hundreds of dinosaur fossils have been found since the 1970s. The museum was the first museum in China to be devoted exclusively to dinosaurs. The museum is quite large, covering a surface area of 25,000 m² and display area of 3600 m². Besides the usual displays, one can also view an excavation pit where…
spots.addr: 268 Shenhaijing Road Section 4, Da'an District (大安区燊海井路4段268号)

spots.name: Changfeng Park

spots.name: Hongluo Temple
spots.desc: This is the largest Buddhist temple in northern China and was built in 378. The temple has been quite important for centuries and has functioned both as temple and monastery. It is beautifully located next to the Hongluo Mountains, which you can climb or reach by cable car. The temple grounds are big, covering almost 800 hectares. You can easily spend a whole day touring the three main scenic…

spots.desc: The largest urban park in China and is a lush green area that flows over acres of hills and includes several lakes. It includes the Ming Dynasty Zhenhai Tower (镇海楼) zhènhǎilóu, now home to the Guangzhou Museum with relics on five floors dating back 5,000 years ago and an up-to-date miniature of modern Guangzhou. ¥10. 09:00 - 11:30, 13:00 - 17:00. Also check out the Stone Statue of the Five Rams…

spots.name: Mt. Lingshan Scenic Resort
spots.desc: With 2300 meters in height, Mt. Lingshan is the highest mountain in Beijing.

spots.name: Moca Shanghai
spots.desc: An art gallery by the park.

spots.name: Zhongshan Park
spots.desc: Established as 'Jessfield Park' in 1914 by a British property developer, it was renamed later in honour of Dr Sun Yat-sen.

spots.desc: The West Bund branch of the private art museum established by the wealthy collectors Liu Yiqian and his wife Wang Wei. The museum also has branches in Pudong District and the western city of Chongqing. Groups of 26 people or more are required to make a reservation at least 2 days before their visit.
spots.addr: 3398 Longteng Avenue (龙腾大道3398号)

spots.name: Jinjiang Amusement Park
spots.desc: Has a 108-metre (354 ft) Ferris wheel with, on a clear day, a fine view over the city.

spots.desc: Square pagoda in the south-east of Songjiang. From the Xilin pagoda central city area to the Fangta pagoda it's a 30 minute walk to the east on Zhongshan Lu. The garden is newly renovated and includes a large peaceful area and some 600 year old trees. A few "attractions", such electric boats, auto scooter for kids and the like at the outer places of the park disturb the peaceful overall…

spots.name: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics
spots.desc: North of Fudan University's main campus. You can reach it by taking buses 406 or 819 from Wujiaochang.

spots.name: Ming Dynasty City Wall Site Park
spots.desc: Beijing's city wall was built around 1435. It stretched for 23.5 km with one part running where Metro Line Two is now (inner city wall) and one part running where the southern part of Ring Road Two is now. Since 1949 (and especially around 1965), most was torn down to make room for Ring Road Two, Metro Line Two and Tiananmen. Now only 1.5 km remains behind Beijing Station. It has been restored…
spots.price: Park is free; ¥10 for the tower

spots.name: Bianyifang
spots.desc: The oldest roast duck restaurant in Beijing with a history dating back to 1416. Many branches throughout the city including three in Chongwen.

spots.name: Cross Temple
spots.desc: The remains of what is generally described as the earliest Christian foundation in the Beijing area, associated with the Church of the East.

spots.name: Dule Temple
spots.desc: The Dule Temple is one of the best preserved ancient Buddhist temples in China and a major tourist attraction in Jizhou District. It was established during the Tang Dynasty and rebuilt in the year 984 AD during the Liao Dynasty. It consists of two wooden buildings: the gate building known as Shanmen (山门) and the Guanyin Pavilion (观音阁), which contains a 16-meter-high statue of Guanyin, the…
spots.price: ¥33 to visit the Dule Temple only; ¥50 for a combo ticket including not only the Dule Temple, but also the Jizhou…
spots.addr: 41 Wuding Street (武定街41号)

spots.name: The Rice Terraces
spots.desc: A short hike through Ping'An to the summit takes about 2 hours to complete, depending on fitness. JinKeng is slightly larger so may take more time. It is possible to hike between Ping'An and DaZhai (JinKeng) in about 3 hours, enquire about guides once at either of the villages. Longer hikes spanning more than one day are possible and will allow you to access more beautiful and less touristy areas…

spots.name: Ciqikou
spots.desc: Meaning "Porcelain Port" as porcelain has long been made & transported from here, in Shapingba, on the banks of the Jialing River. This is a step back in time with several streets of Chongqing as it was, (and still is in some places). It is mostly comprised of small shops selling tourist stuff, but does lead down to the river where it is possible to board a restaurant boat and where the present…
spots.hours: 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

spots.name: Luohan Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple dating from the Song Dynasty, which used to be known as Zhiping Temple (治平寺). During the Qing Dynasty, the temple was extensively renovated and it was during this time that it was renamed Luohan Temple. Luohan (罗汉) is the Chinese word for the Sanskrit term 'arhat', which in the Chinese Buddhist tradition basically means a person who has reached a certain stage along the path of…
spots.addr: 7 Luohan Temple Street (罗汉寺街7号)

spots.name: Fengdu Ghost Town
spots.desc: Across the river from the main town is the Ghost Town which can be reached by ferry. Highlights include the authentic Buddhist temple on Mt. Ming and the Ghost Gate through which the souls of the dead must pass on their journey to the afterlife.
spots.addr: Mingshan Subdistrict (丰都县名山街道)

spots.name: Disneytown
spots.desc: A shopping, dining and entertainment district outside the park.

spots.desc: This square in the heart of the city's financial district is surrounded by some of the best examples of colonial-era architecture in Dalian. Though the square was laid out by the Russians, most of the buildings around the square were built between 1910 and 1920 by the Japanese, the main exception being the Dalian People’s Cultural Club, a Stalinist building that was built by the Soviet Union…

spots.name: Suoyang City Ruins
spots.desc: Suoyang was founded in 111 BC by Emperor Wu of the Han Dynasty and rebuilt at this site in 295 AD by Emperor Hui of the Western Jin Dynasty. The city was an important commercial and administrative center in the region up until its destruction at the hands of the Mongol ruler Mansur Khan during the 16th century. The highlight of the ruins is the Ta'er Temple, a Buddhist temple just outside the…
spots.addr: Nanba Village, Qiaozi Township (桥子乡南坝村)

spots.name: Gozo-ji Temple
spots.desc: the monastery of the fifth Patriarch of Chan (Zen), at East Mountain (TungShan). In 2019, there is a new tourist center next to WuZuZhen Village, and the road to the temple is closed for cars. The bus from the tourist center to the temple (15 minutes) leaves each half hour
spots.addr: 100 meters west of 059 Township Road, Wuzu Town

spots.name: Tianjin Museum
spots.desc: Tianjin Museum has modern exhibition halls with an area of 11,000 square meters as well as cultural and leisure facilities with multiple functions. It looks like a swan spreading its wings to fly from the lake surface. It possesses cultural relics of almost 200,000 items, including calligraphy, painting, bronze, ceramics, jade article, stamp of ruler’s seal, carapace bone, coin, historical…
spots.addr: 62 Pingjiang Road, Hexi District (河西区平江道62号)

spots.name: Tianjin Natural History Museum
spots.desc: Since 2020 all visitors have been required to make an appointment before visiting the museum. Visitor numbers are capped at 4500 on ordinary days and 7500 on public holidays. Appointments can be made on the museum's website (which is in Chinese only) and also on the museum's WeChat account (see website for QR code).

There are "Lion King" cast on the top of the head and under the neck, and the text of "Diamond Sutra" is cast all over the abdomen. However, due to the age, the writings are many and incomplete. The words "Made in the third…

spots.name: Temple of the City God
spots.desc: While the yamen ruled the "yang" of the human world, the Temple of the City God ("Chenghuang Miao") ruled the "yin" of the spiritual world. These two sites were situated so as to balance each other, with both on the same street and placed equidistant from Qing-Ming Street (South Street), with the yamen to the west and the Temple of the City God to the East. Visitors enter the temple, which…

spots.name: Yongle Palace
spots.desc: Yongle Palace ("Palace of Eternal Joy") is renowned for its many Yuan Dynasty murals, which are considered to be some of the finest artistic treasures in China. It is the largest of all Taoist temples remaining from the Yuan Dynasty. This important Taoist temple complex was not always located where it is now; it was moved brick-by-brick, painting-by-painting from 1959 - 1964 to allow for the…
spots.addr: 78 Yongle Street North, Ruicheng County (芮城县永乐北街78号)

spots.name: Dongpo Academy
spots.desc: Probably the most important historical site in Danzhou. The oldest building is the Zaijiutang (载酒堂), which the famous Song Dynasty writer Su Dongpo established as his home in 1098 during his time in exile. Over the centuries, the site underwent several renovations and expansions, eventually becoming the Dongpo Academy in 1548. A number of Su's works are on display at the academy, along with the…
spots.addr: Zhonghe Town (中和镇)

spots.name: Jianmen Pass Scenic Area
spots.desc: Jianmen Pass resides in the interruption of the Great Sword Mountain, both sides of the cliffs, straight into the clouds, the peaks leaning sky like a sword, the cliffs break away from the two walls relative to each other, the shape of the door like, so it is called "Jianmen", "the world's most majestic pass," the name. Jianmen Pass Scenic Area consists of two neighboring scenic spots, Jianmen…

spots.desc: Nice public park with a lake and some walkways. A good place to see older Chinese people practice their dancing. If you play any Chinese board games — Chinese chess (xiangqi) or Go (weiqi) — there are often games going on in the Southeast corner of the park.

spots.name: Milu Yuan
spots.desc: Part deer park, part research centre, holding the world's largest population of milu, or Père David's deer. The species was unknown to Western science until a French missionary saw the imperial herd here in the 19th century; the Chinese population then died out entirely, and the animals here descend from stock returned from England in the 1980s. Reservations are required and are made through…

spots.name: Taikoo Hui
spots.desc: Upscale shopping center. Has a big food court on the floor below ground level.

spots.name: Guangdong Revolutions History Museum

spots.name: The Grand Canyon
spots.desc: Enshi Grand Canyon is located at the junction of Hunan, Chongqing, and Hubei provinces. It is 49 km away from Enshi City and 39 km from Lichuan City. The total length of the canyon is 108 km.

spots.name: Fuxing Park
spots.desc: This European-style park formerly known as French Park has gardens, open spaces and restaurants and clubs dotted throughout. Early in the morning, the park is filled with dancers (some Chinese styles, but mainly Western ballroom) players of various games (cards, mahjong, Chinese chess and Go), Tai Chi artists, and singing groups.
spots.addr: 105 Fuxing Zhong Rd (卢湾区复兴中路105号; Lúwānqū Fùxīngzhōnglù)

spots.name: Shanghai Propaganda Poster Art Centre (PPAC)
spots.desc: This private collection is one of the most relevant and uncensored exhibits available to visitors interested in a glimpse of the politics and art of Mao-era China. Posters, memorabilia, photos, and even "大字报" (dazibao: big character posters) can be found in rotating exhibition. Due to the controversial nature of the historical items stored here, the museum is quite difficult to find, and…

spots.desc: A relatively small park with traditional Chinese gates, curved paths and pavilions. Good park for a walk if you happen to be nearby, but for genuine historical gardens you can consider travelling to Suzhou.

spots.name: Fengjing Ancient Town
spots.desc: This ancient water town dates back over 1500 years, and used to straddle the border between the Wu and Yue states. It has the usual collection of old buildings and bridges, old streets lined with shops, boats ferrying tourists through the canals, and museums and mansions which charge admission. The latter focus more on local communist history than you see in other water towns. The town is famous…

spots.name: Huiji Monastery
spots.desc: The lazy can reach the temple by cable car (¥40 return). Take Bus 2 from the port (¥10). More active visitors and pilgrims take the concrete steps from near Fayu Temple. It takes about 1 hour to climb the mountain. If your interest is old military installations, turn right soon after the start of this stair ascent up a smaller set of stone steps. After 10-15 minutes, this continues through a…

spots.name: Chen Clan Ancestral Hall
spots.desc: This is very well preserved architecture from the 19th century, and one of the finest surviving examples of traditional Cantonese architecture. It used to belong to a wealthy family with the surname Chen and now is a museum that houses many articles including ivory sculptures and artistic statues. Watch for the beautiful rocks in the backyard and the incredibly intricate roof carvings.
spots.price: ¥10 for adults; ¥5 for seniors 60-65 and students; free for children under 18 and seniors over 65. Foreigners need to…

spots.name: Boundary Island
spots.desc: Boundary Island is a small island situated off the coast of Lingshui. It is very popular with visitors to Lingshui thanks to a combination of the beautiful scenery and a wide variety of activities:Aquarium: With daily dolphin and sea lion shows.Watersports such as jet skiing and parasailing are available on the beach.Diving: the waters around Boundary Island have excellent visibility and diverse…
spots.price: ¥128-132 depending on season (includes entrance fee and ferry trip to and from the island)

spots.name: Old Lute Platform
spots.desc: The Lute Platform is a memorial to the famous musician Yu Boya and his close friend Zhong Ziqi who lived in the State of Chu during the Spring and Autumn Period. The first platform was built during the Song Dynasty, and it has been rebuilt several times. The present structures date from the late Qing Dynasty. The nearby Qintai Grand Theatre and Qintai Concert Hall are named after this place.
spots.addr: 10 Qintai Avenue, Hanyang District (汉阳区琴台大道10号)

spots.name: Baotong Temple
spots.desc: A large Chan Buddhist temple, although ancient in origin, had most of its buildings constructed in the modern era. The Hall of 500 Arhats is worth seeing. There are two bixi turtles on premises, although one of them is fairly new, carrying a stele commemorating the temple's renovation in 2006. Hongshan Pagoda (洪山宝塔), although not at Hongshan Hill's top, provides the best viewpoint around.…

spots.name: Jiefangbei Pedestrian Street
spots.desc: The center of downtown Chongqing. Jiefangbei, or the People’s Liberation Monument, formerly known as the Monument of Victory in the War of Resistance (World War II), is a 27.5-meter-high structure. Around the monument is a broad, paved pedestrian square lined by numerous glassy office skyscrapers and highrise hotels, reminiscent of New York's Times Square or Tokyo's Shibuya district. Jiefangbei…
spots.addr: Yuzhong District (渝中区)

spots.name: 816 Nuclear Military Plant
spots.desc: An immense underground facility that was intended to be used for the production of nuclear weapons. Construction began in 1966 and was almost completed at the time the project was cancelled in 1984. Since no plutonium or other radioactive materials were actually processed here, it is therefore safe for visitors. Unlike other nuclear sites in China, the 816 Nuclear Military Plant is open to both…

spots.desc: Nanjishan Islands are located in the southeastern sea of ​​Pingyang County, Zhejiang Province. They consist of 52 islands and have beautiful ocean scenery and a good ecological environment. Nanjishan Islands have shell sand beaches and clear and transparent sea water. In addition, there are scenic spots such as Qifengju, Narcissus Island and Seagull Island where Soong Mei-ling rested. This place…

spots.name: Old City Wall
spots.desc: The small surviving part of the Shanghai city wall. A prominent feature is Dajing Tower. If you want to see a larger and better preserved wall, go to nearby Suzhou, or Nanjing.

spots.name: Fangsheng Bridge
spots.desc: This 70-meter-long bridge is the icon of Zhujiajiao. Resting on 5 symmetric arches, the height of the bridge peaks at 5.8 meters. It was built by the monk Xingchao of Cimen Temple in 1571, and then rebuilt in 1812. The central arch is decorated with a stone relief of eight dragons surrounding a pearl, and the pillars at the ends are sculpted into lions. It's the largest stone arch bridge in…

spots.name: Zhuguang Road station
spots.desc: If you like modern architecture, on your way to Zhujiajiao you can stop at several metro stations for a look. You don't have to get out the paid area, and the next metro will come in 5-10 minutes. Enjoy the architectural splendour of each construction and the inner decorations consisting of murals and natural light effects. Zhuguang Road station is like a museum, with ceramic art exhibits in the…

spots.name: Qingnianhu Park

spots.name: Tianjin Water Park
spots.desc: Tianjin's largest urban park. It consists of three lakes and eleven islands. Surrounding the lakes are gardens and pavilions representing different architectural styles.

spots.desc: Nanling National Forest Park is near Shaoguan in Guangdong, China.

spots.name: Shenzhen Museum
spots.desc: In Wing A of the Shenzhen Civic Centre, the City Government's spectacular wing-roofed building. This is a must-see. The ground floor gallery has temporary exhibits from some of the most famous museums of China, which have ranged from jade burial suits to Shang Dynasty bronzes to contemporary Chinese painting. The upper floors have exhibits of the history of Shenzhen: the incredible number of…

spots.name: Shenzhen Museum of Contemporary Art & Urban Planning (MOCAUP)
spots.local: 当代艺术与城市规划展览馆
spots.desc: If you get a kick out of sleek modern architecture and the story behind how cities grow, MOCAUP in Futian is made for you. Opened in 2016 and designed by Coop Himmelb(l)au, the museum combines dazzling contemporary art with immersive exhibitions on Shenzhen’s past, present, and future city planning. No need to register or show your passport as of 2025.

spots.name: Shenzhen Library
spots.desc: Shenzhen Library and Concert Hall together make up another of the architectural masterpieces of the city. Architect Arata Isozaki designed the buildings with a back of almost featureless black granite and a front of brilliant folded glass. It is a must see for architecture freaks. The library has four million books.
spots.addr: 2016 Fuzhong 1st Road, Futian (福田区福中一路2016号)

spots.name: Hubei Provincial Museum
spots.desc: Exhibit of ancient Chinese artifacts excavated from throughout Hubei Province. Displays range from pottery, jewelry, clothing, and even ancient human skulls. One of the highlights are the well-preserved musical instruments, and a brief concert is played daily on replica instruments. Also houses one very famous weapon: the Sword of Goujian. The museum is a very popular destination, and ticket…
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00, closed on Mondays (except legal holidays) and New Year's Eve

spots.desc: Shunan Zhuhai National Park (蜀南竹海国家公园) is in Sichuan province. It is also known as The Bamboo Forest, The Bamboo Sea and The Bamboo City.

spots.name: Dapeng Ancient Fort
spots.desc: Dapeng Fort is an amazingly well-preserved Ming Dynasty Fort. Founded in 1394, it shared with various other forts the duties of guarding the entrances to the Pearl River and was prominent in the defense of the river during the Opium War. It is extremely well preserved and undergoing restoration as a museum. The old buildings in the adjacent village have been turned into shops selling souvenirs…
spots.addr: 大鹏街道鹏城社区南门围二巷八号

spots.name: Lingshan Islamic Cemetery
spots.desc: The first Islamic missionaries to China came to Quanzhou by ship. Tradition has it that Muhammad himself sent four of his personal disciples and they arrived in the late 7th century. Upon their deaths, they were buried here, and their tombs became a place of pilgrimage for some Muslims.

spots.name: Quanzhou Maritime Museum
spots.local: 泉州海外交通史博物馆
spots.desc: Excellent museum. Quanzhou was, up to the 15th century, one of China's greatest trading cities and a major base for her powerful fleets. Besides a collection of ship models and nautical artifacts, the museum has a large collection of stone inscription and reliefs - from ancient tombstones and temples - demonstrating Quanzhou's historical connections with India, the Middle East, and Europe, and…

spots.name: Meiling Palace
spots.local: 国民政府主席官邸旧址
spots.desc: A stately mansion named after Chiang Kai-Shek's wife Song Mei-ling. This was one of Chiang Kai-Shek's official residences in the 1930s and 1940s. The building has been fully restored and is open to the public. There is a book store and cafe on the second floor. The basement level displays paintings made by Soong Mei-Ling.
spots.addr: No. 9 Sun Yat-Sen Mausoleum, Xuanwu District (玄武区中山陵9号)

spots.name: Ding Hui Temple
spots.desc: A temple on the site of a Tang Dynasty temple. Little more than two huge 300-year-old Ginkgo trees and some stone pillar bases remain from the original complex after it was demolished and a factory built atop in 1949.
spots.addr: DingHui Temple Ln

spots.name: Shantang Street
spots.desc: A restored canal street running from Changmen to Tiger Hill. The southeast end of the street may be mobbed with tourists, but as you walk further north the souvenir shops and restaurants disappear, and you can take a leisurely stroll along the canal through a quiet residential neighborhood.

spots.name: Su Embroidery Studio
spots.desc: This is a Suzhou-based company whose main business is exporting embroidery; the address is for their Suzhou distributor. Their web site is in English and has a lot of good background information on the history and techniques.
spots.addr: 1902 Senso International Plaza, 98 North Dongwu Road

spots.name: Shanghai Expo Park
spots.desc: Shanghai hosted the 2010 World Expo, recording the most visitors in the event's history. Since then, the Chinese Pavilion has remained in operation and there are various other sights.

spots.name: Qing'an Guild Hall and Anlan Guild Hall
spots.desc: Guild halls for the formerly-adjacent shipyard, including a temple for Matu, the goddess who protects sailors. Dating to 1191, demolished several times including in 1949 and the 1960s, and rebuilt 1997-2001, they now also serve as a museum covering shipbuilding in Ningbo dating back to the Neolithic period, and have been listed as part of the Grand Canal UNESCO World Cultural Heritage site.

spots.name: Lu Xun's Hometown Tourism Precinct
spots.desc: An assortment of buildings associated with Lu Xun, a famous early 20th-century Chinese writer.
spots.addr: 241 Luxun Zhong Lu, Yuecheng District (绍兴市越城区鲁迅中路241号)

spots.name: Bazi Bridge
spots.desc: Bazi Bridge is one of the oldest existing overpass bridges in China, built during the Northern Song Dynasty. Named for its unique figure-eight shape, the bridge showcases an ingenious design and structure. Surrounded by flowing rivers and ancient alleys, it represents the charm of Shaoxing’s water-town culture and serves as an important site to explore the city’s history and traditions.

spots.name: Treasures Gallery - Palace of Tranquil Longevity
spots.desc: A palace in itself with its own "Outer Court", "Inner Palace" and "Imperial Garden", this complex (O) was designed for the Qianlong Emperor to enjoy his retirement after abdication - but he was too busy giving his son instructions on government to ever use it. Look for the glaze-tiled Nine Dragon Screen in front of the main entrance. These buildings now house the Palace Museum's Treasures Gallery…

spots.name: Upright Gate
spots.desc: The Upright Gate is located between Tiananmen gate and the Meridian Gate, along the ceremonial way. It is nearly identical to Tiananmen gate, and is also open to the public.

spots.name: Hebei Museum
spots.desc: This is a must-see and contains expositions from two major discoveries: the tomb of King of Zhongshan (中山王) from the late 4th century BCE, and the royal tombs of prince and princess of the Han principality of Zhongshan (Mancheng 满城 Han tombs) from the late 2nd century BCE.

spots.name: Dragon Pavilion
spots.desc: The area around Dragon Pavilion was the site if the Ming dynasty palace of Prince Zhou. At the southern end of the street leading to Dragon Pavilion stands a reconstructed Wu gate. The remainder of the street is lined with many old buildings. In the late Ming period the palace was destroyed by floods, leaving only the foundations buried 5m under modern Kaifeng, however the city walls were later…
spots.addr: Northern end of Zhongshan Rd

spots.name: Yingtian Gate
spots.desc: A stunning historical reconstruction of the grand south gate of Luoyang City from the Sui and Tang Dynasties, restored in 2016. The gate is particularly impressive at night, illuminated by golden lights, creating a lively atmosphere with many cosplayers and visitors exploring the area.

spots.name: Erlitou Xia Capital Site Museum
spots.local: 二里头夏都遗址博物馆
spots.desc: The ancient bronze age city of Erlitou is claimed by some archaeologists and historians to have been the capital of the Xia Dynasty, China's legendary first dynasty. Around 2000 artefacts from the site are displayed in this museum, which opened in October 2019.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:30, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: Gucheng Expressway, Yanshi (偃师市古城快速路)

spots.name: Shandong Art Museum

spots.name: Badaguan

It was founded in the 1930s and is a famous scenic resort in China, covering an area of over 70 hectares. Badaguan is a scenic area that best embodies the characteristics of Qingdao's "red tiles, green trees, blue sea, and blue sky". Eight passes and eight landmarks; Eight different looks and eight…

spots.name: Qingdao Underwater World/Qingdao Aquarium
spots.desc: Qingdao is host to China's first public aquarium, opened in 1932. Today the "Underwater World" consists of four main areas on both sides of the street connected via an underground tunnel. One highlight is the moving platform that takes visitors in a tunnel through the aquarium, one can look all around and see fish from every angle. Also, do not miss the ever-popular mermaid shows. During the day…

spots.name: Harbin Confucius Temple
spots.desc: This Confucius temple is one of the largest of its kind in northeast China. The Heilongjiang Museum of Nationalities can be found inside the temple.
spots.addr: 25 Wenmiao Street (文庙街25号)

spots.name: West Tower Street
spots.desc: was built in the fifth year of Chongde (1640) and completed in the second year of Shunzhi. Emperor Qianlong once wrote plaques for the four temples and hung them on the main halls of the four temples. The plaque of Yanshou Temple is "金粟祥光". Except for the different names and the Buddha statues enshrined, the four towers and four temples have almost the same architectural scale and shape. The Xita…

spots.name: Mati Si Temple
spots.desc: Temples and grottoes are carved into the side of a cliff in several zones spread over several kilometres. Several of these can be visited and climbed through, in some cases through tight vertical passageways using small footholds and handholds. Most of the statues were heavily damaged in the 1960s, but the buildings and passageways are in good shape. Besides the temple you can do a 2-hr horse…

spots.name: Chengtian Temple Pagoda
spots.desc: A nice, medium sized garden area with classic Chinese buildings/architecture. The tower dominates the garden and the view from the top is one of the best you will get of Yinchuan.
spots.price: entry ¥10, plus ¥20 if you want to climb to the top of the pagoda
spots.addr: 121 Limin Street, Xingqing District (兴庆区利民街121号)

spots.name: Daxuexi Alley Mosque
spots.desc: The temple was founded in 705 AD, it is one of the oldest mosques in Xi'an.

spots.name: Banpo Village Ruins
spots.desc: 6,000-year-old ruins of a village site including residential and pottery-making areas, ancient tools, and a burial ground. You should also visit the Shaanxi History Museum to see some of the best examples of the pottery found at Banpo.
spots.price: Tickets are normally ¥65. Children aged 6 to 18 pay half price. Children under 6 and adults over 65 get in for free
spots.addr: 155 Banpo Road, Baqiao District (灞桥区半坡路155号)

spots.name: Qujiang Sightseeing Monorail
spots.desc: An elevated 6.8 km sightseeing monorail looping around the Qujiang cultural district. The ~45-minute ride offers aerial views over Qujiang Pool Heritage Park (Nanhu), Tang Paradise, and surrounding Tang-style parks.

spots.name: Grape Valley
spots.desc: Nicknamed Green Pearl City, an oasis of greenery, made up of more than 200 hectares of grape. The best grapes in China have been grown here for more than 1,000 years.

spots.name: Xingning Academy
spots.desc: This historic Confucian temple was first built in the Song dynasty and moved to its present site in 1484. The complex preserves traditional buildings including the Dacheng Hall, Chongjing Pavilion, side halls, a pool and the Lingxing Gate.
spots.addr: No. 27 Siqian Street, Xingtian Subdistrict

spots.name: Chongxi Pagoda
