spots.name: Fairy Mountain National Forest Park
spots.price: Entry tickets are ¥50; tickets for the sightseeing train are ¥25
spots.addr: Shuanghe Township (双河乡)

spots.name: Shiliang Waterfall
spots.desc: Part of the Shiliang Scenic Area. One of the highlights of the park, this waterfall passes under an extremely rare granitic natural bridge 7m long and nearly 2m high but only 30-50cm thick, on its way down a cliff more than 30m high. Shiliang means "stone beam", so the waterfall's natural bridge lends its name to the waterfall, the scenic area containing it, Shiliang village nearby, and Shiliang…

spots.name: Mount Shiping
spots.desc: The main peak is 668 m high. There is the Great Wall of the South on the mountain. Climbing Shiping Mountain offers a panoramic view of Zhenyuan County.

spots.name: Jingpohu National Forest Park
spots.desc: JIngpohu National Forest Park (镜泊湖国家森林公园) is in Heilongjiang province.

spots.name: Bijia Mountain Park
spots.desc: Less popular but quite a bit nicer than nearby Lianhua Mountain Park. It's full of trees, birds, lots of kinds of flowers, quiet rivers and ponds, and people strolling and doing tai chi. The park strikes a balance: attractively manicured without feeling too artificial. The "mountain" (really just a hill) has two peaks, 178m Bi Guan Peak (笔冠峰) and 164 m Bi Jun Peak (笔俊峰).
spots.addr: 26 Meigang Road, Futian 福田区梅岗路26号

spots.name: Shangqing Palace (上清宫)
spots.desc: Shangqing Palace sits near the mountain summit of Qingcheng Mountain. This ancient Taoist monastery offers mountain‑top views over surrounding hills, with many steles and Taoist cultural remains inside.
spots.hours: Subject to the opening time of Qingcheng Mountain scenic area
spots.price: Covered by the main mountain admission ticket
spots.addr: Peak area of Front Mountain, Qingcheng Mountain scenic spot

spots.name: Samaranch Memorial
spots.desc: Large memorial dedicated to the memory of Juan Antonio Samaranch, a Spanish national who served as president of the International Olympic Committee from 1980 to 2001. Samaranch is fondly remembered in China for supporting Beijing’s bid to host the 2008 Olympic Games. The memorial displays thousands of items from Samaranch’s personal collection, including photos, stamps, books, art work and…
spots.hours: 09:30-16:30, no tickets sold after 16:00, closed on Mondays
spots.price: Standard adult tickets are ¥60; children under 1.2 meters and adults over 70 years old can enter for free
spots.addr: Health Industry Park, Tuanbo Avenue, Jinghai District (静海区团泊大道健康产业园)

spots.name: Song Well
spots.desc: An old well traditionally associated with the Southern Song period. Despite being close to the sea, it is known locally for its fresh-tasting water.

spots.name: Setenling Gompa
spots.desc: A Buddhist monastery of the Jonangpa tradition founded by Namnang Dorje in the 13th-14th centuries. It was reconstituted in the late 19th century by Dro-ge Yonten Gyatso. There are about 800 or 1000 affiliated monks.

spots.name: Xiling Xueshan National Park
spots.desc: Xiling Xueshan National Park (西岭雪山国家公园) is in Sichuan province.

spots.name: Mugecuo
spots.desc: Mugecuo, is in Ganzi (prefecture) of China. It is the name of a national park, and of the largest of five lakes within the park. The entrance lies 21 km from Kangding, and is especially worthwhile to visit during the autumn months.

spots.name: Central Academy of Drama Theater
spots.local: 中央戏剧学院实验剧场
spots.desc: Performances include both plays and dance.
spots.addr: 39 Dongmianhua Hutong (东棉花胡同39号; Dōngmiánhuahútòng)

spots.name: Songhuahu National Park
spots.desc: Songhuahu National Park (松花湖国家公园) is in Jilin province.

spots.name: Shenzhen Science Museum
spots.hours: 10:00-17:00 (Wed to Fri), 09:30-17:00 (weekends and public holidays), closed on Mondays and Tuesdays
spots.addr: 1003 Shangbu Middle Road, Futian District (福田区上步中路1003号)

spots.name: Waterlands Resort
spots.desc: A much-hyped 1.6 square kilometer park by the water, way on the outskirts of the city, full of trees, streams, ponds, and walking paths. The activities scattered around are fun, including obstacle courses, boats, strawberry picking, and a lookout tower. If you like hills this is not the park for you, but it allows for a nice few hours walking around and exploring whatever attractions you stumble…
spots.price: ¥60 for adults; ¥48 for seniors 60–64; ¥30 for children 1.2m–1.5m, seniors 65–69, and students; free for children under…
spots.addr: Shajing, Bao'an 宝安区沙井街道

spots.name: Huafa Snow World
spots.desc: This indoor ski arena brings skiing to the tropics, offering a surreal alpine escape in balmy southern China. Covering 10 hectares with five slopes, including one with an 83-metre drop, it’s one of the world’s largest indoor ski resorts. A perfect place to swap flip-flops for skis, even in the middle of summer.

spots.name: HaiYa Mega Mall
spots.desc: A high-end six-story mall. Brand-name clothes, expensive electronics and handbags, edible bird's nests, elegant porcelain. The first floor is mostly cosmetics and jewelry, second floor mostly brand-name clothes, and the shops gradually get more varied as you ascend to higher floors. Restaurants are clustered on the top levels and on the basement level. The top few floors also have various games…
spots.addr: 99 Jian'an First Road, Xin'an Subdistrict, Bao'an District 宝安区新安街道建安一路99号

spots.name: Mount Guanzhi National Geopark
spots.local: 冠豸山国家地质公园, Guangzhishan National Geological Park
spots.desc: Longyan's most popular scenic attraction. The two main sights within the park are Mount Guanzhi (冠豸山) and Shimen Lake (石门湖).
spots.addr: Liancheng County (连城县)

spots.name: Yundongyan Scenic Area
spots.desc: The only scenic area in Zhangzhou's main urban area to be designated as a 4A-rated tourist attraction by China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism. The main feature is a rocky hill named Yundongyan (literally ‘Cloud Cave Rock'), which stands about 280 metres above sea level.
spots.addr: Caiban Village, Lantian Town, Longwen District (龙文区蓝田镇蔡坂村)

spots.name: China Port Museum
spots.desc: A major national-level maritime museum in the city's busy harbour district.
spots.price: The main exhibition halls are free. A fee of ¥30 is required to access the Harbour Science Exploration Centre and the…
spots.addr: 6 Gangbo Road, Chunxiao Town, Beilun District (北仑区春晓港博路6号)

spots.name: Tangshan Earthquake Museum
spots.desc: Museum built in 1986 to commemorate the Tangshan Earthquake of 1976, the deadliest earthquake to strike China in modern times.
spots.hours: 09:00-16:30 (April to October), 09:00-16:00 (November to March), closed on Mondays
spots.addr: 102 Xinhua East Avenue, Lunan District (路南区新华东道102号)

spots.name: Lijingmen Gate
spots.desc: The grand reconstructed western gate of Luoyang's ancient city, complete with a moat, barbican, and upper-level temples. Climbing the battlements offers elevated views over the old town rooftops, and the gate arch leads directly into the historic pedestrian market streets.
spots.price: Free at street level; ~¥45 to climb the ramparts and tower
spots.addr: Intersection of Jinye Rd and West St, Laocheng District

spots.name: Luoyi Ancient City
spots.desc: A cultural tourism area built in the style of an ancient Chinese city. It is known for its Tang Dynasty-style architecture, night views, and popularity as a Hanfu (traditional Chinese clothing) experience destination. The area includes the Wenfeng Pagoda and the site of the ancient Jin-Yuan city wall.
spots.addr: North side of Jiudu East Road and Liulin Street, Laocheng District

spots.name: Lijingmen Scenic Area
spots.desc: Stroll along West Street from Lijingmeng Gate to the Luoyi Ancient City. Plenty of bustling restaurants and lively atmosphere. Beautiful especially at night.

spots.name: Songhua River Bridge
spots.desc: Built in 1900, this bridge was the first bridge across the Songhua river in Harbin and has served the railway system for more than 100 years. In 2016, with the opening of a new bridge nearby, it was converted into a pedestrian bridge for visitors.

spots.name: White Pagoda Park
spots.desc: This is the tallest, at 70.4 metres, ancient pagoda in the Northeast of China. It dates to the Liao Dynasty and is one of the 6 oldest pagoda towers in China. The park was constructed around the pagoda in 1908.
spots.addr: 60 Zhonghua Road (中华大街一段60号 Zhōnghuá Dàjiē Yīduàn)

spots.name: Mao Zedong's Statue
spots.desc: This is the largest statue of Mao Zedong in China. Around the base of the statue are images of workers, peasants and soldiers in heroic poses. The square is a popular place for locals to relax. Also called 'Taxi Square' by the locals.
spots.addr: Zhongshan Sq, Heping District

spots.name: General Yang Hucheng's Zhiyuan Villa
spots.desc: One of two heritage properties administered by the Xi'an Incident Museum (西安事变纪念馆). the other being General Zhang Xueliang's Official Residence (listed below). Generals Yang Hucheng and Zhang Xueliang were the leading conspirators behind the Xi'an Incident.
spots.addr: 117 Qingnian Road, Lianhu District (莲湖区青年路117号)

spots.name: General Zhang Xueliang's Official Residence
spots.desc: The Xi'an Incident Museum's main exhibition halls are at this site.
spots.addr: 69 Jianguo Road, Beilin District (碑林区建国路69号)

spots.name: Kuàicān Miànshí
spots.desc: Not really a restaurant so much as a couple of tables by the side of the street, but in any case it's the closest place to get a decent bite to eat outside Shaoguan Station, the high-speed rail station. A mom-and-pop noodle shop with a small convenience store next door. It doesn't even seem to have a name—the sign (in Chinese only of course) just says something like "short-order pasta".
spots.price: ¥10 for a bowl of noodle soup
spots.addr: 赤水村

spots.name: Dongguan Botanical Garden
spots.desc: Beautiful, large, and well maintained botanical gardens. See lots of flowers and attractive landscaping, including Chinese-style gardens and ponds with fish. Labels are mostly in Chinese but regardless you can enjoy the scenery – this is one of the prettiest parts of Dongguan. It doubles as a popular park with a playground for children.
spots.addr: 99 Lüse Street, Nancheng District (南城区绿色路99号)

spots.name: Lin Zexu Memorial Museum
spots.desc: Oddly enough, this confusingly named museum seems to cover everything about the opium trade except the Opium Wars. The biggest focus is on Lin Zexu's heroic 1839 campaign to destroy imported opium; the wars that ensued are scarcely given a mention. The museum has lots of interesting artifacts, though the labels and their English translations leave something to be desired in terms of precision.…
spots.addr: 113 Jiefang Road, Humen Town (虎门镇解放路113号)

spots.name: Sea Battle Museum
spots.desc: This is the real museum for the Opium Wars: a detailed presentation of their context, details, and aftermath. The museum represents the official Chinese government interpretation of the Opium Wars – don't expect any kind of balanced presentation (though in fairness, from a 21st-century perspective it's hard to deny the British were in the wrong). For non-military history buffs, possibly the most…
spots.addr: Huandao Road, Humen Town (虎门镇环岛路)

spots.name: Lianhua Mountain Country Park
spots.local: 莲花山郊野公园 Liánhuāshān Jiāoyě Gōngyuán
spots.desc: Literally "lotus mountain", paved with extensive hiking paths. There's a temple not too far up.
spots.addr: Chang'an Town 长安镇

spots.name: Former residence of Su Zhaozheng
spots.local: 苏兆征故居 Sū Zhàozhēng Gùjū
spots.desc: Former home of early 20th-century communist activist Su Zhaozheng (1885–1929). The home has been turned into a museum with exhibits about the history of the area, Su's life, and his role in a major strike in Hong Kong. Unfortunately none of the information is in English. Don't miss the wall made of oyster shells and the various other well-preserved historic houses and structures in the…
spots.addr: 461 Baishi Street, Qi'ao Island 唐家湾镇淇澳白石街461号

spots.name: Cathedral of Saint Victor
spots.local: 维多尔天主教堂, 霞山天主教堂, Xiashan Catholic Church
spots.desc: Built by French missionaries in 1903, this is the largest Catholic Church on the Leizhou Peninsula. It remains an operating cathedral.
spots.addr: 85 Lüyin Road, Xiashan District (霞山区绿荫路85号)

spots.name: Yongzhou Ancient City
spots.local: 邕州古城, Three Streets and Two Alleys 三街两巷
spots.desc: Its core comprises three pedestrian streets—Xingning Road (兴宁路), Minsheng Road (民生路), and Jiefang Road (解放路)—alongside two ancient lanes, Golden Lion Alley (金狮巷) and Silver Lion Alley (银狮巷). The outer perimeter encompasses areas west of Chaoyang Road and north of Minzu Avenue. Established during the Song Dynasty, this district served as the commercial birthplace of ancient Yongzhou. Characterised…
spots.addr: 37 Minzu Avenue, Xingning District (兴宁区民族大道头)

spots.name: Qingxiu Mountain
spots.local: 青秀山, Mount Qingxiu, Qingxiu Hill
spots.desc: Located in the heart of Nanning, Qingxiu Mountain Scenic Area sits on the banks of the winding Yongjiang River. Qingxiu Mountain, with its rolling peaks, verdant trees, steep cliffs, clear springs, and unique rocks, is characterized by its subtropical plant landscape and is surrounded by clouds and mist year-round. Known as the "Green Lung of the City," it is a national AAAAA-level tourist…
spots.hours: East Gate: 06:00-24:00, North Gate and West Gate: 08:00-18:00, South Gate: 08:00-17:00
spots.price: Entry is ¥20. Fees for the sightseeing car are ¥5 for one ride, ¥9 for two rides and ¥34 for unlimited rides. The…
spots.addr: 6-6 Fengling South Road, Qingxiu District (青秀区凤岭南路6-6号)

spots.name: Anhui Museum - Luyang Branch
spots.desc: Also known as ‘the old museum’, the Anhui Museum’s Luyang Branch has exhibitions on modern art and Communist Party history.
spots.hours: 09:00–17:00, last entry at 16:30, closed on Tuesdays
spots.addr: 268 Anqing Road, Luyang District (庐阳区安庆路268号)

spots.name: Anhui Museum - Shushan Branch
spots.desc: The Anhui Museum’s Shushan Branch (also known as ‘the new museum’) includes the massive Warring States Chu Cauldron and a full-scale relocated Huizhou ancient residence, showcasing exquisite wood, stone and brick carvings and tracing Anhui's civilizational history from prehistoric times to the Qing Dynasty.
spots.addr: No. 87, Huaining Road, Shushan District (蜀山区怀宁路87号)

spots.name: Anhui Geological Museum
spots.desc: Large natural sciences museum with an extensive collection of rocks, minerals, gemstones and fossils, including dinosaur fossils.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00 (extended to 18:00 on weekends in July and August), no entry in last 30 minutes, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: 999 Jiahe Road, Shushan District (蜀山区嘉和路999号)

spots.name: Binyang Tower
spots.desc: Binyang Tower, located at the east gate (Yinbin Gate) of Jingzhou Ancient City, is one of the city's landmark buildings. Originally the Ming-era "Yinbin Tower," it was rebuilt several times and reconstructed in 1986–1987 in the Ming style, featuring a large wooden frame and a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof, with a height of about 9.5–12.9 meters. The interior displays Three Kingdoms-themed…
spots.addr: 50 meters east of the intersection of Neihuan North Road and Zhang Juzheng Street, Jingzhou District

spots.name: Yueping Park
spots.desc: Located in the south of Hengyang city. It covers 21 hectares. In the west of the park is the City Museum, where thousands of pieces of cultural antique and relics are displayed. Additionally, the zoo is located here, which includes a Mount Monkey, Birds and Beasts Lake, Fishpond, etc. Skating rink and man-made lake for boating are constructed on the south mountain of Yueping. Yueping Park…

spots.name: Jiangxi Provincial Museum
spots.desc: Jiangxi's main museum. A new home for the museum is being constructed on Ganjiang Avenue North (赣江北大道). When the new museum is completed, the old museum site will become the Nanchang City Museum.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: 2 Xinzhou Road, Donghu District (东湖区新洲路2号)

spots.name: Guanshan Lake Park
spots.desc: Guanshanhu Park is a forested park that lies 12 km from Guiyang’s city center. It lies around a pair of lakes, Guanshan North and South Lakes, and has a main paved path around them.There are also smaller paths that lead to scenic spots. In the center of the park, you can find an 18-meter-tall golden pheasant drum statue, representing luck and happiness. On the opposite side of the lake, there is…
spots.price: Free, but boat rides and children's rides charge fees
spots.addr: Guanshan Bridge, Lincheng West Road, Guanshanhu District (观山湖区观山大桥南北两侧)

spots.name: Xiangshan Temple
spots.desc: This temple dating from the 1920s is the largest in Zunyi. It remains an active temple with worshipers in attendance. The road leading to the temple is a crowded market street thronging with food and fruit vendors, fortune tellers and incense sellers.
spots.addr: 103 Zhongshan Road, Honghuagang District (红花岗区中山路103号)

spots.name: Fish Balls
spots.local: 鱼圆 yú yuán, 鱼丸
spots.desc: They are made of minced fish and egg white, mixed with flour. Some varieties of fish balls have pork or shrimp added, with the most famous one perhaps being the Fuzhou version. These are then cooked in boiling water.

spots.name: Shacha Noodles
spots.local: 沙茶面, sa-te-mī in Minnan, shāchá miàn in Mandarin
spots.desc: A specialty of Xiamen, with the broth having been inspired by the dipping sauce of the traditional Malay dish satay.

spots.name: Tai Chi Taro
spots.desc: Taro nut is cooked and pressed into mud, with sugar, eggs, water and oil. After the taro cools down, people sometimes add chopped kernels, cherry on the surface. It is one of Fujian’s traditional desserts.

spots.name: Light Cake
spots.desc: It is made with raw material of flour, salt, sesame seeds. The shape of light cake is similar to doughnuts. It doesn’t have much taste. In Fuzhou, "light cake" refers to the version without sesame seeds, while the version with sesame seeds is called "Fuqing cake".

spots.name: Wonton
spots.desc: is the most common snack in Fujian. The wonton skin is thin, it cooks in a short time. The boiled dumplings would be required in the process of adding cold water 2 times. After cooked, it looks half transparent.

spots.name: Buddha Jumps Over The Wall
spots.desc: A specialty of Fuzhou, it is perhaps the most famous dish in Fujian cuisine. It contains more than 30 delicacies, including shark's fin, sea slug, chicken breast, duck, pig's trotters, dried scallop, mushroom, abalone, pigeon egg. with other condiments. It's said that after the dish is cooked, the air is heavy with a strong fragrance. Legend has it that it smelt so good that a Buddhist monk…

spots.name: Tieguanyin Tea
spots.desc: Named after a goddess, this oolong tea is grown around Anxi in Quanzhou prefecture. It was the tea American colonists protesting British taxes threw overboard at the Boston Tea Party.

spots.name: White Tea
spots.desc: The white tea is grown in various regions of Fujian including the ShuiJie and Zhenghe counties. The white tea leaves have a unique shape. White tea is a little bit fermented tea with a mild flavor but leaves a sweet taste later.

spots.name: Yantai Mountain
spots.desc: The former Western nations trading area of fuzhou. Several buildings and the general layout remain. The lower part is now shops, cafes and restaurants.
spots.addr: 福建省福州市仓山区仓前路35号

spots.name: Baiyun Mountain
spots.desc: Less heavily trafficked than Gu Mountain. After the grueling top section, you will be rewarded by some genuinely beautiful hospitality and refreshing tea in a cave! Magic. Plus some great views over the city.

spots.name: Gu Mountain
spots.local: 鼓山, Gu Shan; lit.: Drum Mountain
spots.desc: A Taoist temple houses nationally important archives written in monks' blood as well as superb veggie restaurant. It is a 1,900-meter climb, or a 20-minute cable car journey to the top. Take bus 303 from the city to the start of the tourist cable car (鼓山旅游索道).

spots.name: Qi Mountain
spots.local: 旗山, Qi Shan, 旗山国家森林公园 Qi Shan National Forest Park
spots.desc: A forest park with big, waterfalls and stunning views over receding mountain ranges from a vertigo-inducing suspension bridge. All this and monkeys to feed.
spots.addr: Nanyu Town, Minhou County (闽侯县南屿镇)

spots.name: West Lake Park
spots.desc: Attractive urban lake in the center of Fuzhou. Rent paddle or electric boats and explore the lake. Walk over the arching footbridge to the Fuzhou Science Museum, a small but nice museum featuring dinosaurs. Or walk around the lake; it is surrounded by sidewalks and a boardwalk. They also have some pandas in an enclosure where you can see them. There is also an area with some fine bonsai.

spots.name: Wu Mountain
spots.local: 乌山 Wu Shan, literally "Black Hill"
spots.desc: This is near Yu Shan, and is the location of the black pagoda. There are many gazebos and stone-carved calligraphy by various notable people, one of which was written by Emperor Kangxi when he visited. The hill can be reached on the road to the left of the internationally well known brands of luxury shops.
spots.addr: Wu Shan Road, Gulou District (鼓楼区乌山路)

spots.name: Yu Mountain
spots.desc: Overlooking the main square, a short walk to the hilltop which houses a pretty average temple. However, on the way up there is plenty of entertainment in the form of musicians and singers who congregate here to practice. The White Pagoda is also accessed by the same road behind Mao Tse Dong's statue and worth a look. There are several very good arts and crafts shops at the base of the hill.…
spots.addr: Gulou District (鼓楼区)

spots.name: Rongcheng Plaza
spots.local: 榕城广场, Rongcheng Guang Chan
spots.desc: An abandoned shopping plaza by day, Rongcheng Plaza turns into an invariable lively hub of Western Fuzhou at night. Elderly residents of West Fuzhou use the plaza as a space for square dancing, partner dancing and conversing. Kids run around playing. Many of the stores there market clothing for kids, and the restaurants tend to be mid-range. It is worth visiting if you are interested in seeing…

spots.name: Jiangxin Park
spots.desc: Jiangxin Gongyuan is a beautiful small park on a small island. The view is not particularly notable but the community that exists on the island is worth a visit. There is a small children's book store that requires a child and WeChat to enter. The entire park is accessible only by footbridge from the mainland. Getting here and leaving is a problem due to the lack of parking spaces, and you must…
spots.addr: 福建省福州市台江区三县洲大桥

spots.name: Fujian Museum - Nature Museum
spots.desc: The nature branch of Fujian Museum. There are dinosaur skeletons and maps of excavation sites, a very small exhibition about wetlands and a room introducing aquatic life. About half of all signs have English translations. A good place to take kids, adults may not find it very interesting.
spots.addr: Gulou District - Fangqin Road (鼓楼区-芳沁路)

spots.name: Statue of Commissioner Lin
spots.desc: Lin Zexu (林则徐, 1785—1850) was a Fuzhou native who did brilliantly on the Imperial Examinations and became an official. Lin was appointed as an Imperial Commissioner to clean up the opium trade in Canton, where he seized and burned a large supply of opium. This provoked the First Opium War, which China immediately lost. Lin was blamed for some of this, despite his orders, and exiled to Xinjiang.…

spots.name: Lin Zexu Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A museum about Commissioner Lin who tried to stop the opium trade when he was in charge of Canton (now called Guangzhou), provoking the first Opium War. The museum incorporates Lin's former residence and the Lin Wenzhong Ancestral Hall (Lin Wenzhong is the honorary name given to Lin Zexu after his death).
spots.addr: 16 Aomen Road, Gulou District (鼓楼区澳门路16号)

spots.name: Fujian Science and Technology Museum
spots.desc: Not to be confused with the Fuzhou Science and Technology Museum. Unlike that museum, this one does not require visitors to make a booking before visiting.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:45, closed on Mondays and Tuesdays
spots.addr: 89 Gutian Road, Gulou District (鼓楼区古田路89号)

spots.name: Fuzhou Art Museum
spots.desc: The art museum is inside the former residence of Huang Peisong. Huang Peisong was a senior government official during the late Qing Dynasty and this was his official residence.
spots.hours: Tue-Fri 09:00-18:00, Weekends and public holidays 09:00-20:00, no entry in last 30 minutes
spots.addr: 172 Zhongping Road, Taijiang District (台江区中平路172号)

spots.name: Riley's Club
spots.desc: If pool is your game, you would be hard pushed to find better tables anywhere in China than here. Cheap drinks and open very late too.
spots.addr: Yangqiao Road

spots.name: Fuzhou Fighting Ferrets Football Club
spots.desc: A motley assortment of nationalities who play at Jinshan Wentizhongxin every Sunday at 09:15. Like football, only funnier!

spots.name: Paintball
spots.desc: Great fun for those masochists among us who enjoy being hit by high velocity projectiles in delicate parts of the body. Not to be attempted in summertime!

spots.name: Walk in traditional architecture street
spots.desc: Freshly renovated pedestrian street, back into time atmosphere, lots of small alleys to stroll by, great for shopping but avoid overpriced restaurants and bars.
spots.addr: Nan Hou Jie

spots.name: Sauna/spa
spots.desc: Fuzhou is famous for its hotsprings; many hotels have a sauna and spa. They often have three different pools, one hot, one boiling (by western standards), and a normal one. Sauna and Turkish bath used to be available, staff gives you all you need. Most of the saunas have massage center with different services.

spots.name: Wu Qingyuan Game of Go Club
spots.desc: The board game called Weiqi in Chinese or Go in Japanese and English is quite popular throughout East Asia; there are professional players and the better ones are major celebrities. Wu Qingyuan (吳清源, 1914—2014) is considered by many to be the best player of the 20th century and one of the greatest of all time. He was born in Fuzhou but lived in Japan most of his life and is generally known in the…
spots.addr: 78 Wu Shan Road, Gulou District (鼓楼区乌山路78号)

spots.name: Shoushan stone
spots.desc: A unique variety of alabaster found only in Shou Shan (寿山) (about 40km from Fuzhou) used to make name chops and all types of beautiful carving.

spots.name: Lacquer work
spots.desc: Especially the Fujian bodiless lacquerware (脱胎漆器), considered one of the three treasures of Chinese arts and crafts. It is lightweight, durable, and often lovely. There is a factory on Wuyi Road (五一路).

spots.name: Electronic Market
spots.desc: Hundreds of little shops plenty of fake iPhones and similar. Bargaining is recommended, but the first price is not as far off the real price as in Shanghai. There are also some big stores with real stuff.
spots.addr: Wuyi South Road

spots.name: Powerlong
spots.desc: It used to be the highlight mall of Fuzhou, with more than 300 shops and a cinema, but has become considerably less attractive than it was with the construction of several new malls in the region. It has attempted to revitalize itself with a significant new extension building with a department store. Premium brands are in first floor of the main building and have direct access to the street, or…

spots.name: Wanda Plaza
spots.desc: Considered to be the most popular mall in Western Fuzhou, Wanda Plaza offers a Chinese national-only hotel, premium brands, a Walmart and numerous restaurants (ranging from high-end to fast-food such as KFC and Starbucks to budget hole-in-the-walls). The mall is separated into a street portion and covered building portion. The hotel and Walmart are at the south end of the mall. The street portion…

spots.name: Boiled shark
spots.desc: A Geng (thick soup) using shark's meat, it won't have a strong smell

spots.name: Guo Bien Hu
spots.desc: Large steaming hot soft rice noodles inside soup of rice powder and water, hint of shrimp or oyster, under ¥11 a bowl. Only eaten for breakfast.

spots.name: Oyster Pancake
spots.desc: A traditional food in Fuzhou Kind like a pancake but with fly oyster and leek in it. Native people usually eat it in breakfast and prepare in various styles so if you do not find the exact name do not be surprised.

spots.name: Oyster cakes
spots.desc: Oyster cakes (Li bing) are a classic Fuzhou street snack, commonly found at roadside stalls and small eateries. The dish is made from fresh oysters mixed with a rice or wheat batter, often flavored with scallions, garlic, and celery.

spots.name: Dingbianhu
spots.desc: Dingbianhu is a traditional Fuzhou breakfast dish known for its distinctive preparation method. A thin rice batter is poured along the edge of a hot pot, where it instantly sets into delicate sheets before being scraped into a light, savory broth.

spots.name: Daming Food Street
spots.desc: A typical Chinese streetfood street with all kind of 小吃 (xiaochi, snacks) such as BBQ skewers, desserts, etc. A popular place for young locals and couples to hang out at night.
spots.addr: 鼓楼区达明路美食街

spots.name: Hao Shi Jie
spots.desc: Very expensive if you go upstairs, but stay on the ground floor and eat the dim sum which is cheap (under ¥250/head) and delicious.

spots.name: Cafe Forum
spots.desc: Good quality meals in a box and reasonably priced coffee, but the service can sometimes be atrocious. Hit it on a good day, it is great. On a bad day, it is dire.

spots.name: Ajisen Japanese Noodles
spots.desc: A great range of noodles and tasty side dishes. Friendly service and pictures in the menu for those who can not read Chinese which is a real Godsend.

spots.name: Lemon leaf
spots.desc: Very good Thai food. Featured dish: lemon fish and curry crab.
spots.price: Not cheap, ¥50 per person on average
spots.addr: 5F, 66 Hubin Road

spots.name: Roman Holiday
spots.desc: Likely the best Italian food in Fuzhou. Excellent pizza and pasta. Also, some good fusion Japanese/Italian/Chinese dishes.
spots.price: Not cheap, ¥50 per person or more if you get drinks
spots.addr: Jiao Tong Road, by the Hong Yun Xing Cheng Apartments

spots.name: Jazzy pizza
spots.desc: Chinese alternative to Pizza Hut, good pizza and cheaper, salads and pasta are ok, too.
spots.addr: Many locations

spots.name: Bullfighter
spots.desc: Steak house, you choose one steak and can use the salad and dessert buffet.
spots.addr: Many locations

spots.name: Panevino
spots.desc: Italian food, very good quality for Fuzhou standards. They have a set menu for lunch and dinner. Upstairs there is a good Japanese restaurant. Can communicate in English, in which the menu is also written.
spots.addr: Wenquan Park Road

spots.name: Bambino
spots.desc: Good Italian restaurant, cheaper than Panevino. You can also find some Chinese food among the Italian dishes. ¥150-200. Menu in English.

spots.name: Taiyro
spots.desc: Japanese food buffet. Free flow of drinks, sushi, sashimi and teppanyaki for ¥150/person. The sashimi used to be served frozen, not so good but sushi is acceptable and teppanyaki is good.

spots.name: Venue
spots.desc: French restaurant in Fuzhou, and perhaps the only one. More than ¥400/person

spots.name: Mamamya
spots.desc: Another Italian restaurant but not so good, pizzas are small and expensive, salads no good. ¥100 or more per person.

spots.name: Old Shanghai
spots.desc: Typical Shanghainese food, menu only in Chinese but with pictures, less than ¥100/person.

spots.name: Shao Yuan Yi Hao
spots.desc: Has a host of foreign beers, British, German and Belgian as well as fine wines, a few single malts, and beautiful decor and people. Bit pricey, but worth it for the music and atmosphere. It is a beautifully remodelled warehouse, the sort of design you might expect in a Western city or perhaps Shanghai, but unique in Fuzhou.

spots.name: 1-2-3 Bar
spots.desc: Cheap beer, convivial atmosphere, sometimes live music, stays open as long as you are drinking/semi-conscious. The sign says 1-2-3, but Chinese pronounce it "do-re-mi" for reasons that are not at all clear.
spots.addr: Baima Road

spots.name: Club Blog Club
spots.desc: A coffee shop managed by a Western resident that overlooks West Lake.
spots.addr: 136 Hubin Road

spots.name: The Pure Drop
spots.desc: A lively and convivial atmosphere, cheap, cold beer, live music every night.
spots.addr: Hubin Road

spots.name: The Bamboo Bar
spots.desc: Cheap beer, waterside tables, live football games on TV. Pushy owner, but easily ignored after a couple of beers!

spots.name: Saint Nobody
spots.desc: The most mysterious club in fuzhou with cheap beer and good indie music. An anti-fuzhou look which makes you feel like a traveler lost in an unknown city.
spots.addr: Beida Road

spots.name: Prada
spots.desc: The preferred bar for expats in Fuzhou. Local style, people playing dice and live singers. Few staff speak English, try to get a VIP card from the manager. Main drink is beer but you can order some cocktails.
spots.addr: 中国福建省福州市鼓楼区余府巷 中福西湖花园北福楼C区1层

spots.name: Lili Marlens
spots.desc: Similar to prada. Staff dressed in army style clothing. Manager is friendly and speaks a little English
spots.addr: 中国福建省福州市鼓楼区 古乐路117号-2

spots.name: Wooshie Bar
spots.desc: Small bar, live music, cheap beer (¥100 for 10), cocktails (¥25 each) and a relaxed atmosphere. Has a country music theme. Great place to go to enjoy something different from the usual fuzhou bar. Couches for free
spots.addr: Wusi Road, Gulou, Fuzhou

spots.name: Late Market Bar
spots.desc: Maybe the only 'speakeasy' bar in Fuzhou, mimicking the illegal establishments during Prohibition in the US. The bar is hidden behind a noodle shop (thus the Chinese name 喜福食舍 meaning Lucky Food House). Enter the noodle shop and go through a concealed door in the left-most shelf on the wall. The bar offers an upper-class atmosphere with dimmed lights and not too loud music. In addition to a large…
spots.addr: Aomen Lu 47 鼓楼区东街口商圈澳门路47号

spots.name: Tianzi Hot Spring Resort
spots.desc: Tianzi Hot Spring Resort is a resort with 4/5-star hotel and 90 different style hot spring pools.
spots.addr: 4 Jiantan Group, Dongxi Village, Chengjiao Township, Yongding District (永定区城郊乡东溪村箭滩组4号)

spots.name: Nine-Bend River
spots.desc: There are really nice places along this river, most commonly viewed from a bamboo raft leaving from the West Entrance (takes 90-100 minutes, a few minor rapids that could splash your feet). Don't miss the lookout rock between Wuyi Palace and Shuiguangshi (the last area of the rafting), that is probably the best view in the area. A bit past Tianyou peak, the rafts pass a cliff with small caves…

spots.name: Water Curtain Cave
spots.desc: A waterfall (not really any cave) with a small old shrine behind it and a massive rock. Reachable from its bus stop by walking 20-30 min on a road to the base and then 5-10 min up to the waterfall. You can walk a small loop and end up back at the main path to continue to the tea valleys (towards Da Hong Pao and Tianxin Yongle Temple) or just return to the bus station.

spots.name: Eagle Beak Rock
spots.desc: Halfway between Water Curtain Cave and Da Hong Pao Valley. A nicely-shaped rock but you can only walk past it within the valleys and no climbing is possible.

spots.name: Ancient Cliff Dwellings
spots.desc: Ancient wooden buildings built into an inaccessible crack in the cliff, once accessed via a pulley system. Can be seen from the trail but not visited.

spots.name: Da Hong Pao
spots.desc: This magical and enchanted valley produces the best and most expensive tea on Wuyi Mountain and is a tranquil and beautiful place. The tourist stop is not the best place to see anything but walking from here to the Water Curtain Cave goes through tea valleys and past the Eagle Beak Mountain, through some of the best places to see in the northern area. The main area has a tea shop that has cheap…

spots.name: Tianyou Peak
spots.desc: Big stone peak with breathtaking views on the nine-bend river and surrounding peaks. You can only climb one peak these days unless you want to climb over the "do not cross" signs like some tourists do (no-one will stop you), or look for small poorly-maintained trails running into the forest. The main peak can be really crowded and gets a little steep towards the end. You can have a little rest at…

spots.name: Horse Head Rock
spots.desc: Great scenery, which includes tea fields, an old temple, rocks, and rural buildings. This spectacular area is almost completely omitted by domestic tourists because it is a long (>1 km) walk from the nearest bus stop. The north entrance to its trail is a stone stairway at the entrance to the Da Hong Pao parking lot, and in the south it emerges at the back of Tianyou Peak. The connection south to…

spots.name: Tiger Roaring Rock
spots.desc: Great view over the surrounding rocky area, but the peak is closed off. There are still really nice places to see and the path continues to the Ray of Sky cave to the south or to Jade Beauty Peak to the north.

spots.name: Thread of Sky
spots.desc: Two rocks leaning together, leaving a narrow strip of sky visible. There is one part to just take pictures and another one to walk through. The latter is not so recommended if there are lots of tourists because it gets really narrow (30 cm at one point) and people will go really slow, it's steep, the steps are tricky, dark, wet, and slippery. Give this a miss if you are uncomfortable with crowds…

spots.name: Spiral Cave
spots.desc: Not famous but 200 m from Ray of Sky. A rock is carved from the bottom which is an amazing structure. Go there for a photo if you are already nearby anyway. As of Nov 2019, it is not accessible due to track maintenance.

spots.name: Jade Beauty Peak
spots.desc: You see this from the rafting and from a rocky beach at the side of the river. It's a lovely rock, but there is not so much else to see. You can walk there from Tiger Roaring Rock or Ray of Sky.

spots.name: Wuyi Palace
spots.desc: A temple with some display cases. This is included in the ticket prices and actually nobody checks tickets there because there is nothing to see. You can walk through it in 5 minutes and you will end up at this location for either the buses or the rafting trip so you might as well have a quick peek.

spots.name: Great King Peak
spots.desc: You can walk to this place from Wuyi Palace and even up to a nearby pavilion. Not done by most tourists as the rock can not be climbed and is clearly visible from the resort, river, palace, and during the Impressions DaHongPao performance.

spots.name: Lotus Peak
spots.desc: Not much to see here and you have to hike here from the north parking area.

spots.name: Wuyishan Museum
spots.desc: Small museum with 2 sections which is in a small tourist alley after you arrive from rafting and on the way to Wuyi Palace. One section explains the hanging coffins and another the local wildlife and scenery. As it is free you might have a quick break here because it is also cool. Displays have English and Chinese signs.

spots.name: Tianxin Yongle Temple
spots.desc: Tianxin Yongle Temple is a quiet and peaceful temple visit. From the main entry courtyard the left has a tea room which will serve tea to guests at no cost. Further in on the right is the dining hall. Eating with the monks is a fun experience. They have a donation box where you can put a few dollars. Lunch starts at 11:00. To eat grab a bowl and chopsticks off the rack in the back left corner.…

spots.name: Impressions DaHongPao
spots.desc: A 60-minute show about tea. Recommended for night activity (starts 19:30). Hundreds of actors, beautiful lightshow, audience turns 360 degrees for different views.
