Royal Tangshan Hotel offers private hot springs room coupled with spa treatments to follow. With easy access from Huning Highway that provides accessible public or private transportation, Tangshan is the…
spots.addr: 8 Quanyun Road, Tangshan Subdistrict, Jiangning District (江宁区汤山街道泉韵路8号)

spots.name: Xinjiekou
spots.desc: Nanjing's fashion district, the cosmopolitan, fast-paced heart of the city bathed in neon. It's the closest thing Nanjing has to Tokyo or Times Square. All the major retail is centered on this area, which despite its complexity is only a couple of square blocks in size. There are giant department stores including Wal-Mart, Watsons, Suning, and "Fashion Lady"—a bewildering, subterranean complex of…

spots.name: Hunan Road
spots.desc: A slightly more low-key version of Xinjiekou, running between Xuanwu Lake and Zhongshanbei Lu. It has most of the same stores including the Phoenix International Bookstore which has a whole floor of English-language books. There is also a small pedestrianised street running south from Hunan Road which is lined with pretty much every variety of restaurant imaginable, including the usual KFC and…

spots.name: The area around the Confucius Temple
spots.desc: in the south of the city has a lot of shopping, especially clothing and tourist items. It is a maze of tiny individual shops, and fun to explore even if you are not buying. If you are interesting in buying, bargaining over prices is the name of the game here. If you are skilled in the art of bargaining you can easily get an asking price of ¥380 reduced to ¥80 without breaking a sweat. The streets…

spots.name: Chaotiangong
spots.desc: For antique lovers, this place is a small market hosted next to the Confucius Palace. You can find all sorts of small and big objects there, some are real antiques, others are fake. If you want to buy something, be prepared to negotiate the price! This place is fun to stroll around seeing both things to sell and sellers as the environment is quite charming.

spots.name: Soul Mate
spots.desc: Western-style restaurant and coffee bar owned by French expats, with homemade pizzas, burgers, salads and French dishes for reasonable prices. It's a good place to have a few drinks and food in a friendly and relaxed atmosphere.
spots.addr: Nan Xiu Cun 15-1

spots.name: Da Pai Dang
spots.desc: A chain restaurant with an old-style Chinese atmosphere and menu with English. They serve a lot of old-style Nanjing specialties such as Jinling Roast Duck, lotus root, and Lions Head Meatballs. This restaurant is a chain that can be found in cities around China and beyond, but it still provides a comfortable and authentic introduction to Nanjing cuisine -- especially for foreign tourists.…

spots.name: Les 5 Sens
spots.desc: French restaurant with a French chef and a cosy atmosphere, providing traditional and family homemade French dishes.
spots.addr: 52-1 Hankou Lu

spots.name: Old Place
spots.desc: Has reasonably priced Chinese food with English translations, most fun in a group of 4 or more. Try the pineapple pork!
spots.addr: 金银街

spots.name: Skyways Bakery
spots.desc: Owned by a German/Belgian couple. Their sandwiches are of good quality and quite large and include a drink. They also have good salads and coffee at reasonable prices. Check out the bulletin board for employment opportunities in the city.

spots.name: Skyways Bakery location 1
spots.desc: Mostly baked goods, cakes, and chocolates. A few tables outside on the sidewalk, perfect for a relaxed day.
spots.price: About ¥45 for a pastry and coffee
spots.addr: Shanghai Lu

spots.name: German Bread Store
spots.desc: If you're missing some taste from home, or just looking for good bread and sandwiches, try this cafe next to Nanjing Normal University. They serve sandwiches, drinks, and various styles of original German bread. You'll probably find foreign visitors here are all hours, with lots of customers speaking various European languages.

spots.name: Jack's
spots.desc: Barely passable Italian food, but decent enough if you have been in China a few years. Some staff have good English and many of the customers are expats. Pasta or pizza is around ¥40-60, while good steaks start around ¥70.

spots.name: New Cafe
spots.desc: Self-consciously contemporary restaurant/lounge with a fairly extensive selection of western brunch fare: waffles, omelets, French toast, paninis. They also have a good selection of coffee, tea, and rather decadent desserts. The food here - sort of continental American with the inevitable anomalies - is good, particularly in the presentation; however, beware of the service. If you just want to…
spots.addr: Corner of Qingdao and Hankou Lu

spots.name: Prime
spots.desc: The tallest bar, lounge and restaurant in Jiangsu Province, Prime offers a spectacular view of Nanjing in a western setting with superior service and gourmet international cuisine. The Cigar lounge features a live music stage (western jazz musicians play irregularly) and a fully-stocked bar with a large selection of wines, beer, and over 100 specialty cocktails.
spots.addr: Intercontinental Hotel (Zifeng Tower) 78th floor, 1 Zhong Yang Road, Gulou District, 210008

spots.name: Ellen's bar
spots.desc: An always-popular and chaotic expat bar, usually with African DJs. Although there's no dance floor there's many people dancing between tables and in any open space.

spots.name: Bassment Bar
spots.desc: Live music almost every night and a good atmosphere, very spacious. A lot of expats will perform here. There's a dance floor, pool, and some arcade cabinets. People mainly sit at tables, but the bar has seating. A healthy mix of Chinese and expats. Beers start around ¥30-40 and mixed drinks are alright. (Live music has now stopped at Bassment)

spots.name: Langshan
spots.desc: which means Wolf Hill, is at the peak of a riverside hill and has a Buddhist temple dedicated to a Song Dynasty monk, who it is claimed had powers over water demons. The temple is a popular place for sailors, who offer prayers for safe passage.

spots.name: Nantong Textile Museum
spots.desc: Opened in 1985 as a tribute to the city's long association with the weaving industries, the museum was the first of its kind in China and boast six exhibition halls as well as courtyards and gardens.

spots.name: China Audit Museum
spots.desc: A museum that looks at accounting and auditing. It has displays of many different abacuses, including one that can calculate with 40 digits.

spots.name: Nantong Overseas Chinese Museum
spots.desc: The only Overseas Chinese museum in the Yangtze River Delta region.
spots.addr: 19 Haonan Road, Chongchuan District (崇川区濠南路19号)

spots.name: Nantong Laowai Mixer
spots.desc: A monthly get-together of the local expat community. Live music.
spots.addr: Tiger Tiger

spots.name: Suzhou Art Gallery
spots.desc: Exhibits of painting and calligraphy, especially modern Chinese art and local Suzhou artists.
spots.addr: No. 4 Canglangting Houjie, 沧浪亭后街4号

spots.name: Suzhou Opera Museum
spots.desc: The Suzhou Opera Museum has performances of three traditional local arts — Kunqu opera, which is on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list, Suqu opera, and Pingtan storytelling with ballads. All use the Wu language. There are stages for the opera and a teahouse in Qing Dynasty (1644-1911) style for the storytelling. The museum part has exhibition rooms for each of those three arts, a…

spots.name: Suzhou Silk Museum
spots.desc: This museum is dedicated to the city's millennia-old silk production history. Beyond static exhibits, visitors can often watch live demonstrations of intricate traditional weaving techniques like Song brocade, making it a deeply immersive cultural experience[citation:4].

spots.name: Suzhou Stele Inscription Museum
spots.desc: Housed in the former Confucian Temple, this museum holds a rich collection of ancient stone steles, including the renowned "Four Song Dynasty Steles." It's a quieter alternative to the city's more famous museums, focusing on the art of calligraphy and stone carving.

spots.name: Suzhou Pingtan Museum
spots.desc: Dedicated to Pingtan, a traditional Suzhou performing art involving storytelling and ballad singing in the Suzhou dialect. Visitors can enjoy live performances, appreciating the elegant music and the soft, melodic sounds of the local language.

spots.name: Auspicious Light Pagoda
spots.desc: This pagoda, built in 247 CE and rebuilt during the Song Dynasty about 1000 CE, is part of the Panmen complex. It has seven storeys and is 53 m (about 174 feet) high. Visitors may climb it, and the view is worthwhile.

spots.name: Baita Road
spots.desc: Starting from the Northern Pagoda, this street has been sympathetically developed and retains many old-style store fronts. On the east end huge gnarled trees arch over the street.

spots.name: Ligongdi
spots.desc: Li Gong Di is a 1400-meter causeway across Jinji Lake, the largest inner-city lake in China; it was built during the reign of Emperor Guangxu (1874-1908). Some areas near it are being heavily developed. There are metro stations: Ligongdi South on line 5 near the middle of the lake, and Ligondi West on line 3 on the SIP side.

spots.name: Take a boat ride through the city's canals
spots.desc: An interesting way to see the city low down in the network of canals.
spots.addr: Renmin Bridge

spots.name: Explore Guanqian Street
spots.desc: The street is a rather uninspiring shopping street, however the back streets off it harbor many small shops selling local crafts and some interesting restaurants serving local cuisine.

spots.name: Yangshan Hot Springs
spots.desc: A hotel resort with hot spring facilities - you can buy a ticket to soak in hot tubs outdoors. It's quite fancy, has plenty of different baths, illuminations and spas. It's in the outskirts to the west of the city, a 30-minute taxi ride away. By public transportation, take Metro Line 1 to a western station, then take a bus - consult Google Maps for details.

spots.name: Cycle
spots.desc: Suzhou is relatively flat, and once past the ring-road, traffic is light and easy-going enough to enable a pleasant ride about town. Jinji Lake, Dushu Lake and a few outlying temples are within casual cycling distance. Many hostels rent bikes for around ¥25 a day.

spots.name: Weekend cycle rides
spots.desc: Two local cycle shops — Specialized Bicycles and Trek Cycles; see below for contact information — organise one or two day rides to nearby attractions such as Lake Tai (30 km one way), Yangcheng Lake (40 km around the lake), Tongli (20 km one way) and Zhouzhuang (40 km one way). Pace is normally relaxed with regular stops for photos and taking a rest. Joining the tour is free, although…

spots.name: 长江文化节
spots.desc: An annual cultural extravaganza held in Zhangjiagang, Suzhou. It celebrates the diverse cultures along the Yangtze River basin through five main themes: cultural relics, intangible heritage, arts, travel, and openness. The festival features thematic exhibitions, a vibrant intangible cultural heritage bazaar, and electronic guidebooks for exploring riverside cities[citation:6][citation:8].
spots.addr: 主要在中国张家港市举办

spots.name: Shi Quan Jie
spots.desc: Main area downtown for tourist shopping, with everything from cheap tacky souvenirs and ¥10 allegedly silk ties to fine antiques, silks and jewellery

spots.name: Guanqian Jie
spots.desc: Mainly a general-purpose shopping street similar to what one might find in any city, but does have some upmarket shops for silks and other tourist items

spots.name: InCity Plaza
spots.desc: One of Suzhou's most popular shopping malls, with a WalMart, chain fashion stores such as Next, H&M and Uniqlo.
spots.addr: Xiandai Dadao/Sujiahang Xian

spots.name: Times Square & Modern Plaza
spots.desc: A suburban shopping area on the east side of Jinji Lake. Times Square is an open pedestrian area situated alongside a canal with many restaurants and shops, whilst Modern Plaza is a large mall selling many luxury brands. There is a Times Square stop on metro line 1. Alternately, buses 2 and 47 will get you close - get off at the International Expo Centre and walk 10 minutes to the east. Buses 219…

spots.name: Harbin Dumplings
spots.desc: The dumplings are much cheaper than the better-known Yang Yang Dumplings, and just as good.
spots.addr: Shizi Jie

spots.name: Let's Rock Hong Kong Restaurant
spots.desc: A fun, modern little restaurant with great Hong Kong/Cantonese food. Good dim sum- these folks make a serious Barbecued Pork Bun (Cha Shao Bao). The menu offers lots of quick, inexpensive dishes.
spots.addr: 403 Shi Quan St

spots.name: Nanjing Duck Noodle
spots.desc: Traditional duck noodle where the more you pay, the more body parts you get. Some of the non-duck part dishes are worth a bite too.
spots.addr: 95 GongXiang

spots.name: Xi Sheng Yuan
spots.desc: Bowls of wontons in soup (kai yang huntun) for ¥6 or wontons in a sweet sauce (ban huntun) for ¥9. Both delicious. This place is more widely known for its xiao long bao (on sale to eat in or take away) in the steamed baskets to the right of the entrance. At lunch/dinner time it gets very crowded but tables are vacated quickly. A popular light meal with locals. ¥6-9.
spots.addr: 43, Fenghuang Jie

spots.name: 葑门横街
spots.desc: A bustling, narrow market street frequented by locals, not tourists. It's the perfect place to experience authentic Suzhou life, sample seasonal foods and local snacks, and observe the daily rhythm of the city.

spots.name: Da Mario
spots.desc: Good Italian food. There really is a Mario, and he really is Italian. The pasta dish "Rosetta Della Mamma" is an original.

spots.name: Yun-Gei (Ren Ji) Cantonese Restaurant
spots.desc: A sometimes-raucous local favorite for great Cantonese food.
spots.addr: Intersection of Fenghuang Street and Shi Quan Street

spots.name: Tomato Kitchen Cafe
spots.desc: Fantastic ambience and international cuisine. Make reservations if you want a window seat.

spots.name: Rendezvous Restaurant & Lounge
spots.desc: East of Jinji Hu lake, on Jin Hu Wan business street, Rendezvous brings Western food, comfort and service to Eastern Suzhou. You can enjoy their cold beers, cocktails and snacks on their outdoor patio.
spots.addr: No. 102 Zhong Hui Lu 钟慧路

spots.name: Dusanzhen
spots.desc: One of the most famous purveyors of Suzhou-style cold braised duck. Takeaways only.
spots.addr: No. 807 Changxu Road, Gusu District

spots.name: The Southern Cross Restaurant
spots.desc: Respectable Tex-Mex food, steaks, and a wide range of Belgian ales as well as some Belgian food specialties.

spots.name: Song He Lou
spots.desc: The "Pine and Crane" is not just the most famous restaurant in town, but reputedly the oldest in all of China (about 250 years old).
spots.addr: 141 Guanqian Jie

spots.name: The Pub Bar
spots.desc: Supports a large crowd of 'expat locals' and 'repeat visitors' in it's small but friendly interior with more than ten years of photographs and business-cards pasted on the roof and walls. It's a good point to catch up on local gossip and enjoy a drink with 'expat locals'. WiFi Internet, snacks and clean toilets keep the patrons happy.
spots.addr: ShiQuan St

spots.name: Pulp Fiction Bar
spots.desc: This Australian bar is a great place to meet Westerners and English-speaking Chinese, shoot some American pool and play a game of darts. It is fairly quiet until 10PM, then it comes to life.
spots.addr: Li Gong Di bar street

spots.name: Zapata's
spots.desc: Margaritas and view over the lake. Western DJ plays happy tunes from last 4 decades and free tequila pouring on the bar every night.
spots.addr: Rainbowalk, Jinji Lake

spots.name: Blue Marlin
spots.desc: A chain of upmarket restaurant/bars with locations in several cities, with Western food, live music and a largely expat crowd. Sky Sports on multiple TV screens, comfortable seating and good Wi-Fi.
spots.addr: 168 Xinghai St, Wuzhong

spots.name: Ligongdi (李公堤)
spots.desc: Li Gong Di area has plenty of night clubs, bars and one expat-friendly club Pravda (could easily be the only one with a dance floor)

spots.name: The Bookworm
spots.desc: Good coffee and food. Free wireless Internet. Good selection of English books to read in the shop or to borrow if you get a membership. A very nice alternative to relaxing at a bar. This place has become a major focal point for the resident expat community.
spots.addr: just off ShiQuan St

spots.name: The Bookworm, 2nd location
spots.desc: Much smaller than the original Bookworm and with a more limited menu. In an interesting old building.
spots.addr: Pingjiang Road

spots.name: The Minghantang Cafe
spots.desc: In an old traditional house that is more than 400 years old. Good coffee and food. Free wireless Internet.
spots.addr: Santang St

spots.name: SoloCafe
spots.desc: Good coffee and food with a Lotus theme running right through to the shape of the milk in a mocha.
spots.addr: ShiQuan St

spots.name: Fein Coffee
spots.desc: Nice little coffee shop that serves an excellent Americano, (best I've had in Suzhou.) Outside and inside menu in both English and Chinese. Nice staff, some speak English. Very good selection of drinks including Ethiopian Yirga and oat milk lattes. Small but decent selection of food. Croissants salads and cakes. Good Wi-Fi but no toilet.
spots.addr: Remrin Lu

spots.name: Donglin Academy
spots.desc: Enjoy the Ming and Qing Dynasty architecture of this well-preserved site with gardens and classrooms of a famous school that prepared its students for the state exam. If you are in the neighborhood, it is worth the ¥5 entrance fee to visit. Attractions are a stone arch, pool, Donglin monastery, Lize Hall, Yong Tang, Oscillation Temple, promenade, Road South Temple and Donglin Temple.

spots.name: Nianhua Bay
spots.desc: Nianhua Bay is a themed town scenic area with Zen as its main theme, located to the west of the Ling Shan Scenic Area.
spots.addr: 68 Huan Shan Xi Road, Binhu District

spots.name: Jin Gui Park
spots.desc: Jin Gui Park has an area of about 48 hectares, making it one of the largest parks in the city. Every spring, especially from March to April, the park becomes an ideal spot for flower viewing, attracting a large number of tourists to admire the blooming cherry blossoms and tulips.
spots.addr: Intersection of Gonghu Avenue and Gaolang West Road, Binhu District

spots.name: Wuxi Huishan Ancient Town Scenic Area
spots.desc: A historic cultural district located at the eastern foot of Huishan Mountain in Liangxi District, Wuxi, Jiangsu, China, featuring traditional streets, historic architecture, ancestral halls, and cultural heritage sites.
spots.hours: Monday–Friday: 08:00–17:00 (last admission at 17:00) Saturday–Sunday: 08:00–17:30 (last admission at 17:30)
spots.addr: No. 18 Baoshan Street, Liangxi District, Wuxi, Jiangsu, China (approximately 50 m from Exit 6 of Huishan Ancient Town Station, Metro Line 4)

spots.name: Nanchang Street
spots.desc: The scenic area is free of charge all year round, but there is a fee for some of the amusement programs. Lockers can be rented inside, and Nanchang Street is the best part of the traditional style of the ancient canal water town.
spots.addr: No. 472, Qing Ming Bridge, Liangxi District

spots.name: Huishan Ancient Town - Yuchangyuan
spots.desc: The garden can be visited throughout the year and features seasonal flowers including azaleas, begonias and green cherry blossoms. There's a paid parking lot inside, which is about ¥10 to 15 each time, and you can enjoy the flowers inside: there are azaleas, begonias, and green cherry blossoms.
spots.addr: No. 18, Baoshan Street, Liangxi District

spots.name: Wuxi Zoo
spots.desc: The zoo has sightseeing buses and animal areas with signs to help visitors find their way around. There are animal zoning guides inside, so you don't have to worry about getting lost.
spots.addr: No.99 Qianrong Road, Binhu District

spots.name: Wuxi Sunac Land
spots.desc: There is a parking lot in the scenic area. The internal roller coaster is 1,278 meters long, with the fastest speed of 118 km/h. In addition to taking a taxi you can also arrive by subway, the subway is line 1.
spots.addr: 150 meters south of the intersection of Yuanxi Road and Wuzhu Road, Binhu District

spots.name: Wuxi Sunac Sea World
spots.desc: There are a lot of marine life inside Wuxi Rongchuang Sea World. The second phase of the project will add more than 60 species, involving more than 39 subjects such as conical tooth sharks, bearded sharks, squids, stone crabs, bullnose rays, conger eels, etc., and the overall introduction of 1,500 marine species. The interior is spectacular.
spots.addr: Ground Floor, Rongchuangmao, 150 meters south of the intersection of Yuanxi Road and Wuzhu Road, Binhu District

spots.name: Wuxi Hot Snow Miracle
spots.desc: The snow facility consists of one beginner's trail, two intermediate trails, and five magic carpets. There are coaching services, snow gear rental, etc. In addition to taking a taxi, you can also choose bus 8 to arrive, and then walk 616 meters. All the snow inside is artificial snow.
spots.addr: 2/F, Rongchuangmao, No. 66, Rongchuang Culture & Tourism City, Binhu District

spots.name: The First Ancient Town in Jiangnan
spots.desc: You need to consult the scenic spot of the ancient town, which is very large, and which was developed from the former residence of the Chinese Tai Bo.
spots.addr: About 80 meters north of Huaxia Bank (Wuxi Meicun Sub-branch), Taibo Middle Road, Xinwu District

spots.name: Turtle Head Island (Yuantouzhu)
spots.desc: A 5A level scenic spot in China, it is a good place to enjoy cherry blossoms in spring, which bloom from early March to April.
spots.addr: No.1, Soft-shelled turtle road, Binhu District

spots.name: a beautiful place
spots.desc: It boasts one of Wuxi's landmarks, with an interior featuring an 88-meter bronze Buddha statue of Sakyamuni, and a wide range of performances, both large and small, for visitors to choose from.
spots.addr: No.1, Lingshan Road, Binhu District

spots.name: Great Eastern Department Store
spots.desc: Comprehensive food center, two floors of underground parking lot, and a lot of food on the fourth floor.

spots.name: Wuxi MIXC
spots.desc: A high-end urban complex on the Lihu Lake waterfront next to the Wuxi Grand Theater, covering many world famous brands, including specialty restaurants, high-end supermarkets, a large-scale ice-skating rink, karaoke and first-class movie theaters.
spots.addr: No 88 Jinshi Road, Binhu district

spots.name: Swallow House (Wanshun Road Branch)
spots.desc: A specialty store selling bird's nest products where you can taste delicious bird's nest.
spots.addr: 86-35, Building 4, Vanke City Garden, Wanshun Road, Binhu District

spots.name: Camphor Bistro
spots.desc: A French restaurant that offers free WiFi and serves French cuisine and seafood.
spots.addr: 88 Jingshi Road, Binhu District, 1st Floor

spots.name: Sanfengqiao
spots.desc: One of the most famous purveyors of Wuxi-style braised spare ribs. Takeaways only.
spots.addr: 240 Zhongshan Rd, Chong'an District

spots.name: Lao Niu Wo Li
spots.desc: A long-established restaurant specializing in Wuxi cuisine, known for its sweet flavors. The beef stir-fried with rice cakes is the most popular dish on the menu.
spots.addr: No. 8, Nanxia Tang Cultural and Creative Park, 213 Nanxia Tang

spots.name: Xiuyuan Su-style Hotpot (Wuxi First Branch)
spots.local: 绣园苏式火锅(无锡首店)
spots.desc: A popular hotpot restaurant among young people in Wuxi, known for its signature handcrafted tomato broth.
spots.addr: 3 Hua Yuan Lane, Nanxia Tang, Qingming Bridge Subdistrict, Liangxi District

spots.name: Havana Cafe Bar Lounge
spots.desc: Latin-inspired cafe with and extensive cocktail and beer selection.
spots.addr: XianQian Jie

spots.name: Blue Bar Cafe
spots.desc: Western-owned and -managed bar/restaurant in the center of town.
spots.addr: 53 - 1 Chongning lu

spots.name: Now Og One Club
spots.desc: A club-style bar and drinks available in the evening with live entertainment.
spots.addr: No. 12-3, Yongle East Road, Nanxia Tang

spots.name: Huaihai Campaign Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A museum about the Huaihai Campaign, a major military campaign during the Chinese Civil War. The museum is in a large park.
spots.addr: 2 Jiefang Road South, Quanshan District (泉山区解放南路2号)

spots.name: Guishan Han Dynasty Tombs
spots.desc: These tombs contain the remains of Liu Zhu, the sixth ruler of the ancient principality of Chu, and his wife.
spots.price: ¥80 (Covers all attractions within the Guishan Scenic Area)
spots.addr: No. 3 Xiangwang Road North, Gulou District (鼓楼区襄王北路3号)

spots.name: Mausoleum of the Chu Prince
spots.desc: Believed to be the final resting place of Liu Wu, the third prince of the ancient principality of Chu. This is Xuzhou's own miniature version of Xi'an's Terracotta Warriors. The site features three pavilions featuring the warriors (three foot tall statues) in various states of excavation. Replicas are also sold. (Most people in the city have never seen the site and are only vaguely familiar with…
spots.price: ¥90 (Covers all attractions within the Han Culture Scenic Area)
spots.addr: 1 Bingmayong Road, Yunlong District (云龙区兵马俑路1号)

spots.name: Xuzhou Aquarium
spots.desc: This is one of the largest aquariums in Asia. It contains hundreds of different aquatic species from all around the world.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00 on normal days, 08:30-17:30 on public holidays
spots.addr: Huxin Island, Yunlong Lake, Quanshan District (徐州市泉山区云龙湖湖心岛)

spots.name: Xuzhou Botanical Gardens
spots.desc: The Xuzhou Botanical Gardens were established in 2012 on the grounds of what used to be the Xuzhou Nursery. It covers an area of around 400,000 square metres and includes hundreds of different species of plants and trees, as well as some manmade streams and waterfalls.
spots.addr: 3 Pingshan Road, Gulou District (鼓楼区平山路3号)

spots.name: Ximatai
spots.desc: The Ximatai, which literally means 'horse-training terrace', was built several centuries ago (probably during the Ming dynasty) to commemorate the warlord Xiang Yu, who is believed to have supervised horsemanship training here during the 3rd century BC. Few remnants of the original structures survived by the 1950s. Most of what you see here now is a modern reconstruction built in the 1980s.…
spots.addr: 1 Xiangwang Road, Hubu Hill, Yunlong District (云龙区户部山项王路1号)

spots.name: Xuzhou Folk Museum
spots.desc: The Xuzhou Folk Museum occupies two historic courtyard houses on Hubu Hill, including the Zhai Family Compound and the Yu Family Compound. It contains exhibitions on various aspects of everyday life in China during the Ming and Qing dynasties. The body that operates the museum also manages and maintains several other historic houses in the area, all of which are accessible to the public.
spots.addr: 2 Cuijia Lane, Hubu Hill, Yunlong District (云龙区户部山崔家巷2号)

spots.name: No.99 Bar
spots.desc: A bar in the Hubu Hill area, part of the cluster of nightlife venues on and around the pedestrian street near the hill.

spots.name: Britain Bar
spots.desc: A British-themed bar, one of several Western-styled venues in central Xuzhou.

spots.name: Hanlinyuan Museum
spots.desc: A magnificent tomb for Liu Xu, ruler of the Guangling Kingdom. It is five stories deep, with different levels housing things like a warehouse, living quarters, and a coffin on wheels.

spots.name: Tianning Temple
spots.desc: A large Buddhist temple, with multiple buildings (halls) arranged along the south-to-north axis, and landscaped courtyards between them. One of the halls stores a copy of Siku Quanshu, a Qing-era collection of all of China's important literature. Another hall has an exhibit on the history of Buddhism in Yangzhou, with information on other temples that can be visited. Elsewhere in the temple, you…
spots.addr: 丰乐上街3号

spots.name: Yangzhou Museum
spots.desc: The Yangzhou Museum has splendid displays of things like a boat salvaged from the Grand Canal that crosses through eastern China. The museum used to be housed in Tianning Temple downtown (see above), but now it is on the west side, in a new purpose-built building, known as the "Double Museum" (Shuang Bowuguan). It is "double" because the other tenant in the building is a museum of traditional…

spots.name: Shi Kefa Memorial
spots.local: 史可法纪念馆 Shǐ Kěfǎ Jìniànguǎn
spots.desc: The memorial/temple honors a Ming general who refused to surrender the city to the Qing invaders in 1645.
spots.addr: 广储门外街24号

spots.name: The Grand Canal
spots.desc: The old route of the Grand Canal runs along the southern and eastern edge of the historic center city. The new Grand Canal, with a continuous stream of cargo boats and barges, is a few kilometer east of city center, and is accessible by city bus.

spots.name: Yangzhou Shengyan · New Morning Tea · Huaiyang Cuisine (Slender West Lake Branch)
spots.desc: A restaurant serving Huaiyang cuisine and traditional Yangzhou morning tea. Located on Weiyang Road near Baodai West Gate, it offers local dishes such as crab roe dried tofu shreds, braised pork meatballs, crab roe soup dumplings, and Yangzhou fried rice. The restaurant is suitable for breakfast, lunch, and dinner, and is also used for family meals and gatherings.
spots.addr: 199 Weiyang Road, Hanjiang District (near Baodai West Gate)

spots.name: Dong Peng Kao You (Yangzhou Main Branch)
spots.desc: A barbecue restaurant serving grilled meat and Chinese dishes. It is located on Xingcheng West Road, opposite the Jiaxiang Cai Restaurant. The restaurant is suitable for casual meals with friends and family.
spots.addr: 15-12 Dexiangyuan, Xingcheng West Road, Hanjiang District

spots.name: Biyuan Tea House (Dongguan Street Branch)
spots.desc: A restaurant serving traditional Huaiyang cuisine and Yangzhou morning tea. The restaurant offers local dishes and tea-house dining. It is located on Taizhou Road, in Yangzhou Classic Business Plaza.
spots.addr: Building 1, Yangzhou Classic Business Plaza, 188 Taizhou Road, Guangling District

spots.name: Da Mao Huaiyang Restaurant (Slender West Lake Branch)
spots.desc: It specializes in Huaiyang cuisine. It serves traditional Chinese dishes and local specialties. The Slender West Lake branch is located on Shikefa Road in Meiling Subdistrict, making it a dining option for visitors exploring the area.
spots.addr: 59-3 Shikefa Road, Meiling Subdistrict, Hanjiang District

spots.name: Xiangyuan Tea House (Pishi Street Branch)
spots.desc: A traditional tea house serving Yangzhou morning tea and Huaiyang cuisine. Popular local dishes include steamed buns, dumplings, and other traditional Chinese breakfast specialties. The Pishi Street branch is located at the intersection of Xuningmen Street and Pishi Street.
spots.addr: Intersection of Xuningmen Street and Pishi Street, Guangling District

spots.name: Yuantouzhu
spots.desc: This is a park on a peninsula north of Wuxi, popular with tourists (especially Chinese) all year but especially in the spring, when it has a fine display of cherry blossoms.

spots.name: Sanshan Dao
spots.desc: These are three islands (san shan dao means "three hills islands") in the lake near Wuxi. They were once a hideout for bandits but are now a national park. Attractions include temples and statues of both Buddha and Lao Tzu, the founder of Taoism; one statue is 88 m (289 feet) tall.

spots.name: People's Square
spots.desc: What was once the horse-racing track on the edge of the British district is now a large and busy downtown park. The old track's clubhouse now houses a museum and a fine restaurant. Under the square at the edge of the park is a metro station that is one of the hubs of the Shanghai system and one of the busiest subway stations on Earth; lines 1, 2 and 8 meet there. Nearby are several large high-end…

spots.name: The Bund and the International Settlement
spots.desc: The International Settlement was built North and West of the Old City, starting in the 1840s. In colonial-period Western books, "Shanghai" means that settlement. The Bund’s waterfront complex gathers early 20th-century buildings in Neoclassical, Art Deco, Gothic and other European styles, which once hosted foreign banks, consulates and trading companies.
spots.addr: Zhongshan East 1st Road, Huangpu District

spots.name: Shikumen Buildings
spots.desc: Shikumen are unique Shanghai lane houses that blend Western terrace structures with traditional Jiangnan courtyard layouts, marked by their distinctive stone-framed gateways. For shikumen buildings, visit: * Xintiandi, an area of old shikumen houses in the former French Concession, redeveloped with shopping malls, trendy bars and restaurants, and a lot of tourism. * Tianzifang, another area of…

spots.name: Garden Villas
spots.desc: Garden villas in the former French Concession were high-end residences built mainly in the 1920s–1940s, featuring spacious plans, private gardens and modern domestic facilities. Many of these well-preserved properties are former homes of famous historical figures. Key sites are found on Wukang Road, Hengshan Road, and within the Sinan Mansions.

spots.name: Huju
spots.desc: Shanghai Opera is a national intangible cultural heritage and the most representative local opera of Shanghai. It originated from the folk songs and ditties sung by farmers on both sides of the Huangpu River in the late 19th century, and gradually developed into a formal opera as Shanghai grew into a modern city. Different from grand classical Chinese operas, Huju Opera focuses on the daily lives…

spots.name: Shanghai-style Pingtan
spots.desc: Pingtan is a traditional narrative singing art that spread from Suzhou in the mid-19th century. It is a combination of "Pinghua" (storytelling without singing) and "Tanci" (storytelling with singing). Usually, one or two artists perform on stage, accompanied by traditional Chinese musical instruments: the pipa (a four-stringed lute) and the sanxian (a three-stringed lute). Artists tell classic…

spots.name: Shanghai Pub Crawl
spots.desc: In addition to a plethora of watering holes ranging from bars, lounges, dives and world-class clubs, there is a pub crawl that arranges transportation to various popular venues. For non-Mandarin speakers or those in town for just a few days, this service takes the guesswork out of finding the hippest, most interesting spots that bustle with expatriates and locals.

spots.name: Chen Xiang Gui Lanzhou noodles
spots.desc: Lanzhou style noodles. Not halal, as you may expect; for halal food, go to Chinese Muslim Food restaurant in the T2 landside food court

spots.name: Shanghai Museum East
spots.desc: The eastern branch of the Shanghai Museum opened to the public in February 2024. It specializes in ancient art, including bronzeware, jade, ceramics and calligraphy. Visitors are required to make a booking before visiting the museum, as visitor numbers are capped at 8000 per day. Bookings can be made on the museum’s WeChat mini program.
spots.hours: 10:00-18:00, no entry after 17:00, closed on Tuesdays - except when Tue is a public holiday
spots.price: Entry is free; Chinese language audio guides are ¥20 and foreign language audio guides are ¥40
spots.addr: 1952 Shiji Avenue (世纪大道1952号)

spots.name: Shanghai Romance Park
spots.local: 上海千古情, lit. "Shanghai Eternal Love"
spots.desc: A performing arts park that combines immersive themed streets with spectacular stage shows. Its highlight is the one-hour "Romantic Show of Shanghai" main performance, which uses acrobatics, singing and dancing, and high-tech effects (including a stunning scene with 3,000 tons of water simulating the Huangpu River) to tell Shanghai's 3,000-year history from ancient fishing villages to modern Bund…
spots.addr: No. 1750, Shibo Avenue

spots.name: Shanghai Wild Animal Park
spots.desc: Shanghai Wild Animal Park is home to more than 200 species and over 10,000 rare wild animals. It offers drive-through safari areas, pedestrian zones and water adventure routes, letting visitors observe giant pandas, Siberian tigers and other animals in nature-like environments.
spots.addr: No. 178, South Sixth Highway

spots.name: Shanghai Haicheng Ocean Park
spots.desc: Theme park known for its marine life and features rides, animal exhibits, an onsite hotel, and shows. Half of the park is themed to a tundra environment, which includes a conspicuous snow-covered mountain, while the other half of the park is themed to a tropical environment, which includes an equally conspicuous volcano. The two halves are connected by a gondola lift and two large pedestrian…
spots.addr: No. 166 Yinfei Road, Nanhui New Town

spots.name: New Xiang Yang Market
spots.local: 新襄阳路市场, AP Plaza
spots.desc: It is a pretty big underground market and has many areas such as Area A, Area B, etc. They have the usual stuff including fakes of all brands of clothing, watches and handbags. See also Shanghai#Clothing.
spots.addr: Metro line 2 Science and Tech Stn

spots.name: IFC Mall
spots.desc: A mall full of luxury brands and high end restaurants, with a CitySuper supermarket in the basement offering a wide variety of expensive western and Japanese food products. There are also IFC malls in Hong Kong and Seoul; this one is run by the same Hong Kong company and is quite similar to the others, with many of the same shops as well.

spots.name: Super Brand Mall
spots.local: 正大广场; Zheng dà​ Guǎng​chǎng​
spots.desc: A very large mall full of stores and restaurants, including Uniqlo, Toys 'R' Us, and Dintaifung (鼎太丰). The top floor has an IMAX cinema.

spots.name: Decathlon (Huamu Store)
spots.desc: French outdoor equipment retailer. Offers cheap, high quality outdoor clothing, backpacks, sports equipment, gym equipment and bicycles in Western sizes. Metro: lines 2 & 7 Longyang Lu station. Another less convenient location at Jinqiao (no metro).
spots.addr: 393 Yinxiao Road

spots.name: Danieli's
spots.desc: A fine Italian restaurant, this place offers fresh, seasonal home made dishes. The five course set menu is excellent value, while the wines can be pricey. Staff are perfectly groomed and attentive to customers.
spots.addr: St. Regis, 889 Dongfang Lu

spots.name: The Grill
spots.desc: Feast on a fresh, tasty seafood platter or dig in to tender American style steak at this restaurant, which features panoramic views from the 56th floor.
spots.addr: Grand Hyatt, 88 Shiji Dadao

spots.name: Jatujak
spots.desc: Authentic Thai restaurant serving mouth watering dishes in a fantastic atmosphere.
spots.addr: Xinmei Union Towers, S Pudong Rd

spots.name: Julie's Bistro
spots.desc: Claims to be authentic Canadian food but fails to use cheese curds on poutine. Serves breakfast, steak dinner, large wine selection. A bit pricey for what you get.
spots.addr: 100 Century Ave

spots.name: Coco Ichibanya
spots.desc: International Japanese chain serving Japanese style curry rice with a vast array of ingredient choices.

spots.name: Baker & Spice
spots.desc: Western style bakery and cafe, with good quality (albeit pricey) sandwiches and other food.

spots.name: Cloud 9
spots.desc: The highest you can legally get in Shanghai, with excellent nighttime views of Shanghai (particularly if you get a seat facing Puxi). But the views come at a steep price for non-guests, who are charged ¥110 + 15% minimum per head — about the price of a drink and half a cigar. (A cheaper alternative is simply to go to the lobby (54F) and enjoy the view there. Or you can go to the lobby cafe…

spots.name: Spring Dawn at Su Causeway
spots.desc: Almost 3 km long, the Su causeway dates from the year 1189 and has a bunch of willows and peach trees. It is long north-south causeway that starts by the Shangri-La on Beishan Road and goes all the way down to Nanshan Road.

spots.name: Wind and Lotus at the Crooked Courtyard (in Summer)
spots.desc: At the west of West Lake, just in front of the Yuemiao (岳庙), in it there are a lot of shops.

spots.name: Autumn Moon over the Calm Lake
spots.desc: A traditional place to see the full moon reflected in the water.

spots.name: Lingering Snow on Broken Bridge
spots.desc: The Broken Bridge is the most elegant and romantic site in West Lake. When it is snowing, the hole of the bridge just like the bridge is broken. The classic view of West Lake seen from the Broken Bridge is quite fascinating, and the Legend of the White Snake (a famous Chinese legend which takes place here) also brings this ancient bridge much more charm of culture and history.

spots.name: Leifeng Pagoda in Evening Glow
spots.desc: The pagoda (see below for full description) is lit up at night. It is best viewed from across the lake, for example from the spot indicated here.

spots.name: Twin Peaks Piercing the Clouds
spots.desc: The view of the highest mountains north and south of the lake, which can rise above the clouds.

spots.name: Orioles Singing in the Willows
spots.desc: A large park at Qingbomen (清波门), when orioles can be heard singing.

spots.name: Three Ponds Mirroring the Moon
spots.local: Lesser Yingzhou Isle, 三潭映月 Sāntányìngyuè
spots.desc: Built in the early 1600s, this is the largest island on the lake. When there is a full moon, candles inside the pagodas are lit, and in the candle light it appears as though you see the moonlight (if you are romantic enough to see it), hence the name.

spots.name: Evening Bell Ringing on Nanping Hill
spots.desc: A powerful bell in a temple on a mountain, rung at dusk. One does not need to visit the bell, it can be heard across the lake.

spots.name: Mid-Lake Pavilion
spots.desc: Built in 1552, it is the oldest island in Hangzhou. There is an inscription by the Qing Dynasty Emperor Qianlong.

spots.name: Lord Ruan's Mound
spots.desc: An island made by piling dirt dredged from the lake 200 years ago. At night (summer), entertainment activities take place in the garden on the island.

spots.name: Hubin Parks
spots.desc: Hubin Parks 1, 3, 6, and probably the numbers in between, are the parks between Hubin Road and the West Lake. Relatively newly designed as the West Lake Tunnel that goes underneath was being built in early 2004, these parks are good to sit for a bit, buy ice cream or a newspaper, and most importantly hire a boat from the cluster of boat docks at each park.

spots.name: Bai Causeway
spots.desc: Starting at the eastern end of Beishan Road, this cause way leads to Solitary Hill and cuts off the distances between, say, Hubin Road and the Shangri La.

spots.name: Solidary Hill And Zhongshan Park
spots.desc: Where Lou Wai Lou restaurant is located, this is the only natural island on the lake. At least three emperors constructed palaces are here. Besides an expensive restaurant, the popular area is the home of the Xiling Seal-Engravers' Society, and the seals, calligraphy, engraving-masters, and relics that go along with it.

spots.name: Yanggong Causeway
spots.desc: This is more than 3 km long and one road west of the Su Causeway. It starts at the intersection of Beishan and Shuguang Road (which becomes Yanggong Causeway once you are south of this intersection); the causeway runs north-south. Yanggong Causeway includes Quyuan Garden (aka Qu Garden aka Qu Courtyard), which is the most popular spot to see tons of lotus blossoms (late spring > summer). The…

spots.name: King Qian's Memorial
spots.desc: Five kings of the Wuyue Kingdom are buried here in this memorial on the south end of the lake off Nanshan Road.

spots.name: Zhejiang West Lake Gallery
spots.desc: A famous art education and exhibition center in Zhejiang province, near the classic site of Ping Hu Qiu Yue.

spots.name: The English Corner
spots.desc: alongside the West lake is a special place for people to talk with different people in different languages. Everything could be something to talk about here, there is no difference between people and people, and people that are communicating here share their own experience, own anecdote, and own perspectives toward a specific topic. This is just somewhere for people to recreate and communicate…

spots.name: 704 project (704工程)
spots.local: Lin Biao Hangzhou Palace (林彪杭州行宮)
spots.desc: A secret military command center built by Lin Biao in April 1970, hence the name "704" project. The underground tunnels cover more than 4,000 with many heavy doors that could withstand nuclear and gas attack, and an elevator that directly reaches Lin Biao's bedroom.
spots.addr: Zhejiang Hotel, No. 278, Santaishan Road

spots.name: Baochu Pagoda
spots.desc: A stone pagoda located on Gem Hill (宝石山), just off Beishan road. You cannot climb the pagoda, but the view and surrounding Baoshi Hill are awesome.

spots.name: Baopu Taoist Temple
spots.desc: The only Taoist temple in eastern China, also located on the Gem Hill, on the north side of West Lake Scenic Area. It is a large architectural complex comprised of different themed halls. Every year, many Taoist festivals are held here, and the temple is also very popular with tourists.

spots.name: Jade Emperor Hill
spots.local: 皇山公园 Yuhuang Shan Gong Yuan
spots.desc: One of the least-visited sites in Hangzhou despite its somewhat central location. The main temple on top of the hill offers a wonderful view of the city and lake below, and has a restaurant next door. There is another temple partway up the hill. The area can provide a quiet escape and a nice hike, as well as the chance to visit one of the few Daoist sites in the area (most other local temples are…

spots.name: Yue-Wang Temple
spots.desc: A popular temple on the north-west shore of West Lake. It was originally constructed in 1221 in memory of General Yue Fei, who lost his life due to political persecution.

spots.name: Fenghuang Temple
spots.desc: One of the oldest mosques in China, the current construction at the intersection of Xihu Avenue (西湖大道) and the Central Zhongshan Road (中山中路) dating back 700 years to the Yuan dynasty.

spots.name: Longjing (Dragon Well) Tea Fields
spots.local: 龙井茶园 Long Jing Cha Yuan
spots.desc: Longjing and other tea fields further west are best visited during the harvest period, usually from the first week of March till after May Holiday, when everyone is out in the field picking tea and the tea that you can purchase is of the best quality (tea crops from later in the year have had their leaves damaged by the rain). Entrance to the fields is free of charge.

spots.name: Hangzhou Botanical Gardens
spots.desc: If you can't make it to Suzhou, these gardens aren't bad, especially in the spring and during the brief period when the leaves change in the fall. There is also a peacock farm, some nice ponds, and basically a wide range of plants and ecosystems to walk through. The redwood tree that Nixon donated during his visit has since died (in 2001). The flower nursery is also nearby.

spots.name: Xixi National Wetlands Park
spots.desc: Opened in May 2005, this wetlands park is in the extreme west part of the city past the west bus station. One of the easiest ways to get there would be to take a bus from Huanglong Soccer Stadium. While it may be somewhat out of the way and the road signs have the English translation as an uninviting "Xixi Swamp", this area is not to be missed, as there are not many tourists, and it is a great…

spots.name: Dreaming of the Tiger Spring
spots.desc: A spring as well as a scenic and historic destination. The area includes wooded pathways, streams, bamboo groves, tea houses, historic structures, as well as the spring itself and other sights. Admission is ¥15. Tea brewed with the high-quality Tiger Spring water may be purchased for about ¥20 a glass.

spots.name: Wushan Square
spots.desc: Wushan Square and Wushan Hill are major town centres in Hangzhou. The view from the top is excellent on a clear day, and there are also trails around the hills from behind the pagoda. The pagoda itself has been modernized with an elevator and nice open-air tea house at the top, but the original bell is still intact and in use. This area also features easy access to Hefang Jie shopping street at…

spots.name: Song Dynasty Town
spots.desc: A Song dynasty-themed amusement park, approximately 21 minutes from city center. It has numerous cultural performances for tourists, and has also been used as an outdoor film set for historical dramas. Located at 148 Zhijiang Road, across the bank of Qiantang River.

spots.name: Huanglong Cave
spots.desc: On the northern side of Baochu hill near the soccer stadium. This is one of the "New Ten Scenes of The West Lake".

spots.name: Liyuan
spots.desc: A famous village in Fuyang. It is the original place for paper making. The special local products of Liyuan are mao bamboo and bamboo shoot. Many people came here just want to dig some bamboo shoot. Also, there has a famous mountain named Changpu mountain. This mountain does not very huge or high but it is extremely beautiful. The bamboo with green leaves never stop swing among the wind and the…

spots.name: Qianjiang new city
spots.desc: Hangzhou's new business district, including many high rise buildings and some great modern architecture.

spots.name: Museum of Chinese Go
spots.desc: A museum about go (Chinese: 围棋 wéiqí), a classic Chinese board game. The museum is run by the Hangzhou Branch of the China Chiyuan, an umbrella organization for traditional board/card games. Information is available in both Chinese and English.
spots.addr: 1st floor, Tianyuan Building, 2 Qianchao Road, Jianggan District (江干区钱潮路2号天元大厦1层)

spots.name: Impression West Lake
spots.desc: Directed by the golden trio including Zhang Yimou, a love story performed with impressive special effects on the lake. There are two performances every night. Entertaining but not breathtaking, especially if you see some of the newer 'Impressions' shows. Starts from ¥260 with VIP and boat seats at even higher prices. Show lasts an hour and does not need language knowledge.

spots.name: Early morning bike ride
spots.desc: Start on the north side of the lake, and head west towards Zhejiang University, then down Lingyin Road past the Botanical Gardens and into Longjing Village. Keep heading West and south through the tea villages, bamboo forest, and scenic valleys to the river and cut over towards Six Harmonies Pagoda. Go back to the south end of the lake via the road right next to Six Harmonies, past the zoo…

spots.name: Hangzhou Paradise Park
spots.desc: The largest travel and leisure holiday resort in Eastern China, covering an area of 80,000 m². It is the themed recreation area of World Leisure Expo Garden. Includes the Theme Park of Holland Village, the Theme Park of Marco Polo's Tour, Ecological Garden, Niton Hot Spring Holiday Village, Conference Center, Tennis Ball Club, Golf Club, Tiancheng Residential Holdings. Here, you can feel…
spots.addr: No.92, Xianghu Road, Xiaoshan District

spots.name: World Ice Arena
spots.desc: A full Olympic size commercial ice skating rink located in the MIXC mall, new Central Business District near the Qintang River. Weekdays have unlimited skating time for the entry price. Before 17:00, price is ¥50 and after 17:30 is ¥60. Weekends are ¥70 for 2 hour sessions. All prices include the new Canadian rental skate, use of locker, and all safety gear (elbow, knee, wrist and helmets).…
spots.hours: Open 365 days a year from 10:30 to 22:00

spots.name: Car tour
spots.desc: Annoying electric cars that go full circle. For at least half the way around they will be on the same route as pedestrians and cyclists. They might politely announce you should step away but they also have a nice horn equipped and are not shy to use it. Basically ever since this tourist attraction was added walking around the lake is less fun but the tourists enjoy being carted around - it takes…

spots.name: Hangzhou Tower
spots.desc: Hangzhou's first business and tourism complex--Hangzhou Mansion Mall.
spots.addr: West Exhibition Road and North Huan Cheng Road, Xi Cheng District

spots.name: Mingjia seafood workshops
spots.desc: A famous seafood restaurant, built in 2008. Located at the intersection of Tianmushan Road and Huanghushan Road, near the Huanglong stadium. To be a modern restaurant, the decoration is comfortable. This restaurant belongs to the MIngren Mingjia food limited company, which is one of the biggest restaurants in Hangzhou.

spots.name: Lou Wai Lou
spots.desc: The most famous restaurant in Hangzhou and in existence for over 150 years, and visited by President Nixon on his first trip to China. Lou Wai Lou also has a second establishment called "Shan Wai Shan" right on the Botanical Gardens. “West Lake sweet & sour fish” is a specialty of this place, and another dish to try is the Beggar’s Chicken, wrapped in fresh lotus leaves and baked on fire. The…

spots.name: Ming Ren Ming Jia
spots.desc: Not only normal can have a delicious lunch, but also can satisfy some people‘s vanity. It has many kind of food, the characteristic of this restaurant is snake and a variety of Chinese food. There also a book shop named Bo Ku book shop near the Ming Ren Ming Jia.

spots.name: L'Amour French Restaurant
spots.desc: 87 Shu Guang Lu (on the right of youtou bar), +86 57186592191. is a French brasserie serving strictly homemade food in a Shanghaï-Belle-époque themed environment. Closed every Thursday.

spots.name: Provence
spots.desc: Is a restaurant in Hangzhou, serving fresh French and Mediterranean food. Good selection of wines, liquors and cocktails available. Weekend all day brunch.
spots.addr: 1 Baishaquan Rd

spots.name: Indian Kitchen
spots.desc: All you can eat/all you can drink buffet on Saturday & Sunday nights. ¥98, excellent service and tasty food. Serves pretty good masala dosa.
spots.addr: 63 Nanshan Rd

spots.name: Reading Tree Coffee
spots.desc: 24 hour cafe with plenty of table space, good lighting, and shelves of books.
spots.addr: No. 31-1 Qingnian Road, Shangcheng District

spots.name: JZ Club
spots.desc: One of the most sophisticated bars in Hangzhou, with live jazz performances every night and a range of beers, cocktails and wines.
spots.addr: 6 Liuying Rd

spots.name: 7 Club
spots.desc: Small local pub popular with older drinkers. Normally contains a quieter atmosphere and specializes in hard-to-find imported bottle beers. Guinness on tap.
spots.addr: Shuguang Road

spots.name: Shamrock Irish Pub
spots.desc: More a sports bar, but without the TVs. Good pub food on the menu some live music on weeknights.
spots.addr: Jiefang Rd and Jianguo Rd

spots.name: Tree House
spots.desc: A small venue which is the main hub for foreigners living in Xiaoshan district, famous for its cheap beer and outdoor seating.

spots.name: Hemudu Site
spots.desc: In the outer district of Yuyao about 90 minutes by road from down own Ningbo in the flourishing countryside. At Hemudu, archeologists discovered artifacts dating back thousands of years to prehistoric China, and there is a small but good museum with signs in English. Displayed are still playable 6-7,000-year-old bone flute, rice, plough shares, weaving, inlaid-bone and wood carvings, and jade…

spots.name: Shanglin Lake Kiln Site
spots.desc: Shanglin Lake Kiln Site is situated in the area near Shanglin Lake, Cixi City. It is a national key cultural protection unit. The celadon produced by the kiln is famous for its color and quality. Shanglin Lake is an important source and base for celadon in China. The ancient kiln from Han Dynasty to Song Dynasty number more than 100.

spots.name: Ningbo Mahjong Museum
spots.desc: It was the house of Chen Yumen (陳魚門), inventor of modern mahjong. You can see some interesting things about mahjong there.
spots.addr: 天一阁内

spots.name: Modern Art Gallery
spots.desc: A shop with paintings in various styles around the corner from the shopping area of Fuqiao Jie.
spots.addr: 60 Fuqiao Jie, 府桥街60号

spots.name: Showsy Gallery
spots.desc: Beautiful art gallery and coffee shop, original artworks at reasonable prices.
spots.addr: 69 Huayan Jie; 华严街69号

spots.name: Ningbo Ocean World
spots.desc: It is one of the most striking large-sized aquariums in China.
spots.addr: 936 Sangtian Rd, Jiangdong

spots.name: Cicheng ancient town
spots.desc: Cicheng used to be an administration center of Cixi County. As administrative division changes in middle 20th century, the town is now part of Jiangbei District, and the layout and historic details of the town is well preserved. The preservation of the town is honored Asia-Pacific Heritage Awards for Culture Heritage Conservation by UNESCO in December 2009. The most convenient way to take a tour…

spots.name: Hua'ao Stone Forest
spots.desc: Large area of coastal columnar-jointed tuff cliffs, islands, and towers, on an island in southern Xiangshan district, protected in a provincial geopark and not on the main tourist track. Spectacular and comes with a rocky beach, but only takes an hour to visit. The island is mostly natural and has a well-developed trail network accessing a variety of other natural attractions and old buildings…

spots.name: Nanxi Hot Spring
spots.desc: Nanxi Hot Spring lies in the outer district of Ninghai, Nanxi Village of Shentianchuan Township, 76 km (47 mi) to the downtown of Ninghai County. With a forest resource of 9,627 hectares, the scenic area was approved by the State Department of Forestry in 1991 as a national forest park, and thus it became one of the ten best scenic spots in Ningbo. As a well-known hot-spring resort in Zhejiang…

spots.name: Ningbo Five Dragon Pool
spots.desc: This park has a small waterfall, several hundred year old temple, and scenic hiking trails alongside the mountains. A taxi service is available for those that are not interested in hiking to the top, but want to see the mountain ranges in a convenient setting.
spots.addr: Wulongtan Scenic & Historic Site

spots.name: Songlan Mountain Beach
spots.desc: There are many such beaches along the coast of the outer district Xiangshan as well as a great many islands, while Songlan Mountain is the first major developed marine tourism scenic area and has been built into a provincial seaside resort. An on-sea activities center, Songlan Mountain City, and Provincial Sailboat Training Base and Wildlife Park have been completed. The coastal sightseeing road…

spots.name: Sun Lake
spots.desc: The yang to Moon Lake's yin, this newer park has a large lake, ponds, fountains, forest, playgrounds, and plazas.

spots.name: Tiantong National Forest Park
spots.desc: Located in Taibai Mountains, 25 km (16 mi) from Ningbo City proper, the Tiantong National Forest Park covers an area of 334 hectares, with green peaks rising one higher than the other. The park is home to nearly 1,000 species of plants, including a large number of fine tree species, such as Henry emmenopterys, ginkgo trees, Henry ormosias and Tianmu Mountain lily magnolias, in addition to some…

spots.name: Xuedou Mountain
spots.desc: Xikou Xuedou Mount Scenic Spot located in the outer district of Fenghua, labeled as the abode for immortals on the sea, is 35 km (22 mi) away from the downtown area. It is made up of Xikou town, Xuedou Mountain and Tingxia Lake. It covers an area of 85 km² and has over 60 scenic spots. To enable a better appreciation of the natural beauty of the Xuedou Mountain of Xikou, Fenghua, a sightseeing…

spots.name: ZheDong Grand Canyon
spots.desc: Huge sweeping views of lush green countryside, water runs through the canyon as you follow a rough and ready trail.
spots.addr: 315-606 China Ninghai County Baixi Village, Chakou Town

spots.name: Ningbo Delson Green World Golf Club
spots.desc: 18-hole golf course with 6 artificial lakes, par 72, 7200 yards. Visitors welcome.

spots.name: Cheng Huang Temple
spots.desc: Lots of small stalls selling mostly clothes, a great place to find cheap gifts to take back home
spots.addr: Commercial Street 城隍庙商业步行街

spots.name: Gu Lou
spots.desc: Lots of little shops selling items from artwork to knicknacks.
spots.addr: Haishu District, Fu Qiao Street 海 曙区府桥街

spots.name: Golden Centre
spots.desc: A lot of watch shops and international brands on the ground floor.
spots.addr: 279 Zhongshan Dong Lu 中山东路279号

spots.name: Metro
spots.desc: This is a wholesale store for restaurants and caterers, but shelves do stock smaller quantities of most items. In addition to food items, you can for example, buy reliable quality underwear, shoes and jackets, etc. Stock is sometimes unreliable. But given the opening hours of the store which are appropriate for caterers and restauranteurs (early in the morning to late at night) it's possible that…

Decent section of foreign foods: Walkers Shortbread, Lindt and Toblerone chocolate, olive oils, wine, etc.--even Chinese versions of Spam! More orderly grocery area than Carrefour. A CenturyMart card gets you a small discount, but not required.

spots.name: Tesco

spots.addr: 139 Zhongma Lu, Lao Waitan 老外滩中马路139号

spots.name: Spices

spots.addr: 39 Yangshan Lu, Lao Waitan

spots.addr: 320 Zhenming Lu 镇明路320号

spots.name: Inakawa

spots.addr: 79 Qianlong Lu

spots.name: Shipu Restaurant
spots.desc: (石浦大酒店). Two locations, 60 Yangyue Jie (tel:8732 8777) at Moon Lake, and 7 Gongqing Road (tel:8730 7470) at Tian Yi Square. Considered one of the best restaurants in Ningbo.

spots.name: Feast Modern Restaurant
spots.desc: 87 Huaishu Lu 槐树路87号 Probably the best Chinese decor in Ningbo. Located in a 200-year-old Qing Dynasty merchant house which has been totally renovated, the restaurant offers early twentieth century Shanghai furniture style. The dishes offered are mainly from the region but tend to be more sophisticated than the usual fare found in the city, in general it is excellent. The menu is in Chinese but…

spots.name: Legends Bar
spots.desc: One of the infamous girlie talking bars where unsuspecting tourists or business men buy rounds of drinks for the girls with the expectation of a little more change at the end of the night than they actually get. Do not run a tab and pay for the drinks as you get them.
spots.addr: 141 Leigong Xiang 雷公巷141号

spots.name: Z Rocks
spots.desc: Getting a drink is not easy as the bar staff do not speak one word of English, terrible Chinese band tries their best, often empty.
spots.addr: 43-47 Zhongma Lu, Lao Waitan 老外滩中马路43-47号

spots.name: The Garden
spots.desc: A great place when the weather is not too hot and not too cold, outdoor seating next to the river with super cheap drinks and student music makes this the choice place for students and those on an extreme budget.
spots.addr: Lao Waitan

spots.name: Harley Bar
spots.desc: Has a great feeling about the place, pool table, decent food, live music, clean American style bar. Nice, but always empty.
spots.addr: 18 Ma Yuan Rd

spots.name: Barfly
spots.desc: The young and beautiful with stacks of cash flock to this bar. Great shows here. But expensive.
spots.addr: Tian Yi Sq, No. 7 gate, 11C area, 3F 宁 波天一广场7号 门11C区3楼

spots.name: Bass Clef Bar
spots.desc: One of the better bars in Lao Waitan, a small intimate bar that is well lit with a mini stage for live music.
spots.addr: 168 Zhongma Lu, Lao Waitan 老外滩中马路168号

spots.name: Elsa's bar
spots.desc: Young yet not so local girls talk to older western business men until the early hours for increasingly expensive drinks, beware nothing else is available in these kind of talking bars, do not run a tab and pay for each drink as and when it is served and in your hand.
spots.addr: Leigong Xiang 雷公巷

spots.name: Bourbon Street
spots.desc: Latin music bar with live band that starts at 21:30. It has a superb Latin sound and feel.
spots.addr: Zhongma Lu 86 Long 5 Hao

spots.name: Shamrock Irish Pub
spots.desc: A typical Irish bar, with Guinness and a friendly bunch of visitors.
spots.addr: Zhongma Lu 72 Hao

spots.name: Red Lion Pub
spots.local: 北仑岷山路273-277号里仁花园
spots.desc: The best bar in Beilun, outdoor seating, large wine selection and German beers on tap. Very Busy on Friday nights.
spots.addr: Minshan Lu, 273-277 Hao, Beilun

spots.name: Marco Polo
spots.desc: In the outer district of Beilun, Marco Polo offers a friendly talking bar where foreign guys and local girls talk the night away.
spots.addr: Yaojiang Lu 3 Hao, Xinqi Area, Beilun

spots.name: Only Pub
spots.desc: On the busiest bar street with well over 20 bars, Only Pub is run by a tight group of young fun loving people. A simple bar with little choice but a sound start for a good night out.
spots.addr: Yaojiang Rd No 20, Beilun

spots.name: Ocean Pub
spots.local: 北仑岷山路171号里仁花园对面
spots.desc: Another small Beilun bar with attractive staff selling Erdinger for ¥25.
spots.addr: Minshan Lu, 171 Hao, Xinqi Area, Beilun

spots.name: C2 Cafe
spots.desc: Real Italian Lavazza Coffee, tables outside in the summer and smoking upstairs in the winter, the place to go to get an excellent espresso.
spots.addr: No. 115 Portman Jie, Caihong Bei Lu

spots.name: Randy's Café
spots.desc: Western style café with an extensive western and Chinese menu, coffee, juices, and a good beer selection. Western breakfasts on the weekends.
spots.addr: 82 Qian Long Rd (江东潜龙路82号)

spots.name: Club TNT
spots.desc: The top dance club for Ningbo's locals with money to burn, occasionally you can find a few foreigners. Girls dancing on podiums, live DJ's, table service, drinks by the bottle.
spots.addr: 月潮盛园街区盛园巷95号

spots.name: Yangshan Stone Buddha
spots.desc: Stone Buddha Grottoes peaks, one for the southern four stone Buddhas. Buddha, 10 meters high, the left knee fall to be shaking hands with visitors, this attitude is rare in China. Yangshan foot of the lake has Shifosi, Temple, surrounded by water on both sides of solitary backers.

spots.name: The Orchid Pavilion
spots.desc: Lanting is a famous calligrapher of the Eastern Jin Dynasty. According to legend, he once worked here to plant orchids; he set up a pavilion, hence the name Lanting. The site was built in the 27th year of Ming Jiajing (AD 1548) when the county was rebuilt by Shen Qi. It was restored to the style of Ming and Qing gardens in 1980.
spots.addr: foothills of Lancome, 13 km southwest

spots.name: Chinese Yellow Wine Museum
spots.desc: The Shaoxing Yellow Wine Museum showcases the brewing history and cultural traditions of Shaoxing yellow wine. Visitors can explore the fermentation process and enjoy wine tasting and making.

spots.name: East Lake Scenic Area
spots.desc: East Lake Scenic Area is located about six kilometers east of the ancient city of Shaoxing. Known as one of the three famous lakes in Zhejiang Province, East Lake features a unique combination of cliffs, caves, stone bridges, and water. Though small in size, its extraordinary scenery formed by unusual rocks and caves has earned it the reputation of a rare "marvel among lakes" in the tourism…

spots.name: Warehouse bridge straight street
spots.desc: Warehouse bridge straight street is one of Shaoxing's well-preserved ancient streets, showcasing the charm of Jiangnan water towns. The stone-paved road, old bridges, and traditional houses reflect the city's rich history and culture.

spots.name: Kuaiji's Mountain
spots.desc: Kuaiji Mountain, located in the southeastern part of Shaoxing, is renowned for its rich history and picturesque natural scenery. It is the burial site of Yu the Great, an ancient hero of China’s flood control efforts, with the Mausoleum of Yu situated at the mountain's base, making it a must-visit for history enthusiasts. The mountain also offers dense forests, winding hiking trails, and stunning…
spots.addr: Dayuling

spots.name: Shaoxing Downtown Theatre
spots.desc: Shaoxing Grand Theater organizes more than 100 performances every year. It has successfully received and held the 6th World Chorus Festival, the 7th China Art Festival, the Opening (closing) Show of China Yue Opera Art Festival, the 21st Golden Rooster and Hundred Flowers Film Festival and other major performances. Shaoxing Grand Theater has become a window for cultural exchanges between Shaoxing…

spots.name: Lanting Calligraphy Art Center
spots.desc: The Lanting Calligraphy Art Center is a cultural venue dedicated to preserving and promoting Chinese calligraphy. Visitors can admire classic calligraphy works, learn about its history, and enjoy the hands-on experience of creating their own calligraphy.

spots.name: Dongpu Street Antique Market
spots.desc: Ring River Night Market is a lively evening destination, with stalls along the river selling snacks, lanterns, clothing, and daily necessities. Visitors can shop for unique goods while enjoying the scenic night views of Shaoxing’s waterways, making it a vibrant cultural experience.

spots.name: Shusheng Cultural Street
spots.desc: Shusheng Cultural Street is a must-visit landmark to experience Shaoxing’s rich cultural heritage. This street features exhibitions of calligraphy, shops selling traditional Chinese writing tools, and displays on Shaoxing rice wine culture. Visitors can purchase local specialties like handcrafted calligraphy supplies, rice wine, and other souvenirs.

spots.name: Cangqiao Straight Street
spots.desc: Cangqiao Straight Street is not only a picturesque pedestrian street but also a hub for experiencing traditional Shaoxing life. Shops here sell handicrafts, traditional snacks, and the iconic black felt hat of Shaoxing. The street also hosts a small antique market where collectors might find unique treasures.

spots.name: The Lanting Scenic Area Market
spots.desc: The Lanting Scenic Area Market on the outskirts of Shaoxing centers around calligraphy culture. Visitors can buy calligraphy artworks, ink stones, brushes, and other traditional writing tools. The market also has stalls selling local specialties like Shaoxing stinky tofu and pickled goods.

spots.name: Ring River Night Market
spots.desc: Ring River Night Market is a lively evening destination, with stalls along the river selling snacks, lanterns, clothing, and daily necessities. Visitors can shop for unique goods while enjoying the scenic night views of Shaoxing’s waterways, making it a vibrant cultural experience.

spots.name: Shaoxing Decor and Home Goods Market
spots.desc: Shaoxing Decor and Home Goods Market is concentrated around Zhongxing Road, where shops specialize in lighting, furniture, and home décor, attracting visitors seeking unique items for their homes.
spots.addr: Quanxian street

spots.name: Intime Mall (Shaoxing)
spots.local: 银泰百货(聚银时代购物中心店)
spots.desc: One of the largest and most comprehensive malls in the city, offering a mix of international and local brands, along with dining and entertainment options. It’s particularly popular among families and young shoppers.

spots.name: Shimao Plaza
spots.desc: In a bustling area of Shaoxing, it has multiple floors of shopping, a cinema, and a children’s play area, making it ideal for a family day out.

spots.name: Kong Yiji Restaurant · Intangible Cultural Heritage
spots.local: 孔乙己酒家 · 非遗门店
spots.desc: This restaurant specializes in traditional Shaoxing cuisine, blending the city's rich history and culture. It is committed to preserving and innovating local intangible cultural heritage dishes, such as Shaoxing wine and stinky tofu.
spots.addr: 112 Cangqiao Zhijie

spots.name: Xianghui Lou
spots.desc: It is a restaurant specializing in authentic Hunan cuisine. The environment is comfortable, and the prices are affordable, making it popular among both locals and tourists. The restaurant is especially suitable for guests who enjoy spicy food, with generous portion sizes and quick service.
spots.addr: 244 Luxun W Rd, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Shang Ding Xian Special Noodles
spots.desc: This is a restaurant specializing in unique noodle dishes and is known for offering a variety of fresh, flavorful noodle options, made with carefully selected ingredients.
spots.addr: Yuecheng District, 62

spots.name: Zhengshifu Clay Oven Rolls Fried Bread Stick
spots.desc: This is a casual restaurant that specializes in traditional Chinese breakfast items, particularly sesame flatbreads (烧饼) and deep-fried dough sticks (油条).
spots.addr: Jinghu Rd, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Aguo Restaurant
spots.desc: This is a restaurant specializing in authentic Zhejiang cuisine. It is quite popular, and reservations are recommended in advance.
spots.addr: 15-1-5Hushan N Rd, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Ji He Wu Peng Chuan Yan (Lu Xun Store)

spots.addr: 47 Luxun Middle Rd, 47, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Xingchangjiu Vegetable Rice
spots.desc: This restaurant's menu features common Shaoxing specialties such as Drunken Chicken, dishes made with Huangjiu (yellow rice wine), and classic local appetizers that pair well with drinks.
spots.addr: 10, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Xuanermian
spots.desc: This is a restaurant that specializes in traditional Shaoxing noodles, with a focus on authentic handmade noodles paired with local Shaoxing-style snacks.
spots.addr: 192 Xinjian N Rd, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Jungle Cat Bar

spots.name: Fushan Day & Night Store

spots.name: Useless

spots.addr: 150 Pianmen St, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Zhengdian

spots.addr: 695 Jiefang S Rd, Yuecheng District

spots.name: craftbeer

spots.name: Free Coffee improv bar

spots.addr: 287 Jiefang S Rd, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Back Alley Coffee Lab

spots.addr: 4 Xiaochanfa Ln, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Youjian Coffee

spots.addr: 63 Jishan St, Yuecheng District

spots.name: South of City Coffee

spots.addr: 673 Yuecheng District

spots.name: Tuqi Coffee

spots.name: UnderTree

spots.name: Yijia Coffee

spots.name: Liuri Coffee
spots.desc: The barista asks about customers' taste preferences to recommend the right coffee beans.
spots.addr: 151 Cangqiao St, 151, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Jifang Coffee
