spots.addr: 19 Shijiachiyan, Yuecheng District

spots.name: Dongtou Islands
spots.desc: Group of islands off the coast. There is a bunch of "scenic spots"; you have to pay for some. Once there, it is probably easiest to take a taxi to the different scenic spots. Do not believe the touts that approach you when you get off the bus.
spots.addr: Dongtou District (洞头区)

spots.name: East Gate Street
spots.desc: Another pedestrian street, less to see than Wuma Street, but it is longer and has trees on it.
spots.addr: Lucheng District (鹿城区)

spots.name: Jiangxin Island
spots.desc: An island in the middle of the Oujiang river that runs through Wenzhou. The island has an old pagoda and a new pagoda, large areas of garden and lakes, a water park and a theme park. The theme park is known for its Ferris wheel which gives great views of both sides of the river and also a death-defying roller coaster. Make sure you buckle up tight.
spots.price: ¥30 (Adults), ¥15 (Children aged between 6 and 18). Children under 6 years old or less than 1.3 metres in heght are…
spots.addr: Lucheng District (鹿城区)

spots.name: Oubei
spots.desc: The town on the northern side of Ou River. Close to the dock there are some nice temples at the bottom and top of a hill. There is a pagoda on top of the hill as well.
spots.addr: Yongjia County (永嘉县)

spots.name: Wuma Street
spots.desc: Wuma Street is Wenzhou's most popular pedestrian street, known for its vibrant atmosphere and local specialties. It’s a great place to enjoy Wenzhou-style snacks, shop for unique items, and experience the city’s culture.
spots.addr: Lucheng District (鹿城区)

spots.name: Wutian Old Street
spots.desc: Wutian Old Street combines the charm of Wenzhou's traditional residential architecture with the natural beauty of the Tanghe River. The buildings use local materials, featuring grey bricks, wooden structures, and small black-tile roofs, creating a calm and historic atmosphere. Key architectural elements include wooden balconies, arcade-style facades, and intricate designs.The street is an ideal…
spots.addr: Ouhai District (瓯海区)

spots.name: Master and Apprentice Bridges
spots.desc: The most famous site in Taishun County. Two covered wooden bridges in close proximity, namely the Dongxi Bridge (东溪桥, lit. 'East River Bridge'), which dates from the MIng Dynasty and the Beijian Bridge (北间桥, lit. 'North Bridge'), which dates from the Qing Dynasty. Collectively the two bridges are known as the Shitu Bridges (师徒桥), which literally means 'Master and Apprentice Bridges' or 'Teacher…
spots.addr: Xiaqiao Village, Sixi Town, Taishun County (泰顺县泗溪镇下桥村)

spots.name: Taiping Temple
spots.desc: Really new, but very nice temple on the western edge of Wenzhou. The temple actually has a rather long history, having originally been established in 942 AD, but during the Second World War, the temple was converted into an army barracks and later demolished. The current buildings were built between 2003 and 2006.
spots.addr: 812 Lucheng Road, Lucheng District (鹿城区鹿城路812号)

spots.name: Jingshan Park
spots.local: 景山公园, Jīngshān Gōngyuán, lit. Mount Jing Park. Also known as Jingshan Forest Park 景山森林公园
spots.desc: A huge area of trees and greenery. Good place to walk around a get a view of Wenzhou. The mountain overlooks the suburb of Huanglong.
spots.addr: Ouhai District (瓯海区)

spots.name: Jiushan Park
spots.local: 九山公园; Jiǔshāngōngyuán; lit. Nine Mountain Park
spots.desc: A small but picturesque park with a lake and a brand new very high pagoda. Climb to the top for excellent views of the city, which at times can remind one of SimCity. Times refers to the pagoda.
spots.addr: Renmin West Road (人民西路; Rénmínxīlù), Lucheng District (鹿城区)

spots.name: Sanyang Wetlands
spots.desc: A group of around 136 islands with a shitton of bridges connecting them, as well as a bunch only reached by big concrete canoes. In total it is something like 13 km2. They are building a bunch of gazebos, gardens and new bridges and plan to open the garden as an attraction.
spots.addr: Ouhai District (瓯海区)

spots.name: Wenzhou Zoo
spots.desc: They have penguins, lions and the occasional panda. Good times.
spots.addr: 367 Xueshan Road, Ouhai District (瓯海区雪山路367号̠

spots.name: Double Deer Factory
spots.desc: If you are a foreigner, you can wander around the Double Deer Factory. There is some amazing machinery, such as the one that sticks on the labels. You will likely be thrown out after a little while, but it is well worth it. Try not to get your pictures deleted. If you are pretending to write an article about the brewery, then you should have business cards made beforehand.

spots.name: Pool Halls
spots.desc: There are many pool halls dotted around Wenzhou, ranging from free to ¥30/hour.

spots.name: Taxi rides
spots.desc: Taxis are cheap enough that you can just get driven around for an hour or so and not be out too many dough.

spots.name: Learn Chinese
spots.desc: As a very Chinese city it is difficult to find English speakers outside of universities, colleges and certain bars. For this reason, Wenzhou is perfect for the home learner to practice their Putonghua out on the street. Watch out for Wenzhounhua though, it sounds incredibly different from any Chinese you have ever heard before.

spots.name: Wenzhou Amusement Park
spots.desc: Financed and constructed by Sino-US joint venture company and designed by an American designer.
spots.price: ¥130 (adults and children over 1.5 metres in height), ¥70 (Men over 60 years old, women over 55 years old, children…
spots.addr: No. 12 Xia'ao Village, Chashan Town, Ouhai District (瓯海区茶山镇霞岙村12号)

spots.name: Shoes and clothing
spots.desc: You can get all kinds of cheap shoes and clothing near the train station, bring a Chinese person and you get better prices.

spots.name: Times Square
spots.desc: Everything in there is too expensive to buy, but it has clean, shiny floors excellent for sliding on.

spots.name: InTime
spots.desc: There are many boutiques selling expensive stuff. Furthermore, there is a Foodcourt at the top floor as well as an Arcade.

spots.name: Wenzhou InCity MEGA
spots.desc: Opened on November 26, 2021, Wenzhou InCity MEGA is a large-scale commercial complex that stands out for its integration with the Central Green Axis and Century Park. It offers a unique street-style shopping experience, combining shopping, dining, entertainment, and leisure, making it a key destination for modern urban consumption and a highlight of Wenzhou's efforts to become a regional consumer…
spots.addr: Located at 333 Fudong Road, Nanhu Street, Lucheng District

spots.name: Wenzhou MixC Mall
spots.local: 温州华润万象城; Wēnzhōu Huárùn Wànxiàngchéng
spots.desc: Wenzhou MixC Mall is the city’s third urban complex, featuring numerous international brands and popular dining options. It offers a modern shopping, dining, and entertainment experience, making it a prime destination for locals and visitors looking for premium leisure and retail services.
spots.addr: Located at 1999 Ouyue Avenue, Henggangtou Community, Nanbaixiang Street, Ouhai District

spots.name: Wenzhou Wuyue Plaza
spots.local: 温州吾悦广场; Wēnzhōu Wúyuè Guǎngchǎng
spots.desc: Wenzhou Wuyue Plaza is a modern commercial complex, combining shopping, dining, and entertainment under one roof. It offers a convenient and dynamic experience for both locals and visitors, making it a popular spot in Longwan District.
spots.addr: Located at 150 Shangjiang Road, Pujiang Community, Puzhou Street, Longwan District

spots.name: Computer Market
spots.desc: The computer market is three floors of technology, including desktops, laptops, notebooks, external hard drives, webcams, etc. For the best deals, make a Chinese friend before you go.
spots.addr: East Renmin Road (人民东路)

spots.name: Luggage Street
spots.desc: If you require suitcases or other baggage, there are many shops on the west side of this street specialising in Luggage.
spots.addr: East Huancheng Road (环城东路)

spots.name: Xinhua Book City
spots.desc: Wenzhou does not have a store for foreign language books. However you will find some classics as well as plenty of Chinese literature, dictionaries and teaching resources. The Book City also includes a music department, a stationery department and an arts department.
spots.addr: Gongyuan Road (公园路)

spots.name: Watson's
spots.desc: Watson's is where you can find toiletry essentials such as Shower gel (cheaper than smaller stores), sanitary towels, razors, mouthwash and even antiperspirant if you look hard enough.
spots.addr: Renmin Road

spots.name: Renmin Road Music Shop
spots.desc: If you are a musician in Wenzhou and struggling to find a music shop, have no fear as there are plenty around the city. The biggest (and easiest to find) is this one on Renmin Road and stocks guitars, keyboards, drums, and plenty more.
spots.addr: 31 Renmin Road (人民路31号)

spots.name: Bank of China Currency Exchange
spots.desc: Probably the most reliable place to buy currency is this large, official currency exchange. If you fancy taking a risk, you can seek a better rate with the money changers outside the bank.
spots.addr: 168 Renmin Road (人民路168号)

spots.name: Potatoes
spots.desc: Many "Potato-men" stake out good spots around Wenzhou and sell you potatoes.

spots.name: Muslim Noodles
spots.desc: The generic name for an extensive chain of restaurants offering bargain basement prices for solid meals from the Muslim regions of Western China including Pulled Noodles, Fried Rice, and Curries. There are at least 30 of these restaurants in the city and most have a menu on the wall which is helpful for finger-pointing foreigners. Look for the blue shop header with ‘正宗兰州拉面’ or ‘新疆牛肉拉面’. There is…

spots.name: Wenzhou Grand Restaurant Ou Cuisine Hall
spots.local: 温州大酒家瓯菜馆; Wēnzhōu Dà Jiǔjiā Ōucàiguǎn
spots.desc: A true pride of Wenzhou! With over 60 years of history, this iconic restaurant serves up authentic Ou cuisine that brings back childhood memories with every bite. The interior is beautifully decorated with cultural touches, making dining here feel like a trip to a museum—delicious and enriching.Their signature dish, Three-Silk Hammered Fish (三丝敲鱼), is a must-try. Fresh fish fillets are gently…
spots.addr: 106 Chanjie Street (蝉街106号)

spots.name: Lao Beijing
spots.local: 老北京; Lǎo Běijīng; lit. Old Beijing
spots.desc: A great place offering some northern Chinese classics. They have an English menu as well as a Chinese menu with pictures.
spots.addr: North end of Wendilu (温迪路北向 Wēndílùběixiàng)

spots.name: Rio
spots.desc: This fancy place is an excellent value if you get the coupons they generously give away. Free coffee are a godsend when combined with 50% off of many delicious meals. The Yu xiang rou si is excellent as well as a beef dish (look for the "牛肉" characters on the coupon).
spots.addr: Chezhan Street (车站大道 Chēzhàndàdào)

spots.name: India Restaurant
spots.desc: Fine Indian cuisine, possibly a little too much oil for some palettes, but a popular choice for locals and foreigners alike.
spots.addr: Nanpu Road (南浦路 Nánpǔlù)

spots.name: Arabic Restaurant
spots.desc: Friendly staff who speak enough English and a menu in passable English, Chinese and (dubious) Arabic. The curry dishes come highly recommended at the expense of the kebab dishes. If you are caught between yogurt and hummus, pick the yogurt every time as the hummus is heavily on the peanut side.

spots.name: Naples
spots.desc: A long established Italian Restaurant with an English menu and at least one member of staff that speaks English for in-house and take-away phone orders. Very solid menu selection and an ambiance that defies its Chinese location.
spots.addr: Chunhui Road (春晖路; Chūnhuīlù)

spots.name: Delizia
spots.desc: This Italian style coffee shop is worth a miss. High prices and a bad menu contribute to an uncomfortable experience. The coffee is passable but expensive and do not order the ambiguously named 'Sandwich' for ¥20; it is three slices of salami with mayonnaise slipped into bread rolls normally found amongst aeroplane food. On the upside, there are two rolls. Menu is in Italian and Chinese.
spots.addr: Renmin West Road (人民西路; Rénmínxīlù)

spots.name: Do&Me
spots.desc: Another Chinese-style fried chicken fast-food restaurant, many of them dot the city.

spots.name: Super Bee Pizza
spots.desc: The Wenzhou answer to the Western pizza chains, Super Bee Pizza has a wide menu although some choices are a little pricey. There are at least five of these restaurants throughout the city. They offer just decent pizza and not the kind of thing that satisfies a seasoned food lover.

spots.name: Bread Talk
spots.desc: There are two Bread Talks in Wenzhou, one in the downtown area near Wuma Street (五马街) and the other is in the European City shopping district (欧洲城). Eat-in or Takeaway, this bakery has a wide variety of hot and cold drinks and has breads that come closest to matching the taste of Western bakeries, including ring doughnuts and odd-looking but good-tasting Pizza.

spots.name: Sushi
spots.desc: The number of sushi restaurants in Wenzhou has exploded. There are two on Ladies' Street (女人街) near Wuma Street (五马街) with at least one more in the downtown area, and at least two in Xialv Pu (下吕浦) including the cheapest in Wenzhou (off Wendi Lu 温迪路) starting at just ¥6 a dish. A more high class sushi restaurant can be found on Wangjiang Lu (望江路) down by the river near Xicheng Lu (西城路) which has…

spots.name: McDonald's
spots.desc: There are three of the burger giant, one on Renmin Lu (人民路) near the KAITAI superstore, one in the European City shopping district (欧洲城) and one at the Olympic Stadium next to Trust Mart.

spots.name: KFC
spots.desc: The most successful western fast food chain in China can be found throughout the city on Renmin Lu (人民路) Nanpu Lu (南浦路), Wuma Street (五马街), Xicheng Lu (西城路), Chezhan Dadao (车站大道) and Xiushan Lu (秀山路). Some are busier and more likely to stare at foreigners. Nanpu is the quietest and will give the least hassle, while Renmin is the biggest and busiest (as it is near the movie theatre) with large…

spots.name: Pizza Hut
spots.desc: There are three Pizza Huts, one on Renmin Lu (人民路), one on Wuma Street (五马街) and another in the European City shopping district (欧洲城).

spots.name: Papa John's
spots.desc: The one Papa John's in Wenzhou is in the European City shopping district (欧洲城) opposite Pizza Hut. Their cheese sticks are a treat but be warned though they have every dish/pizza/noodles with pork which is frustration for non-pork eaters. There is a children's play area and it is very nice inside. Do not expect traditional American pizza menu!

spots.name: Starbucks
spots.desc: In Times Square. Get sandwiches and coffee. Wireless internet. One of the few places that you can purchase decaf coffee beans. 2nd floor good place to use your laptop or to meet friends. Food is great! Some staff know English as well.

spots.name: Wenzhou Overseas Chinese Hotel
spots.local: 温州华侨饭店; Wēnzhōu Huáqiáo Fàndiàn
spots.desc: This historic five-star hotel has been welcoming guests since the 1960s and remains a staple in Wenzhou’s hospitality scene. The sprawling layout can feel like a maze, but the attentive service and comfortable accommodations make up for it.The hotel is also famous for its Signature Steamed Jinmen Yellow Croaker (秘汁蒸金门黄鱼). Fresh Jinmen yellow croaker is lightly marinated to remove any fishiness…
spots.addr: 17 Xinhe Street (信河街17号)

spots.name: Model Lugang Banquet Fine Arts Restaurant
spots.local: 鹿港·筵·文化艺术高级餐厅; Lùgǎng·Yán·Wénhuà Yìshù Gāojí Cāntīng
spots.desc: Unlike the traditional rustic charm of other Ou cuisine venues, Model Restaurant redefines Ou cuisine with an innovative twist. Located on the top floor of Lugang Tower, this upscale dining spot presents Wenzhou’s signature dishes with the elegance and refinement of Western fine dining.While modern in presentation, the restaurant stays true to its roots, offering a unique contemporary take on Ou…
spots.addr: 25th Floor, Block A, Lugang Building, Oujiang Road (瓯江路鹿港大厦A幢25楼)

spots.name: European City
spots.desc: La Luna (Yong nan lu and Jiang bin xi lu) has the best burgers and french fries in Wenzhou. It has a foreign menu including nachos! It also has English-speaking staff. A favorite of the foreign community. Occasional karaoke or live music. Opens at 20:00. La Luna offers a foreign teacher discount card, so bring copy of contract or foreign expert papers. Discount is 50% off drinks and well worth…

spots.name: Blue Moon Bar
spots.desc: Great little foreigner friendly bar with a cozy feel to it. Customer controlled music playlist (just choose your song from the communal computer and double click!). ¥10 bottles of Qingdao. Also has burgers, fries and other Western food items.
spots.addr: Xia Lü Pu #236, Shuang Long Lu (温州市下吕浦双龙路236号)

spots.name: Cowboy Bar 1
spots.desc: The original home of the Taiwanese Cowboy, expect rowdy Chinese, migrant worker bar staff, and a wild time, especially if Eric hands you a free bottle of Tequila.
spots.addr: 66 Chunhui Road (春晖路66号; Chūnhuīlù)

spots.name: L.V.
spots.desc: Very popular Chinese bar for DJs and live music. A mug of beer will cost you ¥25, so not too pricey, and there's plenty of people to dance with.
spots.addr: 198 Shuanglong Road (双龙路198号)

spots.name: Blue Shell
spots.desc: The longtime foreign owner of Blue Shell has sold this bar to a local lady. It's still open, and John's still the bartender. Western style toilet on second floor.
spots.addr: 13 North Lane, Wendi Road (温迪路北巷13号; Wēndílù Běixiàng)

spots.name: Stephanos
spots.desc: Italian bar in the place of New Age Lounge, great open space. Western style toilet.

spots.name: My Friend Bar
spots.desc: Small bar with a very Chinese flavor, now has an open front. Staff and patrons known to be friendly to foreigners.
spots.addr: Chunhui Road (春晖路; Chūnhuīlù)

spots.name: Bund 18
spots.desc: It offers free alcohol to foreigners who know the right people. Look for other foreigners once you are inside and join them. Normally kicks off around 10PM.
spots.addr: 111 Wangjiang East Road (望江东路111号; Wàngjiāngdōnglù)

spots.name: POP
spots.local: 温州POP酒吧; Wēnzhōu POP Jiǔbā
spots.desc: Once the home to foreign dancers, now just a place where you can drink, dance, play dice.
spots.addr: 110 Wangjiang East Road (望江东路110号; Wàngjiāngdōnglù)

spots.name: Luna Bar
spots.desc: Not to be confused with La Luna near European City, this Chinese bar was renovated and often has live music.
spots.addr: 望江路

spots.name: Hello K.T.
spots.desc: A friendly bar with a barman/manager who can speak English, juggle bottles and eat fire (apparently the 2nd best barman in China, with a certificate to prove it). Upstairs is the Drunkards' Pool, a pool table so wonky you will not even need a drink to see strange things happen on it.
spots.addr: Shuomen Street (朔门街 Shuòménjiē)

spots.name: Cowboy Bar 3
spots.desc: Different from 1 & 2 in that No. 3 is a little quieter, as befits Shuomen Street. The bar area is more comfortable and a back area includes a small indoor stream. Serves Chinese food and steak.
spots.addr: 81 Shuomen Street (朔门街81号; Shuòménjiē)

spots.name: My Bar
spots.desc: Dark and quiet but with a large group of friends (10+) you can take over the bar and make it your own (should be called Your Bar). The long-haired barman (his name is DaTou, big head) has an intriguing taste in music. Drink prices are really good since they always offer buy 1 get 1 free! Always happy hour which actually makes this one of the cheapest places in town. Great music! There is also a…
spots.addr: Shuomen Street (朔门街 Shuòménjiē)

spots.desc: This bar/club is sometimes very popular for its lounge layout, a little open space for dancing, and music.
spots.addr: 117 Shuomen Street (朔门街117号; Shuòménjiē)

spots.name: 419 Bar
spots.desc: Quiet tea house and bar that also plays host to a popular English Corner (Thursday nights 7PM), even if foreigners are rare in attending. If you go, you will have insta-friends.
spots.addr: 66 Shuomen Street (朔门街66号; Shuòménjiē)

spots.desc: Huge club/bar with a wooden palatial decor that boggles the mind. Prices can also boggle the mind.
spots.addr: Renmin West Road (人民西路; Rénmínxīlù)

spots.name: U-Party
spots.desc: Large, established club with banging DJs and dancers. Not as pricey or oppressive as .99, a big group of friends could probably chip in to make the evening cost effective with a Whiskey/Ice Tea Combo.
spots.addr: Renmin West Road (人民西路; Rénmínxīlù)

spots.name: Hike the wild wall
spots.desc: Make seeing the Great Wall a personal experience by hiking an unrestored or wild section where tranquility and isolation can be found. Popular hiking routes in Beijing can be found in the Do section at Rural Beijing.

spots.name: Black Sesame Kitchen
spots.desc: Try your hand at creating a variety of Chinese dishes, from cold starters to famous noodles and dumplings. Classes are conducted in English, and you can also enjoy a fancy dinner with explanations of major flavors and the significance of different ingredients. Reservations are required.
spots.addr: 3 Black Sesame Hutong, Dongcheng District

spots.name: Beijing Cookery
spots.desc: Join a cooking class focused on Hutong cuisine, offering hands-on experiences in preparing traditional dishes. An optional market tour is available for an additional fee.

spots.name: The Hutong
spots.desc: Located in a traditional courtyard home in downtown Beijing, The Hutong offers a variety of Chinese cultural programs. Visitors can attend market tours, cooking classes (both Chinese and international), tea tastings, and traditional Chinese medicine sessions. You can also enjoy private meals, events, or simply relax on the rooftop terrace with a view of authentic hutong culture. Chefs, guides…
spots.addr: 1 Jiu Dao Wan Zhong Xiang Hutong, Dongcheng District (东城区九道湾中巷1号)

spots.name: And More Restaurant
spots.desc: A Mediterranean-style restaurant brand under Beijing Exhibition Center Group, offering Spanish, Italian and French dishes.
spots.addr: S-AR05-007~009, 5th Floor, Terminal Building

spots.name: The Dining Room
spots.desc: Shanghai-style restaurant offering noodles, wonton, Xiaolongbao, etc.
spots.addr: Domestic arrival hall, 2nd Floor, Terminal Building

spots.name: Western Mahua
spots.desc: A branch of Western Mahua Beef Noodles restaurant, a halal restaurant chain in Beijing offering Lanzhou-style beef noodle soup.
spots.addr: S-AR01-001 / S-G01-001, international arrival hall (near Airport Bus Ticket Office), 1st Floor, Terminal Building

spots.name: Outer Court
spots.desc: The imposing set of buildings designed to be the ceremonial centre of the palace. Visitors enter through Meridian Gate (A), the imposing main gate with unique protruding side wings, followed by the Gate of Supreme Harmony (F), where the Emperor sometimes held court. There are then three grand halls set on a multi-tiered marble platform, including the Hall of Supreme Harmony (G), which was the…

spots.name: Paintings and Calligraphy Gallery - Hall of Military Eminence
spots.desc: Somewhat ironically, this set of buildings (H) built to celebrate military valour now houses the Palace Museum's paintings and calligraphy gallery. Works from the Palace Museum's extensive collection are rotated through the gallery and changed every few months. To reach the Hall of Military Eminence, go through the gate on the left after the Meridian Gate but before going through the Gate of…

spots.name: Inner Palace
spots.desc: Form the Outer Court, the central section of the Inner Palace is accessed through the Gate of Heavenly Purity. The Inner Palace, like the Outer Court, is centred on three main buildings. The grandest, the Palace of Heavenly Purity (L) was designed to house the Emperor's bed chamber, but later became a throne room where the Emperor held court with his ministers. The Palace of Earthly Tranquillity…

spots.name: Clocks Gallery - Hall of Ancestral Offerings
spots.desc: Built as a shrine for making offerings to ancestors, this set of buildings on the eastern side of the Inner Palace now houses the Palace Museum's clocks display, the major portion of which are elaborate European-style mechanical clocks - including a calligraphy-writing automaton! Demonstrations are held at 11:00 and 14:00, where some of the fanciest clocks in the collections are put on show.…

spots.name: Imperial Garden
spots.desc: The Palace's main garden is among the smallest of Beijing's imperial gardens, but the emperors have managed to pack a lot of pavilions, ponds, trees and ornamental rocks into the space. It would be a nice place to relax after your tour of the Forbidden City, if it weren't packed with thousands of tourists with exactly the same idea. The Imperial Garden leads in the north to the Gate of Divine…

spots.name: Wall, moat and corner towers
spots.desc: The Forbidden City's imposing walls and tranquil moat can only be admired from outside the complex. As you leave the Forbidden City, the corner towers (E) are well worth seeing for their elaborate roof structure, modelled on mythical "ideal" pavilions in Chinese art.

spots.name: Altar of Land and Grain
spots.desc: Located west of the ceremonial way leading from Tiananmen Square to Meridian Gate in a mirrored position to the Imperial Ancestral Temple, the Emperor came to this altar to venerate the land of his empire, rather than his family. The park surrounding the temple is called Zhongshan Park. There are fewer grand buildings here, but the gardens and greenhouses are famed for their flowers, which are on…
spots.price: ¥3 (park); ¥5 (inner gardens); seasonal prices apply during flowering season

spots.name: Shopping
spots.desc: Souvenir stores and stalls of varying quality dot the Forbidden City. Many of these are overpriced tourist traps, but if you are interested in Chinese art, it can be a good place to find the Palace Museum's high-quality reproductions of paintings and other artworks from its collection.

spots.name: Clocks demonstration
spots.desc: Some of the fanciest mechanical clocks from the Imperial collection are wound up and put into action twice a day - watch them reveal their elaborate surprises.
spots.addr: Clocks gallery - Hall of Ancestral Offering

spots.name: Lai Jin Yu Xuan
spots.desc: This 100-year-old restaurant is located within Zhongshan Park, just outside the Forbidden City's walls to the south west. It was a favourite haunt of Beijing's literati in the 20th century, and is today famed for its "Red Mansion" banquet, with dishes taken from the classical Chinese novel Dreams of the Red Chamber. The Lai Jin Yu Xuan tea house is also in the same park, and is a good place to…

spots.name: Cheng Fu Yan
spots.desc: One of Beijing's famed "imperial cuisine" restaurants that also has a private dining room decorated as a replica of Chairman Mao's study, Cheng Fu Yan's odd combination of the imperial and revolutionary reflects its location - just outside the Forbidden City's south wall and faces the leadership compound of Zhongnanhai across the street. The owner's grandfather spent 22 years cooking for Chairman…
spots.addr: 38 Nanchangjie

spots.name: Forbidden City Cafe
spots.desc: After the controversial Forbidden City branch of Starbucks closed in 2007, the former Duty Room of the Nine Ministers has hosted a very similar café run by the Palace Museum. The prices are high but comparable to Starbucks prices in China, and the selection of drinks and snacks is also similar.

spots.name: Lai Jin Yu Xuan Teahouse
spots.desc: Associated with Lai Jin Yu Xuan Restaurant (see "Eat" listing above), this is a peaceful tea house within Zhongshan Park set amongst mature cypress trees, in the south west of the Forbidden City precinct outside the Forbidden City walls.
spots.addr: Inside Zhongshan Park

spots.name: Baoding Museum
spots.local: 保定博物馆, 保定市博物馆
spots.desc: The Baoding Museum is a large museum with a lot of city and Great Wall history.
spots.hours: Tue to Sun 09:00-17:00 (doors closed at 16:30), closed on Mondays
spots.addr: 1032 Qiyi East Road, Lianchi District (莲池区七一东路1032号)

spots.name: Baoding Natural History Museum
spots.desc: Opened in early 2024, this new museum is a branch of the Paleozoological Museum of China, which is based in Beijing. It is many times larger than the Beijing branch and claims to be one of the largest natural history museums in Asia. Notable items in the museum’s collection include the world’s only complete skeleton of a Chinese velociraptor and some well-preserved pterosaur eggs.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:30, closed on Mon (except when Mon is a public holiday)
spots.price: No longer free: they charge ¥40, and the only payment method accepted is WeChatPay, but there may be someone around who…
spots.addr: Southeast corner of the intersection of East 3rd Ring Road and Dongfeng East Road, Lianchi District (莲池区东三环路与东风东路交叉口东南角方向)

spots.name: Office of the Viceroy of Zhili
spots.local: 直隶总督署, Zhili Governor-General’s Office
spots.desc: Built in 1729, this was the office of the Viceroy of Zhili from the time of its construction up until the fall of the Qing Dynasty. It is considered to be the best preserved Qing-era provincial governor’s office in China and has thus become one of the most popular attractions in central Baoding.
spots.hours: 08:30-17:30 (March 16 to November 14), 09:00-17:00 (November 15 to March 15), no entry in last 30 minutes, closed on Mon
spots.addr: 301 Yuhua West Road, Lianchi District (莲池区裕华西路301号)

spots.name: Hebei University Museum
spots.desc: Visitors are required to make a booking on the museum’s WeChat account before visiting the museum.
spots.hours: Open to the general public on Saturdays only; opening hours are 09:00-11:30 in the morning and 15:00-17:00 in the…
spots.addr: Hebei University Wusi Road Campus North Side, 180 Wusi East Road, Lianchi District (莲池区五四东路180号河北大学五四路校区北院内)

spots.name: Yishui Lake
spots.desc: A man-made lake not far from the Western Qing Tombs. There is a walking path to the area's mountain top with views of the steep rock cliff.

spots.name: Taihang Water Town
spots.desc: A big reconstructed historic town near the Western Qing Tombs. It resembles Gubei Water Town in the Miyun District of Beijing. Activities include drinking a shot and smashing the bowl (from Shanxi) and buying local specialties like cigars (the tobacco leaves are grown locally). Stroll around at leisure and have a cup of coffee by the canal.

spots.name: Fuping Cat Village
spots.desc: A small rural village known for its large population of free-roaming cats. Access is mainly by self-driving, as there is only one main road leading into the village and public transport options are limited. The cats are generally calm and friendly. Many walls in the village are decorated with graffiti murals created by local residents. Visitors are not allowed to bring their own cat food; those…
spots.addr: Longquanguan Town

spots.name: Lianchi Academy Museum
spots.desc: A historic academy built in a Jiangnan-style courtyard layout, combining classical gardens, former official residences, and traditional academy spaces. In summer, the ponds filled with lotus flowers are a highlight.
spots.addr: No. 246 Yuhua West Road, Yuhua Subdistrict, Lianchi District

spots.name: Baoding Banquet Food Culture Museum
spots.desc: The museum recreates scenes of old Baoding, including traditional streets, shops, and workshops. It focuses on the food culture, history, and traditional culinary techniques of Baoding and the wider Hebei region. Visitors can sample local snacks and dishes on site, and some intangible cultural heritage activities are available, such as sugar painting and dough figurine making.
spots.addr: No. 2239 Chaoyang North Street, High-tech Zone

spots.name: Xingrui Holiday Hot Spring
spots.desc: A hot spring resort combining indoor and outdoor pools with water-based recreation. The complex has around 50–60 different hot spring pools, along with sauna facilities and a buffet restaurant. It is a popular place to relax and unwind.
spots.addr: Langwuzhuang Village, Gaolin Village Town, Xushui District

spots.name: Laolütou Donkey Burger (Intangible Cultural Heritage Branch)
spots.local: 老驴头驴肉火烧非遗店
spots.desc: A well-known local spot for donkey meat burger (lǘròu huǒshāo), popular with residents. The signature set pairs a freshly baked donkey meat burger with a bowl of tofu soup, a classic Baoding combination.
spots.addr: No. 555-2 Ruian Road, Lianchi District

spots.name: Shiji Stir-fried Pork Kidney
spots.desc: A restaurant specializing in Baoding-style dishes. The signature dish is stir-fried pork kidney, known for its slightly sweet-and-sour flavor. Another popular dish is Shiji dry-fried chicken, which is mildly numbing and spicy. A good option for trying local Baoding stir-fry cuisine.
spots.addr: Opposite Central Fengjing Block B, Yangguang South Avenue, Jingxiu District

spots.name: Baifu Beef Broth with Flatbread (Niurou Zhaobing)
spots.desc: Beef broth with flatbread is one of Baoding’s well-known local foods, made by serving sliced beef and flatbread in a rich, slow-simmered beef broth. This restaurant specializes in the dish and also offers a range of classic stir-fried dishes, making it a good choice for a full local-style meal.
spots.addr: No. 2837 Fuxing Middle Road, Jingxiu District

spots.name: Shuaifude Hot Pot
spots.desc: A traditional Beijing-style copper hot pot restaurant serving freshly sliced beef and lamb with a house-made sesame sauce. A good choice for visitors who want to try classic northern Chinese hot pot.
spots.addr: No. 481 Yonghua South Avenue, Lianchi District

spots.name: Old Nest Bar
spots.desc: A small, private bar with a vintage-style interior. Jazz music is often played, and the menu focuses on house cocktails and a selection of beers. The bar occasionally hosts a “drinking challenge,” where finishing ten cocktails within a set time qualifies for a free bill.
spots.addr: No. 204 Yuhua West Road, Yuhua Subdistrict, Lianchi District

spots.name: Chao Martini Bar
spots.desc: An American-style bar with both indoor and outdoor seating. The menu includes cocktails, whisky, and a self-serve beer selection, along with a wide range of light meals such as burgers, tacos, and pasta.
spots.addr: No. 88, Phase 3, SuSan Creative Park, Ginkgo Road, Hancun Township, Jingxiu District

spots.name: 5.2 R&B
spots.desc: A livehouse-style bar offering a range of house specialty cocktails. Live bands perform every night, making it a popular spot for music and nightlife.
spots.addr: No. 899, Chaoyang North Street, National High-Tech Zone, Hancun Township, Jingxiu District

spots.name: Shuangta Shan
spots.local: 双塔山; litt. Double Pagoda Peaks
spots.desc: These curious pagodas can be found on twin peaks in the town of Shuangta Shan (named after the peaks). The construction of these ancient pagodas remains a mystery as they are situated on top of two very steep mountains. Admission includes viewing of the peaks and hiking the surrounding area.

spots.name: Hammer (Club) Rock
spots.desc: This unusual rock formation is a hike (or ¥50 ski lift ride) up from Pule Temple (普乐寺). Admission includes entrance to Pule Temple as well as a visit to nearby Toad Rock (蛤蟆峰).

spots.name: Chengde Museum
spots.desc: Visitors are expected to make an appointment before visiting. Appointments can be made on WeChat or by phone.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: Puning Road, Shuangqiao District (双桥区普宁路)

spots.name: LTL Mandarin School Chengde
spots.desc: Offers Chinese Immersion Language Classes in Chengde with Home Stay Families.

spots.name: Ice Skating
spots.desc: During the winter there are ice skating rinks open on Wulie River. Skate rental is available, as are snacks and drinks.

spots.name: 磬锤峰星空观测
spots.desc: Join an organized stargazing session in the park, away from city light pollution. With telescopes and expert guides, explore the night sky and learn about constellations, offering a peaceful and educational retreat.
spots.addr: Qingchui Peak National Forest Park

spots.name: Daqinghua Dumpling Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant is a favorite among foreigners and Chinese alike. There are three locations in the city: Train Station, Summer Mountain Resort, and City Center (on the small street behind the two-story KFC). The menu varies slightly between branches: the City Center location has an excellent menu (in English and Chinese, with colour photos). Try the dumplings, they are unique to this restaurant.

spots.name: Beer Gardens
spots.desc: During the summer, there are a few beer gardens open next to Wulie River on Wulie Lu (south of the Summer Mountain Resort). BBQ, ice cream, and other drinks are also available.

spots.name: Zhaowangcheng Ruins Park
spots.desc: The ruins of the ancient capital of the Zhao Kingdom from the Warring States period. The site includes remains of city walls, gates, and relics from over 2,000 years ago.

spots.name: Handan Museum
spots.desc: Shows some 8,000-year-old CiZhou pottery and bronze unearthed from the Zhou Kingdom. The best thing, however, is the free admission and its central location a bit south of the CongTai Park East Gate.
spots.addr: 45 Zhonghua North Street

spots.name: Daming County
spots.desc: There is an important Muslim (Hui ethnic minority) in the Yingzhen Hui Village (营镇回族乡) in the Daming County. There are many mosques in the county, especially: * 大名县西营清真寺 or 大名县西营镇清真寺 built in 1506 * 大名县南关东街清真寺 built in 1519 * 大名县马时庄清真寺 built in 1489 * 大名县东营镇清真寺 built in 1864 * 大名县大街村清真寺 built in 1024 * 大名县七里店清真寺 built in 1956 * 大名县西杨村清真寺 built in 1948 full list.

spots.name: Handan Opera
spots.desc: Built in 2010 the building is beautiful. All the more beautiful in the evening since it is lit. In Chinese the place is named 邯郸市文化艺术中心, 邯郸文化艺术中心, 邯郸市保利大剧院, 大元宝 or 大剧院.博物馆、图书馆

spots.name: Congtai Park
spots.desc: This park in the city centre contains a lake and a small zoo. For ¥5 the Wuling Cong Tai Terrace with 2 pavilions on top can be visited. The terrace was built by King Wuling of the Zhao State.

spots.name: Zhao Park
spots.desc: A big park in the north-west of the city that has some small re-built structures to remember the old Zhao Kingdom.

spots.name: Jingniang Lake
spots.desc: An artificial Lake with many mountain trails and a suspension bridge for pedestrians. Quite popular tourist destination during summer. It is however quite a journey from Handan, with the Bus 808 to Wuan (武安) then change to another Bus up into the Mountains it takes a good 2 Hours to reach there.

spots.name: Guangfu Tai Chi Festival
spots.desc: Held every September in Guangfu Ancient City, featuring martial arts performances, competitions, and cultural parades.

spots.name: Handan Lantern Festival
spots.desc: Celebrated during the Lunar New Year with lantern displays, temple fairs, and folk dances in Congtai Park.

spots.name: Luer Garden
spots.desc: A non-powered amusement park with a range of family-friendly play facilities. The park also includes a small animal area and offers camping and barbecue spaces, making it suitable for relaxed outdoor activities.
spots.addr: Inside Zhaowangcheng Ruins Park, South Ring Road, Beizhangzhuang Town, Hanshan District

spots.name: Purple Mountain Park
spots.desc: A public park combining seasonal flower viewing and leisure activities. The park is known for large areas of pink muhly grass and Ziyun Lake, which features a small waterfall. Recreational options include fishing, horseback riding, and boating.
spots.addr: East of Hanwu Cement Plant, Xinhanwu Road, Sanling Township, Congtai District

spots.name: Handan Dao Historic and Cultural Street
spots.desc: A mixed-use district combining preserved historic buildings with newly built traditional-style architecture. The area is divided into a historic section and a reconstructed antique-style section. There are many shops and local snack stalls, making it a convenient place to buy souvenirs and local products.
spots.addr: East side of Lingxi Avenue, Congtai West Street Subdistrict, Congtai District

spots.name: 现代轻纺城
spots.desc: Big Clothes and Textile Shopping Mall were items can be bought in bulk, just south of the Bus Station.
spots.addr: 浴新大街

spots.name: Meilecheng Shopping Mall
spots.desc: A large modern shopping mall offering dining, shopping, and entertainment in one place. It has a wide range of restaurants, cafés, supermarkets, and retail stores, making it a convenient stop for meals and daily needs.
spots.addr: No. 456 Renmin East Road

spots.name: New Century Center
spots.desc: An upmarket shopping mall in central Handan, offering dining, shopping, and entertainment. It hosts a range of higher-end retail brands, including luxury goods and cosmetics, and is a good option for visitors looking for more premium shopping.
spots.addr: No. 29 Renmin Road North Avenue, about 80 m from the Zhonghua Street intersection

spots.name: Seventh Factory Cizhou Kiln Art Street
spots.desc: An art district centered on Cizhou kiln culture. The area includes cafes, ceramic homeware shops, and pottery studios offering hands-on experiences. Several antique shops are located just outside the street, and an antiques market is held every Sunday.
spots.addr: No. 2 Pengdong Street, Fengfeng Mining District

spots.name: Deyuan Workshop
spots.desc: A small shop selling Cizhou kiln ceramics. The owner is a recognized inheritor of Cizhou kiln craftsmanship, and all pieces are handmade on site. Prices are reasonable and clearly marked. Recommended for visitors interested in traditional handicrafts.
spots.addr: About 90 m south of the East Gate of the Cizhou Kiln Art Street, Fengfeng Mining District

spots.name: Donkey Meat Hotpot
spots.desc: A local specialty dish featuring tender donkey meat served in a rich herbal broth.

spots.name: Guangfu Noodles
spots.desc: Handmade noodles served with soy-based sauces and vegetables.

spots.name: Cishan Millet Cake
spots.desc: A sweet snack made with millet and brown sugar, inspired by local Neolithic farming traditions.

spots.name: Zhaodu · Ritual Banquet
spots.desc: A large-scale immersive dance and dining performance inspired by the history of the ancient Zhao State. The set menu includes nine courses, each with symbolic meaning. Guests dine as “ancient visitors” while watching staged performances based on historical stories such as Nuwa Mends the Sky, Learning to Walk in Handan, and Returning the Jade Intact to Zhao.
spots.addr: No. 149 Zhonghua North Avenue, Congtai West Subdistrict, Congtai District

spots.name: Abar
spots.desc: Good bar to drink cocktail, tea or milkshakes. Western music.
spots.addr: 广泰街

spots.name: Black Night Bar
spots.desc: A lively bar with a busy atmosphere, featuring nightly DJ sets. The menu includes a range of beers, cocktails, and simple food options. Recommended for visitors who enjoy late-night venues and a more energetic nightlife scene.
spots.addr: Room 1, 2/F, Heping Old Street, No. 202 Heping Road, Congtai District

spots.name: Lotus New Folk Music Bar
spots.desc: A traditional-style bar with a classical Chinese aesthetic. Live folk music performances are held nightly, mainly featuring ballads. Drinks include a selection of beers, and barbecue food is also available.
spots.addr: 4/F, Gome Electrical Appliances Building, No. 2 Chengnan Street, Heping Subdistrict, Congtai District

spots.name: Old Dragon Head
spots.desc: At Qinhuangdao, the Great Wall juts out into the sea. The original wall is long gone, but an extensive rebuilt section has been put up. Bus 25 will take you there for ¥1-3. To get onto the wall and into an area with several rebuilt halls, you need to buy a ticket for ¥60.

spots.name: Shanhaiguan Pass，First Pass under Heaven
spots.desc: The area between the sea and the mountains at Qinhuangdao is called the "First Pass under Heaven", being the place where the Ming dynasty Great Wall began. Guarding the pass is the city of Qinhuangdao, with its (restored) east gate marking the main road through the pass. You can see the tower guarding the gate and, depending on choice of ticket, various exhibitions or take a walk along the city…

spots.name: Shanhaiguan Fortifications
spots.desc: The walls of the old city of Qinhuangdao can essentially be considered part of the Great Wall: the whole city was built as a wall fortification to guard the pass between the mountains and the sea. The walls of Qinhuangdao are square, with a perimeter of around 4 km in length. The walls reach the height of 14 m, and are 7 meters thick. The east, south and north sides of the fortification are…

spots.name: Five Buddha Park, Jiao Shan
spots.desc: Further inland, there's a fairly extensive park near another section of the wall. Here, the wall can be seen snaking it's way over the hills. The lower part has been restored in the 1980s, you can walk up the hill about 2/3 of the way before an unrestored part of the wall has been blocked off by a concrete barrier. Next to the wall, there is a walkway towards a temple further back in the hills…

spots.name: Other Great Wall ruins
spots.desc: When heading out to Jiao Shan (above), you will see a large earth wall on the right side about 50 m from the road. This is actually a (completely unrestored) part of the Great Wall. On the barbarian side (east) you can still see the bricks and the moat, while the top and the western side are overgrown and few bricks remain. Locals can be seen herding sheep or walking their dogs on this part of…

spots.name: Great Wall Museum
spots.desc: Admission is included with some of the First Pass tickets, but it's not inside the compound.

spots.name: Park of Shrine of Emperor's Quest
spots.desc: A coastal park commemorating the legend of Qin Shi Huang searching for immortality. According to historical accounts, the emperor visited this area in 215 BC and sent expeditions into the Bohai Sea seeking the elixir of life. The site includes statues, reconstructed pavilions and seaside viewpoints.
spots.addr: No. 56 Nanshan Street, Haigang District

spots.name: Laodao Ocean Park
spots.desc: Laodao Ocean Park, with the theme of Ocean Park, is 8 km from Qinhuangdao Airport and 2 km to Old Dragon's Head Great Wall. The park offers rich and colorful entertainment items, which all bring happiness in your tour. The park breeds numerous sea animals and the sea lion, dolphin, and beluga will play brilliant performance. At the bottom of the sea, you can get zero-distance contract with wild…

spots.name: Qinhuangdao Wildlife Park
spots.desc: Located near Beidaihe Scenic Area, covering an area of about 5,000 acres, this is a large free-range wildlife park. It contains more than 150 species including tigers, lions, giraffes, and pandas. Visitors can take a sightseeing vehicle through the safari area or walk through designated animal zones.

spots.name: Nandaihe Coastal Area
spots.desc: A seaside resort area south of Beidaihe known for long beaches, summer tourism, and holiday facilities. It forms part of the broader Changli County coastline.

spots.name: Emerald Isle
spots.desc: A sandy coastal peninsula in Changli County known for its dunes, beaches, and coastal scenery. The area is part of a broader protected coastal zone and is often used for beach recreation and nature visits.

spots.name: UCCA Dune Art Museum
spots.desc: A contemporary art museum embedded in the coastal dunes of the Aranya resort development. It is part of a broader cultural and residential complex on the Changli coastline.
spots.addr: Aranya Community, Changli County (昌黎县阿那亚)

spots.name: Pu Shi
spots.desc: This is a favorite for pizza in the city. You can dine in, take out, or have it delivered straight to your door. The handmade crusts and ample toppings make this the best Chicago style pie in the city. The private rooms are classy and elegant. You will not be disappointed with the service and comfort. Watch a movie or a sports match on your own personal flat screen. If you do want some company…
spots.addr: Taiyangcheng Zhengyang Street No. 39

spots.name: Vietnam Youyou Cafe
spots.desc: The Vietnamese owner makes this the only place to go in Qinhuangdao for Vietnamese fare. The decor is refined, the owner speaks English, the food tastes just like what you’ll find in Hanoi, and the live music is a hit. The menu is pleasantly inexpensive considering the posh surroundings and classy atmosphere. It’s a great choice for a night away from the masses. Private parties large and small…
spots.addr: baojie) Sidaoqiao Nanxing 100m

spots.name: Butterfly
spots.desc: Next to People's Square, it sits in the heart of the entertainment district of the city. This is the place to go for quality cuts of meat and plump steaks. The prices are reasonable, and are on par with other western style steakhouses in China. The bar serves a full line of spirits and wines, and has a nice list of imported beers to choose from. A must visit for anyone who needs a "meat" fix.
spots.addr: Qinhuangdao Haigang District Kanglejie No. 1 (Renmin guangchang yingu xice)

spots.name: Haitianyise Hotel
spots.desc: Nestled among the rocks overlooking the ocean, this is the place to go for weekend brunch. The restaurant is connected to the Haitianyise Hotel and Seaside Resort. It’s a top pick among travelers and locals alike. The seafood buffet is always fresh and includes all the sides and drinks (including alcohol) that you care to consume. Enjoy your meal while watching the waves roll in.
spots.addr: Qinhuangdao Haigang District Dongshanjie No. 51

spots.name: Bar Lotus
spots.desc: This is a coffee shop and bar on the beach. It sells coffee during the day and alcohol at night. There are indoor seats and outdoor seats respectively. On Friday nights every week, professional massage doctors will also provide free massage services in the store.
spots.addr: No.1, East Side, Building 13, Zone 9, Anaya Tinghai Holiday Living Area, Binhai New Avenue, Changli County (滨海新大道阿那亚听海假日生活区九区13栋楼东侧1号)

spots.name: Thirteen Invitations Bistro
spots.local: 十三邀小酒馆 Shísān Yāo Xiǎojiǔguǎn
spots.desc: Located in the Aranya cultural and creative district, this small bar is associated with the Chinese interview program Thirteen Invitations. It serves whisky, classic cocktails, wine and light food. The bar has a small interior with a book-and-bar theme. It is open from 6:30 PM to 1:00 AM. The average price is around ¥140 per person, although the final cost varies depending on drinks and food…
spots.addr: No. 13-105, 9th District, Tinghai Holiday Living Area, Binhai New Avenue, Tuanlin Township, Changli County ( 团林乡滨海新大道听海假日生活区九区13-105号)

spots.name: naive
spots.desc: This is a multifunctional cultural space combining books, coffee, and cocktails. It is also a physical space for the publishing brand Ideal City and an offline experience store for Kanli Kan. The space includes a bookstore, reading area, café, bar, and hostel accommodation. The Coffee & Books area is open daily from 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM, while the Cocktails & Books area is open from 7:00 PM to…
spots.addr: 101, Building 14, Phase 6, Anaya Cultural and Creative District, Binhai New Avenue (滨海新大道阿那亚文创街区6期14栋101)

spots.name: North China Military Martyrs Cemetery
spots.desc: A large park with multiple memorials to those who fought and died in the anti-Japanese war. Notable for foreigners are the Canadian-themed memorial dedicated to Norman Bethune, and Indian-themed memorial to Dwarkanath Kotnis and other Indian doctors who assisted the Chinese.
spots.addr: Zhongshan W Rd, Qiaoxi

spots.name: People's Square and Chang'an Park
spots.desc: A park (northern portion) and a square (southern portion) connected. An underground mall is near the southern entrance (with a giant white statue of Mao Zedong). Shijiazhuang Museum is at the western side.

spots.name: Cangyan Mountain
spots.desc: Really beautiful, picture postcard temples built on the steep hillsides. There is a pavilion built on a bridge over a gorge that was filed in the final scenes of the Oscar-winning film Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon. Looking down at the Cangyan Mountains, two mountains stand facing each other from east to west, and one chain of mountains lie across their back from north to south, with the Fuqing…

spots.name: Shitou Village
spots.local: 石头村; Shítoucūn; lit. Stone Village; also known as Yujia Village (于家村; Yújiācūn)
spots.desc: A perfect example of Chinese stone architecture, with an excellent local temple (Qingliang pavilion; 清凉阁; Qīngliánggé) built in the late Ming-Early Qing period (16th-18th centuries). It may serve as an introduction to popular beliefs of the Chinese peasants.

spots.name: Niangzi Guan
spots.desc: For those who really love old towns. The dusty coalminers' town has two major attractions: a small but impressive section of the internal Great Wall, separating Shanxi from Hebei, a site of major battles from the sixth century on; and a beautiful village built on a stream, with private watermills run by many villagers (ask for Shuishangrenjia; 水上人家; Shuǐshàngrénjiā).

spots.name: Bar Angel
spots.desc: Known for its specialty drinks, classic cocktails, and non-alcoholic options, the bar also allows patrons to request custom drinks from the bartender.

spots.name: Fenghuangshan Park
spots.desc: Good views of the city can be obtained from a pagoda atop of a hill in this park.
spots.addr: Wenhua Road, Lubei District (路北区文化路)

spots.name: Kailuan National Mine Park
spots.desc: A major mining heritage park. It includes the site of China’s first mechanized coal mine as well as the starting point of the Tangxu Railway, the first railway built by Chinese people.
spots.hours: 08:30-18:00, the ticket office closes at 16:30, the park is not open on Mondays
spots.price: Standard adult tickets are ¥36 for the Kailuan Museum and ¥40 for the railway museum; various combo tickets are also…
spots.addr: 54 Xinhua East Avenue, Lunan District (路南区新华东道54号)

spots.name: Tangshan Library
spots.desc: The city's principal public cultural facility. Completed in 2015, the new building blends contemporary design with traditional Chinese academy architecture, offering a tranquil and aesthetically pleasing environment. Housing approximately 750,000 volumes, it features self-service borrowing and returning facilities, an electronic reading area, and a children's reading zone, making it ideal for…
spots.addr: No. 6 Danfeng Road, South District (河北路南区丹凤路6号)

spots.name: Anti-seismic Monument Square
spots.desc: This large public square was constructed to commemorate the 1976 Tangshan earthquake. Its imposing central monument features relief carvings depicting scenes of nationwide relief efforts. Surrounded by water features and green spaces, it provides an ideal setting for leisurely strolls and photography.
spots.addr: 102 Xinhua East Road, Lunan District (路南区新华东道102号)

spots.name: Datang Xingguo temple
spots.desc: This Tang Dynasty-inspired architectural complex features a central axis lined with principal structures including the Mountain Gate, Hall of the Heavenly Kings, and Great Hero Hall.
spots.addr: No. 18, Beixindong Road, Qiaotun Subdistrict, Lu Bei District（路北区乔屯街道北新东道18号）

spots.name: Tangshan Zoo
spots.desc: Tangshan Zoo is one of the larger zoos in the region, boasting a diverse array of animal species including pandas, lions, tigers, and various birds. The park offers a beautiful environment, making it ideal for family outings and introducing children to the wonders of wildlife.
spots.addr: Kaiyue Road, Kaiping District

spots.name: Tangshan Flower Sea
spots.desc: During spring and summer, flowers bloom profusely, creating a spectacular sea of blossoms. This location is ideal for flower viewing, photography, picnics, and leisurely walks, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in nature's beauty and tranquillity. Tangshan Flower Sea offers a tree adoption programme. Admission is ¥59 per person.
spots.addr: Kaiyue Road, Kaiping District

spots.name: Hetou Old Street
spots.desc: Hetou Old Street is an immersive cultural and tourism district that integrates culture, tourism, and entertainment. Visitors can wear Hanfu to visit, interact with NPCs to complete tasks, earn silver tickets, and use the banknotes to exchange for fruits and vegetables, cultural and creative gifts, etc. You can also watch many live-action dramas and national intangible cultural heritage…

spots.name: Tangshan Shadow Puppet Theme Park
spots.desc: A cultural theme park dedicated to Tangshan’s traditional shadow puppet art, one of the “Three Blossoms of Eastern Hebei.” Visitors can learn about the history of shadow puppetry, watch live performances, and even try hands-on activities such as operating puppets or creating simple shadow figures. It’s an engaging place for families and travelers interested in local folk culture.

spots.name: Tangshan Banquet
spots.desc: Tangshan Banquet is a highly representative cultural and tourism landmark in Tangshan. As China's first food culture museum, with a "five streets, two lanes, one river and one world" layout, it integrates catering, folk customs, culture and experience. It has become a must-see attraction with its immersive experience and rich connotations.You can not only visit folk items inside, but also taste…
spots.addr: 50 m south of the International Convention and Exhibition Center in the Nanhu Scenic Area, Lunan District

spots.name: Nanhu Lantern Festival
spots.desc: Held every year from January 22 to March 1 during the Lunar New Year at Nanhu Park, the festival features colorful lantern displays, light shows, and cultural performances.

spots.name: Tangshan International Ceramics Expo
spots.desc: This is one of the most internationally renowned festivals in Tangshan. It is held every September at the Tangshan International Convention and Exhibition Center. Tangshan is known as the "Porcelain Capital of the North". The Ceramics Expo brings together many domestic and foreign ceramic brands and works of masters. You can appreciate exquisite artistic ceramics, buy daily ceramics, and see…

spots.name: Hetou Old Street Spring Festival Lantern Fair
spots.desc: Every year during the Spring Festival (16 January to 27 February 2025), Hetou Old Street will be decorated with lanterns and colorful lanterns and Spring Festival couplets, and the lights will be brilliant at night. Visitors can enjoy traditional folk performances, taste local snacks and feel the strong Spring Festival atmosphere in Tangshan.

spots.name: Datang Hundred Plays Festival
spots.desc: A festival blending traditional opera with folk arts, featuring multiple theatrical performances, craft demonstrations and cultural experiences, ideal for immersing oneself in Tangshan's distinctive local character and cultural atmosphere.
spots.price: Most activities are free of charge, though certain special performances may incur a fee
spots.addr: Hetou Old Street

spots.name: Qianxi Pear Blossom Festival
spots.desc: Held annually in spring, typically during mid-to-late April when the pear blossoms are in full bloom. The Pear Blossom Festival centres on admiring the blossoms, combined with spring outings and local folk activities. Visitors can stroll through seas of flowers, experiencing rural scenery and the traditional festive atmosphere.
spots.addr: Qianxi County,

spots.name: Wuyue Plaza
spots.desc: A modern shopping mall offering a wide range of international and local brands, restaurants, and entertainment facilities. It’s one of Tangshan’s most popular commercial centers.
spots.addr: Intersection of Changning West Road and Xueyuan North Road, northwest corner, Lubei District

spots.name: Aegean Shopping Park
spots.desc: A stylish shopping and leisure complex combining retail, dining, and recreation. Known for its open design and frequent weekend events.
spots.addr: Southwest corner of the intersection of Beixin Road and Weiguo Road, Lubei District

spots.name: Tangshan Department Store
spots.desc: A long-established store in downtown Tangshan, selling clothing, cosmetics, and household items.
spots.addr: No. 125 Xinhua East Road, Lubei District

spots.name: Wanda Plaza
spots.desc: One of the most popular shopping malls in Tangshan, featuring international and local brands, restaurants, a cinema, and a supermarket. Located in Lubei District.
spots.addr: No. 100 Xinhua East Road, Lunan District

spots.name: Three Fishermen
spots.local: 渤海三个鱼夫蒸汽海鲜自助
spots.desc: This restaurant offers a unique dining experience where patrons can take a bucket to an aquatic market in the center of the establishment. Here, you can fill your bucket with fresh crabs, shellfish, and other seafood. Once you've made your selection, place it in a large pan in the middle of your table for steaming. The restaurant also features a section with raw salmon and tuna sashimi pieces.…
spots.price: ¥189 and ¥100 deposit in case of waste

spots.name: Chess Piece Biscuits
spots.desc: Small, round pastries shaped like chess pieces, filled with meat, sugar, or mixed fillings. Golden, crispy, and slightly sweet, they are one of Tangshan’s signature snacks.

spots.name: Lecha
spots.desc: A mung-bean pancake dish that can be fried, sautéed, or boiled. It has a soft inside and a crispy edge, with both savory and sour-sweet versions popular among locals.

spots.name: Honey Crisp Candy
spots.desc: A traditional Tangshan sweet with a 400-year history, made from honey, sesame, and osmanthus. Crispy, aromatic, and part of the city’s intangible cultural heritage.

spots.name: Chestnut Stewed Pork
spots.desc: Made with local Qianxi chestnuts and pork belly, slow-cooked until the chestnuts absorb the rich, sweet sauce — a hearty winter favorite.

spots.name: Tangshan Korean-style Noodles
spots.desc: A hot, slightly sour and spicy noodle soup inspired by Korean cold noodles, featuring a rich bone broth and chewy noodles.

spots.name: Spicy Chicken Bites
spots.desc: Sweet and mildly spicy fried chicken chunks with a thick, flavorful sauce, often enjoyed with rice.

spots.name: Small Sichuan Spicy Chicken Nuggets
spots.desc: The same model as the well-known Internet celebrity ‘Wulala’, [Little Sichuan Spicy Chicken Nuggets]. The chicken nuggets are generally sweet. In addition to the spicy chicken nuggets, there are also spicy fish and salted soybeans, which are crispy and rich.
spots.addr: No. 48 Youyi Road, Lubei District

spots.name: Jiujiu Restaurant
spots.desc: The menu at Jiujiu Restaurant is classic Tangshan home-cooked style. The dishes are generous in portions, reasonably priced, and full of the fireworks atmosphere of the market. It is a good place to experience the real food life of Tangshan locals.
spots.addr: No. 99 Xishan Road, Lubei District

spots.name: Lee’s Bar Cocktail
spots.desc: A classic Japanese-style cocktail bar opened in 2008, located on Antique Street. The interior features luxurious vintage décor and a quiet, relaxing atmosphere, with many cats in the bar. The menu offers house-made molecular cocktails as well as a variety of food dishes.
spots.addr: Building B, Shangzuo Commercial Street, Lubei District

spots.name: Folk Collection BBQ Tavern
spots.desc: In the evenings, the bar features live bands and folk acoustic performances, and guests can request songs for free. Drinks are affordable, typically a few dozen yuan per person, and the menu includes Sichuan cuisine, barbecue, and snacks.
spots.addr: Sun City, 1st Floor, Beixin West Road & Weiguo South Road Intersection

spots.name: Dajing Gate
spots.desc: A gate in the Great Wall, famous for its dangerous terrain. In ancient China, Zhangjiakou was a ghetto of several ethnic groups near the Mongolia Grassland, a place of military importance. It also plays an important part in the transportation and trade between Han and Mongolia people. The unique geographical location turns to beautiful landscape. Man of letters in ancient times were attracted to…
spots.hours: As of April 2021, the site is temporarily closed. Normal opening hours are 08:00-18:00
spots.addr: Intersection of Mingde North Road and Zhenggou Street, Qiaoxi District (桥西区明德北路与正沟街交叉口)

spots.name: Zhangjiakou Museum
spots.desc: A comprehensive museum about the city of Zhangjiakou. In the courtyard stands a monument dedicated to Chinese and allied soldiers who died during World War II.
spots.addr: 14 Dongxing Street, Qiaodong District (桥东区东兴街14号)

spots.name: Xuanhua Museum
spots.desc: Established on 18 October 2006, it is a state-owned museum affiliated to the Xuanhua District Cultural and Tourism Bureau.
spots.addr: No. 64, Xuanfu Street, Xuanhua District

spots.name: Genting Resort Secret Garden
spots.desc: Includes Genting Snow Park (云顶滑雪公园), which is one of the venues for the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics.
spots.addr: Wutong Avenue, Taizicheng, Chongli District (崇礼区太子城梧桐大道)

spots.name: Roast Lamb
spots.desc: A signature dish of northern Hebei, often served with cumin and chili.

spots.name: Youmian Wowo
spots.desc: A signature dish of Zhangjiakou made from oat flour. The dough is hand-rolled into small cone shapes and steamed until soft. It is usually eaten with a dipping sauce, minced meat, or pickled vegetables. The dish has a light nutty flavor and chewy texture, representing the hearty northern cuisine of Hebei’s mountain region.

spots.name: Pot-stewed Lamb
spots.desc: A hearty local soup made with lamb offal, ginger, and spices — especially popular in winter.

spots.name: Shang Dynasty Wall Ruins
spots.local: 商城遗址, 商都遗址公园 Shang Capital Ruins Park
spots.desc: You can see remnants of the wall in the east side of town. Be warned: these mounds are not terribly impressive.
spots.hours: Normally open 09:00-17:00. Opens at 06:00 during the first 15 days of Chinese New Year
spots.addr: Intersection of Dongda Street and Chengdong Road, Guancheng Hui District (管城回族区东大街与城东路交叉口)

spots.name: Zhengzhou Confucius Temple
spots.desc: The Zhengzhou Confucius Temple is a historical building complex dedicated to Confucius. The first temple was built here in the first century AD, and it has been rebuilt several times after being damaged or destroyed by wars and fires. The Dacheng Hall, dating from the Qing Dynasty, is the main historic building in the complex, while many of the other buildings are modern reconstructions. The…
spots.addr: 301 Dongda Street, Guancheng Hui District (管城回族区东大街301号)

spots.name: Henan Geological Museum
spots.desc: Contains rock specimens, and many fossils, including dinosaur fossils. Visitors are required to show their ID.
spots.hours: 09:00-16:30, no tickets issued after 16:00, closed on Mondays (except public holiday Mondays)
spots.addr: 18 Jinshui East Road, Zhengdong New District (郑东新区金水东路18)

spots.name: Henan Museum of Science and Technology
spots.desc: One of the largest science and technology museums in China. Before visiting the museum, visitors are expected to make a booking on the museum's WeChat account, which can be found by searching '河南省科技馆' on WeChat. The booking must be done at least two days before the day you intend to visit.
spots.price: General entry is free, movie tickets cost ¥30, entry tickets to the children's amusement park are also ¥30
spots.addr: Northeast side of intersection of Zhengkai Avenue and Yangqiao Avenue, Zhongmu County (中牟县郑开大道与杨桥大道交叉口东北侧)

spots.name: Yellow Emperor's Palace
spots.local: 黄帝宫, 云岩宫, Yunyan Palace, Yunyan Temple
spots.desc: The Yellow Emperor is the mythological ancestor of all Chinese people and is traditionally believed to have ruled over China between 2698 and 2598 BC. The 'palace' is essentially a temple dedicated to the worship of the Yellow Emperor. It was first built during the 10th century AD and has been renovated several times over the centuries. Today, the site is part of the tourist resort known as…
spots.addr: Enjoyland International Tourist Resort, Xinmi City (银基国际旅游度假区)

spots.name: Museum Area
spots.desc: One thing worth knowing about is that the museum area is also the area of the 2 branches of government - federal and communist - so the area is much nicer. We are talking trees and some flowers along with a more neighborhood feel that might remind you of Shanghai. Do not expect wild nightclubs, but it is a more pleasant place to be if you are looking for a walk. Erqilou is fine, but a bit dirty…

spots.name: Century Fun Park
spots.desc: It is quite a huge amusement park. Be aware most rides have a 90-kg limit for anyone using them, sometimes staff can be strict and refuse to let you ride even after you have paid to get in.
spots.price: ¥160 (adults), ¥80 (children between 1.2 and 1.5 metres in height), ¥50 (special price for entry after 17:00). Free…

Between 1938 and 1942, the mansion served as the Luoyang office of the Eighth Route Army, a Communist controlled group army that was created from the Red Army when the Communists and the Nationalists formed the Second United Front against Japan.
