spots.desc: Held in spring, visitors can enjoy large areas of blooming peach trees and spring scenery. The festival also features folk performances and local product fairs, allowing visitors to experience local culture and specialty goods.

spots.name: Jingzhou Lotus Festival
spots.desc: Held during the summer lotus season, visitors can take boat rides through lotus ponds, admire flowers, pick lotus seeds, and participate in photography contests and cultural performances, showcasing local water-town scenery and lotus culture.

spots.name: Jingzhou Chu Culture Festival
spots.desc: A major cultural festival promoting Chu heritage, featuring intangible cultural heritage exhibitions, academic seminars, international exchanges, public performances, and immersive experiences. The festival integrates elements such as Chu lacquer, bamboo slips, and embroidery with modern technology, highlighting both historical depth and contemporary innovation, enhancing the city's cultural…

spots.name: Wuyue Plaza
spots.desc: The plaza is a large shopping and leisure complex featuring a 100,000-square-meter shopping center and pedestrian street. It houses over 200 brands, including several first stores in Jingzhou. The venue offers public facilities such as a children's play area and nursing rooms, and provides a wide variety of dining options, including hot pot, barbecue, and local cuisine.
spots.addr: No. 109, Jianghan North Road, Shashi District

spots.name: Wanda Plaza
spots.desc: Wanda Plaza, opened in 2014, is one of the city's major urban commercial complexes. It contains a variety of retail, dining, cinema, and family entertainment facilities, with over a hundred brands including supermarkets, restaurant chains, apparel stores, and several Wanda-affiliated shops.
spots.addr: 508 West Beijing Road, Jingzhou District

spots.name: Jing Street
spots.desc: Jing Street is a cultural, commercial, and tourist district within the Jingzhou Ancient City. It features local specialties such as Songzi Du's Chicken, Gong'an Guokui, and Maozui Marinated Chicken, which can be enjoyed on-site or purchased as souvenirs. The street also has cultural and creative stalls themed around Chu and Three Kingdoms culture, offering handicrafts and souvenirs, making it a…
spots.addr: Guan Gong Memorial Park, Dongdi Street, Jingzhou District

spots.name: Jingzhou Museum Gift Shop
spots.desc: The Jingzhou Museum Gift Shop offers a wide range of cultural and creative products inspired by the museum's collections of silk, lacquerware, and bronze artifacts. Items include silk goods, ceramics, woodcrafts, jade ornaments, stationery, and accessories, such as the "Tiger Seat and Bird Drum" mini figurine, canvas bags featuring Chu-style patterns, and milk tea cups modeled after Warring…
spots.addr: F1, Treasures Hall, Jingzhou Museum, 166 Jingzhou Middle Road, Jingzhou District

spots.name: Chuxiang Youli Flagship Store
spots.desc: The Chuxiang Youli Flagship Store is a regional brand venue that showcases local culture and specialty goods. Located in a restored Qing-era building, it combines traditional architectural elements with modern retail displays. The store includes cultural and creative exhibition areas, heritage workshops, and experiential spaces. Its products span clothing, food items, daily-use goods…
spots.addr: 38 Nanmen Street, Jingzhou District

spots.name: Shashi Wharf Cultural and Creative Park
spots.desc: Shashi Wharf Cultural and Creative Park is a commercial and leisure area converted from former factory buildings. The Brilliant Outlet Shopping Park features brand outlets, trend shops, and local designer labels. The Grain Warehouse Art Space offers Jingchu-themed cultural and creative products, including original character merchandise, embroidered scarves, and canvas bags. The park emphasizes…
spots.addr: No. 55 Jingdi Road, Shengli Subdistrict, Shashi District

spots.name: Zhang Youcai BBQ Stall
spots.desc: A late-night establishment specializing in charcoal-grilled dishes and claypot stews. Notable items include fire-grilled beef and claypot beef prepared with duck or goose feet, reflecting a common local late-night dining format.
spots.addr: 120 meters east of the intersection of Gongnong Road and Huajian Road, Chongwen Subdistrict

spots.name: Jingzhou Crayfish King (Xintiandi Branch)
spots.desc: Focuses on crayfish dishes such as oil-braised shrimp, steamed shrimp, and shrimp balls, highlighting local crayfish cuisine. It becomes busy during peak seasons, with a menu centered on various crayfish preparations.
spots.addr: Building 9, Unit 105, Xintiandi

spots.name: Xiyuan Noodle House
spots.desc: A long-running breakfast shop with over forty years of history, known for Zaotang noodles and Dalian noodles. Offers toppings such as pork, beef, chicken, and shredded eel. The environment retains traditional features typical of local breakfast places.
spots.addr: No. 1 Gongnong Road, Shashi District

spots.name: Huangjiatang Rice Noodles (Main Store)
spots.desc: Serves smooth, elastic rice noodles in slow-simmered beef bone broth, with options including braised beef, offal, or intestines, reflecting traditional rice noodle practices and local flavors.
spots.addr: Building 3, Huangjiatang, Beijing Middle Road, Zhongshan Subdistrict (directly opposite Huangjiatang Primary School)

spots.name: Grandma’s Hometown (Ancient City Branch)
spots.desc: Offers Jingchu-style home cooking using local ingredients, with dishes such as fish cake and stuffed lotus root, centered on regional household cuisine.
spots.addr: No. 18 Jingnan Road

spots.name: Cowherd Folk Cuisine Restaurant (Jingnan Road)
spots.local: 放牛娃民俗土菜馆 (荆南路店)
spots.desc: Specializes in rural-style dishes with large portions, featuring items such as braised beef brisket with bamboo shoots, spicy yellow catfish, and Hakka tofu, representing local rural food traditions.
spots.addr: 2nd Floor, Workers'Cultural Palace, Jingzhou South Road (near the main entrance)

spots.name: Minjian Kitchen – Private Home Cuisine:
spots.desc: A small restaurant serving homestyle dishes, featuring a rotating blackboard menu. Notable items include rabbit hot pot with crispy yam, dry-fried cabbage, spicy mandarin fish, and salted egg yolk pumpkin. The menu reflects everyday homemade cooking.
spots.addr: Building 16, Jinlong Community, Daqing Road

spots.name: Laojie Fang Restaurant
spots.desc: An established restaurant offering Jingzhou home-style dishes such as fish cake, stuffed lotus root, braised tofu sheets with pork, and stir-fried dishes. Ingredients are sourced locally, and seasonal items—like lotus seed soup in summer and pork rib lotus root soup in winter—are part of the rotating menu.
spots.addr: No. 14 Zhangjuzheng St

spots.name: Wuyi Road
spots.desc: Wuyi Road in Jingzhou is a food street with many eateries operating throughout the day. Common offerings include rice noodles, liangxia jelly, pan-fried dumplings, hot pot and marinated dishes. Most vendors use traditional local preparation methods.
spots.addr: About 80 meters west of Wuyi Art Kindergarten, Wuyi Road, Shashi District

spots.name: Dasaixiang Alley
spots.desc: A historic alley dating back to the Yuan dynasty and renamed during the Ming dynasty. It now functions primarily as a dining area with numerous restaurants and food stalls offering Jingzhou-style cuisine. Many items are prepared using traditional methods.
spots.addr: Intersection of Dasaixiang Alley and Beijing Middle Road, Shashi District

spots.name: Swallow Liangxia
spots.desc: Swallow Liangxia has over 30 years of history, following traditional preparation methods. The liangxia grains are large-headed and small-tailed, soft with slight chewiness, typically served in cold syrup with mint. The shop also offers lotus root starch drinks with apple pieces. It is a commonly consumed summer beverage in the Jingzhou area.
spots.addr: Opposite Haoweidao on Jiefang Road

spots.name: Liangshuiji
spots.desc: Liangshuiji is a liangxia shop that uses rice to make handmade liangxia, prepared fresh daily. The grains are plump, soft, and slightly sweet, and can be served with syrup or osmanthus flavor for a refreshing taste. The shop also offers lianggao and other desserts.
spots.addr: 17-3 Wenhua Gong Road, Shashi District

spots.name: Zhezhe Miniang (Sweet fermented rice)
spots.desc: Zhezhe Miniang is a shop producing handmade fermented rice drinks made with glutinous rice and ingredients such as rose and osmanthus. The drinks have a mild sweetness and light aroma with a slight alcoholic taste. Both traditional and floral versions are available, along with simple snacks and tea.
spots.addr: Outside Fuyi Yayuan Community, Jianghan North Road

spots.name: Ruguo
spots.desc: Ruguo is a fruit tea brand originating from Jingzhou, founded in 2013 and later developed into a fresh fruit tea chain. spots.addr: Longquanyi District, in Qinglonghu wetland park

spots.name: Shuijingfang Museum
spots.desc: Shuijingfang is a liquor company that specializes in the production of high-quality baijiu (distilled rice wine). The company has been operating continuously in Chengdu for over 600 years, albeit under many different names. Around the turn of the last century, archaeologists uncovered the remains of the original distillery that was in use 600 years ago. As the oldest distillery site yet…
spots.addr: 19 Shuijing Street, Jinjiang District (锦江区水井街19号)

spots.name: Qingyang Temple
spots.local: 青羊宫; Qingyanggong; lit. Palace of the Black, Green or Blue Ram
spots.desc: This Taoist temple is the oldest and biggest of its kind in the area, located in the west of downtown. A large and still-active temple that takes into consideration Taoist philosophy in its construction, and with both a park next door and a number of relaxed courtyards inside. While it has a long history, the buildings are modern, cheaply-made concrete constructions, and it quite frequently…
spots.addr: 9 Xierduan, Ring Rd One, Qingyang District (青羊区一环路西二段9号)

spots.name: Huanglongxi Ancient Town
spots.desc: The core area of Huanglongxi Ancient Town preserves Ming and Qing dynasty residences, ancient temples, and key cultural relics, covering approximately 31,200 square meters, with 13,700 square meters of Qing-era wooden structures. The town has rich folk culture, including traditions such as the Fire Dragon Festival and floating river lanterns. It has been designated a Sichuan Provincial Scenic…
spots.addr: Shuangliu District

spots.name: Anren Ancient Town
spots.local: 安仁古镇; ān rén gǔ zhèn
spots.desc: Also called China's Museum Town (中国博物馆小镇) due to the large number of museums, including the Jianchuan Museum Cluster (see below).The entire scenic area west to Liu Xiang riding statue, east to the Convention and Exhibition Road, north to the road around the town, south to the Xiejiang River, the core scenic area of 3 square kilometers, including the old street of the Gongguan, Liu's Manor Museum…
spots.price: Free (Tickets are required for the museums)
spots.addr: Dayi County (大邑县)

spots.name: Jiezi ancient town
spots.desc: 25 km northwest of Chengdu, in Chongzhou, the Fengqi mountain, the mountain connected with Qingcheng.

spots.name: Liujiang Old Town
spots.desc: Liujiang town, located 25 km southwest of the county to spend Hongya River tributary of Liujiang sides. Town was founded in the Southern Song Dynasty, and modern architecture across the water from the Ming and Qing era buildings.

spots.name: Jianchuan Museum Cluster
spots.desc: Industrialist Fan Jianchuan built this campus of museums to explain the history of 20th century China. This is the first privately owned museum in Sichuan (privately operated museums in China have only been permitted since the year 2001). The Museum campus contains four buildings about World War II in China - one explaining the Communist Party role, one about the Kuomintang, one about the…
spots.price: ¥60 for a one-day pass to visit all museums, ¥100 for a three-day pass, ¥20 to visit just one museum
spots.addr: 550 Yingbin Road Section Two, Anren Town, Dayi County (大邑县安仁镇迎宾路二段550)

spots.name: Cosmetics and Hair
spots.desc: Local women love to get their nails and hair done at the mall. You can get your nails done beautifully (filed, buffered, polished and hand painted with beautiful patent) between ¥10-20 at most shopping centre. There are quite a few very popular ones located on the ground floor of Beijing Hualian (北京华联) in Yanshikou. You can also get your hair temporarily straightened or curled at ¥10-15.…

spots.name: Chunxi Road
spots.desc: Take an afternoon or evening to walk down this shopping street in the center of the city. It makes for a good change of pace. There are clothing stores, bookstores, restaurants, arcades, and cinemas. It is a good place to find something to eat, as you can find a great variety including hotpot buffets, Japanese restaurants and Western food. However, the major disadvantage with this area is that…

spots.name: Drink tea
spots.desc: Teahouses are plentiful in Chengdu, and drinking tea and playing Mahjong is how many local people relax. On a sunny afternoon pick a table in the park with an out-door tea house and sip your tea while listening to the locals gossiping. Not for the faint hearted, take the opportunity to have your ears cleaned by local "experts" armed with a tuning fork and a myriad of "insertion tools". Weird but…
spots.addr: Renmin Park (People's Park)

spots.name: Foot and body Massage
spots.desc: Chengdu is famous for its relaxed and laid back lifestyle. The foot and body massage is very popular in Chengdu with a lot of varieties. Generally, these places cater to groups of people who come in together, relax in a private room, perhaps eating fruit, pig ear, or sipping tea, while receiving a fully-clothed massage or foot washing. Prices are very reasonable, often well under ¥80 per…

spots.name: 成都漆器工艺体验工坊
spots.desc: A workshop where you can learn about the intricate art of Chengdu lacquerware, a national intangible cultural heritage. Under master guidance, you can try your hand at polishing or painting a small piece, creating a unique souvenir.
spots.addr: Qingyang District

spots.name: KTV
spots.desc: Spend an evening singing with friends, enjoy popcorn, beer and other refreshments. Songs available in English, Chinese, and more.
spots.addr: various locations

spots.name: Read a Book
spots.desc: The Chengdu Bookworm (see listing in the Eat Section) has a membership-based lending library of English language books, as well as travel guides for sale. Peter's Tex Mex, as well as some of the other restaurants that cater to foreigners, have book exchanges.

spots.name: Sichuan Opera
spots.desc: Most guest houses and travel agencies offer to arrange visits to these traditional shows. It is more like a burlesque cabaret than an actual opera, sometimes including magicians, traditional musicians, shadow plays, comedy (spoken in Chinese though), and dancers besides the traditional pieces. Of course the most famous is never omitted: quick face-changing and fire spitting performed by dancers…
spots.price: The price is not fixed, depending on the program on that day

spots.name: Floraland
spots.desc: The park includes a moderate selection of rides (water, relaxing and thrill), and various recreation activities. Weekends can get packed, so try to go during a weekday.
spots.price: Water park: ¥150; Land park: ¥30 (entry only), ¥130 (including rides)
spots.addr: Wanchun Town, Wenjiang District (温江区万春镇)

spots.name: Grand Hill International Golf Club
spots.desc: 18-hole championship golf course completed in 2009. Somewhat generic but pleasant.
spots.addr: 1188 Qiling Road, Jintang District

spots.name: Luxehills Golf and Country Club
spots.desc: Completed in 2007 by American architect firm JMP, Luxehills is ranked one of the top 10 courses in China.

spots.name: Wolong Valley The Tradition Golf Club
spots.local: 臥龍谷傳統高爾夫球埸
spots.desc: 18-hole championship course with many bunkers and well protected greens. On three sides of the course, tall high-rise condominium buildings are easily visible.
spots.addr: No.1 Wolong Avenue, Longquanyi District

spots.name: Chunxi Road area
spots.desc: A street and a contiguous shopping district. More than 700 shops in the area including shopping malls, department stores, boutiques and street stalls.

spots.name: Songxian Qiao Antique Market
spots.desc: Big market with communist relics, old porcelain dishes, jewellery, calligraphy equipment and also some Tibetan stuff. Great bargains can be found here if you are into antiques, jewellery, and gifts.
spots.addr: Qing Yang District, Song Xian Bridge

spots.name: Lotus Wholesale Market
spots.desc: A huge area of shops selling all kinds of local stuff from clothes to kitchen ware and home decoration to toys. The area employs over 100,000 people and its daily sales are over ¥10 million.

spots.name: Wuhou Tibetan Area shops
spots.desc: About two blocks of shops adjacent to Wuhou Temple selling clothing, textiles, jewelry, Tibetan music etc.

spots.name: Panda Toys
spots.desc: All sorts of plush pandas, and other panda trinkets, are sold at the gate of the panda base, as well as ones of a slightly higher quality at the shop inside the panda base itself.

spots.name: Galleria
spots.desc: New international standard shopping mall with about 200 stores and naturally a lot of international brands.

spots.name: Sabrina's Country Store
spots.desc: If you want to buy American food, and do not mind a 50% premium, this has friendly service and all imported products.
spots.addr: 54 Kehua N Rd

spots.name: Chengdu SKP
spots.desc: Chengdu SKP is a large shopping mall with many brands, including luxury goods. There are also many restaurants inside for shopping customers to choose from. What’s interesting is that the architecture and interior design of this large shopping mall show modernity and creativity. There are squares and fountains on the ground, and the shopping mall is underground.
spots.addr: No. 2001, North Section of Tianfu Avenue, Wuhou District

spots.name: Yulinchuanchuanxiang
spots.desc: Cheap and fast hotpot variety. This is a help-yourself style meal, go to a backroom and choose your own kabobs. Stick the kabobs into a hotpot soup, and have them boil. Pull them out and enjoy. Large kabobs are ¥1, and small ones are ¥0.1 each. Expect to be full for less than ¥25. There are both spicy and non-spicy variations. There is a large selection of meats, vegetables, and other add-ins.…
spots.addr: Various locations throughout the city

spots.name: Lanzhou beef noodles
spots.desc: A bowl of noodles starts for about ¥4, and reach a maximum of ¥7. Varieties include egg, lamb and beef. Other dishes are reasonable in price as well. Breads for 1 kuai a piece, and Mutton Kabobs (羊肉串) go for 1 kuai per stick. Da Pan Ji (大盘鸡) is a great choice if eating with a group. Usually offered in small or large sizes, a small size will cost about ¥40 and feed 3 or 4 people. A large order…
spots.addr: Located everywhere

spots.name: Steamed buns
spots.desc: Sold for breakfast or lunch from street vendors throughout the city. Yagcai bao (芽菜包) is a local Sichuan special variety you are unlikely to find elsewhere and typically contains some mixture of Yacai (芽菜), a type of preserved vegetable, and potentially some meat. Other typical fillings include beef, red bean paste, mushrooms, green vegetables or pork. Three buns cost around ¥1 or larger buns…

spots.name: Lao Chengdu Yi Cheng Xian San Yang Mian
spots.desc: Budget Sichuan noodle restaurant featured in the Michelin Guide. Try the San Yang Mian.
spots.addr: Guojielou St no. 46

spots.name: Zhengzong Fushun Suancai Douhua
spots.desc: A local restaurant serving Fushun-style sour-pickle tofu pudding hot pot. The restaurant is known for its affordable prices, generous portions, and free refills of tofu pudding. Popular dishes include tofu pudding with crispy pork, beef, and pork ribs.
spots.addr: 24-26 Wulidun East Rd

spots.name: Lao Ma Ti Hua
spots.desc: A traditional Chengdu restaurant which serves local Sichuan dishes and is especially known for its tender pork trotters and rich soup.
spots.addr: 6-3 Renmin Middle Rd, Section 3

spots.name: Wenshu Temple Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: In the grounds of a monastery and run by monks. Offers a huge selection of traditional vegetarian dishes, including some containing imitated meat.
spots.addr: 15 Wenshu St (文殊院街15号)

spots.name: Hokkaido Japanese Restaurant
spots.desc: Authentic Japanese food. Serves curry, tonkatsu, unagi-don, fried rices, sushi, ramen noodles, and various other selections. Serves Chinese and Japanese beers, as well as a selection of plum wine and sake. Food quality varies.
spots.price: Meals range from ¥20 upwards, expect a plate of sushi to be quite a bit more expensive, but sides are generally decent…
spots.addr: Various locations throughout the city

spots.name: Chen Mapo
spots.desc: Supposedly opened by the Mapo herself in 1862. The place to eat Mapo Doufu, it does not get any more authentic than this. Spicy food eaters will love this, those who do not like spicy food should probably skip it altogether.
spots.addr: 208 Shuanglin Rd (成都市双林路208号新华公园正门对面)

spots.name: Namaste/Afila
spots.local: 亚非拉-娜玛什蒂印度餐吧
spots.desc: Specializes in Indian and Nepalese cuisine, particularly tandoori and curries. Great for vegetarians and omnivores alike.
spots.addr: 20 Remin Nan Rd, Section 4, Wuhou District (武侯区人民南路四段20号)

spots.name: Fiesta Thai
spots.desc: Specializes in Thai cuisine. Great food and exceptional service when you need a break from oily and spicy Sichuan food.
spots.addr: Linjiang Zhong Lu 6, Right beside Traffic Hotel and the 902 Panda Base Bus Stop

spots.name: Hibiscus Phoenix Garden Restaurant
spots.desc: The transportation here is very convenient. There are many bus lines. After getting off at Guanghua West Station, it only takes a few minutes to walk to the restaurant. Furonghuang Garden Restaurant is one of the restaurants that friends like to choose for gatherings, because the prices here are more suitable for friends with mass consumption, so it is suitable for friends to gather for dinner.…
spots.addr: Annex 7, No.66 Guanghua Village Street, Qingyang District

spots.name: Mike's Pizza Kitchen
spots.desc: Freshly made to order pizza. Authentic New York style pizza pie, stone-baked. Delivery only.
spots.addr: Tongzilin, Europe City

spots.name: Veranda Bridge Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant is actually a historic bridge over Funan River. Sichuan food. Very good reputation within Chengdu.

spots.name: Huang Cheng Lao Ma
spots.desc: Elaborate restaurant featuring hot pot followed by live entertainment, including Sichuan face-changing. Don't miss the diorama scene of ancient Chengdu built into the restaurant lobby's floor. A separate section on the ground floor of the restaurant also features a pan-Asian buffet with contemporary entertainment. Child care is available on premises. Prices are in the range of ¥100 per person for…

spots.name: Chengdu Bookworm
spots.desc: Has something for everyone. It is an English language lending library, a Western restaurant, a bar, as well as an occasional venue for local singing and musical talent. Expats might want to join the membership library or take kids to the children's morning story hours. Evenings, you might find a travel author reading from and signing books, poetry reading, or singing. Great place for to connect…
spots.addr: 28 Renmin S Rd

spots.name: Grandma's Kitchen
spots.desc: Western restaurant with four locations around Chengdu, including one next door to Peter's on Zhong Hua Yuan.

spots.name: Peter's Tex-Mex
spots.desc: Actually an American restaurant with some Mexican dishes. Peter's has good food. The Zhong Hua Yuan location also has homemade ice cream, the best ice cream you will find in Chengdu. If you are coming from out of town, the Zhong Hua Yuan location is right in a major expat area with lots of other restaurants and shopping surrounding it.

spots.name: Paul and Dave's Oasis
spots.desc: A place for volunteers, ex-pats, and all manner of foreigners, a place where you can go and just chill. Though he does serve Chinese food, you're better off going elsewhere for this, it is however a place where you can sit and lose yourself for a day or so. Usually occupied by the local foreigners, usually playing Western music.

spots.name: Club 88
spots.desc: Chengdu's hottest club. Awesome lighting and music, dancing in the walkways and people just trying to get seen. Expect crowds of people, packed tables, and action going on through the night well past the other clubs closing times. Get there early to get a table or come (very) late to wind down the night when everything else dies.
spots.addr: 99 Shaoling Rd, Wuhou District (武侯区少陵路88号)

spots.name: Cafe Paname
spots.desc: A bar with a younger crowd and laid-back environment Expect an occasional DJ event which will make the bar a little more lively on Fridays and Holidays.
spots.price: ¥10 Suntory beer on tap is a perk
spots.addr: 143 Kehua N Rd (科华北路143号)

spots.name: Highfly Cafe
spots.desc: Relaxed place with a tiny outside sitting area. They serve beers and Western food including pizza and breakfast. There is one computer for free Internet access and a small book exchange (2 for 1).
spots.addr: 18 Linjiang Rd

spots.name: Feeling4Seasons Cafe
spots.desc: Good Italian coffee: espresso, cappuccino, especially latte. Also pasta and pizza. They also provide Internet service: wireless access for your laptop, loan of a wireless card if you don't have one, use of a PC if required. You can also burn CDs. It is also one famous China blog freelancer's cafe bar; he published a book named "Ten Years, Flying with one Dream".
spots.addr: Orient Times Mall 2F, Xiadongda St

spots.name: Mooney's Irish Pub
spots.desc: A real classy traditional Irish pub. Sometimes they have a live band or other entertainment. Also they have a free billiard table which is nice. Offering beers on tap, whiskies and signature dishes.

spots.name: Shamrock Pub
spots.desc: This Irish pub is in the hub of Chengdu's small foreign community (of approximately 3,000). Friendly pub atmosphere and live music some evenings. In addition to drinks the pub serves dishes including pizza, meat pies, sausage rolls, steaks, burgers, curries and a range of other snacks. The pub is also an active sponsor of several non-profit organizations, including holding events for moon bear…
spots.addr: 15, 4th Section, Renmin S Rd

spots.name: High Connections Coffee House
spots.desc: Provides a relaxing, comfortable, environment with soft lighting and easy-listening music. They have non-smoking and smoking sections. Bring your computer and hook up to the wireless Internet. Their coffee (both Espresso and good old fashioned drip American style) and muffins are an excellent way to begin a day. They also have large conference rooms available for meetings.
spots.addr: Fu A-20 6 Shuangqing S Rd, Qingyang District

spots.name: 8trees Wine Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: Located in a century old Roman Catholic church, and offers the most unique romantic dinning experience. Recommended signature dishes are the tantalizing mouthwatering North American beef, marinated with fresh herbs and spices; the lamb main simmered with exotic spices. On the lighter side, there is the conscious side dish which is very popular with weight-watching regulars who complement their…
spots.addr: 9 Pingan Alley

spots.name: Little Bar (New)
spots.desc: Rock bar. The bigger shows are on Friday and Saturday and the bands start playing at 20:00 and finish at 22:00. ¥25 entrance fee. A bit hard to find so best to get a cab to take you if you are not familiar with the area. Not to be confused with Little Bar (Old), the sister bar on Yulin West Road.
spots.addr: 87 Fangqin St, Yulin Shangwugang, 1F (成都市芳沁街87号附5号丰尚玉林商务港1楼

spots.name: Empty Bottle
spots.desc: Very popular amongst the locals. Live music and other kinds of shows every night.
spots.addr: 3/F, Yulin Life Plaza, 15 S Yulin Rd

spots.name: Jellyfish
spots.desc: Lively and crowded cocktail bar with a DJ playing music. Lot of expats but also local folk.
spots.addr: Ke Hua Bei Lu #143, Lan Si Jia Le Bi Sq, 2F

spots.name: Leiyin Monastery
spots.desc: This temple, and some of the others temples tucked away in the seams of the mountain, are worthy of exploring, although many are cheaply-made, modern constructions.

spots.name: Jiulao Cave
spots.desc: Close to the Xianfen Temple. Deep Taoist cave. Lots of pilgrims go there to burn incences. It does not seem advised to take this path in winter unless well prepared.

spots.name: Pinnacle Lingyan
spots.desc: Emei Mountain lies seven kilometers southwest of Emeishan City and is one of the four mountain ranges in China that Buddhists consider sacred. It was included in the UNESCO world heritage list in 1996. The mountain stretches more than 200 km from south to north. Its main peak, Wanfo Top, is 3,099 meters above sea level. Since ancient times Emei Mountain has been described as “Beauty Under Heaven”.

spots.name: Barkhor Street
spots.desc: A circular street around the Jokhang Temple in the center of the old section of Lhasa, it is the oldest street in a traditional style in Tibet, where you can enjoy bargaining with vendors for local handicrafts. Barkhor Street is one of the most important religious paths along which pilgrims walk around Jokhang Temple while turning prayer wheels in their hands through centuries. Buddhist pilgrims…

spots.name: Tibet Museum of Natural Science
spots.desc: Tibet's largest museum. The museum is of course primarily devoted to the natural history of Tibet. It also includes the Memorial to the Liberation of a Million Serfs in Tibet (西藏百万农奴解放纪念馆), which has exhibitions on the Communist Party's policies in Tibet since the 1950s. Visitor numbers are capped at 5000 per day.
spots.addr: 9 Zangda East Road, Chengguan District (城关区藏大东路9号)

spots.name: The Yak Museum of Tibet
spots.desc: A museum about yaks and their importance to Tibetan culture. Entry is restricted to 2000 visitors per day.
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:30, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: 6 Chagu Avenue, Liuwu New Area, Doilungdêqên District 堆龙德庆区柳梧新区察古大道6号

spots.name: Former Site of the Amban's Yamen
spots.desc: This was the office and official residence of the amban, the Qing government's representative in Lhasa. The building, which was restored in 2013, houses a small museum, which focuses mainly on the history of the Qing government's relations with the Tibetan local authorities.
spots.addr: Barkhor Street North, Barkhor, Chengguan District (城关区八廓街八廓北街)

spots.name: Norbulingka Summer Palace
spots.desc: It is about 1 km south of the Potala Palace - the Seventh Dalai Lama constructed the first summer palace in 1755 and each successive ruler added his own buildings. The complex contains a small zoo, botanical gardens, and a mansion from the 14th Dalai Lhama built in 1956~8. This was the place that the 14th Dalai Lama escaped from in 1959, and left for India. There is a sign outside the building…

spots.name: Drepung Monastery
spots.desc: Founded in 1416 by a disciple of Tsong Khapa, was the biggest and richest monastery in Tibet and its lamas helped to train each new young Dalai Lama. Drepung was also home to the Nechung, the state oracle. At its height, Drepung had over 10,000 monks, and governed 700 subsidiary monasteries and owned vast estates. Drepung belongs to the Gelupa sect.

spots.name: Ganden Monastery
spots.desc: Located on Wangbur Mountain, 47 km (29 miles) from Lhasa City. It was built in the 15th century with over 50 structures. The main halls in the temple are the Main Assembly Hall (or Coqen Hall), Zhacangs, Khangtsens and Myicuns.

spots.name: Kora
spots.desc: A meditative circumambulation around a sacred site, such as a temple, practiced by many Tibetans.

spots.name: Langma Opera
spots.desc: literally "royal music", a traditional Tibetan singing and dancing show.

spots.name: Blind Massage
spots.desc: English spoken. A vocational project of Braille Without Borders. Great way to adjust to the altitude or to relax.
spots.addr: #59 Beijing Middle Road, 3rd floor

spots.name: Princess Wencheng Live Action Drama
spots.desc: A large-scale musical based on the life of Princess Wencheng. Features almost 1000 performers.
spots.addr: Princess Wencheng Live Action Drama Theatre, Tibetan Culture & Tourism Creativity Park, Cijuelin Village, Chengguan District (城关区慈觉林村中国西藏文化旅游创意园文成公主实景剧场)

spots.name: Snow Leopard Industries
spots.desc: Small shop with a wide variety of traditional and contemporary Tibetan designs made at their own factory. Rug prices are fixed and very reasonable. Owner Phurbu Tsamchu speaks English and can explain about the different Tibetan designs and the process of making rugs. This store also has a fixed-price souvenir shop with very low, set prices. Can arrange shipping of rugs overseas. Credit cards…
spots.addr: #2 East Zang Yi Yuan Road

spots.name: Kharma Gallery
spots.desc: Art gallery offering quality oil paintings by Tibetan artists on Tibetan themes (landscape, people, religious, animals, etc.)

spots.name: Dropenling Handicraft Development Center
spots.desc: This shop is not the cheapest but has very high quality items made in Tibet. Profits go to artisan development programs. Credit cards accepted.
spots.addr: 11 Chak Tsal Gang Road

spots.name: Tibetan Steak House
spots.desc: East of Jokhang Temple and hard to miss from the big sign. Serves Tibetian food as well as Indian, Western, Chinese and the prices are reasonable. Good alternative if the more popular choices are crowded.

spots.name: Ganglamedo Café & Bar
spots.desc: Means 'snowdrop' in Tibetan. It is managed by a Chinese woman from Dalian, Liaoning Province. Visitors are greeted with many elaborate canvases and watercolor paintings. Ganglamedo is well known for its delicious pastry and coffee.
spots.addr: 127 Beijing East Rd

spots.name: Yunnan stones
spots.desc: For the game of Go (围棋 wéiqí). These are the best Chinese stones. They are quite different from Japanese stones, and much cheaper. It is also possible to visit the factory near Kunming. See the Yunzi article on the go players' wiki, Sensei's Library. Boards and bowls are also available.
spots.addr: Kunming flower and bird market

spots.name: Burma Road History Museum
spots.desc: A museum about the Burma Road. The museum was founded by Chen Daya, the author of a book about the Overseas Chinese drivers and mechanics who came to China to work on the Burma Road. The museum does not have a lot of artefacts, but has many photographs, illustrations and models. The most valuable and authentic item on display is an old case used for carrying items along the Burma Road. If you…
spots.addr: Chunyu Road, Xishan District (西山区春雨路)

spots.name: Kunming Flying Tigers Memorial
spots.desc: The Flying Tigers were fighter pilots — officially called the American Volunteer Group — who fought the Japanese in China through much of World War II, both before and after the US entered the war. Despite a whole range of problems, they shot down several hundred enemy planes. Kunming was one of their main bases.
spots.addr: 458 Beijing Road, Panlong District (盘龙区北京路458号)

spots.name: Victory over Japan Memorial Hall
spots.local: 抗战胜利纪念堂, 抗战胜利堂, Anti-Japanese War Memorial Hall
spots.desc: Completed in 1947, this was one of the first war memorials to be commissioned in China following the end of the Second World War. It is now a national heritage site.
spots.addr: 49 Ruixi Road, Wuhua District (五华区云瑞西路49号)

spots.name: Yunnan Art Museum
spots.desc: Occupies the building where the Yunnan Provincial Museum (listed below) used to be.
spots.addr: 118 Wuyi Road, Wuhua District (五华区五一路118号)

spots.name: Yunnan University Wu Mayao Museum of Anthropology
spots.local: 云南大学伍马瑶人类学博物馆
spots.desc: Fascinating museum with an impressive collection of minority and Han artifacts from around Yunnan. Highlights include painted wooden torso armor of the Yi people, fearsome warriors of a traditionally caste society who historically controlled the mountainous region between Sichuan and Yunnan and whose queen was instrumental in negotiating the entry in to Yunnan of the Mongol Horde at the dawn of…
spots.hours: Reportedly closed during the university's summer and winter vacation periods
spots.addr: Yunnan University, 2 Cuihu North Road, Wuhua District (五华区翠湖北路2号云南大学)

spots.name: Kunming Planning Exhibition Hall
spots.desc: A public exhibition hall presenting Kunming's urban development, construction achievements and future planning through models, multimedia displays and interactive exhibits. Free guided tours are offered at 10:00 and 14:30.
spots.addr: 4606 Huanhu East Road, Guandu District

spots.name: Yunnan Literature and Art Museum
spots.desc: An arts and cultural exhibition center presenting visual art, literature and other forms of Yunnan culture. It hosts permanent and temporary exhibitions as well as cultural events.
spots.addr: 4066 Guangfu Road, Guandu District

spots.name: Fulintang Drugstore (Bi'anguo Branch)
spots.desc: Opened in 1857, this is the oldest established drugstore in Kunming. The traditional style building has remained largely unchanged since the 19th century and has been included on China's national heritage list. As of April 2026 the structure was closed and looked dilapidated.
spots.addr: 31 Guanghua Street, Wuhua District (五华区光华街31号)

spots.name: Guandu Ancient Town
spots.desc: An historic town that was founded during the Tang Dynasty and was once part of the kingdoms of Nanzhao and Dali. A number of old buildings are preserved here, including several temples.
spots.addr: Guandu District (官渡区)

spots.name: 斗南花卉市场夜间拍卖
spots.desc: Witness the fast-paced, high-energy night auction at one of Asia's largest flower markets. It's a fascinating spectacle of commerce where millions of flowers change hands in a matter of hours. An unforgettable sensory experience.
spots.addr: Dounan Flower Market, Chenggong District

spots.name: Kunming Pump House
spots.local: 昆明自来水厂泵房旧址
spots.desc: As a result of droughts parching Yunnan, the reservoirs surrounding Kunming are of vital importance. The specter of Kunming's taps suddenly running dry is of great concern for residents. The two-room "History Museum of Kunming Water Supply" (昆明市自来水历史博物馆) is inside the Green Lake Park, and is housed in the building that once pumped 1,000 m³ of water daily from Green Lake's spring-fed Nine Dragon…
spots.addr: 6 Cui Hu East Road, Wuhua District (五华区翠湖东路6号)

spots.name: Zhu De's Former Residence
spots.desc: Zhu De (1886-1976) was one of the Communist Party's most revered political and military leaders in the 20th century. Most notably, he was the Commander-in-Chief of the Red Army during both the Second Sino-Japanese War and the Chinese Civil War. He also held the position of Commander-in-Chief of the People's Liberation Army during the Korean War. This residence was Zhu De's home from 1921 to 1922.…
spots.addr: 4 Honghua Lane (红花巷4号) and 3 Xiaomeiyuan Lane (小梅园巷3号), Wuhua District (五华区)

spots.name: Tanhua Temple
spots.local: 昙华寺; Tánhuàsì; also known as Tanhua Nunnery 昙华庵
spots.desc: Built in 1634. According to historical records, before the temple was erected, there had been a thatched shack where Shi Shiqiao, a scholar of the Ming Dynasty, buried himself in books. Shi Tai, grandson of Shi Shiqiao, donated the estate for the shack whereon the temple was built.In the backyard there was an epiphyllum tree, which is called tanhua in Chinese, hence the name. The temple went…
spots.addr: 533 Tanhua Road, Panlong District (盘龙区光明路昙华路533号; Pánlóngqū Guāngmínglù)

spots.name: Baohai Park
spots.desc: The park covers an area of 250 mu (16.67 hectares) and is one of Kunming's largest modern parks. It features camphor, azaleas and other native plants.
spots.addr: 121 Baohai Road, Guandu District (官渡区宝海路121号)

spots.name: Black Dragon Pool Park
spots.local: 黑龙潭公园; Hēilóng Tán Gōngyuán
spots.desc: Black Dragon Pool Park is a rare large garden, is the Kunming plum resort, known as the" Longquan exploration plum". The" Tang Mei" legend from Nanzhao transplant, with the tranquility Caoxi Temple" Yuan Mei" is considered to be Yunnan's most precious Gu Mei. The park features trees that are rare, not only because of their scarcity in the area, but also for their astounding age and size.
spots.price: Entry is pricey at ¥20 per person per day;
spots.addr: 1 Lan'an Road, Panlong District (盘龙区蓝桉路1号)

spots.name: Jingxing Street Flower and Bird Market
spots.local: 景星街花鸟市场; Jǐngxīng Jiē Huāniǎo Shìchǎng
spots.desc: If purchasing cute little puppy dogs, live crickets, birds, live bird food, tortoises and other things creepy, crawly and/or fluffy is your thing then it is here to be had... along with a few flowers and a great many trinkets. The most obvious stalls begin where Wuyi Road meets Dongfeng West Road but other sellers can be found on other streets within the district.
spots.addr: Jingxing Street, Wuhua District (五华区景星街)

spots.name: Kunming Zoo
spots.desc: The Zoo was built in 1953 and has over 300 species. There is a peacock garden, butterfly enclosure, aviary and aquarium. In spring the zoo is reputed to be a sea of flowers, in particular the blossom of cherry trees and weeping Chinese crab apple trees. Overall the zoo is a pleasant enough place but with a slight air of weariness and decay about it. Local people also use it as a place for…
spots.hours: 07:30-18:30, no entry to large animal section after 16:30
spots.price: ¥20 for general entry with a further ¥80 for the circus
spots.addr: 92 Qingnian Road, Wuhua District (五华区青年路92号)

spots.name: Dragon Gate
spots.desc: The Dragon Gate is the most famous sight here, it is built on the steep rock hills, which was cut in the years from 1781. On March 3, every lunar year, hundreds of Kunming people crowd up to the hills for celebrating their traditional distinguished gathering called Spring Touring, dancing and singing on the green western hills.
spots.price: Entrance to the Dragon Gate is an additional ¥30, a golf cart ¥12.5, and the lift for ¥25

spots.name: Jacarandas blossom at Jiaochang Middle Road
spots.desc: End of April and May jacaranda trees blossom all over the city. Jiaochang Middle Road (教场中路 Jiaochang Zhong Lu) is a popular spot for viewing them.
spots.addr: Jiaochang Middle Road

spots.name: Yunnan Grand Theatre
spots.desc: A major performing arts venue in Kunming with a large theatre, concert hall and multifunctional theatre. It hosts dance, opera, drama, concerts and other stage performances.
spots.addr: 6395 Guangfu Road, Guandu District

spots.name: Kunming Walk
spots.desc: Small-group guided walking tour (up to 6 people) through Green Lake (Cuihu) and the old university quarter, focusing on Kunming's history of foreign influence. Covers the French-built Yunnan–Vietnam railway, a poet and professor turned activist Wen Yiduo, and the wartime National Southwestern Associated University (Lianda) where two future Nobel laureates studied. In English. Book via the website.
spots.hours: Wed & Sat 10:00, 3 hours; other days by appointment

spots.name: Earth Forest
spots.desc: The Earth Forest in Yuanmou County in Chuxiong Prefecture is a scenic spot at the provincial level. Earth Forest, as a representative landscape in the county, comprises Xinhua, Bangguo, Wanbao and Tiger Leaping Beach, covering an area of 50 km². The Earth Forest came into being since geological movement and soil erosion one or two million years ago. Its shape looks like an immense forest and the…

spots.name: Outdoor Equipment
spots.desc: As elsewhere in bigger cities close to mountainous regions, you can buy fairly good quality fake and overrun outdoor and camping gear in Kunming. See our China article for background. Shops can be found in a courtyard at 20 Dongfeng East Road and on Baoshan Street close to the central square, as well as in the enormous garment district on the South Ring Road between the moat and Carrefour…

spots.name: Equipment for Chinese games
spots.desc: In particular, Yunnan stones (云子) Yúnzǐ for the game of Go (Chinese: weiqi 围棋) are the best Chinese stones. They are quite different from Japanese stones, and much cheaper; see the Yunzi article on the go players' wiki, Sensei's Library. It is also possible to visit the factory (Chinese-only web site) near Kunming. Boards and bowls are also available.
spots.addr: Flower and bird market

spots.name: Mandarin Bookstore
spots.desc: Has some English, French and German books. Has the Lonely Planet China guidebook, which is generally hard to find in China.
spots.addr: 52 Wenhua Lane 9-10

spots.name: Xinhua Bookstore
spots.desc: A typical large (2-storey) bookstore of the national Xinhua chain. A decent map section, with some local area maps available right near the entrance. There is a large space with chairs and tables to sit down and read, or to use your laptop.

spots.name: Computer street
spots.desc: If you need some IT stuff. Pay attention to counterfeit, and whether international warranty is available.

spots.name: Bicycles and accessories
spots.desc: A couple of dozen bicycle stores are concentrated within a couple blocks on the South Ring Road, just east from Zhenchi Lu. (Which means, a few blocks west of the Carrefour store). As of 2016, the stores are all next to each other, on the north side of the street, and carry bicycles priced from ¥300-3000, as well as spare parts and accessories. Bicycles and some accessories are also sold in…
spots.addr: South Ring Road

spots.name: Heavenly Manna
spots.desc: Yunnan style restaurant in the very trendy and fashionable Wenlin Street area. Fantastic food at reasonable prices. The drinks are less than ¥10. The cakes are also worth trying.
spots.addr: 74 Wenhua Alley, Wenlin Street (文林街文化巷74号; Wénlínjiē Wénhuàxiàng)

spots.name: Yuanxi Lu
spots.desc: A street full of small restaurants and shops. There's a good place hidden behind an entrance with a small Chinese-style roof on top, selling chou doufu in the entrance. One shop to the left you can try pork brain or just some tasty dumplings. On the opposite side of the street there's a Dai minority restaurant. You can recognize it by its bamboo-style walls.

spots.name: Insane Wontons
spots.desc: A delicious insanely spicy dumpling (wonton) soup with other (including non-spicy) options as well. Try the Sichuan Spicy Wontons (MaLa HunDun) 麻辣馄饨 or the Strange Flavor Wontons (GuaiWei HunDun)怪味馄饨 for the two best.

spots.name: Flavor Street
spots.desc: Restaurant with good pizza and amazing Thai hot pot. The owner is very friendly and the service is superb.
spots.addr: Store 48, Taiyang Xincheng, Longquan Lu (龙泉路泰暘欣城58号商铺; Lóngquánlù Tàiyángxīnchéng)

spots.name: Mazagran Cafe
spots.desc: Has a good selection of Western meals and some delicious cakes and cookies (the millionaire shortbread is a favourite). The clientele is a mix of Westerners (lots of students looking for an afternoon study spot and enjoying the free Wi-Fi) and locals. Its second floor location (the stairs are around the back of the building) and open frontage makes it a good place to people watch. The restaurant…

spots.name: Salvadors
spots.desc: Wide variety of western food and imported beer. They make excellent ice cream. A local favorite.

spots.name: French Cafe
spots.desc: Offers free Wi-Fi internet and serves a list of French options that cannot be found elsewhere in Kunming. Great homemade baguette, real French pastries, good coffee. The lovely atmosphere and the good music is a plus. It has become a popular spot to hang out and have a beer or two in the evenings.

spots.name: Games Cafe
spots.desc: Run by a Frenchman and his local wife, this place offers a stunning collection of boardgames in a few languages (mostly English and Chinese), and is popular with both foreigners and locals. Local and imported beers, home made noodles, various French food and amazing meal-portioned salads.

spots.name: Prague Cafe
spots.desc: Cute cafe with an upper level, has books and magazines. Has a variety of meals including Japanese and Western. While this place largely remains a Chinese hangout, several foreigners looking for a quieter lunch or place to study Chinese can be seen. The staff are friendly and the coffee is probably second best in the area. Food is mediocre, pizza is microwaved from a box. Pricey drinks. Disgusting…

spots.name: Shiping Huiguan
spots.desc: Traditional Yunnanese restaurant in an old courtyard; the amazing building is reason enough for a visit, though the food is also very good. The plate of various fried insects is interesting to try; the river shrimps and the baked fish is also a must.
spots.addr: Cuihu Nan Lu, 24 Zhonghe Xiang (翠湖南路中和巷24号)

spots.name: Makye Ame
spots.desc: A Tibetan restaurant with fantastic atmosphere and design, and nightly stage performances of Tibetan songs and dances. Some dish with yak meat must of course be tried; there is plenty in the menu.
spots.addr: Jinhuapu Lu (Inside the Kunming office of Diqing Prefecture) (近华浦路迪庆州驻昆办二楼)

spots.name: Soho
spots.desc: This is a popular national franchise bar. They have singers throughout the night and DJs to spin the music. The distinction this place has is that they don't hire bar girls. In most Chinese clubs, the hot girls you see work for the club to give the place an image or to sell you beer and sell more tables. The girls you see in this club are customers or brought by customers. So you get a more real…
spots.addr: In the Kundu Bar District

spots.name: s.Muse
spots.desc: Another franchise club that opens until 06:00. They have the best location in the whole district. Right in front of the square.

spots.name: Shelter Bar
spots.desc: The bar is unique. Entering through the doors, there is a jazzy scene with plenty of comfortable places to lounge. Sometimes they even have video games set up. But the thing that sets this bar apart from other bars lies through the doors next to the bar. Passing through them, you go down some steps about 2 m (6 feet) and enter through three doors, each of them 7 cm (3 inches) thick. This second…
spots.addr: 295 Yuantong East Road (圆通东路295号; Yuántōngdōnglù)

spots.name: Dyonysos (狄俄尼索)
spots.desc: A high class live-music bar. Very good Yunnan snacks and great selection of drinks. Usually six singers a night with other musicians playing in between. Little bit pricy but great to entertain guests in the city center.
spots.addr: Baoshanjie 1, 8th floor (盘龙区宝善街宝善1号8楼(近前景动感天下));

spots.name: Freedom Bar
spots.desc: A club and bar with dance music, a small dance floor, and plenty of alcohol. During happy hours foreigners are allowed three free drinks: either 3 whiskeys or 3 beers.
spots.addr: Renmin East Road (人民东路; Rénmíndōnglù)

spots.name: Aoma Meili Pub
spots.local: 敖玛梅里餐厅; Áomǎ Méilǐ Cāntīng
spots.desc: This well-known western restaurant is undergoing some changes to be more of a bar. There are no other bars near the Camellia Hotel, so it is really nice! It is one of the few places with a Western bartender as well. He has lived in Yunnan for a few years, and is really good to get information from. He said he just started here, so as soon as he gets all the equipment he promised some great…
spots.addr: 60 Dongfeng East Road (东风东路60号; Dōngfēngdōnglù)

spots.name: Mu Palace
spots.desc: The palace where the Mu Clan of the Naxi people ruled for over 400 years. It is a large complex that extends part way up the hill behind it. There used to be a lot of high quality paintings in the palace and finely carved wooden doors, but most were destroyed during the Cultural Revolution. At the back hill of the Mu's Palace is the 'Lion Hill Scenic Area', which requires additional ¥40 entrance…
spots.price: Entry fee is ¥40 (as of Mar 2019). Discounts are available for children over 1.2 metres in height and adults aged…
spots.addr: 49 Guanyuan Lane, Guangyi Street, Gucheng District (古城区光义街官院巷49号)

spots.name: Shuhe Old Town
spots.desc: Better than Lijiang if you want a place less commercialized; a horse ride in the town is an attraction.
spots.addr: Shuhe Road, Gucheng District (古城区束河路)

spots.name: Old Tea Horse Road Museum
spots.desc: One of the main attractions in Shuhe Old Town. The museum is housed in a former Buddhist temple, which was historically known as the Dajue Temple (大觉宫) and dates back to the late Ming Dynasty. So besides the exhibitions on the Old Tea Horse Road, one can also view some old Buddhist murals. More murals from the same time period may be seen at Baisha Old Town (see below).
spots.addr: North Gate, Shuhe Old Town, Gucheng District (古城区束河古镇北门)

spots.name: Dongba Valley
spots.desc: On your way to the Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, you may stop by at the Dongba Valley culture center. They moved some families from other places to this village and let them live their normal lives. Such domestic scenes as the husband in a family counting change while the wife is comforting the baby or two young siblings baking cookies and selling them to visitors are common. There are live singers…
spots.addr: Yuquan Road (玉泉路)

spots.name: Baisha Ancient Town
spots.desc: Baisha Town was once Lijiang's political, economic and cultural center. It is the original settlement of the Naxi people who came to the greater Lijiang Valley over a thousand years ago. Made up of at least 12 smaller villages, the main village is Sanyuan (三元村), which has one main stone street called of course, Baisha Street. Have a drink some Yunnan coffee eat a Naxi Pie. Good for a half day…

spots.name: Baisha Murals
spots.desc: The Buddhist murals here reflect a fusion of both Han Chinese and Tibetan painting techniques with Naxi cultural traditions.
spots.addr: Baisha Ancient Town (白沙古镇)

spots.name: Baisha Naxi Embroidery Institute
spots.desc: The Baisha Naxi Embroidery Institute. It is a typical Naxi courtyard with a very nice surroundings. The mission of the institute is to save, protect, inherit and promote the Naxi traditional hand-made embroidery. It occupies 800 m² and there are many embroidery masters and students. You can try how to do hand-made embroidery there if you have time. Also you can buy some very nice embroideries…
spots.addr: No. 17 Group 1, Sanyuan Village, Baisha Ancient Town (白沙古镇三元村一组17号)

spots.name: Lashihai Lake Wetland Park
spots.local: 拉市海湿地公园, Lashihai Wetland Park, Lashi Lake Wetland Park
spots.desc: A popular area for bird-watching, particularly during the winter months when thousands of migratory birds flock here from distant lands. You can also go horse-riding around the lake. Boating activities, however, have been banned since October 2018.

spots.name: Zhiyun Monastery
spots.desc: A Tibetan Buddhist monastery. Unlike many other sights in Lijiang, the monastery has so far resisted commercialisation and sees relatively few tourists.
spots.addr: Hainan Village, Lashi Township, Yulong Naxi Autonomous County (玉龙纳西族自治县拉市乡海南村)

spots.name: Gold Dragon Bridge
spots.local: Jinlong Bridge 金龙桥, Zili Bridge 梓里桥
spots.desc: Built between 1876 and 1880, this iron chain suspension bridge spans the Jinsha River, a tributary of the Yangtze. It is said to be the oldest bridge on the Yangtze still in use today.
spots.addr: Yongsheng County (永胜县)

spots.name: Naxi Concert Hall
spots.desc: Enjoy the traditional Naxi music Culture Show performed by the Naxi Orchestra, which includes some 70-90 year old men. The music itself is a combination of traditional Chinese music dating back to the Tang dynasty and local instruments and flavours. The music is well performed, however be prepared for long explanations of its musical history in Mandarin between each piece and the sometimes…
spots.addr: 86 Mishi Lane, Xinyi Street, Gucheng District (古城区新义街密士巷86号)

spots.name: Float styrofoam boats
spots.desc: Along the main streams are girls selling candles that float on delicate flower-shaped styrofoam boats. Tourists can purchase one, make a wish, and send their candle down the waterways. Late in the evening after groups have had significant amounts of alcohol you can see many floating candles sailing down the waterways. If you are environmentally conscious and have reservations about sending…

spots.name: Biking
spots.desc: Rent a bike downtown, e.g. at Ali Baba's near Mao Zedong's statue, and see the sights. Ali Baba's will give you a handmade map of smaller surrounding towns that capture the quaint styles of Lijiang without the heavy tourism and the tacky souvenir shops. There are at least three towns, ranging from converted hippy communes to remote farming villages. There is a beautiful remote Buddhist monastery…
spots.price: About ¥40 per day including a map

spots.name: Walk the canal path
spots.desc: To get to the Black Dragon Pool you can walk the canal path north near the main water wheel. It will take you to the south entrance of the park. The north part of the park is free and you can get there by walking around the south entrance and keep heading north. You should reach a street with the main entrance to the park. Keep going north and you will see a small bridge that leads to a large…

spots.name: Visit Naxi villages
spots.desc: If you would like to visit some of the Naxi villages in the hills surrounding Lijiang, you can rent a small van to take you around for ¥100-300, depending on the driver and how much Chinese you speak. There are regular minivans on Shangrila Road, the main road on the west side of town, which take locals to and from the villages. Sometimes it can be difficult to find a mini-van to go back to…

spots.name: Impression Lijiang
spots.desc: A cultural show demonstrating the traditions and lifestyles of the Naxi, Yi and Bai peoples of the area. The show takes place inside Jade Dragon Snow Mountain Park at 3500 m in an outdoor theater specifically designed to showcase the mountain which is used as a backdrop. The production itself was designed by Zhang Yimou (director of Hero, House of Flying Daggers), Fan Yue and Wang Chaoge, a cast…

spots.name: Dry Sea Meadow
spots.desc: The closest chair lift up the mountain to Lijiang. It transports visitors to a large meadow located at 3050 m.

spots.name: Cloud Fir Meadow
spots.desc: From the reception centre which is next to Impression Lijiang on the Lijiang-Daju road a fleet of buses transports visitors to a cable car. Both bus transfer and cable car costs a total of ¥110 for a return trip. From the upper terminus of the cable car a vehicle takes you to the Cloud Fir Meadow for ¥50. The view is not very spectacular which makes this trip highly overpriced.

spots.name: Yak Meadow
spots.desc: The furtherest from Lijiang at a distance of 60 km, this cable car, costs ¥60 for a round-trip. At an elevation of 3,500 m and the least-visited of the three chair lifts this area offers grazing yaks, a Tibetan temple and a number of hiking possibilities. On the way to the chairlift’s lower terminus the road drips down and crosses a river. A number of yaks are located here where for a fee you can…

spots.name: Go hiking to local Naxi villages
spots.desc: Get out of Lijiang and discover the real place, by hiking in the Lijiang valley or in the hills to temples, lakes, villages and scenic lookouts. Agencies like Lijiang Guides can arrange trips to remote villages, as well as Tiger Leaping Gorge, Lugu Lake and Baoshan stone village.
spots.addr: Old Town Lijiang

spots.name: Naxi hand-made Embroidery
spots.desc: You can find many nice Naxi hand-made embroideries in the Baisha Naxi Embroidery Institute. Some of them are arts, very unbelievable, made by the famous Naxi masters.
spots.addr: Baisha Village

spots.name: Prague Café
spots.desc: The food is good and fairly reasonably priced (given the touristy area it is in) and it has a friendly atmosphere, but the drinks are expensive. Especially green tea at ¥15/cup!

spots.name: Country Sky
spots.desc: Serves lunch and dinner and offers vegetarian and traditional dishes at fair prices.
spots.addr: Hongye Street, Shuhe Ancient Village

spots.name: N's Kitchen
spots.desc: Serves western breakfast, tasty sandwiches, monster burgers, and pizzas. Free Internet and WiFi. And they have very nice bikes for hire. You could also get lots of information on biking and hiking here. the view from the balcony is nice and you can chill out a while.
spots.addr: 2/F, 17 Jishan Alley, Xinyi St

spots.name: Qiuyuege Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves Naxi foods. Free live music and free Internet and WiFi.
spots.addr: 32 Cunwen Sect, Xinhua St

spots.name: Adam Restaurant
spots.desc: A unique restaurant inside the old town. There is no menu in this restaurant. Adam, the owner, will only cook when the visitors come in. You only need to enjoy the food he cooks and pay the food as your convenient. It is worth trying for the food adventure.

spots.name: Nordic Delight
spots.desc: A bakery and café with very good cheese cake and coffee. Seems closed.
spots.price: ¥25 for a slice of Oreo cheesecake

spots.name: Freshnam Cafe
spots.desc: Western/Korean bar. Easily accessible, 5 minutes walk from old town center. In the day, it is a quiet cafe, ideal for some hot tea or smoothies. Live music starts from 20:30 every night, perfectly located away from the tourist crowds. Refreshing cocktails served at reasonable prices, definitely worth a visit. Free wifi available and even a shelf of books for your reading pleasure.

spots.name: LMC - Lijiang Millionaire's Club
spots.desc: LMC is a new cafe/bar in old town, the only one in the old town run by foreigners, and a good meeting place for travelers. Has free Wi-Fi, live music every night, film nights on Tuesdays, local and imported beers, wines from all over the world, as well as pizza, pasta and Indian meals.
spots.addr: Bai Sui Qiao

spots.name: Stone the Crows
spots.desc: Down-to-earth Irish pub with a fine selection of drinks, pool table and big movie playing TV. It can be a little hard to find as it is located down a small quiet alley, but it is well worth doing so. Popular with both foreign tourists and locals, this is a great place to escape the busy main streets and guarantees absolutely no karaoke. The kitchen stays open until 02:00 offering snacks, burgers…
spots.addr: 134-2 Wenzhi Alley, Wuyi St, Lijiang old town

spots.name: Sweet Air
spots.desc: This is probably the best bar in the old town that is not touristy. Once you step inside, you can tell they spent a lot of money on the renovations. There is a see through floor where the wine cellar lies below, and stone walls. They have a live band that starts playing at 21:00. They have a drummer from Africa and a bass guitarist from USA. You won't find people trying constantly sell you…
spots.addr: 古城区 崇仁巷(饮玉巷(近振兴巷))

spots.name: Meizhou Confucian Temple
spots.addr: Lingfeng Road West, Meijiang District (梅江区凌风西路)

spots.name: Ren Shan Su Shi
spots.desc: Very tasty Chinese-style vegan buffet.
spots.price: ¥28 per person, buy a ticket at the health food store downstairs, then go upstairs to get your plate and bowl
spots.addr: 11 Changdi Road, Zexu District, Humen Town 虎门镇则徐区长堤路11号

spots.name: Mixed Salad
spots.desc: Authentic American-style food with a focus on salads.
spots.addr: 44 Chaoyang Third Street, Changping 常平镇朝阳三街44号

spots.name: Nanning Confucius Temple
spots.addr: 9 Qinghuan Road, Qingxiu District (青秀区青环路9号)

spots.name: Da hong pao
spots.desc: This is another famous oolong tea, from Mount Wuyi.

spots.name: Fuzhou National Forest Park
spots.price: Entry to the park is free; entry to the aviary costs ¥25
spots.addr: Shangchiqiao, Xindian Town, Jin’an District (晋安区新店镇上赤桥)

spots.name: Yutian Ancient Chinese Jade Museum
spots.desc: Private museum specializing in old jade artifacts.
spots.addr: Ground floor, Jingchengmingteng Center, 468 Liuyi North Road, Gulou District (鼓楼区六一北路468号景城明腾中心一层)

spots.name: Restaurants near the white pagoda
spots.desc: More than a dozen restaurants, mostly upmarket.

spots.name: Longyan Museum
spots.addr: No. 2 People's Square, Longyan Avenue, Xinluo District (新罗区龙岩大道人民广场中2号)

spots.name: Nanping Museum
spots.addr: 266 Makeng Road, Yanping District (延平区马坑路266号)

spots.name: Putian Xiuyu Wanda Plaza
spots.addr: 99 Xidadao Road, Hutou Town, Xiuyu District

spots.name: Zhengrong Times Square
spots.addr: at the intersection of Dongyuan East Road and Beida North Street in Licheng District 荔城区东园路与北大路交汇处

spots.name: Bart's Kitchen
spots.desc: Southeast Asian and Western cuisine, with an English menu.
spots.addr: at Dong fang min zhu #115 (东方明珠) on Feng zi street (丰泽街)

spots.name: Yuan pan
spots.desc: Japanese sushi with buffet prices starting at ¥118.
spots.addr: on Quan xiu road (泉秀路).

spots.name: Lan zhou hand-pulled noodles
spots.addr: on Hu xin street (湖心街) opposite Mr. Chiu's beef noodles

spots.name: Thai-Vietnamese Restaurant
spots.addr: 2 locations in town

spots.name: Pu Ti
spots.addr: Nanjun Road

spots.name: Wumingzi
spots.desc: Decent, buffet style place.

spots.name: Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: Good and quite fancy.

spots.name: Nicola Coffee
spots.desc: Wen hua gong (文化宫).
spots.addr: Next to Hua qiao hotel (华侨大夏)

spots.name: Zhangzhou Museum
spots.desc: Zhangzhou's main museum.
spots.hours: 09ː00-12ː00, 14ː30-17ː00 (15ː00-17ː30 during the summer), closed on Mondays
spots.addr: Intersection of Yingbin Avenue and Longwen South Road, Longwen District (龙文区迎宾大道与龙文南路加叉口)

spots.name: Changzhou Museum
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:00, closed on Mondays
spots.price: Entry is free. English tour guides are available for ¥100
spots.addr: 1288 Longcheng Avenue, Xinbei District (新北区龙城大道1288号)

spots.name: SUPcz
spots.desc: "Artists Co-op" in Changzhou.

spots.name: Hu Jintao's birthplace
spots.desc: The former Chinese leader Hu Jintao was born in an old neighborhood in Jiangyan. Good luck figuring out which house it is if you don't have a local to show you around—it's not marked in any way. But the old houses are interesting to walk through regardless.

spots.name: Jiaoshan Park
spots.desc: A park on a small island with a mountain on it in the Yangtze River. It includes a temple called Dinghui Temple, a large pagoda, peacock farm, and many winding paths through dense foliage. Bamboo forests partially cover the island.

spots.name: Citadel of Jiaxing
spots.desc: Jiaxing is one of the few cities in south-east China that retains any vestige of a citadel. It's at the center of the old city. The citadel was built in 231 AD, and remained the fortified administrative center of Jiaxing until 1912, when it became a barracks, and later a school and a hospital. Much of the citadel was demolished in the 20th century, and today only the imposing front gate on Fuqian…
spots.addr: Fuqian Street

spots.name: Meiwan Street
spots.local: 梅灣街, Plum Blossom Bay Street
spots.desc: A picturesque neighborhood in the southwest corner of the old city on the bank of the western South Lake, this area has been redeveloped, with several historic buildings restored and new buildings built in a sympathetic style. Apart from the traditional buildings - housing small museums, restaurants and bars - the area features winding brooks, willows and small lakeside parks. It is a favourite…

spots.name: Yuehe Street
spots.desc: Another restored neighbourhood, this one on the north side of the old city, Yuehe Street or "Moon River Street" is named after a system of canals connected to the city moat, so-called because they are curved like the crescent moon. This used to be a centre of traditional commerce and light industry. As opposed to the elegant houses of prominent people featured on Meiwan Street, Yuehe Street…
spots.addr: Zhongji Road and surrounds

spots.name: Xitang Ancient Town Scenic Area
spots.desc: The core of the old town is a scenic area. You must buy a ticket if you are entering on the weekend, but you can avoid this fee by visiting on a weekday, after midnight, or simply by entering the "scenic area" via a small lane rather than one of the main gates (the area is not fenced). It gets very crowded every weekend, as daytrippers from Shanghai, Hangzhou and other nearby cities descend on…
spots.price: ¥100 (weekends), free weekdays and after midnight on weekends
spots.addr: 258 Nanyuan Road (near Shanjiang Highway)

spots.name: Take a boat around South Lake
spots.desc: Be like the Communist Party's founding fathers, and take a boat onto the South Lake! A regular ferry service takes visitors around South Lake and to the island in the middle of the lake to visit the Pavilion of Mist and Rain and the Communist "Red Boat". Tickets are sold only at the main ticket desk on Nanxi West Road. A ¥60 ticket allows you to get off at each stop, explore the sights, and get…
spots.addr: Nanxi West Road, corner of Haiyantang Road (ticket desk)

spots.name: Jinhua Central Lake Park
spots.desc: Central Lake Park is a beautiful urban park in the center of Jinhua City. The park features a picturesque lake, lush green spaces, and walking paths, making it a perfect spot for relaxation, jogging, and family gatherings.
spots.addr: Central

spots.name: Ancient Weir Painting Village
spots.local: 古堰画乡景区(香樟古埠)
spots.desc: Tourist site on both banks of the river. There's small shops, restaurants, cafes, a small temple, bamboo boat rides for ¥20. It's very picturesque and you'll see many with easels painting the area. Some places take commissions if you'd like your portrait done. Ferry rides from one bank to the other are included in the entrance price.
spots.addr: 浙江省丽水市莲都区大港头镇古堰画乡景区

spots.name: East and West Scenic Area, aka Dongxiyan
spots.desc: Dongxi Scenic Area has lots of pretty rock formations, canyons, caves and temples. You can take a circular hiking route that will take maybe 1.5 hours (there's lots of signage everywhere) or just go explore for hours. There's a restaurant and tiny gift shop by the entrance and some small stalls at various points along the trails.
spots.addr: 丽水东西岩景区

spots.name: Panjiayuan Antique Market
spots.desc: Beijing’s largest flea and antique market, now operating largely as a curated mix of antiques, replicas, collectibles, and cultural crafts. While genuine antiques exist, the majority of goods are modern reproductions or decorative items. The market remains popular for browsing and souvenir hunting rather than serious antiquities trading. Bargaining is still expected, especially for higher-priced…
spots.addr: 29 Tianya Hongqiao Rd, Chaoyang

spots.name: Yuyuantan Park
spots.local: 玉渊潭公园; Yùyuāntán Gōngyuán; also known as Jade Lake Park

spots.name: Wuyi Square
spots.desc: The square is ideal for a casual evening stroll, people-watching, and trying local street foods. In the evenings, the area comes alive with vendors and locals hanging out. Several small parks and streets nearby offer additional spots for relaxation or short walks.

spots.local: 伊春兴安森林公园 Yīchūn Xīng'ān Sēnlín Gōngyǘan
spots.desc: A popular attraction for most of the visitors to Yichun. Located just a little south to the city, the park owns 6,093 acres of forest (however only a hill is open for visitors), mostly covered by rare Korean pines. The spring on the way to the top is also popular for Yichun locals, who believe that the water is good for their health. (The spring water is safe to drink, as it's just normal mineral…

spots.name: China Lindu Wood Carving park
spots.local: 中国林都木雕园 Zhōnggúo Líndū Mùdiāoyuán
spots.desc: A park in the west end of the urban area of Yichun City, next to a river, and is home to many famous wooden carvings. The long gallery, with a 160 meter long wood carvings in relief showing the history of Yichun area is one of the must-see sights in the city.

spots.name: Lüshun Railway Station
spots.desc: Built by the Russians between 1900 and 1903 as part of what was then known as the Chinese Eastern Railway. The station is noteworthy for its Russian architectural style. Passenger rail services ceased in 2014, but the station remains open to visitors.
spots.addr: 8 Jinggang Street (井岗街8号)

spots.name: Wanzhong Grave Memorial Hall
spots.desc: The Wanzhong Grave is a mass grave containing the remains of thousands of Chinese soldiers and civilians who were killed by Japanese forces during the infamous Port Arthur Massacre of 1894. The memorial hall at the grave displays photographs and artefacts pertaining to the massacre.
spots.addr: 23 Jiu San Road (九三路23号)

spots.name: Baiyu Mountain Scenic Area
spots.local: 白玉山景区, Baiyushan Scenic Area, Baiyu Hill Scenic Area
spots.desc: This small mountain (130 metres above sea level), is said to offer good views of the Lüshun Military Port. A memorial tower stands at the peak of the mountain. The memorial tower was built by the Japanese to commemorate their victory in the Russo-Japanese War. It now stands as a reminder of the Japanese invasion.
spots.price: Entry is free. The cable car costs ¥15 each way
spots.addr: 158 Baiyushan Street (白玉山街158号

spots.name: Laotie Mountain
spots.desc: This small mountain and the surrounding area constitute the largest part of the Snake Island & Laotie Mountain National Nature Reserve (蛇岛老铁山国家级自然保护区). Besides, natural scenery, the area also features an old lighthouse, which was built in France and erected here by the British in 1893. As of 2018, however, the lighthouse is not open to the public and can only be viewed from the outside.

spots.name: Hengshan North Putuo Cultural Theme Park
spots.local: 横山北普陀主题文化公园, 横山寺森林公园, Hengshan Temple Forest Park

spots.desc: Learn the art of brewing health teas and making medicinal meals based on traditional Chinese medicine practices. Ideal for visitors interested in health and wellness.

spots.name: Folk Handicraft Learning
spots.desc: Learn traditional Tongchuan arts such as paper-cutting and embroidery at the local folk culture center. A great experience for anyone interested in regional handicrafts.

spots.name: Yaoyao Kiln Ceramic Culture Festival
spots.desc: The Yaoyao Kiln Ceramic Culture Festival brings together local ceramic artists and collectors, where visitors can experience pottery making and appreciate traditional ceramic art.
spots.addr: Yaoyao Kiln Museum

spots.name: Yaowang Health and Wellness Culture Festival
spots.desc: A large health and wellness event at Yaowang Mountain, featuring Chinese medicine lectures, Taoist rituals, and traditional handicraft exhibitions.

spots.name: Chenlu Ancient Town Lantern Festival
spots.desc: The lantern festival in Chenlu Ancient Town features beautifully decorated streets, local pottery, and a traditional food market, attracting large numbers of visitors.
spots.addr: Chenlu Ancient Town

spots.name: Feilai Temple
spots.desc: A historic Buddhist temple on the bank of the Beijiang River. The temple was founded in 520 and is one of Qingyuan's most important historic religious sites.
spots.addr: Beijiang River, Qingyuan, Guangdong

spots.desc: A major outdoor attraction with a gorge, waterfalls, glass viewing platforms and rafting. The scenic area is a national 4A tourist attraction and a national sports tourism demonstration base.
spots.hours: Yuntian Boba / Gulong Secret Realm / Great Waterfall Group: 09:00-16:00; rafting season generally runs from mid-April…

spots.name: Dragon Mother Temple

spots.local: 石花水洞地质公园, Shihua Water Cave Geopark
spots.desc: One of Hainan's most beautiful caves. The cave is partly filled with water from a nearby lake. You enter via a dry entrance, and then later board a boat, which will take you out onto the lake. Just beyond the lake, there is a mini stone forest, which includes a rock shaped like a phallus.
spots.price: Standard ticket prices are ¥70 between October and April or ¥58 between May and September; students and persons aged 60…

spots.desc: One of eleven city gates that still survive. Tieniu Gate was built during the Song Dynasty and rebuilt in 1394. It used to be known as Lizheng Gate (丽正门).

spots.name: Qianwei County Confucian Temple
spots.local: 犍为县文庙, 犍为县文庙博物馆 Qianwei County Confucian Temple Museum
spots.desc: This temple, which is on China's national heritage list, was founded during the Northern Song Dynasty and rebuilt during the Ming Dynasty. It is the fourth largest Confucian temple in China and the largest one in Sichuan Province.
