Free internet cafe for customers, 10 computers available. Bar has a fussball table, and roof-top area has a pool table.…
spots.addr: lianfeng lane #44

spots.name: The Brew Yangshuo
spots.desc: Located right in the centre of Yangshuo's nightlife area in a pedestrian zone and is a great place for a few drinks and good western food (pizza and steaks are excellent), very nice music selection. This bar offers a great variety of imported beers (Duvel, Leffe, Stella and Erdinger), and plenty of cocktails as well as harder stuff (absinthe, single malts etc.) They have a foosball table and…
spots.addr: Sunshine 100, E 110 B

spots.name: The London Tavern - Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: The London Tavern is an authentic English pub right in the middle of Yangshuo. They sell London Pride and other beers on draught and carry a reasonably wide selection of bottled English ales. The manager is English and they sell the best British food in Yangshuo. A hangout for local expats who drop in for a taste of home and even a game of darts!
spots.addr: Guihua Rd

spots.name: Rusty Bolt
spots.desc: As the sun sets, Bike Asia turns into the Rusty Bolt, a hangout for climbers and cyclists. An interesting mix of folks who have been in town for hours, months and years. Wednesday the bar hosts a card game night. Thursday is a dice game night (Farkle) starting at 20:30. Other bars on West Street often have very overpriced drinks and too-loud techno music; this place has neither offering more of a…
spots.addr: 22 Guihua Rd

spots.name: Huangyao Ancient Town
spots.desc: Huangyao Ancient Town is just over an hour outside of Yangshuo by coach. It is a lovely, rustic old town where the film, "The Painted Veil" was shot.

spots.name: Beili Village
spots.desc: Founded around 2000 years ago, during the Han Dynasty, Beili Village was originally known as Changxing Village. By the Ming Dynasty, the village had become quite prosperous thanks due to its location on the Beili River. Gradually, however, the river became silted up and Beili's usefulness as a port began to decline. The final blow to the village economy came during the Second World War, when the…

spots.name: Burial site of laborers killed in Basuo during the Japanese occupation of Hainan
spots.local: 日军侵琼八所死难劳工遗址
spots.desc: During their occupation of Hainan, the Japanese army used forced labor to complete several infrastructure projects on the island, most notably the Daguang Dam in eastern Dongfang, the Shilu Iron Ore Mine in Changjiang County and the railway line connecting the mine to the ports in Basuo and Sanya. At first the Japanese mainly relied on Chinese labor but later they began importing POWs that they…
spots.addr: Intersection of Bianmao Road and Bianmao Yi Heng Road (边贸路与边贸一横路交汇)

spots.name: Hainan Railway Museum
spots.desc: A museum about the history of railways on Hainan Island. Hainan's first railway line was built by the Japanese army in the 1940s using forced labour. The museum's main exhibition hall was originally a Japanese military command center and was later converted into an office for the Hainan Railway Company.
spots.addr: Binhai Road South (滨海南路)

spots.name: Yulinzhou Scenic Area
spots.desc: A small scenic area on the coast near Basuo Port. The main feature is a large rock with a lighthouse on top. This is probably the most recognizable landmark in Dongfang.
spots.addr: Jiefang Road West (解放西路)

spots.name: Baicha Village
spots.desc: Considered to be the best-preserved traditional Li minority village in Hainan. The village is comprised entirely of boat-shaped thatched cottages. Many of the original inhabitants no longer live here, however, so today the village is more like an open-air museum than a living village.

spots.name: Exian Ridge
spots.desc: Possibly one of Hainan's best-kept secrets, the park features karst scenery similar to that normally associated with Guilin. Hence it is sometimes referred to informally as Little Guilin (小桂林). As of January 2021, however, the infrastructure at the park is under development and parts of the park are either closed off or subject to intermittent closure. Therefore, if you are considering visiting…

spots.name: Gull Force Memorial
spots.desc: A small memorial dedicated to the Gull Force. a battalion of Australian soldiers who were defeated by the Japanese in the Battle of Ambon in 1942. 263 of the captured soldiers were brought to Hainan to work as laborers. Some of the soldiers managed to escape from the Basuo labor camp with the help of local resistance fighters. Two of them later died from disease and are buried in a grave near the…
spots.addr: Lao'ou Village (老欧村)

spots.name: Hai Dongfang Park
spots.desc: A beach park with a Ferris wheel and a few other amusement rides.
spots.price: Entry to the park is free
spots.addr: Haijing Road, Basuo (八所镇海景路)

spots.name: Baishi Ridge Scenic Area
spots.local: 白石岭风景区, White Stone Ridge Scenic Area
spots.desc: Baishi Ridge, which stands 326 metres above sea level, is the highest land formation in Qionghai. There is an old Buddhist temple near the summit.
spots.price: Entry fee: ¥30 (off-peak season), ¥36 (peak season). Cable car ticket: ¥45
spots.addr: Jiaji Town (嘉积镇)

spots.name: Coconut Village Battle Site
spots.desc: This was the site of the Battle of Coconut Village (1927), the first battle of the Chinese Civil War to take place on Hainan Island. There is a monument and a small museum at the site.
spots.addr: Intersection of Bashiling Avenue and County Highway 356, Jiaji Town (嘉积镇白石岭大道与356县道交叉)

spots.name: Duohe Culture Valley
spots.desc: A cultural park that aims to educate visitors about the history and culture of the Wanquan River region. There are statues of famous figures such as Madam Xian, a famous 6th century female military leader from Guangdong who is credited with bringing an end to the uprisings that had plagued the island since it became part of the Chinese empire. There is also a small Buddhist temple and a folk…
spots.addr: Yonggan Village, Xinghai Road, Jiaji Town (嘉积镇兴海南路勇敢村)

spots.name: Red Detachment of Women Memorial Park
spots.desc: Dedicated of course to the famous Red Detachment of Women, a Red Army affiliated detachment of female soldiers who fought the Nationalists during the Chinese Civil War. There is a small museum in the middle of the park. Other sights in the park include a mural and an assortment of disused military equipment.
spots.addr: Jiaji Town (嘉积镇)

spots.name: Red Detachment of Women statue
spots.desc: A statue representing a member of the Red Detachment of Women. The statue may not be particularly impressive (there's a bigger one at the memorial park). Nonetheless it's probably the most recognizable landmark in downtown Qionghai.
spots.addr: 73 Dongfeng Road, Jiaji Town (嘉积镇东风路73号)

spots.name: 紫悦汤面
spots.desc: The store is decorated in a tropical style, and the wooden tables and chairs are more distinctive. Pasta, fast food, fresh juice, etc.
spots.addr: Domestic Terminal Building Security Check Phase 3 Remote Aircraft Stand

spots.name: Hainan Qilou
spots.desc: Hainan Qilou Old Street is the most distinctive streetscape in Hainan and has won the title of the first ten "Famous Historical and Cultural Streets in China" for its uniqueness and distinctiveness. The restaurant has a strong Hainan style, which can taste Hainan specialties.

spots.name: N18° Restaurant Bar
spots.desc: This fast-food restaurant mainly serves simple meals and drinks.
spots.addr: Domestic Terminal Security Check B1-1, International Terminal Security Check Gate 4-5

spots.name: Phoenix Impression Restaurant
spots.desc: Phoenix Impression Restaurant offers a wide range of Chinese food, special set meals and Hainan local specialties.

spots.name: Weiyi Noodle House
spots.desc: “Weiyi Noodle House” is a specialty noodle house that mainly sells noodles from all over China and has its own innovative noodle brand.

spots.name: Yogurt HO
spots.desc: Yogurt HO yogurt ice cream originated in the United States. The company uses green and healthy ingredients to make ice cream, and yogurt soft ice cream of various flavors and types. It also sells cold drinks of various flavors and Western desserts.

spots.name: Kentucky
spots.desc: Western fast food such as fried chicken, hamburgers, French fries, and soda.

spots.desc: These stone carvings began in the Sui Dynasty and continued through the Tang Dynasty, and along with the Song Dynasty continued through the Republican era, very interesting to see some of the stone statues and learn about history through them.
spots.addr: Nankan Mountain, 5 km south of the city

spots.name: Micangshan National Forest Park
spots.desc: Micangshan National Forest Park, located on the southern slopes of the Micang Mountains in the Qinba Mountains, covers a total area of 40,155 hectares. The forest has a coverage rate of 97.3% with a total standing timber volume of 2.4 million cubic meters, earning it the nickname "Natural Oxygen Bar." The park was established in 1995, designated as a National Forest Park in 2002, and recognized…
spots.addr: Nanjiang County

spots.name: Tongjiang silver tree-ear fungus
spots.desc: Bazhong is the birthplace of the silver fungus, known as the hometown of China's silver fungus, cooking is quite delicious, especially silver fungus soup. Available in local supermarkets and other speciality shops.
spots.addr: Tongjiang County

spots.name: Luo Cun tea
spots.desc: Local speciality tea of Pingchang County, with a taste similar to green tea.
spots.addr: Available in supermarkets

spots.name: Nanjiang yellow sheep
spots.desc: Famous for the taste of its meat due to its unique rearing method, you can see many lamb shops advertising discounted Nanjiang yellow sheep on the streets in winter.

spots.name: Bashan ginkgo (tree with fan-shaped leaves and yellow seeds)
spots.desc: Because of its unique geographical characteristics, as a ginkgo suitable for growing areas of high nutritional value of the white fruit, you can buy a taste!

spots.name: Zao Lin Fish Flagship Store (Hui Feng)
spots.desc: A variety of fish soups made from wild fish, ranging from clear to spicy, are locally famous.
spots.addr: No. 120, Huifeng North Road, Bazhou District

spots.name: Grandma's Pot Rice (Jiangbei Avenue)
spots.local: 阿婆罐罐饭(江北大道店)
spots.desc: A small, ordinary restaurant in an obvious location, but with great flavours, Szechuan cuisine, rice made in a casserole tastes great and is not too expensive.
spots.addr: No.378, Middle Section of Jiangbei Avenue, Jiangbei Street, Bazhou District

spots.name: QianGuo Xin (Main Store)
spots.desc: The food is plentiful and slightly heavy on the flavours. Famous for its ribs in dry pots, goose palms, etc., but also a lot of soup pots, which have been open locally for many years, with several branches.
spots.addr: Approx. 110 metres north-east of No. 4 Primary School, Wenquan Lane, Bazhou District

spots.name: Li Tangyuan Speciality Snacks
spots.desc: It's an old shop that's been open for 20 or 30 years, specialising in noodles and rice noodles, as well as soup dumplings, which are tasty and inexpensive.
spots.addr: 88 Nanquansi Street, Bazhong

spots.name: Lui's BBQ (Main)
spots.desc: Grilled on a tin plate, the dishes are plentiful, with a variety of meats and vegetables, and the dishes are marinated in advance for good flavour.
spots.addr: No. 316, middle section of North Binhe Road, Bazhou District

spots.name: Kajia Mentor Sai Wah Home (Sai Wah Street Shop)
spots.local: 加佳名特西华家园(西华街店)
spots.desc: Medium to large restaurant with halls and private rooms, mainly Sichuan cuisine, all tastes OK.
spots.addr: 150 Xihua Street, Bazhou District

spots.name: Kiwi Chicken Village (Wah Chuan Mansion)
spots.desc: A restaurant with chicken as the main dish, freshly made to order, whole chickens made into different dishes, featuring spicy fried chicken, which tastes spicy and fresh, very tasty.
spots.addr: No.157, Middle Section of Jiangbei Avenue, Jiangbei Street, Bazhou District

spots.name: Old Town Roasted Vegetables
spots.desc: A small restaurant with two floors, to every meal time business is very hot, their speciality is limited daily stews, the soup is very good, other stir-fry dishes are also good.
spots.addr: 20 Wenquan Lane, Bazhou District

spots.name: Laowu Pork Bun Shop
spots.desc: A very small breakfast place that sells freshly made and steamed pork buns with sauce, which have a strong flavour, followed by noodles and various other common breakfast items.
spots.addr: No. 89, Hongjun Road, Bazhou District

spots.name: Wang Bao Qi Sesame Pepper Fish
spots.desc: The fish hotpot made with Sichuan style hotpot as the seasoning is numbing and fragrant. The flavour is good and the price is not too expensive.
spots.addr: No.51 Xihua Street, Bazhou District - 1F Jindu Xijin

spots.name: Yipin Tea House (一品茶楼)
spots.desc: A traditional Chinese tea house offering green tea, jasmine tea, and pu’er tea. The taste is smooth and mellow, suitable for long, relaxing conversations. Mostly visited by local residents and elderly customers.
spots.addr: Near Jiangbei Avenue, Bazhou District (巴州区江北大道附近)

spots.name: Shuxiang Tea House (蜀香茶馆)
spots.desc: Provides covered-bowl tea (盖碗茶) with a strong tea fragrance and slight bitterness that fades into a sweet aftertaste. A good place to observe local daily life.
spots.addr: Residential area near the old town of Bazhong (巴中老城区附近)

spots.name: Night Beer Street (夜啤酒街)
spots.desc: A casual evening area with outdoor seating serving draft beer, bottled local beer, barbecue, and spicy Sichuan snacks. Beer is light and refreshing, while the food is typically spicy and oily. Best visited after 7 PM.
spots.addr: Near Binhe Road, Bazhou District (巴州区滨河路附近)

spots.name: Local BBQ Beer Stall (烧烤啤酒摊)
spots.desc: Simple roadside stalls offering cold draft beer and bottled Snow Beer (雪花啤酒). The beer is mild and crisp, ideal with grilled lamb skewers and spicy tofu.
spots.addr: Around Central Night Market, Bazhou District (巴州区夜市周边)

spots.name: Batai Mountains
spots.desc: Batai Mountains is a National AAAA Tourist Attraction and a National Geopark. Its main peak, Xinbatai, rises to 2,272.3 meters and is known as the “Second Peak of Bashan.” The mountains feature unique peaks shrouded in mist, with ever-changing landscapes. With abundant rainfall and ample sunlight, the area offers distinctive natural phenomena such as sunrises, Buddha’s rays, seas of clouds, and…
spots.addr: Northern Dazhou

spots.name: Bashan Grand Canyon
spots.desc: Bashan Grand Canyon, once called Xuanhan Bailixia, is a national 4A-level scenic spot, geological park, and nature reserve. Known for its karst landscapes and historical relics, it is also the birthplace of the Tujia folk music Hao Cao Luo Gu. The area offers two routes: Route A (best in summer) and Route B (best in winter).
spots.addr: Xuanhan County

spots.name: Wufeng Mountain National Forest Park
spots.desc: Wufengshan National Forest Park, also known as "Bamboo Sea Park," covers a total area of 876 hectares, with an elevation ranging from 600 to 1,080 meters. It has a subtropical humid climate, an average annual temperature of 12.5°C, distinct four seasons, abundant rainfall, and mild winters and cool summers. The park is dominated by bamboo forests and also features forest ecosystems, lakes, and…
spots.addr: Dazhu County, Dazhou City

spots.name: Dazhou Phoenix Mountain Park
spots.desc: Phoenix Mountain Park, named for its mountain shape resembling a phoenix in flight, is a forested urban park and the largest city park in Dazhou. Key attractions within the park include Phoenix Tower, Phoenix Pavilion, Red Army Pavilion, Songjun Pavilion, the Yuan Zhen Memorial Hall, and several cultural squares.
spots.addr: Tongchuan District

spots.name: Wufengshan National Forest Park
spots.desc: National AAA tourist area and national forest park. Also known as Zhuhai Park, it is located in Wufeng Mountain, Yuehua Township, Dazhu County. It is 18 km away from the county seat. It is named because of its vast bamboo area and various types of bamboo. The scenery in the scenic area is beautiful, with a vast sea of bamboo, lush trees and gorgeous mountain flowers.
spots.addr: Wufeng Mountain, Yuehua Township, Dazhu County

spots.name: True Buddha Mountain
spots.desc: It consists of cultural landscapes such as Dehua Temple, Jade Buddha Temple, Jingang Temple, and Lingyun Village, as well as natural landscapes such as Rouge Lake, Sanxian Stone, Conch Cave, Lotus Temple, Yunhua Mountain, and Daojiliang. It has a long historical and cultural background and a simple and profound The connotation of folk customs.
spots.addr: Tingbai Road, Fushan Town, Dachuan District

spots.name: Daxian light shadow beef
spots.desc: Daxian Danying Beef is a local traditional food in Dazhou. Many large supermarkets carry it. Lantern shadow beef has a history of more than 100 years, the beef tendon after slicing, curing, drying, steaming, frying and other procedures made. It is named for its thin and wide slices of meat, which can be seen through the shadow of a lamp and have the effect of a folk shadow play. Meat thin as…

spots.name: Dongliu glutinous rice wine
spots.desc: Dongliu glutinous rice is a local specialty of Daxian County, famous for its delicious taste and fine production. It is made from glutinous rice, koji medicine and other materials through fermentation. It has the effects of nourishing qi and activating blood, nourishing yin and kidney, producing body fluid and quenching thirst.

spots.name: Kai Jiang Bean Bamboo Shoots
spots.desc: Kaijiang bean bamboo shoots are a local specialty of Kaijiang County, Dazhou City, and are also an intangible cultural heritage. It is made from soybeans and refined through more than a dozen processes. It is rich in nutrients and has a strong taste. It can be stewed, stir-fried, pot-baked, etc. It can also be used for hot pot, cold dishes, etc.

spots.name: Kaijiang salted duck
spots.desc: Renshi salted duck is a local specialty of Kaijiang County. It is made from Kaijiang duck as raw material, pickled and baked. Its salted duck has golden color, tough meat, unique flavor, rich fragrance and rich nutrition.

spots.name: Dazhou Crispy Plum
spots.desc: Known for its refreshing, crispy and sweet taste. The fruit is plump, bright in color, crisp but not dry at the same time, and juicy enough. One bite satisfies all the senses.

spots.name: Xichang Ancient City
spots.desc: Not exactly one of the finest ancient cities in China. Most iconic building is the Ming era city gate (巍巍大通门).

spots.name: Liangshan Yi Slave Society Museum
spots.local: 凉山彝族奴隶社会博物馆
spots.desc: Slavery remained in the Liangshan area until the 1960s. This is the only museum in China with exhibitions on the slavery system of the Yi people.
spots.addr: 6 Lushan Road (泸山路6号)

spots.name: Qionghai Lake and Lushan Mountain Scenic Area
spots.desc: Qionghai Lake and Lushan Mountain are south of the city center. There is a surrounding wetlands area with a bike path which is approximately 40 km all around. There is a ticket fee of ¥55, but there are many sections of the lake which can be accessed without purchasing a ticket.

spots.name: Luoji Mountain
spots.desc: It spans two counties and one city, Puge, Dechang, and Xichang, and is the Qiong It is part of the Hai-Luoji Mountain Scenic Area and is the largest Yi-inhabited area in China. It has simple folk customs and culture. The tourist area covers more than 1,000 km². The main peak is 4,359 meters above sea level. There are 72 peaks above 4,000 meters above sea level. Because the main peak towers into…
spots.addr: Luojishan Avenue, Luojishan Town, Puge County

spots.name: Xichang Dashiban Ancient Village
spots.desc: It is a rural revitalization demonstration area supported by Liangshan Prefecture and Xichang City. The ancient village was built in the Ming Dynasty and rebuilt during the Daoguang period of the Qing Dynasty. With a history of nearly 600 years, it was an important town and post station on the ancient "Southern Silk Road" and the Ancient Tea Horse Road. The ancient village is located in Qionghai…
spots.addr: Hainan Street

spots.name: Xichang Satellite Launch Center
spots.desc: Xichang Satellite Launch Center (XSLC) was founded in 1970 and delivered for use in 1982. Since the launch of China's first communication satellite in January 1984, it has carried out more than a hundred satellite launches at home and abroad.
spots.addr: Zeyuan Township, Aerospace North Road

spots.name: Qionghai National Wetland Park
spots.desc: A plateau wetland nature reserve with high ecological value, it is one of the largest urban wetland parks in the city. The total area of the wetland is about 20,000 acres. It has multiple functions of conserving water sources, regulating urban microclimate, purifying water quality, and providing habitats for animals and plants and ecological landscapes.

spots.name: Moonlight style town
spots.desc: It is one of the three most beautiful tourist towns in Liangshan. It is composed of moonlight culture and fishermen culture. Its natural style The ethnic customs can be compared with Erhai Lake and Kuanzhai Alley. It is a scenic spot to appreciate the customs of Liangshan.

spots.name: Small fishing village
spots.desc: The small fishing village is the most important natural fishing base in Qionghai. Because Qionghai is an important natural fishery base in Liangshan Prefecture, there were 829 fishermen in Qionghai in the past. They mainly lived here, so they were named "small fishing villages". With the continuous development of society, most of them no longer make a living from fishing.

spots.name: Dada Shopping Plaza
spots.desc: the largest shopping mall in Xichang and has three branches in Xichang.
spots.addr: Pedestrian Street in Xichang City

spots.name: Nantan Farmers Market
spots.desc: Here you can achieve fruit freedom! There are all kinds of fruits including strawberries, mangoes, and blueberries.
spots.addr: The junction of Southeast Street and Shizhu Road, Xichang City

spots.name: Mianning Local Restaurant
spots.desc: The cuisine is Sichuan cuisine, and the per capita consumption is about ¥42. Recommended dishes: Two pepper mushrooms, tofu, three delicacies, crispy broth, chanterelles, stir-fried meat, Qionghai Lingjiao, stir-fried ham, golden bars, bee pupae, vegetables, stir-fried ham, twice-cooked meat, drunken shrimps, cold crucian carp, Qionghai drunken shrimps, sour and spicy fungus, potato sauerkraut…
spots.addr: Section 1, Haiting Road in Liangshan

spots.name: Old Town
spots.desc: The old town is rapidly being turned into a mini-Lijiang, complete with endless shophouses selling tourist trinkets (including fake tiger skins and counterfeit North Face jackets), minority costumed dancers and too-clean streets. However, there are still plenty of small charming streets to explore. The temple at the top of the hill gives a free taste of what can be seen in Songzanlin Monastery.…

spots.name: Horses
spots.desc: Tibetan horses are available for hire outside of town. Taxi drivers should know how to get there.

spots.name: Biking around Napa Lake
spots.desc: Rent a mountain bike and ride out into the grasslands west of the Old Town near Napa Lake. There are checkpoints on the road that stop bikers and ask them to buy a ¥60 Napa Lake Ticket. It is possible to avoid this depending upon where you ride, however villagers can get aggressive if they stop you and you refuse to pay. Do not attempt to ride the full 30 km around the lake because the road on…

spots.name: Nixi Tibetan Village
spots.desc: Archaeological evidence shows that the Tibetan tradition of crafting pottery in Nixi Village dates back at least 2,000 years. Visit the master potters and learn to make the pottery; have lunch in a traditional Tibetan home; take a walk or hike around this scenic village.

spots.name: Private homes
spots.desc: Visit the homes of local people. Many of the locals open up their homes to tourists. They ask for a small fee to compensate for the food. You can hang out with the family, and the younger adults will lead you to ride horses in the open field. Mind you the Tibetan horses are trained, but they can be very unfriendly towards strangers.

spots.name: Skiing
spots.desc: A new ski resort has opened. T-bars and chair lifts available.
spots.price: Price starts at ¥160 (including all equipment, fees) for 2 hours

spots.name: Countryside
spots.desc: Hire a vehicle for a few hours to just explore the countryside, or rent bikes and go see the surrounding villages.

spots.name: Shika Mountain
spots.local: 石卡山; Shí​kǎ​shān; also known as Blue Moon Valley (蓝月谷; Lán​yuè​gǔ​)​
spots.desc: Climb the mountain or take cable car (¥220, 45-minute ride to the top).

spots.name: Thin Air Adventures
spots.desc: Thin Air Adventures provides horseback riding and guided mountain biking tours in the area's surrounding Shangri-la (Zhongdian). No office was to be found in Aug 2017 in the old town. Best is to SMS or contact through Web site.

spots.name: Tianshenqiao Hot springs
spots.desc: Natural outdoor amphitheatre. Public bath mostly Chinese, women may feel uncomfortable.
spots.price: A bit expensive. ¥20 per person park entry fee plus ¥80–200 per person for public/private hot springs

spots.name: Turtle Mountain Gear and Outfitters
spots.desc: TMG has camping and outdoor gear rental, motorbike rental, and jeep hires. They take people on hiking and backpacking trips in the surrounding area or can point you in the right direction to go on your own. They don't have an agency in the old town anymore. The best way to contact them is to send a SMS to the phone number on their web site (WhatsApp mentioned there but not used since Jan 2017.…

spots.name: Dropenling Tibetan Handicraft Center
spots.desc: A non-profit social enterprise handicraft project selling high-quality, authentic Tibetan handicrafts from over 500 artisans, both local in DiQing Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture and from the Tibet Autonomous Region. All profits are reinvested into the sustainability of the enterprise and the Tibetan artisan community in the form of technical and business training, business loans, and product…
spots.addr: Old Town

spots.name: Arro Khampa !
spots.desc: Tibetan cuisine. Run by a Franco-Chinese couple, Damien and Ting, Arro Khampa is a local restaurant housed in an authentic two-storey Tibetan house in the middle of the Old Town. The restaurant offers a wide range of classic Tibetan dishes and nice French wines. Its Tibetan-French raclette is unique in Yunnan.
spots.addr: Pijiang po, Old Town

spots.name: Bhaskar's Kitchen
spots.desc: Himalayan cuisine. Rated the top eatery in Shangri-la, Bhaskar's Kitchen has a reputation throughout Yunnan for the quality of its food, due largely to its chef: Nepalise chef Bhaskar, who prepared fresh a variety of Nepalise, Indian and Tibetan dishes. Authentic cuisine, cosy atmosphere and friendly staff make it place for travellers, foreigners living in town, monks, musicians and locals. Best…
spots.addr: Dawa Road, across from old town entrance and car park, Old Town

spots.name: Compass Cafe
spots.desc: Serves excellent authentic Western food (homemade spaghetti sauce!) and delicious cakes. Equipped with an Espresso machine. Cozy atmosphere, it has several heaters and is great for family. Free wireless available. In & Out bakery next door sells breads, muffins and other savouries.

spots.name: Karma Cafe
spots.desc: Good food and hospitable staff. Owner Afang speaks perfect English. Not located in busy old town but off the beaten path. Tibetan house and meals, though western meals are also served. Rooms available, though only two rooms.

spots.name: Hiker's Coffee
spots.desc: Established by Charles Tang. He loves hiking very much. You can take bus No. 1 or No. 3 to "Huajun Square". "Huajun Square" is just across from "Sto Express". If you raise your head, you can just see four Chinese words "华骏广场". Then follow the arrow on the map and find "Building 8B". After reaching the 4th floor, you will turn right in the hallway and get to "Hiker's Coffee" immediately. Western…
spots.addr: Room 409, Building 8B, Huajun Square, Changzheng Road, Shangri-La, Diqing, Yunnan, China

spots.name: Hongxin Restaurant
spots.desc: Decent restaurant, serves some Tibetan dishes (baba, pipa meat).
spots.addr: Heping Road

spots.name: Korean Restaurant
spots.desc: Tasty Korean fare including seafood pancakes, sushi, zucchini rolls, table-top BBQ, bibimbap. They rent bikes from the front of restaurant (¥20-30), and the boss even has a private stash of higher quality mountain bikes in storage for a slightly higher rental price. He will give you his cell number and come out to help you if you have any trouble with the bikes.

spots.name: The Olive (previously Noah Cafe and Inn)
spots.desc: Best western food in town. Also Middle Eastern food. Free Wireless available. Their guest house is just across the street. 100m west of the old town square.

spots.name: Puppet Restaurant
spots.desc: Great Tibetan food in a warm and friendly atmosphere, although there is only one page of the Tibetan food in their menu. They also serve Indian and Korean cuisine. Full of locals rather than tourists. If you have a sweet tooth, 奶渣炒面团 is worthwhile trying.
spots.addr: Old Town Street

spots.name: Sean's Cafe No 2
spots.desc: Authentic Tibetan food, great for breakfast. The Tibetan porridge and yak cheese dumplings are recommended. Daisy, daughter of the Tiger Leaping Gorge's Sean, speaks great English and can give good local travel advice.
spots.addr: North Gate Street, Old Town

spots.name: The Shangri-La Yak Cheese Shop
spots.desc: A specialty cheese shop that produces locally sourced yak cheese with Western methods. Great selection of local wines to pair with the cheese, as well as a wide selection of cheese-inspired local and Western dishes.
spots.addr: No. 3 Chi Lang Shuo, Old Town

spots.name: Soyala Tibetan Diner & Bar
spots.desc: Burgers, patties and dumplings are made with free range 100% organic Yak meat and burger buns are prepared daily. The restaurant staff are former residents from the Children Charity Tendol Gyalzur in both Shangrila/Gyalthang and Duilong/Lhasa. The owner is a Swiss-born and educated ethnic Tibetan married to a local Tibetan. Good pizza, great Lentil soup, and tasty Shangrila brand beer (go…
spots.addr: Cangfang St 1

spots.name: N's kitchen
spots.desc: Bread served by French baker, Good quality western food, nice breakfast menu, cozy place with sunshine design. Best yak burger in town.
spots.addr: old town, 5 meters to main squre

spots.name: Yunnan Mountain Heritage Center
spots.desc: A locally-run non-profit organization dedicated to preserving Yunnan heritage, the YMHC features a shop selling local traditional handicrafts from the Tibetan, Yi, and Naxi peoples and a Small Library with books in Chinese, Tibetan, and English. Volunteers from across China and abroad contribute to a diverse and lively environment, teaching free English and Chinese classes to local Tibetans…
spots.addr: Old Town

spots.name: Black Pottery Coffee
spots.desc: The owners of Black Pottery Coffee, Russ & Kesang, know the region well, so you can get up to date travel information and arrange local excursions with them. They specialize in day trips to Kesang's village, and trekking at Meili Snow Mountain 梅里雪山 (Kawa Karpo). Kesang, Russ, and their daughter Fei Fei, will make you feel welcome in Shangri-la, and help you plan your adventures there. The Cafe…
spots.addr: Old Town, Cang Fang Street, #5 Chi Lang Gang

spots.name: Tashiis Lodge/Guesthouse
spots.desc: Where European cuisine mixes with a quiet gentle breeze of Tibetan infuence. It is pretty good, but who's goes for the food though?

spots.name: Helen's Pizza Ristorante
spots.desc: When you feel like a respite from local food the friendly and helpful English speaking Italian owner serves authentic pizzas and pastas.The homemade tagliatelle is particularly good. And best pizza in Yunnan. Serves also Chinese and Korean food and excellent curries and Indian tee. The stove at the window table is very comforting on a cold night and the owner is very willing to give advice and…
spots.addr: Dawa Road Zhong Dian

spots.name: Marco Polo
spots.desc: Excellent Western Food at reasonable prices. Good pizza. Opened in July 2010 and run by Dawan who set up N's Kitchen and restaurant and established the western menu there.
spots.addr: Opposite the Raven Pub

spots.name: Shangri-La Beer
spots.desc: Shangri-La Beer is the only craft brewery of its kind in China. Their local Tibetan beers are brewed using only 3 all-natural ingredients (Tibetan mountain spring water, Tibetan barley, and premium hops) and come in six varieties, from a dry lager to the newly released Fat Douma, a sweeter, double bock wheat beer. It was founded in 2015 by Swiss businessman Sonny, of Tibetan heritage. His parents…
spots.price: brewery tours are ¥80-90 per person, bottles ¥15-30
spots.addr: Qingkou Industrial District

spots.name: Gyalthang Dzong Hotel
spots.desc: Opened in 1996, the hotel is the home base for travelers heading to/from the Kham region of Tibet and beyond. Beautifully situated on an alpine meadow in the lap of Rutapo Hill, it was designed in the traditional Tibetan dzong architectural style. The renovation preserved the traditional character of the hotel and enhanced many of the Tibetan aesthetic elements, while making it more comfortable…

spots.name: The Compass Lodge
spots.desc: Has 4 units of town house that are suitable for families, fully heated (double story per unit), as well as 4 new budget rooms for backpackers at a lower price.

spots.name: Banyan Tree Ringha
spots.desc: A wonderful resort in a stunning location. Each private 2-storey villa is gorgeously appointed and fully heated, with 24 hours hot water supply and wireless access. The spa is excellent, and with the most gracious and attentive of staff, the service is just downright amazing all round, all of the time.

spots.name: Shangri-la Dara Glamping
spots.desc: This is the first glamping with traditional yurts/gers in the Tibetan County of Shangrila or Gyalthang. 15 minutes from Shangrila Old Town and 10 min from the airport. Come to enjoy the nature in the Tibetan "Dara Village". They are next to their partner "Dara Eco-lodge", so you can also use all their facilities (hot shower, meals, etc). They have trekking programs, hiking, horse riding, biking…

spots.name: Moon Bay Wetland Park
spots.desc: A lakeside wetland park on the northeastern shore of Fuxian Lake, with walking paths, open lawns and views across the lake. It is a popular stop for short walks and lakeside sightseeing.
spots.addr: near No. 8 Huanhu North Road

spots.name: Huxianfu Fish Restaurant
spots.desc: A local restaurant in Guanglong Town specialising in fish dishes and regional Yunnan cuisine, convenient for visitors staying around the northern shore of Fuxian Lake.
spots.addr: Building 37, B101, Dongpu Liuhong, Guanglong Town

spots.name: Mengle Temple
spots.desc: The biggest temple in Xishuangbanna. In the southern area in Jionghong, you can hire bicycle to go there.
spots.addr: No. 1 Mengle Ave

spots.name: Manlei Temple
spots.desc: A tranquil temple that offers insight into local Buddhist practices and a serene escape from daily life.

spots.name: Tropical Flowers and Plant Garden
spots.desc: Large park visited by many Chinese tour groups. Definitely a disappointment for foreign tourists.
spots.addr: Yunnan Institute of Tropical Crops Science, 99 Xuanwei Avenue

spots.name: Peacock Lake Park
spots.desc: A pleasant "park" with an artificial lake and a fountain. If it's not raining, during the evening check the corner just outside the park on the roundabout, locals gather and dance on the open for many hours.
spots.addr: crossroads of Mengle Dadao and Xuanwei Dadao

spots.name: Wangtianshu Scenic Area
spots.desc: This rainforest reserve features towering trees, a skywalk, and an abundance of biodiversity.

spots.name: Tropical Rainforests
spots.desc: Enjoy the exotic flora and fauna in the forests surrounding Menghai, perfect for eco-tourism.

spots.name: Dai Villages
spots.desc: Visit traditional Dai villages, where you can see bamboo houses, colorful festivals, and experience their hospitality.

spots.name: Local Markets
spots.desc: Visit morning or night markets to taste fresh, authentic street food.

spots.name: Songkran
spots.desc: If you are in the town during the Thai (Dai in that area) New year there is a massive celebration with Dragon boating and capped off with a massive city wide water fight on the final day of celebration.

spots.name: Riverfront Walks
spots.desc: The town is on the Nancang River, a wide tributary of the Mekong. There is excellent walking along the riverfront.

spots.name: Mekong Starlight Night Market
spots.desc: Every night there is a big night market in Xishuangbanna Park just on the right of the New Bridge. (The new bridge is the suspension bridge all lit up at night, and the right side is looking at it as you would be leaving Jinghong across it). You can buy almost anything here and there are endless street food stalls. The river side is all bars serving food, some with good live music.
spots.addr: Gaozhuang Xishuangshi Scenic Spot, on the right side of the New Bridge

spots.name: Riverside Night Market
spots.desc: It takes approximately 1 hour and 15 minutes to walk from start to finish without stopping. It's a very long night market stretching along the river, offering a great variety of local specialty clothing, snacks, toys, and souvenirs. It's very lively, and the prices are quite reasonable.
spots.addr: West side of Thailand Street, Binjiang Avenue, Yunjinghong Sub-district

spots.name: Thailand Avenue (Tai Guo Jie)
spots.desc: A large open market and Thai themed stores centered around a stage. There are at least two bars on premise. Free live music at night at around 19:00.

spots.name: Xishuangbanna pedlars' market
spots.desc: It is the largest market in the area and many locals also go there to buy food. There are plenty of local speciality vegetables and meats, as well as some gourmet meals made on-site, for which you only have to pay a processing fee. If you want to know more about the food culture of this place, it is highly recommended that you visit this place.
spots.addr: No.3 Mengla Road

spots.name: Mange market

spots.name: Happiness Alley
spots.desc: If you happen to be nearby, it's worth to see the cafés, the pond, the fountain and the funny statue on this alley-shortcut between Panyu Road and Xingfu Road.
spots.addr: 381 Panyu Road

spots.name: Cloud Nine shopping center
spots.desc: 9 flours above ground (hence the name) and 2 below heading into metro line 2. Floors 1 to 5 are mainly clothing and fashion accessory Asian and western brands. Floors 6, 7 and 8 have an extensive selection of good restaurants. In the basement is a Carrefour supermarket, a small pharmacy and plenty of fast food restaurants. Worth a look.

spots.name: Xujiahui Park
spots.desc: On the location of a former brick factory now stands the Xujiahui Park, which contains a man-made meandering brook (modelling in miniature the course of the Huangpu River), a lake with two black swans, basketball courts, and a children's playground.

spots.name: Former site of Pathé
spots.desc: The Red House, which once housed the Pathé China record company, is at the edge of Xujiahui Park.
spots.addr: 811 Hengshan Road

spots.name: Metro station exhibition
spots.desc: Small, free museum exhibition at Shanghai Xujiahui station between exits 5 and 7. The exhibits are changed several times a year and sometimes English explanations are included. The history or tradition-related items are brought from nearby museums.

spots.name: ASE Mall
spots.desc: A huge mall finished in 2017, hosting mostly elite and highly decorated restaurants, Will's Fitness and a cinema. The building features a panoramic elevator, an inner yard, and neon signs that resemble old shopping streets.
spots.addr: 33 Caobao Road

spots.name: North Bund and Shikumen Houses
spots.desc: A pleasant walk would start from International Cruise Terminal metro station, line 12. Visit the Baiyulan Square Shopping Center to admire its architecture. Then head towards the river and a bit to the right, where you can climb and jump in the adventure park, both adults and children. Walk along the river bank towards east, you will find old pictures and stories about the wharf and see ships…

spots.name: Confucius Temple
spots.desc: Large and well preserved temple built in 1219. Nowadays it is mostly a museum of Chinese imperial examination. On Apple Map you can search for Jiading Confucius Temple or Shanghai China Keju Museum.
spots.addr: 183 Jiading South St (嘉定区嘉定南大街183号; Jiādìngqū Jiādìngnándàjiē​)

spots.name: Jiading Museum
spots.desc: History museum with a modern design, having exhibits in real size: Chinese pavilions, people (craftsmen), large animals. Ceramic exhibition in the basement (as of 2018). The backyard has an elegant pond with water lilies, and the other side of the pond is the wild Qiuxia Garden, but no direct access.
spots.addr: 215 Bole Road

spots.name: Qiuxia Garden
spots.desc: Built in 1502, this is one of Shanghai's famous old gardens. Former private garden of Gon Hong, a head of the Ministry of Works in the Ming Dynasty. A pleasant, compact, classical garden.
spots.addr: 314 Dongdajie St

spots.name: Fahua Pagoda
spots.desc: This 40.85 meters tall tetragonal brick-wood tower with seven floors is the symbol of Jiading. It was first constructed during Emperor Kaixi's reign (1205-1207). As of 2018 it's not possible to climb the pagoda, but it is free to walk around it and to visit the Gu Weijun Exhibition Hall in the same yard. Gu Weijun (1888-1985), a Jiading native diplomat, was one of the founders of the United…
spots.addr: 349 Jiading South Street

spots.name: Yuncaitang Spa
spots.desc: It's a large complex of Japanese style spa. The ¥39 entrance fee covers wet and dry sauna, jacuzzi, other water pools and tubs (all bathing is men and women separately), children's play room, heated pebble beds, many types of relaxation rooms and beds. Paid services are restaurant, mahjong and massage. It's possible to stay overnight for an extra ¥30 with passport (4-bed rooms). Inscriptions are…
spots.addr: 1501 Meijiabang Road

spots.name: National Anthem Gallery
spots.local: 国歌展示馆 guógē zhǎnshì guǎn
spots.desc: Relics, artifacts and modern technology are used to tell in Chinese and English how the theme of a patriotic movie became the Chinese Anthem. You can include the gallery into a whole walk by the North Band and Shikumen Houses.
spots.addr: Jingzhou Road No.151

spots.name: Yang Yuan Shan
spots.desc: "Male Mountain" or "Male Stone", bizarrely enough the most famous attraction in the whole park. It's a mountain that, thanks to erosion, bears a striking resemblance to a certain erect male body part. If you want you can lie down in front of it and have your friends take a picture of you with the "enhanced" anatomy. Once you get your giggles out, keep walking to see the real beauty of the park.

spots.name: Xi Mei Zhai
spots.desc: A high viewpoint, one of the best places in the park to see the sunset. Only reachable by hiking a steep trail (around the north of the mountain via Xuan Ji Tai) or an even steeper trail (from the east, around the south of the mountain).

spots.name: Xuan Ji Tai
spots.desc: Another great viewpoint and the other best place in the park to see the sunset. Somewhat easier to get to than Xi Mei Zhai—the steps aren't quite as steep if you come via the trail to the north.

spots.name: Female Stone
spots.desc: A boulder with a tall, narrow slit to match the "male stone" in the other scenic area. Quite a walk from the most popular areas near Zhang Lao Feng and not particularly beautiful, only really appealing for the novelty.

spots.name: Tongtian Cave
spots.desc: A long, dark cave eroded by water, connected to , a slot canyon. Bring a phone or flashlight to light your way through.

spots.name: Jinshiyan Temple
spots.desc: An old Buddhist temple on the side of a cliff. It's at the end of a long-ish side trail that also takes you to Mengjue Pass and Tongtian Cave.

spots.name: Zhang Lao Feng / Sungazing Pavilion
spots.local: 长老峰 Zhǎnglǎofēng / 观日亭 Guān Rì Tíng
spots.desc: The area's namesake: a high peak with gorgeous views of the striking, steep mountains all around.

spots.name: Shaoyin Pavilion
spots.desc: A great viewpoint, a short walk from the cable car station. Best place to view the sunrise (see below).

spots.name: Tomb of the Young Song Emperor Zhaobing
spots.local: 宋少帝陵; Sòng​ Shào​ Dì​ Líng​
spots.desc: This is putatively the tomb of the last Emperor of the Southern Song Dynasty (d. 1279). There is little doubt that he died in this general area after fleeing from the Mongols who had taken the dynastic capital Hangzhou. Modern knowledge of the tomb dates back to the latter years of the 19th century when the Zhao (Cantonese Chiu) Clan of Hong Kong (Zhao was the Song Imperial surname) researched…
spots.addr: Chiwan (赤湾​)

spots.name: Xin'an (Nantou) Ancient City
spots.local: 新安(南头)古城; Xīn​'ān​ (Nán​tóu​) Gǔ​chéng​
spots.desc: This is the original county town for the county which used to encompass Hong Kong and Shenzhen. There has been a town on this site since the 4th century. Much of the old town has been demolished and replaced by residential buildings in the "urban village" style, but Xin'an has still maintained the flavour of a Cantonese town throughout the ages with vibrant street life along narrow streets. The…
spots.price: Free (including the museum and historic buildings)

spots.name: Tanglang Mountain
spots.desc: A big green forested mountain between Nanshan and Futian, crisscrossed by a huge network of trails. Wildlife on the tree-covered slopes includes butterflies, ferns, lychees, several endangered plants, and lots of birds, especially near the trailhead. Expect lots of stairs, as usual in Shenzhen, but also plenty of benches to rest. The 432-meter peak has great views of the skyscrapers in Nanshan…
spots.addr: Longzhu Sixth Road 龙珠六路

spots.name: Miàndào
spots.desc: A popular local joint for northern Chinese noodles. Choose from the chilled appetizers and assorted fried pancakes, then order one of various kinds of noodles. Menu and signs only in Chinese, though the notoriously complicated characters for "Biang biang" noodles are omitted in favor of letters, so you should be able to read that menu item at least.
spots.addr: 赤湾六路18号山海逸居

spots.name: Jintian Uprising Site
spots.local: 金田起义旧址, 金田起义景区 Jintian Uprising Scenic Area
spots.desc: This is the site where in 1851 Hong Xiuquan launched the Jintian Uprising, the first military engagement in what later became known as the Taiping Rebellion. Today the site is a historical park. It features a museum, some archaeological ruins, and a number of statues.
spots.price: Entry to the museum is free. Entry to the park is ¥20
spots.addr: Jintian Village, Jintian Town (金田镇金田村)

spots.name: West Mountain National Scenic Zone
spots.local: 西山国家重点风景名胜区 Xishan Guojia Zhongdian Fengjing Mingsheng Qu
spots.desc: A typical small scenic mountain with temples, pavilions, strange rocks, etc. Known for Xishan tea, which you can purchase from one of the shops near the entrance. This is also a good place from which to get a bird's eye view of the city. Climbing the 678-metre-high summit requires a certain level of fitness but you can take the cable car part of the way.
spots.hours: 04ː00-19ː00 (The temples open at 08ː00), no entry is permitted after 16ː00
spots.addr: 3 Xishan Road (西山路3号)

spots.name: Longhua Temple
spots.desc: One of Guiping's oldest temples, the Longhua Temple was founded in the Song Dynasty and has been rebuilt several times.
spots.addr: West Mountain National Scenic Zone (西山国家重点风景名胜区)

spots.name: Zhongshan Park
spots.desc: A park dedicated to Sun Yat-sen (Sun Zhongshan), founder of China's first republic. There are of course many Zhongshan Parks in China but this one is unique as Sun visited the park in 1921 (when it was called something else) and advised on its development. A large statue of Sun stands just inside the entrance to the park.
spots.addr: 84 Guangchang Street (广场街84号)

spots.name: Hankou Riverfront
spots.desc: Note the tall monument which, from far away, appears to be a monument to Mao Zedong, but which actually commemorates Wuhan's complicated relationship with its great river. Erected in 1969, it's inscribed with Mao's poem "Swimming" (which not only celebrates the Yangtze in Wuhan, but also foresees the creation of the mighty hydro dams farther upstream), and decorated with reliefs depicting the…
spots.addr: Yanjiang Avenue, Jiang'an District (江岸区沿江大道)

spots.name: Vegetable seed shops
spots.desc: If you are interested in the origin of all the produce you see in Chinese markets and restaurants, you can visit the stores from which farmers and amateur gardeners buy vegetable seeds. There are several dozens seed shops in Wuhan, mostly having the word 种苗 zhongmiao ("seedling") in their names, and they all are concentrated on one block of Zhongshan Road, conveniently located next to a train…
spots.addr: The west side of Zhongshan Road (中山路) between Ziyang Road and Wuluo Road in Wuchang District

spots.name: Datang Plaza
spots.desc: A gravity-defying square perched atop a building—street level on one side, but dropping an astonishing 22 storeys on the other, a true showcase of Chongqing’s wild topography.

spots.name: Drone show "Glamorous Chongqing”
spots.desc: Each Saturday night (and on major holidays), Chongqing’s skies become a canvas for a spectacular drone show, with thousands of synchronized drones dancing above the confluence of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers. In June 2025, the show even set a Guinness World Record with 11,787 drones creating the largest aerial image ever seen. Pro tip: the best views are from a bar or restaurant at level 6 of…

spots.name: Dujiangyan old city
spots.desc: While little in the old city is original, it has been beautifully reconstructed as a tourist site. The old city is absolutely worth strolling through for its architecture, and there are interesting descriptions of the place's history. But the stores are of no particular interest and you'll probably choose to avoid them. Be sure to see the east city gate (very impressive, but rebuilt only in…

spots.name: Grain Stack
spots.desc: Grain Stack, a beloved spot in Dujiangyan, shines with its unique drinks that blend flavor and texture. In its Coconut Latte, creamy coconut milk merges with aromatic brewed coffee, offering a sweet yet not cloying taste, ideal for pairing with the shop’s pastries. The Americano stands out too, with a smooth, well-balanced profile, boasting subtle nutty undertones that cut through the richness of…
spots.addr: No.31 - 33 Shenjia Lane

spots.name: Xianyue Teahouse
spots.desc: Xianyue Teahouse is a serene teahouse tucked into a renovated traditional house in Dujiangyan. With a minimalist, Zen-inspired design using natural wood tones, it creates a tranquil atmosphere for guests to unwind. The space includes a small courtyard, indoor rooms, and private tea rooms, allowing visitors to relax in solitude or with friends. Their tea menu is broad, offering white tea, pu-er…
spots.price: According to local guides, tea per person is moderate — many teas are around ¥50–100 for a tasting or a pot, depending…
spots.addr: 342 Wai Bei Street, Dujiangyan City

spots.name: Zhongtian Tower
spots.desc: Both this tower and the Huaguang Tower are about three storeys high and are fine locations from which to overlook the town and river.

spots.name: Zhangfei Temple
spots.desc: Where the warrior king was laid to rest after being betrayed by his closest advisors.

spots.name: Fengshui Museum
spots.desc: An exhibition of geomantic principles including a scale model of the town. There is also a beautiful, small courtyard with well-kept vegetation and multiple levels. A (Mandarin only) fortune teller is sometimes available. The attached museum houses multiple displays without English captions.

spots.name: Gongyuan
spots.desc: A preserved ancient examination hall. Up until the Communist Revolution, individuals seeking government employment memorized ancient Confucian texts and were later grilled on the quality of their memorization as the sole qualifier for employment. This hall is one where students were examined, and houses a tribute to Langzhong's top scholars.

spots.name: Confucian Temple
spots.local: 文庙, 孔庙，阆中县文庙 Langzhong County Confucian Temple
spots.desc: It was built in the northern part of the town during the Tang Dynasty, then relocated to the East Gate during the Ming Dynasty, and moved to its present location in 1851 during the Qing Dynasty.

spots.name: North Sichuan Daotai Yamen
spots.local: 川北道署, 道台衙门 Daotai Yamen
spots.desc: From 1730 to the early 20th century, the yamen served as the main office and residence of the daotai (high-ranking mandarins) who were tasked with the administration of northern Sichuan. Unfortunately, the yamen was largely destroyed during the 20th century. The current building is a modern reconstruction, though nonetheless still worth a look.

spots.name: Hu Family Courtyard
spots.desc: A classical courtyard-style residence with a history dating back to the early 18th century. There are eight rooms on display, each of which has been carefully arranged in the traditional style with antique furniture. The Hu family still live here and will usually give you a guided tour in Mandarin.
spots.addr: 25 Xuedao Street (学道街25号)

spots.name: White Tower Pagoda
spots.desc: A prominent spike-shaped erection conspicuously visible from town, the first pagoda was built in the 1600s, severely damaged in the May 2008 Sichuan earthquake, and was rebuilt by the end of that year. If the attendant is present, you can climb the stairs inside the pagoda for a small price.

spots.name: Chuxiong Yi Autonomous Prefecture Museum
spots.local: 楚雄彝族自治州博物馆
spots.desc: A museum showcasing the history and ethnic cultures of Chuxiong Prefecture, with exhibitions on local archaeology, Yi clothing and regional culture. The museum is also a national 4A-level tourist attraction.
spots.addr: 471 Lucheng Nan Lu (鹿城南路471号)

spots.name: Zixi Mountain Forest Park
spots.desc: Said to be the largest nature park in Yunnan Province. Covers an area of 16000 hectares and contains a wide variety of plant and animal species. Historically, the area was very important to Chinese Buddhists and at one time there were claimed to be 88 temples and 77 nunneries here. While the vast majority of Buddhist sites have been lost to history, a few have survived, most notably the Ziding…
spots.addr: Zixi Mountain, Zixi Town

spots.name: Major Stone Forest
spots.desc: A dense area of boulders and caves filled with winding paths. It's easy to lose the crowds as you wander around between the stones. Try to find the peak viewpoint (just keep going up)—it gives you a stunning view of all the karst. The viewpoint is too small for more than two or three people and the path up to it is narrow, so this isn't really an option for tour groups—which is a shame, as it's a…

spots.name: Yongzhen Gate
spots.desc: The northern gate of the former walled city of Lin'an. It formed part of the four-gate layout established when Jianshui's city walls were rebuilt in brick during the Ming dynasty. The original gate tower no longer survives, but the site remains a recognizable landmark.

spots.name: Fu'an Gate
spots.desc: The southern gate of the former walled city of Lin'an. It was one of the four historic gates that defined the old city's street layout, together with Chaoyang Gate in the east, Qingyuan Gate in the west and Yongzhen Gate in the north.

spots.name: Qingyuan Gate
spots.desc: The western gate of the former walled city of Lin'an. Together with the eastern Chaoyang Gate, southern Fu'an Gate and northern Yongzhen Gate, it formed part of the traditional four-gate layout of the old city.

spots.name: Temple of Confucius
spots.desc: Billed as "the largest Confucian temple in Southern China", Jianshui's temple was founded in 1285, during the Yuan Dynasty, although the existing buildings date mostly to the late 18th century (and probably have been heavily restored in the late 20th). Unlike its better known namesakes in Qufu or Hanoi, Jianshui's temple includes a large lake, known as Xuehai ("The Sea of Learning"). A pavilion…

spots.name: Jianshui Examination Hall
spots.desc: Long before Americans started studying for SAT, GRE, and bar exams, a system of local, provincial, and imperial examinations served to select deserving candidates for the government apparatus of imperial China. The Jianshui examination hall is a complex of buildings where, during the Ming and Qing dynasties, young Yunnan scholars would come to take the high-stake exam that could decide the course…
spots.addr: 134 Lin'an Rd (临安路134号)

spots.name: Double Dragon Bridge
spots.desc: The 17-span bridge, now standing in the middle of a pond, as most of the waters in the Lin'an River has been diverted elsewhere. The tourist train makes a short stop nearby.

spots.name: Wenbi Tower
spots.desc: On a hill south of town, this early 19th-century structure is meant to resemble a writing brush (文笔 wenbi), although to a modern traveler it may look more like a factory smokestack. You cannot drive to the tower, but there is a more or less informal trail people use to approach the tower from the southwest, starting at a roadside sign in Baishuihe Village (白水河村). The tower is a solid stone…

spots.name: Guanyi Village
spots.desc: A Muslim (Hui) village, with two ornate mosques. You'll pass through it if you're traveling to Jianshui by road from Tonghai

spots.name: Jianshui Old City Train
spots.desc: The century-old narrow gauge railway serving Jianshui (a branch of the better known Yunnan-Vietnam Railway) has no regular passenger service anymore; but a tourist train runs twice a day from the restored Lin'an Station 临安站 to Tuanshan Station 团山站, in a village of the same name west of town. On its way, the train stops at the Double Dragon Bridge. Note that this is not the only place in Yunnan…

spots.name: Jukui Pavilion
spots.desc: The symbolic center of Tonghai's old downtown (now, the town's tourist / shopping district).

spots.name: Da Hui Village
spots.desc: Decorated with Arabic inscriptions, Da Hui Cun and Xiao Hui Cun (the Greater Hui Village and the Lesser Hui Village, respectively), are known for their ornate mosques

spots.name: Qutuo Pass Village
spots.desc: Qutuo is the first village in Tonghai County as you enter the county from the west on Yunnan Hwy 319 (former S304), over the Qutuo Pass. As seen from the road, it mostly consists of shops selling the region's local products, of which the most famous is, apparently, is something called "Red sweet liquor" (红甜白酒 hong tian bai jiu). The other famous local product - seen at numerous roadside vendors -…

spots.name: Foochow Arsenal Culture City
spots.local: 中国船政文化城, 福州市中国船政文化景区 Foochow Arsenal Cultural Scenic Area
spots.desc: In the 19th century, the British wanted to counter Russian influence, so they helped both China and Japan modernize their navies. Mawei became home to Foochow Arsenal, China's first modern naval shipyard with docks, a Naval School and other military facilities that were built to protect the arsenal. Nowadays, the relics of Foochow Arsenal are open for visitors. On the site of the arsenal, the new…
spots.addr: 83 Gangkou Road (港口路83号)

spots.name: Fuzhou Majiang Sea War Memorial
spots.desc: Not far from the arsenal, at the base of Maxian Mountain, there is a small memorial temple, the Zhaozhong Temple (昭忠祠), which is dedicated for those who fell in the battle of Fuzhou on August 23, 1884. The temple is now part of the Majiang Sea War Memorial and hosts an exhibition on the battle. This was the opening battle of a Sino-French War, mainly over Chinese objections to France's expansion…
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:30, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: 1 Zhaozhong Road (昭忠路1号)

spots.name: Maxian Mountain Park
spots.desc: On Maxian Mountain, there are the sites of an English-style prison and the Maxian Mountain Mesoslope Battery, subordinate facilities of the Foochow Arsenal.
spots.addr: Zhaozhong Road (昭忠路)

spots.name: Luoxing Pagoda Park
spots.desc: About two kilometres southeast of the Mawei Shipyard, is Luoxingta (Luoxing Pagoda). The government of Mawei District have built a beautiful park around it. Visitors can climb a small hill to reach the bottom of Luoxingta.
spots.addr: Gangkou Road (港口路)

spots.name: Tanshishan Site Museum
spots.desc: A museum built over the top of the Tanshishan Site, the oldest Neolithic site in Fujian Province. The museum displays stone tools, pottery, and other items discovered at the site.
spots.addr: 1 Wenbo Road, Ganzhe Subdistrict (甘蔗街道文博路1号)

spots.name: Kuan Yin Pavilion

Song's tomb was severely damaged during the Cultural Revolution and rebuilt in the early 1980s.

The five story pagoda underwent renovations during the Qing Dynasty, and unlike a pair of historic pagodas in the historic downtown of Pinghu, survived the iconoclastic destruction of the reign of Mao Zedong. During national festivals, locals carve watermelons, the tasty symbol of Pinghu, into intricate carved lanterns, which if you are lucky you'll find hanging from the roofs of the wooden-framed buildings surrounding the lake. spots.name: Pinghu Zao Eggs
spots.desc: Pinghu Zao Eggs are a traditional specialty made by marinating fresh eggs in fermented glutinous rice mash. The egg whites become semi-transparent with a light sweetness and mild rice wine aroma. Commonly served as a side dish or cold appetizer, they are a staple in local households and festive meals.

spots.name: Zhapu Seafood
spots.desc: Zhapu, a historic port area of Pinghu, is known for fresh seafood such as swimming crabs, yellow croaker, shrimp, and clams. Local restaurants typically prepare seafood through steaming, poaching, or scallion oil techniques to highlight natural flavors. It is one of the best places to try Hangzhou Bay seafood.

spots.name: Guangchen Mutton
spots.desc: Guangchen Mutton is a well-known regional dish from Guangchen Town, using locally raised goats. Common preparations include braised mutton, clear mutton soup, and mutton noodles. The flavors are mild and warming, making it popular especially in autumn and winter.

spots.name: Pinghu Glutinous Rice Wine
spots.desc: Pinghu Glutinous Rice Wine is a sweet, low-alcohol rice wine brewed from glutinous rice. It has a gentle aroma and is used both as a beverage and as an ingredient for marinating or cooking local preserved foods.

spots.name: Pinghu Rice Ball
spots.desc: This traditional breakfast item is made by pressing cooked glutinous rice into a firm ball, often wrapped around pickles, meat floss, or fried dough sticks. Simple and filling, rice balls are a common morning option across Pinghu.

spots.name: Pinghu Wheat-Shimp Soup Dumplings
spots.desc: Despite the name, “wheat shrimp” contains no shrimp. It is a handmade noodle-like dough shaped into small pieces and cooked in broth with vegetables, dried shrimp, or salted pork. It is a simple, comforting local home-style dish.

spots.name: Danghu Pastries
spots.desc: Danghu Pastries include sesame crisps, small rice cakes, and cloud cakes produced by long-established bakeries in the Danghu area. These traditional sweets are easy to store and commonly purchased as local souvenirs.

spots.name: Fenghu Theme Park
spots.desc: Fenghu Theme Park is located on the Fenghu natural lake, surrounded by mountains and waters, with beautiful scenery. The lake is wide and the water is clear, which is very suitable for walking, cycling or quietly enjoying the beauty of nature, especially in the evening when the sunset by the lake is very charming.

The carvings and decorations on the door are also of high artistic value.
