spots.name: Vineyard Cafe
spots.desc: Great place for Western-style breakfast and brunch in a restored hutong home. Also great European/fusion dishes, including some vegetarian options. A good dessert choice is the chocolate brownie with ice cream.
spots.addr: 31 Wudaoying Hutong (五道营胡同31号)

spots.name: Xiao Xin's Cafe
spots.desc: One of the original cafes along this hutong, and now has many imitators. Great coffee and desserts, although the rest of the food is not particularly special.
spots.addr: 103 Nanluoguxiang (南锣鼓巷103号)

spots.name: Pebbles Courtyard
spots.desc: This restaurant's Mexican offerings are authentic, and the soft-shelled tacos are excellent. It's a nice location to spend a laid-back evening.
spots.addr: 74 Wudaoying Hutong 雍和宫五道营胡同74号

spots.name: Saveurs de Coree
spots.desc: Korean food in a fancy setting. Can be expensive, but special set menus are a good deal.
spots.addr: 29 Nanluoguxiang (南锣鼓巷29号), 20 Ju'er Hutong

spots.name: 12SQM
spots.desc: Very small bar/café that takes its name from its original floor space (website claims it's the smallest in Beijing, although it has expanded to 45 m² since).
spots.addr: 1 Fuxiang Hutong, Nanluoguxiang (南锣鼓巷福祥胡同1号; Nánluógǔxiàngfúxiánghútòng)

spots.name: Guitar Bar
spots.desc: Very small bar with standard drink and Italian food. Guitar jam most nights.
spots.addr: 40 Nanluoguxiang (南锣鼓巷40号; Nánluógǔxiàng)

spots.name: alba
spots.desc: Bar serving signature cocktails, mixed drinks, rums and whiskeys.
spots.addr: 70 Gulou Dongdajie (鼓楼东大街70号; Gǔlóudōngdàjiē)

spots.name: Mao Live House
spots.desc: Live rock music venue. The stage is great, the sound system is okay and the concert room and furniture are very basic.
spots.addr: 111 Gulou East Street (鼓楼东大街111号; Gǔlóudōngdàjiē)

spots.name: Salud
spots.local: 老伍酒吧 Lǎowǔ Jiǔbā; e.a.t
spots.desc: A Spanish-style tapas bar. Blues jam every Thursday, 21:00. ¥20 for 0.5l Tsingtao.
spots.addr: 66 Nánluógǔxiàng 南锣鼓巷66号

spots.name: Tree House
spots.desc: Small and quiet pub/café, one of the few to be open also in the morning. Evening events now and then.
spots.addr: 81 Ju'er Hutong (菊儿胡同81号; Júérhútòng)

spots.name: Great Leap Brewing I 大跃啤酒
spots.desc: Quite possibly the most difficult bar to find in Beijing. Although it's in the center of everything it's nestled so snugly inside a residential neighborhood that it's nearly impossible for first-timers to locate. It's one of Beijing's first (if not the first) real microbrewery. Founded by a few American guys and one's Chinese wife they have been a huge hit in China and internationally and have…
spots.addr: 6 Doujiao Hutong 角胡同6号

spots.name: Pass By Bar
spots.desc: Cool bar in the heart of Nanluoguxiang, serves beer and food, with open-air upstairs to look out over the hutongs. Lots of great posters to admire.
spots.addr: 108 Nanluogu Xiang 南锣鼓巷108号

spots.name: Drum and Bell
spots.desc: Best part of this bar is the comfortable rooftop patio (especially if you can score a table with couches) that overlooks the Bell Tower and the square (which at night is clear of tour buses and used by locals playing badminton).
spots.addr: 41 Zhonglouwan Hutong

spots.name: Jiangjin Bar
spots.desc: The cocktails are not good, but the live folk music jam is great.
spots.addr: 2 Zhongku hutong (钟库胡同2号; Zhōngkùhútòng)

spots.name: Zen Bar
spots.desc: Very small and quiet bar hidden away in a hutong. Nice simple surroundings including a lot of Buddhas.
spots.addr: 18 Zhonglouwan Hutong (钟楼湾18号; Zhōnglóuwān)

spots.name: Mao Mao Chong Bar
spots.desc: This relaxed hutong pub serves reasonably priced international beers, wines and stellar cocktails. The walls are decorated with art and t-shirts for sale by the bar's owners, a husband-wife team who also cook up some of the city's best pizzas. Just east of Nanluoguxiang, Mao Mao Chong is the perfect escape from Beijing's flashy bar districts. Pizzas ¥45–75, antipasto ¥45, cocktails from ¥40…
spots.price: Cheaper than most bars in Beijing
spots.addr: 市东城区交道口南大街板厂胡同12号; 12 Banchang Hutong

spots.name: Modernista
spots.desc: Modernista is a European-inspired cafe, restaurant and bar in the heart of Beijing traditional hutongs. They also showcase what they say is "the best of Beijing´s live music, performances, art and cultural events".
spots.addr: 44 Baochao Hutong, Gulou Dongdajie 鼓楼东大街宝钞胡同44号

spots.name: Gubeikou
spots.desc: Gubeikou is also far from central Beijing than other sections but the extra time it takes to get there is rewarded with a very significant reduction in crowding and tourist traps.

spots.name: Simatai
spots.desc: The most authentic part of the wall is at Simatai; the wall here is of original construction unlike Badaling. Simatai in combination with the adjacent Gubei Watertown, a reconstructed historical town, has become a popular weekend travel destination for domestic and international tourists. Night tours overlooking the well illuminated Gubei Watertown are popular and tickets are sold separately.

spots.name: Mount Yumeng
spots.desc: The forest park has good views of the Miyun Reservoir and a wild part of the Great Wall. From the last park shuttle stop is the start of a 4.2 km walking trail to the top (2.5 hours). The park shuttle on the way back from the top stops at an observation point overlooking the Lupiguan section of the Great Wall where the remnant of a three window watchtower is in the left foreground.

spots.name: Gubei Watertown
spots.desc: Gubei Watertown is a reconstructed historical town at the foot of Simatai Great Wall. Visiting at night is recommended as there is an electric light show in the town and a night tour of Simatai can be done in one go. As a fancy high end tourist development by a venture capital fund, Gubei Watertown has been successful in marketing overnight tours.

spots.name: Tianyun Mountain
spots.desc: The destination has a 160 meter glass bottom bridge and small viewing platform built over 1,000 meters above the valley. The surrounding landscape of mountain peaks is lush in the summer, making for one of the most beautiful outdoors sights in Beijing.
spots.addr: Huangtuliang, Huangsongyu Town

spots.name: Shilingxia
spots.desc: The park's large hiking loop will take you past steep rock formations and small waterfall streams. The scenery is not as spectacular as in nearby Tianyun Mountain. However, the star attraction isn't the nature but a UFO shaped structure that is the world's longest cantilever viewing platform. The bottom of the UFO platform is glass and the structure is perched over the highest peak in the park.…
spots.addr: Diaowo Village, Huangsongyu Township

spots.name: Jingdong Grand Canyon
spots.desc: Easy hiking circuit ideal for families to stroll. The main path passes through waterfalls, pools, and cliffs and branches off to viewpoints overlooking the Jingtai Mountain and barely visible remnants of the Great Wall. Along the main path is a short detour to the Tong Tian Gorge, a more challenging climb to the location of the crevice concealing an ammunition depot during the Second…
spots.addr: Yuzi Village

spots.name: Hiking Jinshanling to Simatai
spots.desc: The hike from east Jinshanling to west Simatai is roughly 10 km. The majority of the wall east of Jinshanling is unrestored and makes for a significant hike in distance and elevation change. You will be rewarded with spectacular views and a good day of exercise. Expect to spend anywhere from 2.5 hours to 6 hours on the wall, depending on your fitness level, ambition and frequency of photo ops.…

spots.name: Chateau Changyu AFIP Global
spots.local: 北京张裕爱斐堡国际酒庄
spots.desc: A French chateau-style hotel and winery complex in Miyun where guests can indulge in Changyu wine, explore the wine-making process, and take a leisurely stroll through the replica village.

spots.name: Juyongguan
spots.desc: The nearest section of the Great Wall to the center of Beijing and among the most popular. It was a fortress guarding an important mountain pass during the Ming Dynasty. The wall in this section forms a full circle.

spots.name: Jiaozhuanghu Tunnel Warfare Site Museum

spots.desc: A 23-kilometer network of underground tunnels built by residents of Jiaozhuanghu Village in the 1940s during the Japanese occupation of Beijing. The tunnels were used by Chinese resistance fighters to evade capture and launch attacks on Japanese forces. An 830-meter section of the tunnels is open to the public. As of April 2021, visitors are requested to make a booking at least 24 hours in…
spots.addr: 38 Jinianguan Road, Jiaozhuanghu Village, Longwantun Town, Shunyi District (顺义区龙湾屯镇焦庄户村纪念馆路38号)

spots.name: Beijing Waxworks Palace of Ming Dynasty
spots.desc: Here you can see China's historical and cultural figures in wax.
spots.addr: Xiguanhuandao, Changping District (昌平区西关环岛)

spots.name: Happy Land Arts and Crafts Center
spots.desc: The center offers pottery, painting, paper folding, jewelry making and other.
spots.addr: Xibaixinzhuang, Houshayu, Shunyi District (顺义区后沙峪西白辛庄; Shùnyìqū Hòushāyù Xībáixīnzhuāng)

spots.name: Tianyi Strawberry Garden
spots.desc: A large strawberry farm where visitors can inside the farm's greenhouses pick strawberries for purchase from December to June.
spots.addr: Changping District

spots.name: International Shooting Range
spots.desc: One of the few shooting ranges in China open to the public. Shotguns, handguns, and rifles are available. Silencer equipped handgun available for use with letter of introduction from company of employment.
spots.price: ¥15 for each rifle and handgun bullet
spots.addr: 1 Mafang Cun, Nankou, Changping District

spots.name: Ban Ruo
spots.desc: Buddhist vegetarian restaurant. Try the fake Beijing Duck and other fake meat dishes.
spots.addr: 33 Gulou Dongjie, Changping District (昌平区鼓楼东街33号)

spots.name: Yangfang Shengli Mutton Hotpot (Original)
spots.desc: Beijing-style mutton hot pot restaurant established in 1984, well-reputed in Beijing
spots.addr: 10 Wennan Rd, Yangfang, Changping District (昌平区阳坊镇温南路10号)

spots.name: Yangfang Shengli Mutton Hotpot (Main)
spots.desc: 400 meters south of the original Yangfang Shengli restaurant (under the same group)
spots.addr: Yangfang, Changping District (昌平区阳坊镇)

spots.name: Haru Teppanyaki and Sushi Bar
spots.desc: Sushi is served at the bar while you can have both sushi and teppanyaki in the private rooms. Unusually high level of service here.
spots.addr: 902 Pinnacle Plaza, Jingshun Lu, Shunyi District (顺义区京顺路荣祥广场902)

spots.name: Llama
spots.desc: Mexican themed bar with very good Tex-Mex food. The chimichanga is recommended. Coronas are ¥25.
spots.addr: Pinnacle Plaza

spots.name: Arxan Geopark
spots.desc: Listed as a UNESCO geopark, a volcanic region with crater lakes and hot springs.

spots.name: Alxa Desert National Geopark
spots.desc: In Alxa League (also known as Alashan League) of Western Inner Mongolia.

spots.name: Hongshizhai
spots.desc: A leisure area beside Zhaizi Reservoir, also known as Xiangshan Lake, with red-stone buildings, waterfront scenery and recreation facilities. The main sights here are the lakeside setting and buildings; nearby Zhuquan offers village lanes and traditional crafts.
spots.addr: Near Zhuquan Village

spots.name: Maquan Leisure Park
spots.desc: An agricultural leisure park with orchards, landscaped grounds and displays about rural culture. Activities include seasonal fruit picking. Before visiting, ask which fruit is available to pick and whether fruit picking requires payment in addition to the admission fee.
spots.addr: Maquan Village, Quanxiang Avenue

spots.name: Tianjin Drum Tower
spots.desc: The tower was built in the Ming Dynasty, but was destroyed during the Cultural Revolution. It was rebuilt in 2001, and now houses a bell instead of drums. The tower is home to varying exhibitions.
spots.price: General admission is free. A fee of ¥10 is charged for special exhibitions
spots.addr: Gulou East St, Nankai District (南开区鼓楼东街 Nánkāiqū Gǔlóudōngjiē)

spots.name: Tianjin Confucian Temple
spots.local: 天津文庙, 天津文庙博物馆 Tianjin Confucian Temple Museum
spots.desc: Early Qing Dynasty temple with a hall to honour Confucius and other halls for prayers.
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:00-16:30, no entry after 16:00, closed Mon
spots.addr: 2 Dongmennei St, Dongma Rd, Nankai District (南开区东马路东门内大街2号 Nánkāi Qū Dōngmǎ Lù Dōngménnèi Dàjiē)

spots.name: Tianjin Grand Mosque
spots.local: 天津清真大寺; Tiānjīn Qīngzhēndàsì
spots.desc: Built in 1644 and constructed with wood in traditional Chinese style. The mosque is still in use by the Tianjin Muslim community. Access for tourists and non-Muslims to the interior is restricted. The mosque should not be confused with the more modern Hongqiao Mosque that lies just a little further up the road.
spots.addr: Xiaohuo Lane, Dafeng Road, Hongqiao District (红桥区红桥区大丰路小伙巷 Hóngqiáoqū Dàfēnglù Xiǎohuǒxiàng)

spots.name: Machang Dao
spots.desc: Lined with large English style homes, another cultural street in Tianjin.

spots.name: Jiefang Road North
spots.desc: Running north-south a couple of streets back from the River Hai, this street is where colonial banks built their branches in Tianjin during the treaty-port era and will definitely be of interest to those interested in colonial architecture or history. Many of the buildings have been retained and are well-preserved, giving the street a distinctly European feel. No longer the central business…

spots.name: Gulou Street
spots.desc: Ancient cultural street full of cheap and tasty cafes. The street is named after the Tianjin Drum Tower, which divides the street into east and west sections. Other notable buildings include the Guangdong Guild Hall (home to the Tianjin Opera Museum) and the Xu Family Grand Courtyard (home to the Tianjin Old City Museum).
spots.addr: Gulou West Street-Gulou E St, Nankai District (南开区 鼓楼西街-鼓楼东街; Nánkāiqū Gǔlóuxījiē-Gǔlóudōngjiē)

spots.name: Memorial Hall of Zhou Enlai and Deng Yingchao
spots.local: 周恩来邓颖超纪念馆; Zhōu'ēnlái dèngyǐngchāo jìniànguǎn
spots.desc: Dedicated to the late Chinese premier Zhou Enlai (1898-1976) and his wife Deng Yingchao (1904-1992), both of whom are widely celebrated in China for their contribution to the socialist revolution. The memorial hall has an extensive collection of photographs and artefacts pertaining to the lives of the two individuals. Some notable artefacts include the printing press used to print the Tientsin…
spots.hours: 09:00-16:30, no entrance allowed after 16:00; closed on Mondays
spots.price: General entry is free but there is a ¥10 fee to view Zhou Enlai's plane
spots.addr: 9 Shuishang Gongyuan West Road, Nankai District (南开区水上公园西路9号)

spots.name: Tianjin Opera Museum
spots.desc: The museum is housed inside the Guangdong Guild Hall (广东会馆), a well-preserved historical building dating from the late Qing Dynasty that was used as a meeting place for merchants from Guangdong Province. The guild hall has a colorful history. Sun Yat-Sen gave a speech here in 1912. During the May 4th Movement of 1919, political activists, including Deng Yingchao, gathered here to talk and hold…
spots.addr: 257 Dongmenli Street, Nankai District (南开区东门里大街257号)

spots.name: Former Residence of Zhang Ailing
spots.desc: Early modern Chinese writer whose stories have been adapted into films such as Ang Li's "Lust, Caution". Zhang Ailing lived here for a very brief time during her early childhood years. The building is now a cafe.
spots.addr: 83 Chifeng Road, Heping District (和平区赤峰道83号)

spots.name: Garden of Serenity - Former Residence of Pu Yi, The Last Emperor of China
spots.desc: Jingyuan Garden with a history of 80 years is a famous residence combined both Chinese and European architectural styles. It is now one of the important heritage sites under the city's protection. Built in 1921, Jingyuan Garden, also named Qianyuan Garden, was the private residence of Lu Zongyu, minister-counselor to Japan appointed by the Northern Warlords’ Government. Later it was named by…
spots.addr: 70 Anshan Road, Heping District; 和平区鞍山道70号 (hépíngqū ānshāndào 70 hào)

spots.name: Tianjin Art Museum
spots.desc: Visitors are expected to make a booking before visiting the museum. Bookings can be made on WeChat (see here for QQ code).
spots.hours: Tue-Sun 09:00-16:30, no entry after 16:00, closed Mon (public holidays excepted)
spots.addr: 60 Pingjiang Avenue, Hexi District (河西区平江道60号)

spots.name: Tianjin Science and Technology Museum
spots.local: 天津科技馆, 天津科学技术馆
spots.desc: Visitors are advised to make an appointment before visiting the museum, but it's possible to visit without a prior appointment as long as the daily limit on the number of visitors has not been exceeded.
spots.hours: Wed-Sun 09:00-16:30, closed Mon Tue (public holidays excepted)
spots.price: General entry is free. Admission to the planetarium is ¥20. English guides are available for ¥50 (assuming a group size…
spots.addr: 94 Longchang Road, Hexi District (河西区隆昌路94号)

spots.name: Haihe River
spots.desc: The Haihe River is one of the great rivers of northern China. North Canal, the Yongding River, Daqing River, Ziya River, South Canal, five rivers on three sides, north, west and south convergence to Tianjin.

spots.name: Binjiang Dao Business Street
spots.desc: Enormous street with block upon block of stalls and shops containing almost anything you may need.

spots.name: The Ancient Cultural Street
spots.desc: Has a lot of souvenirs and trinkets, but you must know (or learn) how to bargain. A small silk handbag is worth ¥12-20; a set of 4-6 chopstick sets is worth about ¥50-60 in Beijing and about ¥35-45 in Tianjin; large dolls are worth about ¥80-120 depending on how excited you seem to the seller.

spots.name: Shenyang Dao Antique Market
spots.desc: Biggest antiques market in China, this is a place that is a must see on any travelers list. Shenyang Dao Antique Market is filled with all kinds of shops selling porcelain items, paintings, gold, silver, copper, jade, etc.

spots.name: Goubuli
spots.desc: Tianjin style steamed buns restaurant also serving other dishes.
spots.addr: 77 Shandong Rd, Heping District (和平区山东路77号 Hépíngqū Shāndōnglù)

spots.name: DaFuLai
spots.desc: Locals all know and love DaFuLai. It serves halal breakfast. According to legend, Empire Qianlong once visited this noshery in Tianjin, and at that time it mainly sold pancake. After having the pancake, the emperor asked for some soup. The hostess was unprepared, and she broke a pancake into small pieces, added boiled water, spices and seasoning. The emperor liked the taste, and gave the dish a…
spots.addr: a few branches in the city

spots.name: Sheraton Hotel
spots.desc: Fine dining available at one of three top quality restaurants available onsite.
spots.addr: Zijinshan Rd, Hexi District

spots.name: Bawarchi
spots.desc: Great Indian food, cooked in a traditional Indian tandoor clay oven by Indian chefs.
spots.addr: 3/F Shanggu Business Complex West Building, 69 Tianta Rd, Nankai District

spots.name: Helen's Cafe
spots.desc: An excellent place to eat simple western food like hamburgers, fries, and pizzas. During the day, it is a nice and quiet place to study while you eat lunch. At night time, it's a very lively place for foreign expats to get drunk. Free Wi-Fi is available.
spots.addr: Heping District, He Yan Dao Number 116, (close to Qixiangtai Lu and the Wu Jia Yao Number 2 Bridge); Tiānjīn shì hépíng qū hé yándào 116 hào (wú jiā yáo 2 hào…

spots.name: YY Beer House
spots.desc: A great inexpensive Thai restaurant offering a wide selection of beers. A great place to visit during the Thai Water Splashing festival in the spring!
spots.addr: 3 Aomen Rd, Heping District

spots.name: Aulare Urban Latin Restaurant
spots.desc: At Aulare, you can experience Latin, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian and South and Central American flavors.
spots.addr: Magnetic Plaza Building A4 2-16

spots.name: Kudos Thai
spots.desc: Well decorated Thai restaurant where the environment is cozy and modern. All food is authentically made by a Thai chef, without MSG or artificial additives. They've got a beautiful yard and nice terrace with a good view.
spots.addr: 88 Chengdu Rd, Heping District

spots.name: Amazon Brazilian B.B.Q. Bar
spots.desc: Does exactly what it says on the tin and has an enthusiastic, if slightly kitschy Filipino band providing live music as you munch.
spots.addr: 189 Nanjing Rd, Heping District

spots.name: Alli Baba
spots.desc: Featuring international cuisine and foreign student clientele close to the Nankai University campus, which has a whole range of dishes such as pasta, pizza, salad, etc.
spots.addr: 2 Hutong, Tongan Rd, Nankai University

spots.name: The Spot Café
spots.desc: An American-owned coffee house providing great coffees, teas, and pastries, as well as a variety of art and cultural events on a regular basis.
spots.addr: Heping District, Nanfu Fang Dajie

spots.name: Jingwumen Chinese Martial Arts Park
spots.local: 精武门·中华武林园, 霍元甲纪念馆; Huò yuánjiǎ jìniànguǎn, Huo Yuanjia Memorial
spots.desc: A large museum devoted to the life of Huo Yuanjia (a historical figure played by Jet Li in the film "Fearless") and his contributions to China and Kungfu. The museum also displays a wide variety of weapons he collected. Just outside the museum is the tomb of Huo Yuanjia. Also surrounding the museum and residence is where you can find a professional wushu/kung fu school.
spots.addr: Xiaonanhe Village, Jingwu Town, Xiqing District (西青区精武镇小南河村)

spots.name: Yangliuqing Ancient Town
spots.desc: A small historical town beside the Grand Canal. It is especially notable for its old mansions, the most famous of which are the An Family Grand Courtyard (安家大院) and the Shi Family Grand Courtyard (石家大院). The latter is actually one of the largest traditional mansions in northern China.
spots.price: Entry to the town is free; museums in the town typically charge a small fee
spots.addr: Yangliuqing Town, Xiqing District (西青区杨柳青镇)

spots.name: Beidahu Skiing Ground
spots.desc: Renowned for a long snowing season, it has arguably the most number of slopes for intermediate skiers and above of all ski resorts in China. Snow sports section of the 6th Asian Winter Games was held here. Ski lifts are good by Chinese standards and operate from 8:30AM-4PM daily, although the gondola tends to close around 3PM. Snowmaking machines are used when there is not enough natural snow…

spots.name: Maitreya Buddha scenic spot
spots.desc: This is the world's largest naturally formed image of Buddha. It is fully 70 m high. On the peak overlooking the Buddha mountain is the Maitreya Buddha temple and pagodas. The site was discovered in the mid-1990s. A stepped path leads up to the summit. A cable car runs part way up the mountain but not all the way.

spots.name: Heaven above Heaven
spots.desc: Near the main gates of the park, this summit can be reached by several routes. Either climb the stairs past Wuliang Taoist Temple or use the cable car. However, the cable car route here is relatively short and there remains a significant climb both before and after the car journey. If you continue along the ridge, you will pass such sites as Seventh Heaven, the Ninth Heaven, the Narrow Path…

spots.name: Five Buddha Summit
spots.desc: This is the second highest peak in the park. At the top there are five statues of the Buddha. The site is said to date to the Tang Dynasty. Direct access is only by cable car followed by a very steep climb by foot. The ridge way runs to Heaven above Heaven though decent can also be made about half way along via the Longquan Buddhist temple.

spots.name: Immortal Summit - China's forest park
spots.desc: To the south of the main park, this area has its own entrance and separate charges. Here ancient pine trees, many over 100 years old, can be seen as can Buddhist temples. The peak here, at 708.3 m above sea level, is the highest in Qianshan park.

spots.name: Garden of Birds
spots.desc: Situated towards the back of the park near the cable car to the Five Buddha Summit, the Garden of Birds contains over 100 types of birds.

spots.name: Dragon Spring Temple
spots.desc: Legend has it that Taizong, Li Shimin, an Emperor of the Tang Dynasty, drank of the waters here and found them to be sweet. Today two spring waters can be found, one is bitter in taste and the other sweet. The film The Bell of the Ancient Temple was made here.

spots.name: Qianshan Ski Resort
spots.desc: Situated just outside the main National Park area, this new ski centre has several runs for novice and accomplished skiers. Ski hire is available on site and the centre is well staffed and has modern equipment. It is only open during winter months.

spots.name: Qianshan Hot Spring Resort Area
spots.desc: Several natural hot spring spa baths are around the north entrance to the park. Here travellers can relax in the waters and receive other treatments such as massage.

spots.name: Qianshan Golf Range
spots.desc: Golf courses are not common in China. In Qianshan district there is a driving range where you can practice your swing.

spots.name: Mangya Emerald Lake
spots.desc: Mangya Emerald Lake is a large artificial salt lake on the southeastern side of Huatugou. The lake is known for its bright green and blue waters, which vary in color depending on the concentration of minerals and the lighting conditions. Surrounded by the dry landscape of the Qaidam Basin, the colorful lake contrasts strongly with the surrounding desert and salt flats.
spots.addr: Huatugou Town, Mangya City, Haixi Mongol and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture; at the eastern edge of Lake Gasi and the southeastern side of Huatugou Town

spots.name: Aiken Spring
spots.desc: Aiken Spring is a geothermal spring located at the foothills where the Qimantag and Ahati mountains meet. The spring continuously bubbles from the ground, while minerals deposited around the spring have created reddish and yellowish rings. Viewed from above, the spring resembles a large eye, earning it the nickname “Eye of the Earth.
spots.addr: Moherbuluke Village, Huatugou Town

spots.name: Gasikule Lake
spots.desc: Gasikule Lake is a large salt lake located in the western part of the Qaidam Basin. Its surroundings consist of extensive salt flats and desert landscapes, while the lake and nearby salt formations create a distinctive high-altitude landscape. The lake is also associated with salt springs and colorful mineral formations in the surrounding area.
spots.addr: Along National Highway 315, Huatugou Town

spots.name: Qianfo Cliff
spots.desc: Qianfo Cliff is a distinctive Danxia landscape in Youyuangou northeast of Huatugou. Long-term erosion by wind and rain has shaped the red sandstone cliffs into numerous formations resembling Buddhas, bodhisattvas and arhats. The cliffs form one of the characteristic landscapes around Huatugou and can be viewed from higher ground in the valley
spots.addr: Youyuangou, northeast of Huatugou Town

spots.name: Oil Sand Mountain
spots.desc: Oil Sand Mountain is a geological and petroleum landscape associated with the development of the Huatugou oilfield. Oil-bearing strata and exposed geological formations can be seen in the area, while oilfield equipment and pump jacks are scattered across the surrounding landscape. The site also has historical importance as one of the early areas of petroleum exploration in the Qaidam Basin.
spots.addr: Near Huatugou Oilfield, south of Huatugou Town

spots.name: Mongolian Fire Festival
spots.desc: It is held to pray for peace, prosperity and the well-being of families and livestock, and local celebrations may include fire-worship rituals, bonfires and traditional dancing.

spots.name: Chinese Farmers' Harvest Festival
spots.desc: The Chinese Farmers’ Harvest Festival is a celebration of the agricultural and pastoral harvest season. In Huatugou, local celebrations have included ethnic music and dance performances, traditional sports such as tug-of-war and archery, as well as local food.

spots.name: Qinghai Goji Berries
spots.desc: Qinghai goji berries and black goji berries are local agricultural products that can be used to make tea.
spots.addr: Next to the southeast gate of the Huatugou Farmers' Market

spots.name: Dried Yak Meat
spots.desc: Dried yak meat is a popular snack in the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau region. It is convenient for travelers and can be purchased as a gift.
spots.addr: Mangya Ruida General Merchandise Store

spots.name: Sizzling-Oil Fish
spots.desc: is a Chinese restaurant located in HuTuGou Town, Mangya City, Qinghai Province. Its signature dish, qiangguo fish, is typically prepared with fish, chili peppers, Sichuan peppercorns, and other seasonings, creating a spicy and aromatic flavor. It is an option for visitors looking to enjoy a Chinese-style meal while exploring the town.

spots.name: Old Beijing Lamb Hot Pot (Qianjin Road Branch)
spots.local: 老北京涮羊肉（前进路店）
spots.desc: is a traditional Beijing-style dish featuring thinly sliced lamb cooked briefly in a pot of boiling broth. The meat is typically served with traditional dipping sauces, such as sesame paste and fermented chive sauce. Unlike heavily seasoned hot pots, this style emphasizes the natural flavor of the lamb and the simplicity of the broth, offering visitors an authentic taste of traditional Chinese…

spots.name: Local favorites: Dry-pot duck, spicy shrimp, *diguo* chicken (braised chicken with flatbread), and charcoal-pot fish.
spots.local: 家门口干锅鸭香辣虾地锅鸡碳锅鱼
spots.desc: is a Chinese restaurant specializing in a variety of pot-style dishes, including dry pot duck, spicy shrimp, clay pot chicken, and charcoal pot fish. The dishes feature bold seasonings and rich flavors, with a variety of meat and seafood options. It is a suitable choice for visitors who enjoy hearty Chinese food and sharing meals with family or friends.

spots.name: Sangu Maocai (Mangzhou Commercial Street Branch)
spots.local: 三顾冒菜（茫州商业街店）
spots.desc: a traditional Sichuan-style dish. Various ingredients, including meat, vegetables, tofu, and mushrooms, are cooked in a seasoned broth and served with a choice of spice levels. Known for its bold, savory, and spicy flavors, maocai is a convenient meal option for both individual diners and groups looking to experience Sichuan cuisine.

spots.name: Little Mustache Lamb Rice Noodle Soup Shop
spots.desc: Its meals typically feature lamb served with vermicelli or rice noodles in a hot, flavorful broth. Hearty and warming, lamb soup is a popular style of food in northwestern China and offers visitors a taste of regional Chinese cuisine.

spots.name: Zhang Family Beef Offal Soup
spots.desc: made with various cuts of beef offal, such as tripe, intestines, and tendons. The ingredients are simmered until tender, creating a rich and flavorful broth. Some versions include radish, chopped green onions, and cilantro for extra flavor. It is a hearty dish for visitors interested in traditional Chinese cuisine and regional food culture.

spots.name: Loulan Museum
spots.desc: This museum holds artefacts excavated from archeological sites associated with the ancient kingdom of Loulan.
spots.addr: 966 Tuanjie Road (团结路966号)

spots.name: Loulan Red Date Ecological Garden
spots.desc: An agricultural tourism site focused on Ruoqiang's well-known red date cultivation and local farming landscape.

spots.name: Treasure Island
spots.desc: A rocky headland linked to local pirate-treasure folklore, with short walks and sea views.

spots.name: Qing'ao Bay sunrise and beach activities
spots.desc: Qing'ao Bay is a crescent-shaped beach and a popular spot on the island for sunrise.Come before dawn to watch the sun rise over the sea, then spend the day swimming, paddling in the gentle surf or joining small-boat and sea-fishing trips from the bay.
spots.addr: Provincial Highway 336 in Nanao County

spots.name: Hike in Huanghua Mountain National Forest Park
spots.desc: Huanghua Mountain is an island national forest park with coastal forest, signed hiking trails and viewpoints, cliff carvings, wartime tunnels and memorials. Allow half a day to a full day for hiking.

spots.name: Danji Nan'ao Specialty Products Store
spots.desc: An established local specialty store selling dried seafood, seaweed, honey and snacks.
spots.addr: First floor of the Science and Technology Building, Haibin Road, Houzhai Town

spots.name: Trendy Goods Collection Creative Store (Nan'ao Houzhai Store)
spots.desc: This cultural and creative products store combines traditional crafts with local specialties, offering Chaozhou-style souvenirs such as postcards, fridge magnets, mugs, and canvas bags. It also sells cookies, Chaozhou snacks, and some dried seafood.
spots.addr: No. 03, Building B, Houzhai Waterfront Plaza, opposite the Starfish Hotel

spots.name: Nan'ao Souvenirs (Specialty Products)
spots.desc: A large specialty shop selling Nan'ao snacks and souvenirs such as dried squid, dried shrimp, seaweed, biscuits and boxed gift sets.
spots.addr: No. 03, Building B, Houzhai Waterfront Plaza, opposite the Starfish Hotel

spots.name: Houjie Square
spots.desc: An expansive flat space at the heart of the city, and is the sight of all celebrations and festivals. Midway through the evening on any day, it's typical on the west end to see a sizable group line dancing to techno music. Feel welcome to copy the steps and join in, but don't expect the electric slide.
spots.addr: Kangle North Road

spots.name: Fang Family Ancestral Hall
spots.desc: A traditional Lingnan style ancestral hall dating from the Ming Dynasty.
spots.addr: 120 Hetian Avenue (河田大道120号)

spots.name: Jinyi Foot Washing
spots.desc: While seldom do the staff speak English, they have a menu of options in English and the rest is not difficult to figure out. Service and facilities are always tip top, and prices are competitive. Foot massage - ¥58, 60 min; body massage - ¥138-158, 90 min. Body massage includes admission to an area with a sauna, steam room, TV, internet, and pool table.

spots.name: Sports Park
spots.desc: (体育馆, Mandarin: Tiyuguan) has indoor badminton and pingpong courts for rent, outdoor basketball, a pool, and a large running/walking track. The park is a popular hangout for the locals on nights when the weather is nice.

spots.name: Qiaodong Bowling Hall
spots.desc: A 4.5-km drive north on Guantai road will bring you to this bowling hall, on the left side of the street a bit past Chenwu East Road.

spots.name: Kangle South Road
spots.desc: The main drag in Houjie, this street has eight blocks of clothing stores, shoe shops, mid range restaurants. Higher quality Chinese brand names are found here, as well as some genuine stores international brands, and a few stores peddling piles of cheap clothes and accessories. Busiest around the hours of 20:00-22:00.

spots.name: Neoclassicism Studio
spots.desc: A long walk down Kangle street to the south will take you to this two-story DVD seller. They have a range of foreign movies and TV series, software, and music. Quality is good, English movies are in English, and they function fine in the US. You can request to have them demo it for you. The software is generally not recommended.

spots.name: Xiang Fe Ge Wine Shop
spots.desc: Not a wine shop at all, this place serves terrific Hunan style food.
spots.addr: 镇康乐北路11号

spots.name: BoTon
spots.desc: On the high end of mid-range, this tastefully decorated establishment has an impressive range of food options. Includes Chinese, Italian, Thai curries, steaks, and fish. Food is pretty good considering how far they've stretched themselves.
spots.addr: Tiyu Road

spots.name: Al Pozzo
spots.desc: This Italian restaurant boasts great food and ambiance. Run by an Italian expat, you can't go wrong with most of the menu. Call them, and for free they will pick you up anywhere in town and drop you back off again. At the end of the meal you'll be given a small glass of homemade limoncello, which they'll gladly refill as many times as you can handle it (gratis!)
spots.addr: HouJie Road

spots.name: Houjie Bar Street
spots.desc: A small bar street on Kangle Folk Street, an angle street a ways south on Kangle Road. There are a couple trendy-seeming dance clubs with hired dancers, who will play Chinese dice with you when they aren't on stage. A live band will typically play two sets also, usually sappy sounding Chinese ballads. 350 ml beers can be bought for ¥30 each, although they are a much better deal when bought in…

spots.name: Buddha Bar
spots.desc: on Houjie Street serves beer, wine, and many options in spirits. Several of the wait staff speak English, and may sit down and chat with you if business is slow and you're alone.

spots.name: Irene's Bar
spots.desc: The only expat pub in Houjie, good range of beers on tap and in bottles, wine and spirits. Busy most nights of the week, relaxed atmosphere and friendly staff.
spots.addr: Yuefanshan Daodao

spots.name: Jiangmen Wuyi Overseas Chinese Museum
spots.local: 江门五邑华侨华人博物馆
spots.desc: Museum built in 2010 to commemorate the overseas achievements, lifestyle and journeys of the Jiangmen (Wuyi) region's massive number of overseas migrant Chinese in countries as diverse as Australia, Canada, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico, Singapore, South Africa, the United States and Vietnam in fields including agriculture, architecture, aviation, engineering, tin and gold mining and railways. Also…
spots.addr: Wuyi Overseas Chinese Plaza, Beixin Area, Pengjiang District (蓬江区北新区五邑华侨广场)

spots.name: Tea Hut Park
spots.desc: Site of the Tea Hut Temple (茶庵古寺), a temple built during the Ming Dynasty in honour of Zhang Sui (张遂), a famous Tang Dynasty astronomer monk who once lived here in a straw hut dubbed the Tea Hut. The park is contiguous with the much larger Baishuidai Park (白水带公园).
spots.addr: Waihai Subdistrict, Jianghai District (江海区外海街道)

spots.name: Changlang Eco Park
spots.desc: As of September 2019, the children's amusement rides are closed for renovation.
spots.addr: Donghai Road, Dongren Village, Liyue Subdistrict, Jianghai District (江海区礼乐街道东仁村东海路)

spots.name: Guan Shanyue Art Gallery
spots.desc: The Guan Shanyue Gallery is dedicated to the works of Guan Shanyue, a modern master of the Ling Nan school of Chinese ink painting. The Ling Nan (Ling Nan is the Tang Dynasty name for Guangdong and Guangxi provinces) originated in the early 20th century inspired by Japanese westernising schools. Guan Shanyue studied under the masters of the school and produced some very competent art in that…
spots.hours: 09:00-17:00, no entry after 16:30, closed on Mondays
spots.addr: 6026 Hongli Rd. Futian (福田区红荔路6026号)

spots.name: Zhizheng Art Museum
spots.desc: Claims to be the largest privately-owned museum in China. Visitors must show their ID card or passport before being allowed to enter. - Closed according the only review on Google Maps since may 2024.
spots.addr: 5th floor, Block A, KK100, 5016 Shennan East Road, Guiyuan Subdistrict, Luohu District (罗湖区桂园街道深南东路5016号京基100大厦A座五层)

spots.name: Shenzhen Chess Room Museum
spots.local: 深圳市棋国象棋博物馆
spots.desc: A private museum dedicated to xiangqi (Chinese chess). It has a collection of over 50,000 xiangqi-related objects, including chess boards, chess pieces, books and art work.
spots.addr: 1210, Sunny Golf Building, 7008 Shennan Avenue, Futian District (福田区深南大道7008阳光高尔夫大厦12楼1210)

spots.name: Shenzhen Piano Museum
spots.desc: Displays a collection of 46 old pianos obtained from various parts of the world.
spots.hours: 09:00-18:00, closed on the eve of Chinese New Year
spots.addr: Sector C, Level 4, Shenzhen Musical Instrument Mall, Guo Qi Building, 1002 Shangbu Road South, Futian District (福田区上步南路1002号国企大厦深圳乐器城四楼C区)

spots.name: Shenzhen Gas Science Museum
spots.desc: The first museum in China to be exclusively devoted to the science of gas.
spots.hours: Open on Wednesdays, Saturdays and Sundays. Wednesdays and Saturdays are reserved for school groups. All other visitors…
spots.addr: West Side, Level 1, Shenzhen Gas Building, 268 Mei'ao First Road, Futian District (福田区梅坳一路268号深燃大厦1楼西侧)

spots.name: Shenzhen Industrial Museum
spots.desc: Groups are required to make a booking before visiting. No booking is required for solo visitors.
spots.hours: 09:30-17:30, closed on Sundays and public holidays
spots.addr: Floors 2 to 10, Yellow Tower, Wing B, Shenzhen Civic Center, Fuzhong San Road, Futian District (福田区福中三路市民中心B区黄塔2-10楼)

spots.name: Fairy Lake Botanical Gardens
spots.local: 仙湖植物公园; Xiān​ Hú​ Zhí​wù​ Gōng​yuán​
spots.desc: This is Shenzhen's most beautiful park and surely one of the most beautiful in China. It sprawls over miles of foothills, valleys, rivers and lakes before climbing half way up Wutong Mountain. Main attraction is the Hong Fa Temple (see entry above) but there are beautiful and peaceful lakes surrounded by teahouses and pavilions which could inspire great poetry. Don't miss the azalea garden, the…
spots.price: ¥15 is charged for entry between 08:00 and 18:00. Entry before 08:00 or after 18:00 is free
spots.addr: 160 Fairy Lake Road, Luohu District (罗湖区莲塘仙湖路160号)

spots.name: Shenzhen Garden and Flower Exposition Center
spots.desc: This park started life as the site of an international garden exhibition in 2004. It is an enormous garden with an area of 660,000 m². It ranges from gently undulating to quite steep and contains gardens in many different styles, not only Chinese but from all over the world. Make sure you visit the hot houses and climb the hill past the waterfall to the pagoda on top of the hill. Views back to…
spots.addr: Zhuzilinxi, Futian District (at the intersection of Shennan Avenue and Qiaocheng East Road) (深圳市福田区竹子林西 (深南大道与侨城东路交汇处); Fútián​ Qū Zhú​zi​lín Xī (Shēn​nán…

spots.name: Mangrove Ecological Park
spots.desc: Hong Kong's Mai Po Marshes are one of the world's great birdwatching paradises as birds migrating from Siberia rest in the fishponds. The same birds also rest in the mangroves on Shenzhen Bay a scant two miles north of Mai Po. In the late 1990s when the Binhai Freeway was being built, there was public outrage at plans to route the road through the bird habitat of the mangroves, subsequently the…
spots.addr: main entrance at Furong Road and Xinzhou Road (福荣路 Fúróng Lù, 新洲路 Xīnzhōu Lù), Futian

spots.name: Oriental Palm Spring International Spa Club
spots.desc: Refurbished with a strong Thai themed interior decor, you almost think you are in a Thailand resort especially on the new first floor. One of the many big spas in the Futian area and well worth a try if you're not into the hanky panky business. OPS is famous for providing excellent service, massages and really good Chinese cuisine. The food is excellent although a little pricey for local…

spots.name: SLF International Spa Club
spots.desc: Branded as Water Cube is brand new, hence in excellent condition, and tastefully designed with an interior resembling a luxury hotel. Although English is barely spoken by anybody, the staff are clearly trained to be first class and they try their best to be helpful — and sell massages, which cost ¥48 for 45 minutes of lounge-chair massage through ¥128–238 for 90 minutes of full-body massage in…

spots.name: Queen Spa
spots.desc: This spa is showing its age like an old resort hotel in Las Vegas, although it remains a popular tourist destination in part because it has the notable advantage of having English-speaking staff on duty and identified with clearly visible tags year-round. The entry fee of ¥98 is waived after ¥168 of spa services paid, not including the 10% service charge and tips of ¥10-30 per 45 minutes.…

spots.name: Gold Coast Club
spots.desc: Beautiful interior, entry fee of ¥138 with 10% service charge. Party room rental for ¥60/hour to ¥120/hour depending on size with karaoke and chess and games included.
spots.addr: Building 1-4, Kaili Hotel, 2027 Jiabin Road East, Luohu

spots.name: Sentosa International SPA Club
spots.desc: Shuttle available, offering in March 2009 four hours of Chinese massage for ¥108 and ¥88 for any three types of foot, head, or leg massage.

spots.name: Shenzhen Golf Club
spots.desc: This is one of China's two oldest golf courses. When it was established in 1985 it was way out in the country but now it is surrounded by skyscrapers, providing a pleasant oasis in the heart of Futian. This is where the locals prefer to play.
spots.addr: Shennan Boulevard, Futian District (福田区深南大道)

spots.name: Luohu Commercial City
spots.desc: Offers a very different experience to shopping in Hong Kong and is therefore worth a visit if only spending a short time in China. Spread over several levels are many small stores, each selling similar products: watches, jewellery, handbags, clothes and DVDs. These products are rarely authentic but they are often very well made and detailed fakes. There are many stallholders pressuring shoppers…

spots.name: MixC Shopping Mall
spots.desc: The largest (and easily the most expensive) shopping mall in Shenzhen. Highlights include the following: Olympic size indoor Ice Skating Rink, Golden Harvest Cinema movie theater, Ole (high end supermarket with many imported items), Spaghetti House and Starbucks. Good option

spots.name: Central Walk
spots.desc: Another Shopping complex in Shenzhen. Base tenant is Carrefour, but also has usual shops, restaurants and a cinema. Three floors of shops arranged in a circle. Mostly women's clothes. Starbucks and Italian Best Coffee (Illy Coffee) are located here. Subway (Sandwiches) also has opened here.

spots.name: King Glory Plaza
spots.desc: A mall, along the lines of MixC. It is fairly high priced. It includes a movie theater as well as the "IN" bar/nightclub (that's the name of it) and "Yellow" bar. Eight floors connected by criss-crossed escalators give you enough stores to stay occupied for a few hours. Lots of restaurants in the sub-ground levels. Connected by a walkway to Rainbow Mall. There's a Pacific Coffee on the ground…

spots.name: Shun Hing Square
spots.desc: On Shennan Road, across from the MixC. Go to the Da Juyuan (大剧院) metro station. You won't miss it, because Diwang Dasha is among the tallest buildings in Shenzhen. The shopping center is actually very small, with just a few stores on three small levels, but it's in a nice area of town with lots of other attractions, so you might dart in to see what's to be found. Starbucks on the ground floor…

spots.name: City Mall
spots.desc: Six-story upscale shopping mall. Includes a bunch of restaurants, and nearby Songling Road (松岭路) also has a bunch of more authentic, distinctive, and reasonably priced cuisine.
spots.addr: 1095 Shennan Middle Road, Futian 福田区深南中路1095号

spots.name: Mingtong Electronics Market
spots.local: 明通数码城, Míngtōng Shùmǎ Chéng
spots.desc: Four floors. Watch parts, electronic toys, gadgets, and mobile phone parts, as well as a lot of cosmetics on the third floor and one section of the first floor.

spots.name: Yuanwang Digital Mall
spots.local: 远望数码商城, Yuǎnwàng Shùmǎ Shāngchéng
spots.desc: Three floors, mostly consisting of mobile phones and accessories. Behind it is an alley of reasonably priced restaurants.
spots.addr: northeast corner of Zhenhua Street (振华路, Zhènhuá Lù) and Huaqiangbei Street (华强北路, Huáqiángběi Lù)

spots.name: Jiahua Foreign Trade Clothing Market
spots.desc: Series of stalls selling lots of cheap clothing. It's not quite as huge as Luohu Commercial City, but it's worth a look.
spots.addr: Address: 广东省深圳市福田区华强北路2007号 English: No.2007, Huaqiang North Road, Futian District

spots.name: Shenzhen Book City
spots.desc: Bills itself as the biggest bookshop in the world, and it's really more of a mall anchored by a bookstore, with lots of restaurants and other shops in the same building. Great selection of books and related products. There is a small shop which specialises in English books, Eon Books.
spots.addr: 2014 Fu Zhong One Road, Futian District (福田区福中一路2014号)

spots.name: Tea World Terminal Market
spots.desc: A whole warehouse with many stores selling all things related to tea. Wonderful selection of everything from Pu'er-teas to tea-ware. They seem not to be focused on selling to tourists, which is very nice, but they still take time with you if you want to go through the tea ceremonies.

spots.name: Bagua First Road Eat Street
spots.desc: This was Shenzhen's first Eat Street. Food was originally Cantonese brought by homesick Hong Kong factory owners. It's now a smallish Eat Street compared to some of the others. Cantonese food is still good here but you can get food from all over China.
spots.addr: Bagua First Rd, Futian 福田区八卦一路

spots.name: Chegongmiao Eat Street
spots.desc: A particularly large eat street, with good Sichuan, Hunan and Taiwanese food. There is also a good if unauthentic Macau style restaurant. Centered around Tairan Fourth Road (泰然四路) up to Tairan Ninth Road (泰然九路).
spots.addr: Terra Industrial Zone, Futian District 福田区泰然工业区

spots.name: Huaqiangbei Eat Street
spots.desc: The food's in the streets and alleys parallel to Huaqiangbei. Hunan and Chaozhou are specialities. There are several shops specialising in Uyghur "naan" bread. An alley behind the main street specialises in Muslim food.
spots.addr: Huaqiang North Rd Futian 福田区华强北路

spots.name: Xinwen Road Eat Street
spots.desc: A bunch of moderately-priced sit-down restaurants near the press building—lots of Hunan food as usual, and other cuisines as well.
spots.addr: Xinwen Road, Futian 福田区新闻街

spots.name: Happy Together
spots.desc: Busy dim sum place. Menu only in Chinese, but it has some pictures.
spots.addr: 2038 Shennan Middle Road, Futian 福田街道深南中路2038号

spots.name: Modern Toilet Restaurant
spots.desc: Taiwanese chain's first branch in the mainland. Toilet themed restaurant, featuring toilets as seats and squatter toilet plates. Food is nothing special and costs about ¥25-35/dish, but come after dinner with a friend and bring the camera for the ¥10 chocolate ice cream. The surrounding Laojie commercial district goes from cosmopolitan to near-dystopian in the course of about two hours every…
spots.addr: 2nd Floor Jiefang Lu 1004 Dongmen Buxing

spots.name: XPats Bar
spots.desc: It's in Central Walk, top floor on the right hand walkway (outside the building) directly opposite the Great China Building. Beer, wine and pizza served. Big screen sports coverage.
spots.addr: FL1016 Street Lvl Eastern Sidewalk Central Walk Mall 福田取中心城大中华大厦对面.

spots.name: Base Bar
spots.desc: A live rock music venue. Great vibe and great interior deco. There are nice three-sided booths along the walls for larger groups. A variety of acts play into the early morning. Friendly waitstaff with Communist Star armbands.
spots.price: Door cover can sometimes run up to ¥100, cocktails from ¥30 (the Gin-Tonic is excellent), bottles of Jim Beam ¥380
spots.addr: 1019 Shangbu South Road, Futian District (福田区上步南路1019号; Fú​tián​ Qū​ Shàngbù​ Nán​ Lù​​)

spots.name: Ibiza
spots.desc: A European style two-story pub. It is quite popular among foreigners.

spots.name: Ren Jian Du Hui In Club
spots.desc: This is a KTV that has a lounge with performances on the 2nd floor, and private rooms on the rest of the floors. You can pay to have male or female hosts sit with you - for a tip. 200+ for the girls and 500+ for the gigolos. You can have them line up for you and you can pick the one you like.
spots.addr: 深圳市春风路桂都大夏2F-5F

spots.name: 3D Bar
spots.desc: Guinness is available on tap. There are also many other international beers available (bottled mainly). The outside tables along the walkway are good for a relaxing pint, the inside tables and the outside tables closest to the front door are if you're looking for a livelier atmosphere, better
spots.addr: Block B, Bar Street, Citic Plaza, 1093 Shennan Rd

spots.name: Club Viva
spots.desc: Just north of Coco Park shopping mall, in the middle of the boardwalk. Usually packed on weekends with many foreigners.

spots.name: Cross-Sea Bridge
spots.desc: The Donghai Island Cross-Sea Bridge is 32.5 km long, one of the longest cross-sea spans in the world.

spots.name: Longhaitian Tourism Area
spots.desc: Longhaitian is in the eastern part of the island. It is a natural area formed by mountains, valleys, hills, beaches, and green forests. Longhaitian is one of the most remarkable scenic spots in the area. It is believed to have formed from a volcanic eruption in ancient times. Standing at 110 meters, the area is perpetually lush and picturesque. It is said that before the French colonizers took…

spots.name: Longshuiling
spots.desc: Longshuiling is the gateway for ships entering and exiting Zhanjiang Port, a natural "green marker." Beneath it, there are abandoned military tunnels carved through the mountain, full of clever mechanisms. It is planned to be developed into a multifunctional entertainment spot called the "Underground Dragon Palace." Longshuiling is not high, and compared to the average natural elevation of about…

spots.name: Longhaitian Beach
spots.desc: Also known as Longhai Beach, it is recognized by world tourism authorities as the second longest beach in the world, stretching 28 kilometers long and 150 to 300 meters wide. It ranks just behind Australia's Gold Coast and is the longest beach in China.

spots.name: puolao gong
spots.desc: Puolao Gong is a famous sea harvesting spot close to Dongshan Town, easily accessible by electric scooter. Sea harvesting activities are closely tied to the tidal schedule, so it’s important to check the tidal times before setting out. When the tide goes out, a large variety of seafood appears on the beach, attracting many people to collect them. The first wave of participants usually gathers the…

spots.name: Zhuang Clan Ancestral Hall
spots.desc: The Zhuang Clan Ancestral Hall carries an 800-year history and serves as a spiritual and cultural hub for the Zhuang family. Dongshan Village, renowned for its rich heritage, has produced numerous notable figures who made significant contributions in various fields. The ancestral hall honors the Zhuang ancestors, including Zhuang Qiang (a scholar official), Zhuang Guanghan (a scholar of the…

spots.name: Donghai Island God Parade Activities
spots.desc: In Zhanjiang, many towns and villages share a tradition of processions known as “You Shen” (God Parade), a custom deeply rooted in the region’s culture. Activities like piercing with “Ling Jian” (divine arrows) or walking on “Zhang” (rods) are part of these vibrant rituals. Commonly referred to as the “Nian Li” (Annual Festival), this unique tradition in western Guangdong centers on communal…
spots.hours: Every year on the 4th day of the Lunar New Year

spots.name: Donghai Island Traditional Customs and Beliefs
spots.desc: Donghai Island preserves many traditional customs and folk beliefs. One of these is “Bai Gongzu”, a long-standing local custom where, on the 2nd and 16th day of each month, as well as during important festivals, every household prepares offerings to honor the family gods and ancestors, praying for peace and happiness. Another unique spiritual treasure of the island is the Ji Tong culture.…
spots.hours: Every year on the 2nd and 16th day of the Lunar Month and during important festivals
spots.addr: Min’an Town, Donghai Island, Zhanjiang

spots.name: Donghai Island Human Dragon Dance
spots.desc: The Donghai Island Human Dragon Dance is an ancient traditional dance art that originated in the late Ming and early Qing dynasties, with a history of over 300 years. The dance consists of three parts: the dragon head, body, and tail, performed by both strong men and children. The dragon head symbolizes the spirit of the dragon, with a strong man carrying three children to represent the dragon’s…
spots.hours: Every year on the 16th day of the Lunar New Year
spots.addr: Dongshanwei, Dongshan Town, Donghai Island, Zhanjiang Development Zone

spots.name: Dongshan Goose
spots.desc: The white-cut goose is served in large portions with a rich and fragrant taste, with a side of sweet dessert soup.

spots.name: Yi Cha Yi Dian
spots.desc: A popular restaurant, known for its tea and meals. The restaurant offers a wide variety of food, blending local Guangdong specialties with creative cuisine. The restaurant serves various traditional Cantonese snacks, such as siu mai, shrimp dumplings, and spring rolls. The shrimp dumplings are thin-skinned, tender, and flavorful. The restaurant offers a wide selection of dim sum, from traditional…

spots.name: Oyster Feast · Zhanjiang Oysters (Donghai Branch)
spots.local: 蚝抵食·湛江生蚝（东海店）
spots.desc: The oysters here are of excellent quality, with varying sizes – the small ones are delicate and charming, while the larger ones are bold and impressive.

spots.name: Fresh Flavor Stone Mill Rice Noodle Rolls
spots.desc: A restaurant that makes rice noodle rolls using traditional stone mill techniques, resulting in a smooth and delicate texture. Popular among both locals and tourists.

spots.name: Guoxing Plaza
spots.desc: A key commercial hub in the area. Facilities include a clothing mall. There are several hotels in the vicinity.

spots.name: Dongshanli Teahouse
spots.desc: Tea house with distinctive local characteristics, representative of Donghai Island’s traditional tea culture. Also traditional snacks, such as dim sum. The design of the teahouse blends modern and traditional elements. Tea masters demonstrate the tea ceremony, guiding guests.

spots.name: Bird's View Pavilion
spots.desc: This pavilion, perched on the Karst peak on the Southern end of the waterfront on the Yi River gives a spectacular view of both the town of Xingping and the distinctive surrounding scenery. The climb is a bit challenging in sections and you are advised to do it in the cool part of the day. It comprises 1159 steps taking you to an altitude of 220 metres above the town. The path as you get higher…

spots.name: ¥20 Point
spots.desc: The landscape on the ¥20 note is just outside Xingping, You may think that the Chinese are looking for money from you when really they are pointing this out. You can take a photo from the exact same spot as this picture. Free

spots.name: Lotus Cave
spots.desc: While not a great cave to explore (any cave in the Yangshuo/Guilin area is much better), the bicycle ride to and from is quite pleasant. Relatively free of traffic, and well-paved by GuangXi standards, Lotus cave is locate on the southeastern edge of a beautiful valley. ¥45/person

spots.name: Li River Boat Trip
spots.desc: Take a boat trip along the most famous parts of the Li River for an hour and a half. These small boats are much more enjoyable that the large cruise ships that cruise by and far cheaper. Bargain hard.

spots.name: Yangdi - Xingping
spots.desc: As of Aug 2013, this 18-24 km walk can be done both ways and it is a far more peaceful way to enjoy the Li river and mountain scenery than a loud noisy boat down the river. It takes you along the pebbly shores of the river, through many small villages, fields and bamboo forests. You will have to take three bamboo rafts across the river at about ¥10-30 each after bargaining. Just tell someone you…

spots.name: Hike to Fisher village
spots.desc: This is an hour's or so walk south of town. One can also reach the village by boat. Local will take you to the roof tops if you like for a panoramic view for ¥5. There are pictures of the Clinton's when they visited the spot on the walls. The youth hostel in town has a map with directions.

spots.name: This Old Place Cafe
spots.desc: This cafe, which is linked to the Hostel by the same name, offers a good range of Chinese traditional dishes, as well as some more Westernised versions (like Sweet & Sour Chicken without bones!) The staff are extremely attentive, lovely and go out of their way to make you comfortable and welcome. And interesting feature of this restaurant is the pond and washbasin between the bar and the…

spots.name: Love Landscape Restaurant
spots.desc: An interesting little place with a limited English menu, LLR has very few vegetable dishes, but quite a few beef, chicken, or pork dishes. What is memorable about this place, though, is two-fold. Firstly, just in front of the restaurant on a little patio, the management keeps live animals for consumption, including Li Jiang fish, quail, chickens, ducks, and bamboo rats. Secondly, try their Snake…
spots.addr: Rongtan St.

spots.name: 7# Cafe
spots.desc: A lovely little place run by some very friendly staff, with good music playing, and heaters under the tables which are perfect when Xingping isn't being too kind weather-wise. The owners always brought out a game of Connect 4 to play while waiting for food, and it makes a nice cosy alternative to TOP Cafe down the road. The food is decent value.
spots.addr: Old Street

spots.name: Local Jiu Place
spots.desc: Sells local Osmanthus wine (of varying strengths) for very little money. The extremely nice sales girl even speaks a little English and offers a couple of free tastes from the large jugs.
spots.addr: Rongtan St

spots.name: Liyuan Park
spots.local: 梨园公园, 梨园 Li Garden
spots.desc: One of the oldest and most accessible parks on the East Lake, all summer long it is a popular swimming area for the youths and families alike. Elsewhere on the lake, there are fancier beaches where admission is charged.
spots.addr: 189 Donghu Rd, Wuchang District (东湖路189号)

spots.name: Mao Zedong's East Lake Villa
spots.desc: The East Lake is home to another one of Chairman Mao's villas. He returned here annually and typically stayed a few months. The decor was designed in the 1950s fashion, which strikes many visitors as odd, yet there are plenty of indicators that it is no ordinary person's home. One of the most interesting sites is Mao's large indoor swimming pool. Mao's pool seems to no longer be accessible. Also…
spots.addr: East Lake Hotel, 142 Donghu Road, Wuchang District (武昌区东湖路142号东湖宾馆内)

spots.name: Museum of Hydrobiological Sciences
spots.local: 水生生物博物馆, Museum of Aquatic Organisms
spots.desc: A museum attached to the Institute of Hydrobiology, a research institute run by the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The museum holds over 400,000 individual specimens, including some from extinct species such as the Yangtze River Dolphin. Visitors are required to make an appointment at least one day before visiting.
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 08:30-12:00, 14:30-17:30, no entry in last 30 minutes, closed on weekends
spots.addr: 7 Donghu South Road, Wuchang District (武昌区东湖南路7号)

spots.name: Former Residence of Zhou Enlai
spots.desc: Communist Party statesman Zhou Enlai lived here with his wife for four months in 1938 while helping to coordinate the war against Japan. The residence has been fully restored and is open to the public.
spots.addr: No. 27 Zone One, Luojia Hill, Wuhan University (汉大学珞珈山一区27号)

spots.name: Yifu Museum of China University of Geosciences
spots.local: 中国地质大学逸夫博物馆
spots.desc: Has a large collection of minerals and an impressive display of dinosaur skeletons.
spots.hours: Weekend opening hours: Oct-Apr 08:00-12:00, 14:00-17:00; May-Sep 08:00-12:00, 14:30-17:30. Weekend and public holiday…
spots.addr: China University of Geosciences (中国地质大学)

spots.name: Shimen Peak Memorial Park
spots.local: 石门峰纪念公园, 石门峰名人文化公园 Shimen Peak Famous People Culture Park
spots.desc: The slopes of the Stone Gate Peak (石门峰) are occupied by a large cemetery whose owners apparently are very serious about sponsoring public art. As a result, the hill's foothills are home to what may be the largest sculpture park this side of Skopje. The 100th anniversary of the Xinhai Revolution were commemorated by a series of monuments to its participants. Another memorial complex commemorates…
spots.addr: 9 Shimenfeng Road, Hongshan District (洪山区石门峰路9号)

spots.name: Museum of Huazhong Agricultural University
spots.desc: Visitors are expected to make a booking before visiting the museum. If you need a guided tour (which might only be available in Chinese), you should book at least 2 or 3 days in advance.
spots.hours: Mon-Fri 14:30-17:30, public holidays 08:30-11:30, 14:30-17:30. May be closed during summer and winter vacation periods
spots.addr: Huazhong Agricultural University, 1 Shizishan Street, Hongshan District (洪山区狮子山街1号华中农业大学)

spots.name: Ethnology Museum of South Central University for Nationalities
spots.local: 中南民族大学民族学博物馆
spots.desc: The museum displays a collection of cultural items from several of the major ethnic minorities in southern China, including the Miao, Zhuang, Li, Tujia and Yao minorities. Visitors are required to make an appointment at least one day before visiting.
spots.hours: Tue-Fri 09:00-11:30, 14:30-16:30, closed on Mondays and weekends

spots.name: Museum of Wuhan Iron and Steel Group Corp
spots.local: 中国武钢博物馆, WISCO Museum
spots.desc: The official museum of the Wuhan Iron and Steel Group Corp (WISCO). Founded in 1958, WISCO was the first iron and steel company to be established after the founding of the People's Republic. The museum has exhibitions about the history of the company and the Chinese steel industry in general. Closed as of March 2025 for renovation.
spots.addr: 30 Zhijin Avenue, Qingshan District (青山区冶金大道30号)

spots.name: WISCO Cultural Tourism Area
spots.desc: While branded as a tourism area, it is essentially a guided tour to the operating factories of WISCO, which features the preserved Blast Furnace No. 1 that was used from 1958 to 2019. Depending on the price you paid, your tour will also consist of a visit to remote control rooms and a hot rolling production line that processes steel slabs into sheets. As an off-the-beaten-path destination, guided…
spots.addr: WISCO Gate 1

spots.name: Zhanggongshan Village
spots.desc: A tourist resort on the north shore of Yanxi Lake in eastern Wuhan. One major attraction here is the Li Zhuang Museum of Ancient Architecture (李庄古建筑博物馆), also known as the Zhanggongshan Museum of Ancient Architecture and Folk Culture (张公山寨古建民俗文化博物馆), which consists of a variety of traditional houses and other old buildings that have been relocated here from other parts of China. In addition, the…
spots.price: The standard fee is ¥90. Persons over 65 pay ¥60. There are no charges for children under 1.2 metres in height. The fee…
spots.addr: Yanxi Lake, Baiyushan Subdistrict, Qingshan District (青山区白玉山街严西湖畔)

spots.name: Optics Valley Book Store
spots.desc: A major book store, next to the numerous shopping malls of Optics Valley Square (Guanggu Guangchang 光谷广场). Has a small section with books China in foreign languages (mostly English), and books for foreigner studying Chinese. The actual book store is, as of 2018, part of the national Xinhua chain. This is the part of the city where all the universities are, so if you look like a Westerner, you'd…
spots.addr: Level B1, Optics Valley Capital Building, 1 Minyuan Road, Guanshan Subdistrict, Hongshan District (洪山区关山街道民院路1号光谷资本大厦B1层)

spots.name: Desi Masala
spots.local: 德西玛莎拉巴基斯坦餐厅, Pakistani Cuisine Restaurant
spots.desc: Traditional Pakistani dishes such as Chicken/Mutton/Beef Karahi, Vegetable Pakora and Samosa, Cheese Naan, Garlic Naan, Shahi Kheer, Seekh Kebab, Chicken Tikka, Raita, Daal Makhni, Beef Handi, Pizza, Burger, Salad, Soup and Tandoori BBQ with a vegan option. The restaurant also hosts a weekly buffet on Saturdays for which the price for lunch is ¥52 and the dinner for ¥68. The restaurant is…
spots.addr: F1-002 Future City Building, 147 Luoshi South Road, Hongshan District (洪山区珞狮南路147号来城购物公园F1层002)

spots.name: Kebab Kingdom
spots.desc: kebabs in Turkish style plus some Indian dishes. Deliveries from 11:30-21:00, free a 2-km radius and ¥4 for orders more than ¥30 for a 3-km radius.
spots.addr: Shop 1, Zone A, Manjianghong Building Annex 1, Central China Normal University, 152 Luoyu Road, Hongshan District (洪山区珞喻路152号华中师范大学满江红大楼附一楼A区1号门面)

spots.name: Real Taste
spots.local: Real Taste 巴基斯坦餐厅
spots.desc: Traditional Pakistani dishes such as Biryani, Chicken Curry, Cheese Naan, Gol Gappay, Seekh Kebab, Chicken Handi. The restaurant also hosts a weekly buffet for ¥55 per person which is quite popular in international students of Wuhan.
spots.price: ¥50 for a decent meal with a soft drink
spots.addr: 14-66 Shizishan North Street, Hongshan District (洪山区狮子山北路66-14号)

spots.name: Indian Marka
spots.desc: Traditional Indian cuisine with a vegan option. Indian Marka is a quite popular chain of restaurants in Wuhan with at least three franchises in the City.

spots.name: Grammy Club International
spots.desc: One of Wuhan's international clubs, playing R'n'B, hip hop and rap music.
spots.addr: 124 Minzu Avenue, Optics Valley Square, Hongshan District (洪山区光谷广场民族大道124号)

spots.name: Helen's Cafe Zhuodao Spring Branch
spots.local: Helens小酒馆 武汉卓刀泉店
spots.desc: Pizza, pasta, hamburgers that are fine for the taste and great for the price. Beer, shishah and a wide variety of cocktails means the dance floor fills up as the night gets on. Wednesday night is ladies night and it is the place to be. Lots of foreigners, good pizza, good drinks. Can play your own music if you like - sometimes a blessing, sometimes a curse. Ladies night Wednesday night - a weekly…
spots.addr: Level 2, Building 1, Zhuodao Spring Antiques & Jewellery City, 370 Luoyu Road, Hongshan District (洪山区珞喻路370号卓刀泉古玩珠宝城四合院1楼2层)

spots.name: Pin Club
spots.local: 品酒吧, formerly known as Top One Bar
spots.desc: Chinese style club, lots of tables, live entertainment and not a lot of dance floor.
spots.addr: 88 Luoshi North Road, Hongshan District (洪山区珞狮北路88)

spots.name: Queens Bar
spots.desc: In Wuchang's own little club district, refurbished. Limited dance floor, plenty of tables, liquor by the bottle. Friendly atmosphere towards foreigners.
spots.hours: As of December 2019, the bar is reportedly closed for renovations
spots.addr: 82 Luoshi North Road, Hongshan District (洪山区珞狮北路82号)

spots.name: VOX Livehouse
spots.desc: The most popular bar in Wuhan for non-Chinese, VOX is a small bar which regularly has shows on the weekend playing host to underground Chinese acts ranging from rock, punk and indie to experimental. Has a DJ after shows playing electro, indie-dance-rock among other things.
spots.addr: Guoguang Building, 118 Lumo Road, Hongshan District (洪山区鲁磨路118号国光大厦)

spots.name: Wuhan Prison
spots.desc: A dirty, frenzy free for all anything goes dive bar. They have absinthe. Good luck getting out of there sober. Staff is friendly (by Chinese standards); clientele includes locals as well as European and (to a slightly lesser extent) Anglophone expats.
spots.addr: Block A semi-basement, Guoguang Building, 118 Lumo Road, Hongshan District (洪山区鲁磨路118号国光大厦A座半地下室)

spots.name: Dayuwan Village
spots.desc: One of the best preserved traditional villages in the Wuhan region. Has around 50 stone buildings dating from the Ming and Qing dynasties.
spots.addr: Shuangquan Village, Mulan Township, Huangpi District (黄陂区木兰乡双泉村)

spots.name: Jinligou Tourist Resort
spots.local: 锦里沟旅游城 Jinli Valley Tourist Resort, 锦里沟 Jinligou
spots.desc: A tourist resort in a scenic mountain valley with a Tujia minority theme. Cultural performances are held here daily. Other amusements include a glass bridge and a 1800-metre long mountain slide. Accommodation is available at the site.
spots.addr: Daoshichong Village, Caidian Township, Huangpi District (黄陂区蔡店乡道士冲村)

spots.name: Mulan Grassland
spots.desc: According to legend, this is where Hua Mulan learnt to ride a horse and use a bow and arrow. The area is now a kind of Mongolian-esque theme park. Visitors can practice archery, go horse riding, rafting, rowing, grass skiing or ice skating (though these activities attract extra charges). There is also a special performance, which depicts some of the cavalry battles from the Mulan legend.
spots.hours: Normally open 08:00-20:00. Mulan Grassland closed in November 2019 for renovations but is expected to reopen in 2020
spots.price: General admission is ¥78. Tickets for the performance cost ¥120
spots.addr: Zhangjiazha Village, Wangjia River Town, Huangpi District (黄陂区王家河镇张家榨村)

spots.name: Mulan Qingliang Village Scenic Area
spots.desc: Features a traditional village surrounded by lakes, rolling hills, forests and flower gardens. Besides walking around and enjoying the scenery, visitors can also partake in a range of activities such as skiing, boating, swimming, riding a cliff swing, or simply relaxing in the hot springs. The village itself is called Luojiashan Village (刘家山村) and lies at the far northern end of the park.
spots.addr: Caidian Subdistrict, Huangpi District (黄陂区蔡店街道)

spots.name: Mulan Rose Garden
spots.desc: The largest rose garden in central China. Has over 160 varieties of roses covering an area of around 2800 mu (about 187 hectares). The flowers begin to bloom in March or April and can be seen until around November.
spots.addr: No. 1 Luojiadawan, Shengtian Village, Wangjiahe Subdistrict, Huangpi District (黄陂区王家河街胜天村罗家大湾1号)

spots.name: Mulanshan Scenic Area
spots.local: 木兰山风景区, Mount Mulan Scenic Area
spots.desc: Mulanshan (or Mount Mulan) is named after Hua Mulan, the legendary female Chinese warror who is now widely known outside China thanks to Disney. According to some versions of the story, Hua Mulan lived in the area with her grandmother before joining the army. There is a small museum about Hua Mulan near the entrance to the scenic area. The mountain is dotted with old Buddhist and Taoist temples…
spots.price: ¥80; some individual sights charge their own fees; the temple area charges ¥30. The cable car charges ¥35 for a return…
spots.addr: Huangpi District (黄陂区)

spots.name: Shengtian Farm Scenic Area
spots.local: 武汉木兰胜天农庄风景区, 木兰胜天风景区, Mulan Shengtian Scenic Area
spots.desc: A hilly scenic area adjacent to a water reservoir. Offers a range of activities, including hiking, rock climbing, ziplining, rafting, go-kart racing and more. Special events such as music and cultural festivals are sometimes held here. Accommodation is available on site.
spots.price: The standard ticket price is ¥90, which is discounted to ¥70 for children over 1.2 metres in height and adults aged 60…
spots.addr: Wangjiahe Town, Huangpi District (黄陂区王家河镇)

spots.name: Yaojiashan Scenic Area
spots.local: 姚家山风景区, Mount Yaojia Scenic Area
spots.desc: A tourist resort in a scenic mountain village. The village played an important role in the Second World War, being the site of a base for the Fifth Division of the New Fourth Army (a Communist-controlled unit of the Chinese national army). The old army office has been preserved as a heritage site and there is a museum nearby.
spots.price: The entry fee is ¥80. Accommodation is available for ¥418 per night
spots.addr: Yaojiashan Village, Caidian Subdistrict, Huangpi District (黄陂区蔡店街道姚家山村)

spots.name: Yunwushan Scenic Area
spots.local: 云雾山风景区, Mount Yunwu Scenic Area
spots.desc: Best known for its many azaleas, which are in full bloom during the months of April and May.
spots.price: General admission is ¥65. A combo ticket, which includes both general admission plus entry to the wax museum, the ice…
spots.addr: Paotongdian Village, Lijiaji Town, Huangpi District (黄陂区李家集镇泡桐店村)

spots.name: Plough Age Agricultural Park
spots.local: 农耕年华农业风情园, 农耕年华 Plough Age
spots.desc: Designed to educate people about agriculture. Features a variety of different gardens, as well as greenhouses, animals pens and a fish pond. Visitors can pick their own fruit and catch their own fish. There is also a museum where you can learn about traditional Chinese farming techniques. Other features of the park include a re-creation of a traditional village, as well as facilities for sports…
spots.price: Ticket prices: ¥70 (Mar-Jun, Sep-Oct), ¥60 (Nov-Feb, Jul-Aug). Fishing rod hire fees: ¥10-20 (plus a deposit of…
spots.addr: Zhongxin Road, Wuhu Farm, Huangpi District (黄陂区武湖农场中心路)

spots.name: Crape Myrtle Garden
spots.desc: A crape myrtle garden covering an area of around 133 hectares, which will eventually expand to about 333 hectares. A museum at the garden explains the history and science of growing crape myrtle trees. Other attractions include walking and cycling tracks, a glass bridge, a flying fox, an archery range, and a children's amusement park. The garden also provides camping grounds and hotel…
spots.price: Tickets are ¥80 (discounted to ¥60 if purchased online). Children over 1.2 metres in height and adults aged from 60 to…
spots.addr: No. 1 Fenglesi Village, Cangbu Subdistrict, Xinzhou District (新洲区仓埠街丰乐寺村特1号)

spots.name: Liangjiang Evening Cruises
spots.desc: A 1-hour trip on the Yangtse (Chang Jiang) and Jialing rivers gives you a night view of Chongqing's modern skyline.

spots.name: Yangtze River cruises
spots.desc: Longer cruises on the Yangtze River will take you through the cradle of China, while giving you the opportunity to see some spectacular scenery. There are several different companies operating these cruises.

spots.name: Baolin Museum
spots.desc: A large private museum established by retired PLA general Chen Baolin. The museum's name is incorrectly translated into English as 'Baolin Art Museum'. In fact, this is more than just an art museum. The museum's exhibits pertain to a broad range of subjects, including arts, culture, history and paleontology.
spots.addr: 99 Longzhan Road (龙展路99号)

spots.name: Chinese Contemporary Art Museum
spots.local: Museum of Contemporary Chinese Art, 华人当代美术馆
spots.desc: Established in 1995 with the assistance of the director of the National Art Museum of China, the museum is claimed to be the PRC's first privately-owned art museum. The museum features works by contemporary artists from all over China.
spots.addr: 59 Hubin Road East, Huixing Subdistrict (回兴街道湖滨东路59号)

spots.name: Long Museum Chongqing
spots.local: Dragon Art Museum Chongqing Branch, 龙美术馆重庆馆
spots.desc: A private art museum established by the wealthy collectors Liu Yiqian and his wife Wang Wei. The museum also has two branches in Shanghai. Groups of 26 people or more are required to make a reservation at least 2 days before their visit.
spots.addr: Levels 1-3, Building A, Guohua Finance Center, 9 Juxianyan Plaza (聚贤岩广场9号国华金融中心A栋1-3层)

spots.name: Emperor Ming Yuzhen's Tomb
spots.local: 明玉珍皇帝陵, 明玉珍睿陵, 明玉珍墓
spots.desc: Ming Yuzhen (1331-1336) was a peasant rebel leader who founded the short-lived Xia Empire, officially known as the Great Xia, which controlled parts of modern-day Sichuan and Chongqing from 1362-1371. He is the only emperor known to have been buried in Chongqing. A museum at the site displays artefacts that have been recovered from the tomb. Visitors can also view the inside of the tomb.
spots.addr: Jiangbeizui Central Park (江北嘴中央公园)

spots.name: Chongqing Garden Expo Park
spots.local: Expo Garden Center, 重庆园博园
spots.desc: The park was established in 2011 for the 8th China (Chongqing) International Garden Expo and has since become one of the city's most popular parks.
spots.addr: 1 Longjing Road (龙景路1号)

spots.name: Liangjiang International Film City
spots.local: 两江国际影视城, Liangjiang Movie City, 民国街 Republic Street
spots.desc: A recreation of downtown Chongqing as it looked in the 1940s. It was built for Feng Xiaogang's 2012 film Back to 1942, and is now a tourist attraction. The streets feature replicas of many well-known buildings from the time, as well as staff dressed in period costumes.
spots.addr: Longxing Industrial Park (龙兴工业园区内)

spots.name: Outside beer gardens
spots.desc: Serve reasonably priced drinks and is always crowded with good atmosphere and live premiership matches on big screens, do not eat here though!

spots.name: Zhaoxing Guesthouse Restaurant
spots.desc: A small restaurant attached to a guesthouse in Zhaoxing serving Chinese dishes.
spots.addr: Zhaoxing Village, Liping County, Guizhou, China

spots.name: Sertri Gompa
