spots.desc: (Dacanglangmu Saichisi) temple where traditional Tibetan sky-burials are still practiced (last rites are private), located on northern hill.

spots.name: Hui Mosque
spots.desc: Located close to the Sichuan side temple near the entrance gate

spots.name: Wind Horse Trekking
spots.desc: Offers guided horse treks from one to three days into the beautiful surrounding grasslands, hills, and valleys. On the overnight treks, you will have the opportunity to stay in a tent with Tibetan nomads and learn about how they live. Sonam, the owner, is an experienced local guide who speaks English, and he will give you a great introduction to traditional nomad life.

spots.name: Langmusi Tibetan Horse Trekking
spots.desc: Langmusi Horse Trekking also offers anything from 1 to 3 day horse treks where you can stay with Tibetan nomads. The lady at the horse trekking place speaks excellent English. They also sell a useful map of Langmusi and surroundings for ¥10; can be bought at their shop or at guesthouses around town.

spots.name: Bicycle Rental
spots.desc: Langmusi Horse Trekking also offers mountain bikes to rent. You can bike to a few destinations on the roads (Flower Lake is 36km, Zhagana about 97 km) or take some of the trekking trails. The White Dragon River trail is bikeable, and if you're strong and adventurous you can ride past the nomad camps all the way to the Ocean of Flowers and then take the road back into town. Challenging ride, at…

spots.name: Lesha's Restaurant
spots.desc: Has been open for more than a decade here and has a great, lively atmosphere. Run by a Muslim family that speak basic English, but are very friendly. The food is very good (try the apple-pie) and quite cheap and their couch is the best place in town for meeting other travelers.

spots.name: Xunshi Hot Springs
spots.desc: Xunshi Hot Springs is one of the most famous natural hot springs in southern Sichuan. The spring water is rich in minerals and maintains a temperature of 53–56°C year-round. Visitors can enjoy soaking in outdoor pools while surrounded by picturesque hills and rivers. The resort offers spa services, relaxation areas, and restaurants serving local Sichuan cuisine. It is ideal for a day trip or…
spots.addr: Wenquan Road, Xunsi Town

spots.name: Spring Wind Village
spots.desc: Spring Wind Village is a picturesque rural village in Júnlián County, known for its traditional Sichuan-style architecture and cultural heritage. Visitors can stroll through narrow lanes, observe local farming practices, and experience folk customs. The village hosts occasional cultural festivals and craft workshops, making it an excellent destination for those interested in rural tourism and…
spots.addr: Chunfeng Township

spots.name: Chuanhong Teahouse
spots.desc: Great place to taste local Sichuan tea and relax. Content: Serves authentic 川红茶 and traditional tea snacks. Perfect for a casual tea break.
spots.addr: South Gate Street, Junlian County

spots.name: Alley Coffee House
spots.desc: Cozy interior, good for reading or resting.Content: Serves coffee, tea, and light snacks. Popular with young locals and tourists seeking a quiet break.
spots.addr: Entrance of the old street and alley in Yunlian County

spots.name: Jianfu Palace (建福宫)
spots.desc: This is the first major Taoist architectural complex visitors encounter upon entering the mountain. Featuring traditional courtyard layouts and ancient wooden structures, it presents a quiet and refined ancient temple atmosphere at the start of the scenic route.
spots.hours: Hours follow the Front Mountain scenic area schedule
spots.price: Access is covered by the Front Mountain admission ticket
spots.addr: inside the Front Mountain scenic area of Qingcheng Mountain

spots.name: Qingcheng Jia
spots.desc: A well-known local farm-style restaurant. The signature ginkgo stewed chicken has a gentle, sweet broth; try also smoked mountain bacon and stir-fried wild greens. A quiet courtyard setting, great for groups.
spots.addr: No.52-2, Group 6, Shangyuan Community, Qushan Road

spots.name: Luo Chicken Restaurant
spots.desc: Long-running local eatery famous for cold poached chicken. Ginkgo chicken soup and green pepper chicken are popular picks. Simple, no-frills dining room, popular with day trippers.
spots.addr: No.76, Group 3, Taohua Village, Qingchengshan Town

spots.name: Taoist Vegetarian Restaurant at Tianshi Cave
spots.desc: Authentic temple vegetarian food. Mock meat dishes, mushroom hot pot and seasonal mountain vegetables. Peaceful atmosphere for visitors wanting a Taoist dining experience.
spots.addr: Front Mountain, inside the Tianshi Cave Taoist temple

spots.name: Hot Springs
spots.desc: Some guesthouses can arrange tours to go there, or just hail a taxi, Or just hitch Hike There. There are indoor tile bathtubs where you can bathe in privacy. The baths are dingy and muddy and not much of a visual experience, but may be enjoyable for their therapeutic effect. You can also find some hot water in open streams however it's not very deep and not really suitable for a good soak.

spots.name: Tian Tian Restaurant
spots.desc: Tian Tian is a little restaurant sporting an English menu. The owner, Mr. Zheng, is not a local (he arrived from his native Chengdu in 2003), but has zealously taken on the role of town ambassador for foreign visitors. He is very friendly and happy to indulge in some chat with his basic English, and is always willing to learn more and keeps a handwritten journal to document new words learned. He…

spots.name: Snow Mountain Restaurant
spots.local: 贡嘎雪山民族特 Gòng gā xuěshān mínzú
spots.desc: Tasty, simple, reasonable, and authentic Tibetan food, with both English and Chinese menus.
spots.addr: 222 Xingfu Donglu

spots.name: Yihun Lhatso (Lake)
spots.desc: A clear and nice Lake. You can hire a horse in the lake, or come from town with a horse- takes 2-4 hours of Beautiful riding. You can also take a taxi from town or just walk or hitch hike.
spots.addr: 13 km West from town Near the road that goes to Dege

spots.name: Horse Treks
spots.desc: A good way to see the countryside around the town. One nice option is to ride to Yihun Lhatso- A nice Lake 13 km from town. The owner at Pani Hotel can Help organize horses and guides - His wife\Daughter Understands a little English.

spots.name: Tagong Grassland
spots.desc: Open grasslands surrounding Tagong with views of the surrounding mountains and Tibetan settlements.
spots.addr: Tagong, Sichuan, China

spots.name: Friday Market
spots.desc: As the last remaining market town on the ancient Tea & Horse Caravan trail, Shaxi still hosts the local market every Friday. The Bai people from all the villages in Shaxi Valley and the Yi people from the surrounding mountains all come together to trade everything from fresh produces to supplies and horses. Minority women will be dressed in their colorful traditional costumes, and men will often…

spots.name: Pear Orchard Temple
spots.desc: The temple complex houses four unique shrines on four levels, together representing a mix of Buddhist, Daoist and Chinese folk religious traditions. Originally known as 'Ci Yin An' (Temple of Hidden Compassion), this breath taking multi-level temple complex is known as the Shaxi Pear Orchard Temple. Commanding spectacular views across the valley from its vantage point at the head of Diantou…
spots.addr: 084 County Road 县道, Diantou Village 甸头村

spots.name: Bailong Tan
spots.desc: A pool formed by a clear underground spring, this small lake is believed to be sacred to the local Bai people. It supplies drinking water to the villages in Shaxi Valley.

spots.name: Mapingguan Village
spots.desc: Located between Shaxi Valley and the three major Dianxi salt wells to the west, Mapingguan was an important checkpost during the time of the Tea & Horse Caravan Trail where the government collected tax on the salt trade.

spots.name: Sideng Street，Shaxi
spots.desc: Sideng Street is located in Shaxi Town, southern Jianchuan County, Dali Prefecture. It is an important part of the Ancient Tea Horse Road and is called "the surviving market on the Ancient Tea Horse Road" by the World Architectural Heritage Conservation Foundation (WMF). At the end of October 2001, it was listed on the "2002 World Monumental Architectural Heritage Protection List" along with the…
spots.hours: All day long (Preferential treatment policy :1. Free admission for those under 1.2 meters (excluding 1.2 meters), half…

spots.name: Yujin Bridge
spots.desc: Yujin Bridge has a span of 12 meters, a height of 6 meters, a length of 35.4 meters, a width of 5 meters, and stone pillars and slab guardrails. There is a stone turtle head on the top of the vault, looking at the upper reaches of the Heihui River. On the other side, there is a stone turtle tail connecting the lower reaches of the Heizhanjiang River. There are four "salam fish" stone sculptures…

spots.name: Hiking
spots.desc: There are a lot of hiking trails in the mountains both to the east and to the west of Shaxi Valley. The trails are what the local villagers use to go between villages, or to collect firewood, wild herbs, and mushrooms. There are no markers, the trails are easy to follow, but a good sense of direction is needed to not get lost.The 46 Horse Pen Hostel hosts weekly guided hikes around the mountains…

spots.name: Cycling
spots.desc: The Shaxi Valley and its numerous villages is a great place to explore on a bicycle. A day spent riding on the small single-track trail between green farm fields can yield many surprises and hidden gems.

spots.name: Kayaking
spots.desc: It's possible to kayak down the shallow and slow moving water of the Heihui River to see Shaxi Valley from a different angle. Starting from the northern edge of Shaxi Valley and Shibaoshan and ends in Sideng village, the water is mostly flatwater, with a couple small dams that can be navigated.Professional guiding is required.

spots.name: Torch Festival
spots.desc: A major festival for the Bai and the Yi minorities around Shaxi, it is held every year on the 25th day (24th for the Yi people) of the 8th month on the lunar calendar. The local villagers will light torches and big barn fires everywhere, and dance and sing around the fires.

spots.name: Taizihui Holiday
spots.desc: The biggest religious holiday in Shaxi, it is held every year on the 8th day of the second month on the lunar calendar.

spots.name: Dancing Mule Cafe
spots.desc: The main building has tables for at least twenty people, including three balcony tables overlooking the temple courtyard and the fields beyond. All the dishes are sourced locally in the family fields and signature dishes include fried goat cheese in sugar, sweet and sour aubergines and 'Duan Jia' Bai style Noodles. Traditional music performance for groups is available with prior request. All…
spots.addr: Duanjiadeng Village

spots.name: Pear Blossom Temple Restaurant
spots.desc: The Pear Blossom organic Shaxi restaurant offers authentic Shaxi local cooking in an active local folk temple. Their specialties include fresh, handmade "Buddha's Hand" pizza from local ingredients, 10 kinds of home-style jiaozi (dumplings), sweet and savory baba (a Shaxi specialty pastry), farm to table organic vegetables and cheese and a great selection of Chinese and imported wines.…

spots.name: Gui Ju Hotel
spots.desc: The English sign says "hotel", but it's actually just a restaurant. A good budget option to taste some local dishes and the food is good.

spots.name: Horse Pen 46 Youth Hostel
spots.desc: They serve nice coffee, nice western breakfast, as well as Sichuan & Cantonese-style cuisines.
spots.addr: at the south of the theater stage on the old town square

spots.name: Xi Lu Inn
spots.desc: Located in the inner courtyard of the inn, this is one of the cleaner (and more expensive) eateries in town. They serve a mixture of local and Sichuan-style cuisine.

spots.name: Hungry Buddha
spots.desc: Vegan restaurant with 8 seats in front of the kitchen. Pizza and bread are sour dough, seasonal menus offer choices of different degustation menus. Good choice of imported wines; elegant shop with local TCMs, dry mushroom, organic tea cakes and many other selected local products.
spots.addr: Sideng rd

spots.name: Meimei's restaurant (美美饭店)
spots.desc: Serves Yunnan dishes along with Chinese traditional favourite fried dishes (炒菜). Great local food, and far cheaper than the places along Sideng Street (寺登街). No English spoken, but you can just point to what you want in the fridge, and they will do good things with it. Very friendly service.
spots.addr: 084县道

spots.name: The town
spots.desc: The many different routes down to the river provide a pleasant walk among traditional houses, orchards, and cultivated fields. Getting to the bank of the river can be a bit tricky as there is a steep drop-off as you approach the bank, but if you persist you will come across one of the purpose-built staircases. It is no longer necessary to take a boat to get the other side of the river, as there…

spots.name: East Bamboo Forest Temple
spots.local: 东竹林寺; Dong Zhu Lin Si; Tibetan: Dhon-Drupling Gompa
spots.desc: A wonderful temple built on the side of the gorge around 15 km northwest along the main road to Deqin. The monastic village that surrounds it is also quite lovely. Dhon-Drupling Gompa was founded in 1667 by Kusho Dondrub and received its name by the Fifth Dalai Lama in 1670. It has many beautifully intricate paintings inside and houses several precious statues. Getting there by hitch-hiking or…

spots.desc: Black Lake is a mountain lake, elev 4,100 meters, in a wide basin several km northwest of Haba Snow Mountain. Excellent views of the peak and lower rugged crags from the shore and surrounding slopes. A good time to visit would be May and June, when nearby forests burst into color with rhododendron and azalea blossoms. A brisk walk around the entire lake takes half an hour. Three trails or routes…

The high point is a 3,000-meter ridge about an hour from Haba. From…

spots.desc: The trek around Haba Snow Mountain takes 5-8 days. Total distance 85 km of which about 20 km is on paved roads. The high point is Jizhi Pass (4,350 m) south of Black Lake, the low point Qiaotou (1,850 m) near start of Tiger Leaping Gorge. General route: Haba, Black Lake, Jizhi Pass, Jizhi Valley, Qiaotou, Tiger Leaping Gorge, Ennu Village, Haba. Most of the route is shown on maps online.

Apparently best seen in the morning to catch rainbows. 4-5 hour hike. The path starts by crossing lower Yubeng, and turning right near the stupa. There are green trash cans along the path. There is a tea shop about 2/3 of…

spots.desc: Beautiful glacier fed lake above a meadow. 5- to 8-hour hike. The path starts after passing through upper Yubeng - locals can point you in the direction. Along the path there are green trash cans: just follow them. The first part of the trail is flat, and goes through a forest where you will cross a small stream. After, there is about a one hour ascent to the top of a mountain pass. The path up…

spots.desc: A striking, two-story watchtower with arched windows and a flat viewing roof. Originally erected by troops hailing from southern China's Jiangsu region who named it in honor of Jinshan Island in the Yangtze River. The museum focuses on Bao'an district and celebrates the recent history of the city: Deng Xiaoping's "reform and opening up" and the subsequent fast-paced industrial development that has come to define Shenzhen. Fittingly, the museum itself is located in a former factory.At…

Adjacent to the lake is Wangniuting Park (望牛亭公园 Wàngniútíng Gōngyuán), with hiking trails on a small hill. The area is very green and good for a lakeside walk—it's not worth making the trip all the way from the city center just for this, but stop by if you're in the area.

spots.name: Honghua Mountain

The pagoda on top is nice but not old (built in 2009). From the main (south) entrance the walk to the top takes ten minutes if that, but the steps are steep. From the north and east entrances there's a more leisurely…

There's an adjoining park to the north with a big sandpit which is fun for kids. It's not too big, but nice for an hour or so walking around, though the peaceful atmosphere is spoiled by the screeching noise of metro line 11 trains passing by and the sound of planes taking…

Lots of nice restaurants and fancy shops, and the bookstore next to the food court on the third floor has a selection of paperbacks in English. On the lowest level (B1) are a few shops with beautiful traditional Chinese products like statues, porcelain, and inkstones. Even if shopping here is beyond your budget, it's an interesting place for…

The specialty is Taiwanese food, but there are various other restaurants with the usual variety of Chinese cuisines as well. Good place to stop for a snack or a meal after you finish hiking down the mountain.

No one specialty predominates; you'll find all the usual suspects plus some less common ones like Henan…

But at night is when it really gets going: every evening from 17:00 to midnight, the sidewalk becomes Lefan Night Market (乐翻夜市), a bustling row of stands and carts selling tasty snacks and greasy dinners. spots.name: Kylin Screen Wall Watchtower
spots.desc: Houses an intricate brick-carved relief of a Kylin (Qilin, a mythological Chinese hooved chimerical beast symbolizing fortune and peace) embedded into the interior wall. This decorative carving is extremely rare on Great Wall fortifications and represents one of the section's artistic highlights.
spots.addr: Eastern section of Jinshanling

spots.name: Inscribed Brick Wall Sections
spots.desc: Clear historical stamps carved directly into individual clay bricks. Inscriptions state the year (e.g., Wanli Er Nian / 1574) and identify the specific military unit, such as the Zhending Brigade, confirming strict quality-control mechanisms enforced during the Ming dynasty.
spots.addr: Scattered along the central ramparts

spots.name: Classic Ridge Hike #ba2481
spots.desc: The standard half-day trek (3.5 to 4.5 hours). Enter at the , ascend via the Zhuanduokou trail to , walk eastward past Small Jinshan, Big Jinshan, and Hualou, then descend via the exit at to the , where you can catch a shuttle van back to the main entrance. Note that since 2025, Dongwuyan closes at 17:00; passing through the tower to ascend or descend is not permitted after this time according to…

spots.name: Extended Ridge Hike #63a1b5
spots.desc: For a longer and more challenging route, start further west along the ridge at . To reach this point from the valley, turn onto the trail at the opposite the Jinshanling campsite. Like the Classic Ridge Hike, this route continues east along the wall to finish at the East Five-window Tower (Dongwuyan).

spots.name: Gubeikou to Jinshanling Hike #ffff00
spots.desc: A classic, rugged 10 km (4–6 hours) point-to-point traverse connecting wild, unrestored ruins with dramatic restored ramparts. Important detour: At the (二十四眼楼, Èrshísì Yǎnlóu), the ridgeline enters an active military restricted zone. Do not attempt to stay on the wall or cross military fences; descend the marked dirt path to the north/valley side to bypass the military installation through…
spots.price: Panlongshan entry: 25 or North City Gate entry: 33 plus entrance to Jinshanling section 33

spots.name: Sunrise & Sunset Photography
spots.desc: Jinshanling is renowned as one of the best locations in China for dawn and dusk landscape photography. Gates open early (from 06:00, earlier for registered photo groups in peak summer) to accommodate sunrise shoots. A very popular spot for sunrise photography is a .

spots.name: Jinshanling Great Wall Marathon
spots.desc: Held annually in mid-spring (usually April), drawing international runners to tackle thousands of stone steps along the mountain ridges. Either half-marathon or 10k.

spots.name: Noodle House
spots.desc: Quick, convenient option serving bowls of hot beef noodles, fried noodles, steamed pork buns (baozi), and bottled drinks for visitors heading up the mountain or waiting for the return bus to Beijing. Do not expect too much taste wise.
spots.addr: Jinshanling Commercial Street

spots.name: Unique Dream of Red Mansions
spots.desc: A grand, immersive theatrical park directed by Wang Chaoge based on the classical Chinese novel "Dream of the Red Chamber". Features over 100 indoor and outdoor performance spaces and surreal architectural gateways.
spots.addr: Heping Road, Guangyang District, Langfang

spots.name: Langfang Cultural Art Park
spots.local: 廊坊文化艺术中心 / 廊坊文化艺术公园
spots.desc: A massive central park featuring landscaped gardens, lakes, museum exhibition halls, and the Silk Road International Arts Center.
spots.addr: Guangyang District, Langfang

spots.name: Qixing Lake Hot Spring Resort
spots.desc: Bazhou is famous for its geothermal resources. This resort area offers traditional Chinese hot spring baths and leisure gardens.
spots.addr: Bazhou, Langfang

spots.name: Langfang Nature Park
spots.desc: A large city park with wooden boardwalks, lakes, pine forests, and a small zoo, ideal for walking and weekend picnics.
spots.addr: Guangyang District, Langfang

spots.name: Silk Road International Arts Center
spots.local: 丝绸之路国际艺术交流中心
spots.desc: A grand venue hosting international art exhibitions, musicals, concerts, and theatrical performances.
spots.addr: Guangyang District, Langfang

spots.name: Grand Epoch City (First City Under Heaven)
spots.desc: A large scale replica complex modeled after the ancient city walls, gates, and classical architecture of old Beijing.
spots.addr: Xianghe County, Langfang

spots.name: Langfang Wanda Plaza
spots.desc: A modern multi-story shopping complex featuring international fashion brands, a cinema, supermarkets, and diverse dining options.
spots.addr: Guangyang District, Langfang

spots.name: Xianghe Furniture City / Local Souvenirs
spots.desc: Xianghe is renowned nationwide for its massive furniture markets. For food souvenirs, local specialties such as smoked chicken from Bazhou and traditional pastries make great gifts.
spots.addr: Xianghe County, Langfang

spots.name: Xianghe Donkey Burger
spots.local: 香河肉饼 / 驴肉火烧
spots.desc: A must-try local specialty. Crispy flatbread filled with savory seasoned meat or donkey meat, popular for a quick and satisfying traditional local meal.
spots.addr: Guangyang District, Langfang

spots.name: Xianghe Meat Pie Restaurant
spots.desc: Famous throughout northern China, Xianghe meat pies feature thin, multi-layered dough stuffed with minced pork or beef and green onions, pan-fried to golden perfection.
spots.addr: Anci District, Langfang

spots.name: Tea House & Cafe in Cultural Park
spots.desc: A relaxing spot located near the lake inside the Cultural Art Park, offering traditional Chinese teas, modern espresso drinks, and a quiet ambiance for afternoon chats.
spots.addr: Inside Langfang Cultural Art Park, Guangyang District

spots.name: Hechangyuan Museum
spots.desc: A private art museum specialising in paintings, calligraphy and ceramics.
spots.addr: Building 9, COFCO Yipin Lanshan, Danzi Avenue, Pingshan District (坪山区丹梓大道中粮一品澜山8栋)

spots.name: Dongjiang Column Memorial
spots.local: 东江纵队纪念馆, East River Column Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A museum devoted to telling the story of the Dongjiang Column, a column of Guangdong-based Communist guerrila fighters who fought the Japanese in World War Two. All information is in Chinese only.
spots.addr: 1/230 Dongzong Road, Pingshan Subdistrict, Pingshan District (坪山区坪山街道东纵路230号-1)

spots.name: Shenzhen Natural History Museum
spots.desc: Officially opened in July 2026, this is now the largest natural history museum in the South China region.
spots.hours: 09:30-18:00, no entry after 17:30, closed on Mondays
spots.price: Standard adult tickets are ¥80, discounts are available for children aged 6 to 17 and adults over 60, children under 6…
spots.addr: 6 Wenxiang Road, Pingshan District (坪山区文祥路6号)

spots.name: Dapeng Peninsula National Geopark
spots.local: 大鹏半岛国家地质公园, Dapeng Peninsula National Geological Park
spots.desc: There is a geological museum at the entrance to the park, displaying lots of different rocks, minerals, and fossils, mostly from China with a focus on Guangdong. The museum's information panels are mostly bilingual in Chinese and English, and nearby are trailheads for hikes into the park. The park is open all day; the museum is open Tu-F 09:30 to 16:00, Sa Su 09:30-17:00, closed on Mondays.
spots.addr: 1 Geopark Road, Nan'ao, Dapeng New District (大鹏新区南澳地质公园路1号)

spots.name: Longgang Public Golf Course
spots.desc: This course was the brainchild of a former official of the Shenzhen Government who wanted to bring golf to the masses. It is as an eighteen-hole 72 par course, situated on rolling hills in the Longgang District. The founders of the course wanted to keep green fees at 20-30% of commercial golf courses.
spots.addr: Next to the International Velodrome, He Keng, Henggang Town, Longgang District

spots.name: OCT East Golf Club
spots.desc: Shenzhen's newest and poshest golf course. It has two 18-hole courses, each with its own luxury clubhouse. Set in spectacular mountains overlooking Dameisha and Mirs Bay.
spots.addr: OCT East, Dameisha (盐田区大梅沙东部华乔城)

spots.name: Century Seaview Golf Club
spots.desc: An 18-hole PGA golf course set in beautiful mountain and sea surroundings near Nan'ao Town, Dapeng Peninsula.
spots.addr: Yangchou Bay, Nan' ao Town, Longgang (龙岗区南澳洋畴湾)

spots.name: Dameisha Beach
spots.desc: The most well-known beach in Shenzhen. Easily accessible from downtown, but it's often crowded and the water is dirty.

spots.name: Xiaomeisha Beach
spots.desc: Close to Dameisha. Also crowded and the water is also dirty. Especially avoid going on the weekends and during summer vacation (July and August).

spots.name: Beizaijiao Beach
spots.desc: A small beach, a few hundred meters long, not far past Dameisha and Xiaomeisha, but less developed, less crowded, and cleaner.

spots.name: Jin Sha Wan Beach
spots.desc: From Shenzhen take one of several buses (e.g. 364, E11, or H92) to Dapeng Station (大鵬站) in Wangmu (王母虛) Village in Dapeng. Then you can take a quick shuttle bus south to JinSha Beach. Entry is ¥10. On weekends and holidays the beach can be quite crowded. The sand is rather coarse and not particularly clean, but it can be fun to go here and people watch. Also it is interesting that you can look…

spots.name: Xichong Beach
spots.desc: Beautiful Xichong beach is far from the downtown core, well past Dameisha. Less developed, this beach is much more peaceful and clean than other beaches in Shenzhen. Visit Sun Sailing for watersports or local fine dining.

spots.name: Longgang Book City
spots.desc: The Longgang branch of Book City, Shenzhen's local chain of large bookstores. Look for a big red building.
spots.addr: Cultural Center Area C, 8028-4 Longxiang Boulevard, Longcheng Subdistrict 龙城街道龙翔大道8028-4号文化中心C区

spots.name: China Printmaking Museum
spots.desc: China's largest printmaking museum. Part of the China Guanlan Original Printmaking Base (中国·观澜版画原创产业基地).
spots.addr: Yuxin Road, Guanlan Subdistrict, Longhua District (龙华区观澜街道裕新路)

spots.name: Hezheng Art Museum
spots.local: 深圳市合正艺术博物馆
spots.desc: Private art museum established by businessman Li Weiqing in 2016. Items on display include paintings, calligraphy, ceramics and sculptures.
spots.addr: Level 2, Building 7, Zhongzhou Huafu, Yu'an 2nd Road, Bao'an District (宝安区裕安二路中洲华府七栋2楼)

spots.name: Ebohr Timepiece Culture Museum
spots.local: 依波钟表文化博物馆, Ebohr Horologe Culture Museum
spots.desc: Owned and operated by Ebohr, one of China's leading luxury watch manufacturers. Solo visitors and small groups (with less than 10 people) are required to make an appointment before visiting (this can be done either by phone or on WeChat). Visitation time is limited to 60-90 minutes and visitors are expected to follow the directions of their tour guide at all times.
spots.hours: Groups of 10 or more people may visit the museum between 09:00 and 17:00 on any day of the week. Solo visitors and…
spots.price: ¥30 (the fee is waived if you make an appointment on WeChat)
spots.addr: Ebohr Building, Jin'an Road, Gongming Subdistrict, Guangming New District (光明新区公明街道金安路依波大厦)

spots.name: China Military Uniforms Museum
spots.desc: Displays a wide variety of military uniforms from ancient times to the early 21st century.
spots.addr: Building A, Bennishi Industrial Park, Dalang Garments Base, Longhua District (龙华区大浪服装基地奔霓诗工业园A栋)

spots.name: Shiyan Lake Hot Spring Resort
spots.local: 石岩湖温泉度假村; Shí​yán​hú Wēn​quán​ Dù​jià​cūn​​
spots.desc: This has been a popular attraction since the 16th century when it was named as one of the "Eight Great Views of Xin'an County" (the county of which Hong Kong and Shenzhen were part). It's on a man-made reservoir at the back of Yangtai Mountain, and is not easy to get to but it is worth the trouble. Water springs from the ground at over 60 °C, but is cooled to about 40 °C before being fed into…
spots.addr: Shiyan Town, Bao'an District (宝安区石岩镇; Bǎo​'ān​ Qū​ Shí​yán​ Zhèn​)

spots.name: Mission Hills Golf Course
spots.desc: The world's biggest golf course with 216 holes. Each course is designed by a different world champion golfer. The Golf World Cup has granted a twelve-year franchise to Mission Hills

spots.name: Bao'an Book City
spots.desc: The Bao'an branch of Book City, Shenzhen's local chain of large bookstores.
spots.addr: 新桥街道沙井中心路89

spots.name: Pingzhou Eat Street
spots.desc: Quiet during the day but a happening area in the evening. A variety of Chinese restaurants, including seafood and barbecue, as well as a slightly hidden but authentic Mexican restaurant (across from KFC).
spots.addr: Haicheng Road, Bao'an District 宝安区海城路

spots.name: Chetian Doufu Fang
spots.desc: Delicious Hakka food. The specialty is Chetian-style tofu (Chetian being a town out in Heyuan, Hakka country to the northeast of Shenzhen). Good vegetarian options, though if you're vegetarian you should order carefully as Hakka-style tofu is sometimes stuffed with meat! Recognize the restaurant from across the street with the big white characters spelling its name, or from close up with the…
spots.addr: 68 Fanshen Road, Xin'an Subdistrict, Bao'an District 宝安区新安街道翻身路68号

spots.name: Laojun Cave Taoist Temple
spots.desc: The largest and most important Taoist Temple in Chongqing. The temple was founded in the Tang Dynasty and greatly expanded during the Ming Dynasty. It was largely rebuilt after suffering extensive damage during the Cultural Revolution.
spots.addr: 29 Laojunpo, Anshan Subdistrict, Nan’an District (南岸区南山街道老君坡29号)

spots.name: Shengdeng Mountain Forest Park
spots.local: Shengdengshan Forest Park, 圣灯山森林公园, 圣灯山原始森林公园
spots.desc: Shengdeng Mountain is 1064 m above sea level. Legend has it that the emperor Jianwen of the Ming Dynasty built a house here and lived here when he took refuge. Hence, the Chinese name of the mountain is sometimes written as '圣登山', which literally means a mountain which was climbed by a sage.
spots.addr: Tiaoshi Town, Banan District (巴南区跳石镇)

spots.name: Chiang Kai-Shek's Mount Huang residence
spots.local: 黄山蒋介石官邸, 蒋介石旧军事总部 Chiang Kai-Shek's old military headquarters
spots.desc: When Chongqing was the capital of China during World War II, Jiang Jieshi (Chiang Kai-Shek) established his military headquarters up in the mountains above Chongqing. As a result the Japanese bombers never found it, and it is now a museum, preserved as it was during the war. There are many buildings in the beautiful compound and you can visit his work room with the motto over his desk "all…
spots.addr: Mount Huang Scenic Area, Nan'an District (南岸区黄山风景区)

spots.name: Old French Naval Barracks Site
spots.desc: It was built in 1903 to serve the French navy. The French Embassy was temporarily based here during the Second World War. The building was reopened to the public in June 2018 after having undergone more than a year of restoration work.
spots.addr: 142 Danzishi Qiantai Lane, Binjiang Road, Nan'an District (南岸区滨江路弹子石谦泰巷142号)

spots.name: Shenzhen Traditional Chinese Medicine Museum
spots.local: 深圳中医药博物馆, 龙岗区中医药博物馆 Longgang District Museum of Traditional Chinese Medicine
spots.addr: Level 2, Science Education Building, Longgang District Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, 1 Dayun Road, Tiyu Xincheng, Longgang District…

spots.name: Qiniang Mountain
spots.desc: The second tallest mountain in Shenzhen, at 867.4 meters.
spots.addr: Dapeng

spots.name: Meilian Mahogany Art Museum
spots.addr: 348 Golf Avenue, Guanlan Subdistrict, Longhua New District (龙华新区观澜街道高尔夫大道348号)

spots.name: Changjiang Museum of Contemporary Art
spots.local: Yangtze River Museum of Contemporary Art, 重庆长江当代美术馆
spots.addr: Yangtze River Art Square, Nanbin Road, Nan'an District (南岸区南滨路长江艺术广场)

spots.name: Nanshan Botanical Gardens
spots.price: ¥30 to ¥50 depending on how many attractions you wish to visit
spots.addr: 101 Nanshan Botanical Gardens Road, Nan'an District (南岸区南山植物园路101号)

spots.local: 南温泉风景区, 南温泉公园
